iMouse API:
what the rack can do

Everything the Phonefarm / iMouse XP kernel lets software do with a rack of real iPhones, verified against the vendor documentation and the measurements taken on this rig, organized by what it is good for: marketing automation, account management, operations, data, testing, and the ideas nobody wrote on the box.

Two independent channels. Control is USB HID into the phone; video is AirPlay back out. Every capability in this document is built from those two primitives plus one side channel: an iOS Shortcut the kernel can trigger with a hotkey.

Section 1 · Executive summary

Executive summary and which edition you have

This document maps what your iMouse rack can actually be made to do, function by function, against the API that is installed on it and against measurements taken on the rig itself on 7 to 10 September 2026. It covers 165 use cases across marketing, accounts, commerce, data collection, QA, fleet operations and integration, and it is explicit about the sixteen things people commonly expect from a phone rack that this one cannot do. Every claim below is traceable either to the vendor documentation or to a measurement on these two iPhones and nineteen boards.

What the rack is

The rack is real iPhones, not emulators and not a jailbreak. Each phone is a stock handset with no app installed on it. Two entirely separate channels reach each phone, and almost every failure mode in this document is a failure of one channel while the other is healthy.

Control runs over USB. A small WCH HID board (VID 720A, one unique PID per board) sits between the PC and the phone's Lightning port and presents itself to iOS as a mouse and keyboard. IMService.exe owns those boards and reports them through /config/usb/get. One board drives exactly one phone. Control does not use Wi-Fi at all.

Video runs over Wi-Fi. The phone casts its screen by AirPlay to a receiver advertised by this PC over Bonjour, and AirplayMirroring.exe decodes the stream on TCP 17000. Video is reported separately, through /device/get (state and air_pid).

The practical consequence is that a phone can be fully controllable with no picture, or perfectly visible and deaf to every input. Any health display you build must show both states per slot, or it will lie to you.

What the API fundamentally gives you

Stripped of detail, the kernel offers three things:

  • Pixels in. /pic/screenshot returns the current decoded mirror frame for one phone, as raw BMP, JPEG or base64 JSON, optionally cropped by rectangle or written straight to disk.
  • HID events out. /mouse/click, /mouse/down, /mouse/move, /mouse/up, /mouse/swipe, /mouse/wheel, /mouse/reset, /key/sendkey, /key/down and /key/up, each taking a comma-separated id list so one request fans out to many phones at once.
  • An iOS Shortcut side channel. The /shortcut/* family drives an iMouse-supplied iOS Shortcut on the phone to do things a pointer cannot: push files into the camera roll or the Files tree, set and read the clipboard (the only route to non-ASCII text), open a URL, toggle some system switches, restart the handset.

Around those sit device and group management, per-device AirPlay settings, kernel configuration, account and licence state, and a WebSocket on the same port that broadcasts callbacks for device, USB and cast events. That is the whole surface. There is no element tree, no log access, no app install, no telemetry and no outbound webhook.

The headline: what is achievable

Of 165 use cases examined, 149 are achievable and 16 are refuted. Only 3 are recorded as verified without qualification, because on a rig whose only oracle is a decoded video frame, nearly everything carries a real caveat worth reading before you build on it.

VerdictCountWhat it means here

The single biggest structural fact in that table is the Shortcut column. Thirty-eight percent of everything useful runs through the iOS Shortcut channel, so installing and testing that Shortcut on every phone is not an optional extra, it is the difference between a pointer toy and a working rack.

Strongest opportunities, by domain

  • Publishing and marketing. Push one asset into every phone's camera roll with a single multi-id upload, put the caption on every clipboard with a single clipboard call, then drive each app's own composer with mirrored taps. Platform-specific sequences for TikTok, Instagram, Threads, Facebook, YouTube Shorts, Pinterest, X, LinkedIn, Telegram and Discord are in section 4. Launching a composer by URL scheme avoids home-screen icon hunting entirely.
  • QA and testing. This is where the rack is strongest, because everything QA wants is exactly what the rack produces: golden-frame visual regression on raw frames, deep-link and universal-link matrices, push notification render and arrival latency, localization sweeps at native resolution through the Shortcut screenshot, ad slot fill timing, keyboard focus-order audits, and synchronized N-phone race testing that no simulator can reproduce.
  • Data collection and monitoring. With no OCR plug-in, the exact-text channel is select-all, copy, then read the phone clipboard. That yields page text out of Safari, post identifiers and order numbers out of native feeds, and structured answers from a Shortcut you write yourself. Frame differencing covers the rest: grid diffs, autoplay detection, hang detection.
  • Fleet operations. Two-channel health boards, pointer-nudge liveness probes that actually prove input is honored, USB flap watchdogs driven by the usb_change callback, stuck-click self-healing, cast-on-connect sweepers, Wi-Fi link scoring by delivered frames per second, and physical slot roll-call by torch.
  • Integration. The kernel WebSocket is a usable event bus with msgid-correlated RPC. Around it you can build a per-phone job queue with one lease per board, a coordinate registry keyed by model and mirror geometry, an idempotent verify-then-escalate action wrapper, and a vision-model loop that takes a raw frame in and emits a tap out.

The clearest limits

  • No SMS or iMessage send, and no way to read an incoming message, OTP or notification body. Only the sms: composer deep link plus a tap.
  • No phone telemetry at all: no battery, temperature, storage, GPS or carrier.
  • No structured app state. No accessibility tree, no DOM, no element list, no logs, no crash hooks, no network capture.
  • One pointer only. No pinch, rotate, two-finger or pressure gesture exists, and the board walks the pointer at roughly 0.6 ms per pixel, so velocity-dependent flicks are out of reach.
  • No Apple Pay, Face ID or side-button confirmation. Anything requiring a physical button press stops the rack.
  • A comma-separated id list is a fan-out, not a batch: every listed phone gets the same parameters.
  • No kernel-originated webhooks, and no caller authentication whatsoever.

Which edition this rig runs, and what that means

This rig runs the iMouse XP International Edition. That is settled by probe, not by inference.

  • IMService.exe listens on TCP 9911 and serves both HTTP and WebSocket there. The WebSocket path is /api.
  • Port 9912 is closed. Nothing listens on it, so the Phonefarm document's HTTP endpoint cannot be reached at all.
  • Phonefarm-style function names posted to 9911, for example {"fun":"get_device_list"}, return HTTP 500 with a list-index error. The XP kernel splits fun on a slash and expects a path, so a bare name is rejected before dispatch.
  • Documented XP paths answer correctly on the same port: /api/device/get returns both iPhones, /api/config/usb/get returns nineteen boards, /api/device/group/get returns an empty list.

Practical rules that follow. Address everything as GET http://127.0.0.1:9911/api/<path>?k=v, or as a JSON POST to /api with fun set to that same path. Use id, not deviceid. Read the real result from data.code, where 0 is success, and treat the top-level status of 200 as nothing more than "the request was accepted". Match on codes, never on message text, because XP returns Chinese-language messages where the Phonefarm document shows English. A guessed path returns 404 with a Chinese "interface does not exist" string rather than a structured error.

The Phonefarm-edition document you were supplied is still worth keeping. It describes the same hardware and broadly the same capabilities, and it is a useful concept map when the XP documentation is terse. It is simply the wrong wire format for this machine, and a handful of its features do not exist here at all, notably server-pushed screenshot streaming and multiple AirPlay receivers.

Trap Two sibling APIs, one of them not yours

Sample code found online, and most of the vendor's own examples, may be written for the Phonefarm edition. It will fail against this rig in three distinct ways: connection refused on 9912, HTTP 500 for bare function names on 9911, and 404 for paths that only exist in the other edition. Section 2 gives the mapping and section 14 the full path tables.

Open The vision plug-ins are not installed

/api/pic/ocr answers HTTP 200 with data.code 28, "plug-in not connected". Assume /pic/find-image, /pic/find-image-cv, /pic/find-text and their enhanced variants are in the same state until you probe them. Server-side OCR and template matching are documented capabilities of the XP edition, so this is an install question, not an architectural one, but until it is resolved every "find the button" design has to run client-side on raw frames.

The numbers that shape every design

RAW FRAME FETCH
2 ms
p50 for BMP, 84 req/s flat out, 1.6 MB per frame
JPEG FRAME FETCH
40.5 ms
p50, capped near 21 req/s, kernel re-encodes
POINTER WALK
0.6 ms/px
1000 px move measured at 592 ms
AIRPLAY SOURCE RATE
28.9 vs 4.5 fps
two identical iPhone XRs, same iOS build
MIRROR GEOMETRY
500 x 1080
click space, not the 414 x 896 iOS point space
CONCURRENT POLLERS
512 req/s
ten pollers, p50 3 ms, no shared bottleneck
RACK SIZE
19 boards, 2 phones
three 7-port hubs, 19 of 21 slots populated
SCREEN-CHANGE FLOOR
0.02 vs 20+
idle mean pixel diff against a real reaction

Four of those deserve a sentence each. Frame capture is effectively free on loopback, so build a wall of live thumbnails without guilt, but reuse one buffer per poller because every frame is far above the .NET large object heap threshold. Movement is not free, and a move's latency is meaningless without its distance, so coalesce drags and hovers to the newest position. The two phones deliver frames at rates that differ by a factor of six because of their Wi-Fi links, not because of contention, so never time out a screen check on a 30 fps assumption. And "did the screen change" must be a mean absolute pixel difference against an idle control, never a hash comparison, because the clock and encoder noise change every frame.

Wrong A success response does not mean the tap landed

HTTP 200 with data.code 0 means the board accepted the report. It says nothing about what iOS did. Measured on 10 September 2026: a phone reached a state where /mouse/move visibly moved the pointer and the Home key still worked, while /mouse/click produced a 0.09 mean pixel difference, indistinguishable from an untouched screen. /mouse/up did not clear it; /mouse/reset did, and it stayed cleared. The frame is the only oracle.

One last thing to carry into every section that follows. The kernel has no authentication of any kind, and the documentation's own examples call it across a LAN. Anyone who can reach port 9911 on this PC can drive all nineteen boards. Treat that as a property of the product, firewall the port to trusted hosts, and never put this machine on an untrusted network.

Also worth knowing

When not to use the rack

Everything above holds, and none of it applies to an app whose source you control. If you own the Xcode project, XCUITest run locally, or Appium's XCUITest driver talking to WebDriverAgent, over the same USB connection this rack uses for control, gives you a real element tree, first-party logs, crash reports and app install and reinstall on demand. The rack has no route to any of that. It is not an oversight in the API: /pic/screenshot hands you a decoded video frame, not a view hierarchy; /mouse/click and /key/sendkey hand you a coordinate or a keycode, not an accessibility identifier to assert against; /shortcut/* reaches the clipboard and the camera roll, not a debugger or a log stream. Spending months turning those four primitives into element-aware, log-backed automation for your own app produces a weaker Appium, built the hard way, for a problem Appium already solved.

Use the rack for what XCUITest cannot reach at all. Other people's apps, where there is no project to attach a test target to and no way to link WebDriverAgent in. Real carrier and Wi-Fi egress through an actual SIM and antenna, which a simulator, and most cloud devices, do not reproduce. N-phone simultaneity through one comma-separated id list, rather than orchestrating N separate simulators or sessions by hand. And physical hardware behavior, AirPlay mirroring quality, a real Lightning HID board, real battery and thermal state under load, that a simulator run on a Mac cannot produce. A commercial device cloud sits between the two: real hardware without owning a rack, billed by the minute, with no guarantee of the same physical unit run to run, a reasonable choice for broad device coverage on a short test pass rather than a fixed rack running continuously. And when the job is really "post to this account" or "read this account's data" rather than "operate this UI", the platform's own published API is faster, authenticated, and does not depend on a mirrored tap landing, so it belongs ahead of the rack whenever that door is open.

Section 2 · The API surface, end to end

The API surface, end to end

This is the full map of what the kernel exposes: every device, input, screen, vision, shortcut, casting, recovery and calibration call, plus the events it pushes back. The installed kernel on this rig is IMService.exe, the XP edition, listening on 127.0.0.1:9911 for both HTTP and WebSocket. The Phonefarm-edition document describes a sibling API on a different port with different paths; where the two disagree, this section says so and gives the XP path to actually call. Every Phonefarm function name probed against this kernel returned HTTP 500, so build against the /xp/... paths below, not the bare Phonefarm names.

Phonefarm functions catalogued
48
46 numbered + get_group_list + ocr_ex
Shortcut sub-functions
24
ids 1-24; 9 undocumented, 12 & 14 withdrawn
WebSocket callbacks
8 + 13
Phonefarm events + XP-only events
Working port on this rig
9911
9912 (Phonefarm HTTP) is closed

Wrong Phonefarm names do not work here

Posting a Phonefarm-style body such as {"fun":"get_device_list"} to this kernel returns status 500, "List index out of bounds (1). TStringList object range is 0..0." The XP kernel splits fun on "/" and expects a path with at least two segments, so a bare snake_case name is rejected before it ever reaches a handler. Every row below gives the XP path that actually answers on this rig.

Device and group management

Devices and groups are the addressing layer underneath every other call. A device only exists in the kernel after its first AirPlay connection; group ids are opaque numeric strings the kernel assigns.

FunctionXP pathPurposeKey paramsTransport / edition
set_dev/device/setBind a device to a USB board (vid+pid), assign a group, rename it, or point it at a calibration record by CRC.id (comma list for name/gid/crc; hardware binding is one device per call), vid+pid (send both or neither), gid, location_crc, nameHTTP+WS, all editions
del_dev/device/delRemove a device record. Refuses while the phone is online.id (comma list on XP)HTTP+WS, all editions
set_group/device/group/setCreate a new group (gid "0") or rename an existing one.gid, nameHTTP+WS, all editions
del_group/device/group/delDelete a group by id. XP refuses a non-empty group.gid (comma list on XP)HTTP+WS, all editions
get_device_list/device/getReturn every known device, online and offline, with full properties.none on Phonefarm; optional id filter on XPHTTP+WS, all editions
get_group_list/device/group/getReturn all device groups.noneHTTP+WS, all editions
get_usb_list/config/usb/getList the connected vendor USB control boards.noneHTTP+WS, all editions
get_devicemodel_list/config/devicemodel/getReturn the supported-model table and the mouse-calibration library.noneHTTP+WS, all editions

Watch out

  • location_crc must come from a manual collection or an official library record, never invented; a wrong CRC silently mis-positions every tap.
  • Verified on this rig: /device/get returns both XRs with imgw/imgh 500x1080, location_crc B0DBD800, and the mirror-geometry fields Phonefarm records do not carry at all.
  • XP renames several fields: username→user_name, srvname→srv_name, airhandle→air_handle. Result containers also change shape: XP always returns data.list arrays, never an object keyed by id.
  • Group id is a string that looks like a Unix timestamp; treat it as opaque, not as a sortable number.

Mouse input

Five calls cover every pointer gesture: absolute click, absolute move, press, release, and a canned swipe. Coordinates on this rig are proven to be mirror-image pixels, 500 x 1080, not the phone's logical 414 x 896 points.

FunctionXP pathPurposeKey paramsTransport / edition
click/mouse/clickTap, or long-press when time > 0 (context menus, icon wiggle, haptic touch).id (comma list drives N boards in parallel), button (Phonefarm "left"/"right"; XP numeric 1-8), x, y, time msHTTP+WS, all editions
mouse_down/mouse/downPress and hold a button at the current position; pair with moves and an up for an arbitrary-path drag.id, buttonHTTP+WS, all editions
mouse_move/mouse/moveMove the pointer to an absolute position (hover, or one segment of a drag).id, x, yHTTP+WS, all editions
mouse_up/mouse/upRelease a button.id, buttonHTTP+WS, all editions
swipe/mouse/swipeDirectional drag, either by screen percentage (kernel picks the start/end points) or between explicit coordinates, as a stepped loop.direction, length/len, sx/sy/ex/ey, for/stepping, XP adds step_sleep and brakeHTTP+WS, all editions

Watch out

  • Measured: the board walks the pointer at about 0.6 ms per pixel. A 1000 px move costs about 592 ms; a full-height 1080 px swipe takes roughly 580 ms, which iOS may read as a slow drag rather than a flick. Driving several phones costs the same as one, since the boards act in parallel.
  • In percentage mode, swipe has the kernel pick the start and end coordinates itself on each call rather than using one fixed pair; the doc does not state the magnitude, nor whether it still applies when explicit sx/sy/ex/ey are given.
  • Measured trap: a phone can silently stop honouring click while move and hardware keys keep working. mouse_up does not clear it; only the reset call in Recovery does.
  • Phone-side settings invisible to the API — AssistiveTouch on, tracking sensitivity and speed at maximum, Full Keyboard Access enabled, Auto-Lock never — are the usual cause of "looks fine but ignores input."

Keyboard input

Single-key press/release and hotkey combos are ASCII-only and ship natively; Unicode text rides a separate bridge through the iMouse Shortcut.

FunctionXP pathPurposeKey paramsTransport / edition
key_down/key/downPress and hold one key (modifiers, chords, game controls).id, key; XP also lists fn_key here (leave key blank when using it)HTTP+WS, all editions
key_up/key/upRelease one key.id, keyHTTP+WS, all editions
send_key/key/sendkeyType an ASCII string, or fire a modifier combination such as Home or screenshot.id, key (text) or fn_key (combo, mutually exclusive)HTTP+WS, all editions

Needs

  • Full Keyboard Access enabled on the phone for any key call to register.
  • For send_text: the iMouse Shortcut installed, the kernel IP entered, run once with permissions granted, and bound to an AssistiveTouch custom key from the console; both the USB channel (to fire the hotkey) and the LAN channel (Shortcut to kernel) must be up.

Watch out

  • send_key and key_down/key_up accept English letters, digits and ASCII punctuation only; there is no Unicode path except through send_text or shortcut id 10 (clipboard) plus a paste hotkey.
  • Named keys on Phonefarm: BACKSPACE, SPACE, TAB, WIN, ENTER, SHIFT, CTRL, ALT, ESC, PAGEUP, PAGEDOWN, arrow keys, F1-F12, FN. XP's documented hotkey table is considerably larger — see the XP-only table further down.
  • Measured: hardware keys such as Home keep working while the pointer is in the stuck-click state, making send_key WIN+h a useful liveness probe for the control channel.
  • send_text is accept-only on the synchronous reply; the characters appear on screen roughly 3 seconds after the completion signal, and over plain HTTP that signal cannot be received at all.

Screenshots and screen capture

One call captures a single frame; Phonefarm's second call turns that into a server-push stream. The XP kernel has no push stream, so a live view is built by polling.

Watch out

  • There is no push stream on this kernel. A live view is client-side polling of /pic/screenshot?binary=true; a still screen yields almost no new frames, and the source frame rate is per-phone and content-dependent (one XR here runs about 29 fps, its twin about 4.5 fps).
  • Phonefarm's original flag returns a resolution different from the phone's logical size, requiring the caller to convert coordinates; XP screenshots are already in the same imgw x imgh mirror-pixel space that mouse calls use, so no conversion is needed there.
  • Input traffic does not interfere with screenshot polling on this rig, measured directly.

Vision: image search, OCR and colour matching

Five recognition calls exist. Two need a picture-search plug-in, two need an OCR plug-in, and two need no plug-in at all. On this rig the OCR plug-in is confirmed not connected (probe returned code 28); the picture-search plug-in's status is unconfirmed and should be assumed unavailable until separately probed.

FunctionXP pathPurposeKey paramsTransport / edition

Trap OCR-dependent chain is dark on this rig

ocr, ocr_ex, and — because they need OCR internally — save_autoscreen_point and save_restart_point (and by extension the fully-automated form of auto_connect_screen and restart_device) cannot work until the OCR plug-in is installed and connected. find_multi_color is unaffected and is the practical plug-in-free option today.

Needs

  • XP adds /pic/find-image-cv (OpenCV template matching) and /pic/find-text / /pic/find-text-ex (OCR plus string matching, with a contain flag) — same plug-in dependencies.
  • XP's iMouse Shortcut version 1.3+ exposes /shortcut/other/screenshot, find-image, find-image-cv, ocr, ocr-ex, find-text, find-text-ex and find-multi-color as on-phone fallbacks that need no server-side plug-in. Their parameters are not separately documented beyond the path names — probe before relying on them, but this is the likeliest route to OCR on this rig without installing the plug-in.

Watch out

  • Result shapes differ by edition: Phonefarm returns top-level result/rectangle/confidence/code; XP always returns data.list of {index, centre, rect, similarity, code}.
  • Colour-match encoding differs: Phonefarm uses a relative offset-colour list with a 0-3 scan direction; XP uses a flat list of absolute x|y|RRGGBB-tolerance points with no scan-order option.

Watch out

Casting and AirPlay control

These calls start, stop and tune the video channel — separate from the USB control channel used by mouse and keyboard calls.

Watch out

  • Phonefarm's document gives rough figures for its three presets — energy-saving around 5 Mbps per landscape game and roughly 100 phones per PC; normal around 10 Mbps and 50 phones; high-performance around 20 Mbps with basically no delay — but does not define the measurement, and it is a Phonefarm-edition figure, not a measurement on this rig.
  • XP runs a single AirPlay receiver (this rig advertises as iMouseXP-5429 on port 17000); there is no multi-receiver service count to read or set. The nearest XP lever for casting reliability is connect_failed_retry in /config/imserver/set, and /imserver/regmdns to re-advertise the receiver if phones stop seeing it.
  • Per-device /device/airplay/set changes disconnect the current cast and apply on the next connection.

Recovery

The rig has one recovery call per failure layer, from the pointer up to the whole kernel.

FunctionXP pathPurposeKey paramsTransport / edition
mouse_reset_pos/mouse/resetReset the pointer to (0,0). Measured on this rig: the only call that clears a silently stuck click state, and it stays cleared.id (comma list on XP)HTTP+WS, all editions
key_release_all/key/upallRelease every key currently held, recovering from an interrupted chord.idHTTP+WS, all editions
restart_usb/device/usb/restartReset a USB control board on both the PC and phone side, without restarting the kernel.Phonefarm: deviceid; XP: id = "VID|PID" (comma list, so several boards reset in one call, even unbound ones)HTTP+WS, all editions; needs kernel ≥1.2.0.3 and board firmware ≥3.0
restart_device/device/restartRestart the phone by driving its Settings UI (or, on XP, via /shortcut/switch/device or the hotkey CTRL+ALT+SHIFT+WIN+r).idHTTP+WS, all editions; Phonefarm needs a captured restart coordinate first, which itself needs the OCR plug-in
restart (kernel)/imserver/restartRestart IMService. Drops every mirroring session and websocket connection; devices go offline until they re-cast.noneHTTP+WS, all editions

Tip Five layers, five recoveries

Pointer stuck → /mouse/reset. Keyboard chord stuck → /key/upall. Board unresponsive → /device/usb/restart. Mirror session degraded → disconnect and re-cast. Phone unresponsive → /device/restart or the shortcut/hotkey alternative. Kernel itself wedged → /imserver/restart, the most disruptive option since it drops everything.

Mouse calibration

Calibration teaches the kernel where a phone's screen actually is under a given board, producing a "location" string and a CRC that other phones of the same model and iOS version can reuse.

FunctionXP pathPurposeKey paramsTransport / edition
mouse_collection_open/device/collection/mouse (cmd=1)Enter collection mode for one device so its browser can open the kernel's collection page.idHTTP+WS, all editions
mouse_collection_close/device/collection/mouse (cmd=2)Leave collection mode. XP adds cmd=0 to query status without starting or stopping.idHTTP+WS, all editions
mouse_collection_cfg/device/collection/mouse (cmd=1, over HTTP or WS on XP)Run the automated collection: the kernel drives the pointer while the phone's collection page reports where it landed.idWS-only on Phonefarm; result arrives via the collection_mouse / mouse_collection_cfg_ret callback
save_dev_location/device/collection/mouse/savePersist a collected calibration into the shared library so same-model, same-iOS phones auto-match on connect.id, describeHTTP+WS, all editions
del_dev_locationnoneRemove a calibration record from the library.model, version, crcHTTP+WS, Phonefarm only; XP has no delete, only add

Watch out

  • The collection page must be launched full-screen from a home-screen icon, not a Safari tab; the collection callback's state field (or, on XP, the collection_mouse codes 8/9) is how the kernel tells the two apart.
  • By default the kernel auto-matches a phone's calibration from the shared library on connect; manual collection is only needed when no match exists or taps land offset. This rig's XRs auto-match a shared library CRC, B0DBD800.
  • The XP doc does not document the phone-side collection URL — the console shows a QR code instead of the raw ?fun=collection link Phonefarm uses.

Callbacks (server-pushed events)

The kernel pushes state changes to every connected websocket client, unsolicited. There is no equivalent over HTTP.

CallbackFires whenPayload highlights

dev_disconnectThe video channel drops; USB control may still be alive.Same record, state 0.
dev_rotateThe mirrored screen changes orientation.rotate 0 portrait / 1 landscape; imgw/imgh swap meaning.

mouse_collection_cfg_retAutomated calibration finishes (Phonefarm name; XP calls it collection_mouse).Phonefarm: {deviceid, location}. XP: data.code only — read the resulting location from /device/get or dev_change.

send_text_okThe Shortcut has fetched text submitted by send_text.Payload undocumented. Phonefarm only.

XP-only callbacks, all wrapped in {fun, status:200, message, msgid, data}: im_connect (kernel version, on socket open), dev_change, dev_delete, group_change, group_delete, collection_mouse, airplay_connect_log, restart_log, user_info (pushed every 30 seconds), im_log, error_push (which function failed and why — the only async signal that an input call failed at the board), im_config_change, logout, and dev_sort_change.

Implicit capabilities

Nothing here is a separate function; each is a consequence of how the documented calls compose.

  • Long-press is click with time set to 800-1000 ms rather than a dedicated call.
  • A right-click primitive exists (button "right"/2), which under iOS pointer support maps to a secondary or context action — a second gesture alongside long-press.
  • mouse_down, a sequence of mouse_move calls, and mouse_up compose any arbitrary-path gesture — icon rearrangement, slider drags, drawing, map panning — not just the canned swipe. Coalescing intermediate points costs nothing extra, since the board walks the path regardless.
  • In percentage mode, swipe has the kernel choose the start and end coordinates itself on each call, so repeated swipes are not pixel-identical by default.
  • Held modifiers via key_down/key_up support shift-selection, multi-key chords and game controls; key_release_all is the recovery when a chord is interrupted mid-sequence.
  • A hotkey can trigger any user-authored iOS Shortcut bound to that AssistiveTouch key, not only the vendor's built-in ones — send_text is simply the vendor's own use of that generic channel. This opens on-phone automation (opening apps, running device actions) that has no dedicated API call.
  • One shortcut call with a devlist runs the same sub-function across several phones in a single round trip; XP's comma-separated id lists give the same fan-out for mouse and keyboard calls.
  • Shortcut ids 2/5 (download) and 7/8 (upload) plus 3/6 (delete) form a complete file-transfer pipeline between the PC and each phone's album or Files app.
  • The high-resolution "original" screenshot (Phonefarm) is well suited to building template images and OCR ground truth at native quality; the caller then rescales into the coordinate space used by click.
  • Request/response correlation via msgid lets many calls be in flight on one websocket connection at once, matched asynchronously as replies arrive.
  • Groups plus gid on every device record let a controller partition the rack — by client, campaign or model — and filter get_device_list accordingly; XP's /device/group/get-dev does the reverse lookup.
  • The dev_connect/dev_disconnect/dev_rotate/usb_change callbacks give a live inventory of both channels — video and control — without polling; on XP every change is broadcast to every connected client, so several consoles stay in sync automatically.
  • A saved calibration (save_dev_location) becomes reusable across every phone of the same model and iOS version via its CRC; get_devicemodel_list doubles as a compatibility oracle for which models and calibrations exist.
  • set_usb_autoairplay (or the XP global auto_connect flag) plus auto_connect_screen_all together make a rack self-healing after a power cycle: boards re-cast their phones automatically, and any still offline can be swept in one call.
  • Device state (state/airhandle, the video channel) and USB binding/usb_change (the control channel) are independent, so a console can distinguish "mirroring but not controllable" from "controllable but blind" rather than collapsing both into one status.

Also worth knowing

/pic/find-image takes two request parameters that do not appear anywhere else in this map: delta_color ("Color Cast") and direction ("Find directions"). Both are typed as plain strings, and both are documented with the same three words: "Reference DM." The doc is telling you the values follow the conventions of the third-party DM-style matching engine XP borrows for this call, not spelling them out itself, so treat the exact syntax as unverified until it is probed against this kernel rather than assumed from the parameter name. Neither parameter is optional filler: they sit in the request table alongside img_list, rect and similarity as first-class inputs to the same call.

Read against what similarity already does, the pairing makes sense. similarity is a single floating-point threshold on overall match confidence, greater than 0 and less than 1. delta_color is a different axis entirely: a color-cast tolerance, letting a template still register as a match when the live frame's colors have drifted from the frame the template was cut from, rather than forcing the caller to lower similarity and accept more false positives everywhere else on screen. That distinction matters on this rack specifically because /shortcut/switch/bril lets a console set a phone's brightness anywhere from 0 to 1 on command, and a brightness change, an iOS light/dark mode switch, True Tone's automatic warm-cool drift, and the lossy color handling of an AirPlay mirroring encoder all move the same kind of pixel values that a color-cast tolerance exists to absorb. direction is documented too thinly to say what it changes with confidence; by name it reads as a search-order control rather than a tolerance, so treat it as a secondary lever and confirm its effect before depending on it.

Both knobs are specific to the DM-style engine at /pic/find-image. /pic/find-image-cv, the OpenCV alternative XP adds alongside it, has no delta_color or direction field in its own request table, only img_list, rect, similarity, all and same — so a color-cast tolerance is a reason to prefer the DM engine over OpenCV on this hardware, not an incidental feature of whichever one is faster. Feasibility is unchanged from the rest of this group either way: both calls need the picture-search plug-in, whose status on this rig is unconfirmed and should be assumed unavailable, Needs plug-in With caveats, until it is separately probed alongside the delta_color syntax itself.

MARK-MARKETING-MARK

Section 3 · Marketing automation

Marketing automation

The rack's most obvious job is turning N phones, each signed into an account the operator owns, into posting infrastructure: push a creative and a caption once, drive each app's own composer with mirrored taps, and verify per phone. Every path below runs on the installed XP kernel with the parameters shown. The catch is verification: the OCR and image-search plug-ins are not connected on this rig (code 28), so nothing here can read a success banner or a button label, only compare raw screenshots by pixel difference. Media and Unicode text both depend on the iMouse iOS Shortcut, a per-phone manual install that has never been probed on this rig, not on anything gated by XP versus Phonefarm edition specifically. XP does not gate the shortcut dispatcher by edition; Phonefarm marks the equivalent "professional version only", but licensing on both editions is per device through the vendor account.

Publishing through the app's own composer

Album push plus native composer: publish a feed post on every phone

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Push the same JPEG or MP4 into the Recents album of every bound phone with one multi-id call, put the caption on every clipboard with another, then drive the social app's own composer with mirrored taps: home, app icon, '+', newest thumbnail, 'Next', caption field, paste, 'Share'. Every tap is one comma-separated request that the boards walk on all phones in parallel, so a 19-phone batch costs roughly the wall time of one phone plus the media transfer. This is the core reason to own a rack: real accounts, on real iPhones, posting through the app's own UI with no platform API access.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get (optionally ?id=a,b) — build the id list from phones that are mirroring (state != 0) and share one imgw x imgh (500x1080 on both XRs here); a coordinate on a different mirror size is a different place.
  2. get_usb_list GET /api/config/usb/get — confirm the control channel separately: state 2 means the board is enumerated and the phone is cabled. Video state proves nothing about control.
  3. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<all ids> — clears a measured silent fault where a phone stops honoring /mouse/click while moves and hardware keys keep working. Send it whenever the target set changes.
  4. shortcut#7 POST /api/shortcut/album/upload {id, files, album_name, zip, outtime} — pushes the creative into Recents on every listed phone in one call. outtime is milliseconds on XP; the Phonefarm equivalent takes seconds.
  5. shortcut#10 POST /api/shortcut/clipboard/set {id, text, sleep, outtime} — the only documented Unicode or emoji text path on XP; sleep is seconds. POST JSON so the caption is not mangled in a query string.
  6. send_key GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<all ids>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — normalizes every phone to home page one; the first press leaves the app, the second returns home.
  7. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=<all ids>&x=&y= — drives app icon, '+', newest album thumbnail, 'Next'. Coordinates are mirror pixels, never the 414x896 logical points.
  8. click + send_key …&fn_key=WIN+v — focuses the caption field, then pastes.
  9. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=<all ids>&x=&y= — Share. Irreversible: one request publishes on every phone in the id list at once. Treat as a separate, explicitly approved call.
  10. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true — per-phone raw BMP, compared to the pre-Share frame by mean absolute pixel difference.
  11. find_multi_color POST /api/pic/find-multi-color — optional stronger check by absolute anchor-point color match, single device only; the plug-in status behind this endpoint is untested here.

Needs

  • IMService.exe plus IMConsole.exe running and logged in on TCP 9911; Phonefarm function names return HTTP 500 on this kernel.
  • iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-edited to the kernel, and bound to an AssistiveTouch key on every phone — unverified on this rig; prove it first with GET /api/shortcut/device/ip?id=<id>&state=0.
  • Board bound (vid+pid together) and at /config/usb/get state 2; location_crc non-empty or every mouse call returns code 11.
  • iOS settings the API cannot see: AssistiveTouch on with max tracking, Full Keyboard Access on, Trackpad & Mouse speed max, Auto-Lock never, portrait lock, StandBy off.
  • Every phone on the same owned account, app version and composer layout — the two XRs here have different home screens, so shared coordinates must be aligned by hand.
  • Kernel logged into a licensed vendor account; unlicensed devices are refused.

Watch out

  • The Shortcut is the hard gate for both media and Unicode text; without it, only ASCII typing remains and no file can reach the phone at all.
  • No OCR or image-search plug-in: verification is blind pixel diff, unable to read a success or error banner.
  • Screenshots are single-id; every input step is one comma-list call, but verification is a per-phone loop.
  • A multi-id call reports one result code for the whole list — a partial failure inside the fan-out is invisible except through per-phone screenshots.
  • The creative stays in every phone's Recents afterward; cleanup calls are destructive and deserve their own confirmation.
  • An identical caption pasted from one call is byte-identical on every account, which platforms treat as duplicate content; distinct captions cost one call per phone.
  • outtime is milliseconds on XP and seconds on Phonefarm — a value copied across editions times out 1000x too early.
  • Only 2 of 19 boards have ever mirrored simultaneously on this rig; extrapolating today's numbers to a full 19-phone run is unproven.

Trap Pixel diff is a change signal, not a success signal

A permission sheet, an OTP prompt, an app crash, or a content-moderation interstitial all produce a mean pixel difference as large as a genuine post. Without OCR, treat any post-Share diff above threshold as "needs a human look," never as a checkmark.

Scale

Album upload and clipboard set are each one request for the whole id list, but the bytes move as N separate LAN transfers — a 20 MB video to 19 phones is roughly 380 MB total, so raise outtime into the minutes and use zip=1 for small images. Every tap, hotkey and reset also costs one request regardless of N at about 0.6 ms per pixel of pointer travel, so the nine-step composer sequence runs roughly 10-15 seconds of board time for the whole group. Verification is the per-phone cost: raw BMP grabs take 2 ms each, but the real wait is frame production on the slow XR's AirPlay link (about 4.5 new frames per second against its twin's 29), so budget 220 ms or more per frame before trusting a "closed" read. Because the Share tap is irreversible and belongs behind a human confirmation, realistic throughput lands around 20-40 full-rack post cycles per hour with an operator actively confirming each one, well below the sub-minute figure raw API latency alone would suggest. Keep per-account posting frequency far below that ceiling: platforms treat identical simultaneous content across many owned accounts as coordinated activity regardless of how fast the rack fires the taps.

Stories and Reels vertical video with a dragged sticker placement

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Push a 9:16 MP4 into each phone's camera roll, confirm it is the newest album item by name and create time, then drive the Story or Reel composer: pick the clip, open the sticker tray, paste link or mention text from the clipboard, and place the sticker with a real press-hold-drag (mouse/down to mouse/move to mouse/up) rather than a canned swipe. Stories and Reels are mobile-only surfaces with no usable desktop composer, and the sticker drag has no web equivalent at all — it is exactly the gesture the vendor's own console uses, and mirroring it to N phones costs the same wall time as one because the boards walk in parallel.

How

  1. get_device_list + get_usb_list GET /api/device/get?id=<ids> and GET /api/config/usb/get — preflight both channels and read imgw/imgh per phone (the mirror-pixel coordinate space, not 414x896).
  2. shortcut#7 POST /api {"fun":"/shortcut/album/upload", …, "outtime":180000} — pushes the clip into every phone's camera roll in one call; leave zip=0 for a single large video.
  3. shortcut#1 GET /api/shortcut/album/get?id=<single id>&num=1 — confirms the clip is genuinely the newest item (name, ext, create_time) before trusting a "tap the first thumbnail" coordinate. Single id only; loop per phone.
  4. shortcut#10 GET /api/shortcut/clipboard/set?id=<ids>&text=&sleep=1 — stages the sticker's link or mention text; the only Unicode-safe text path on XP.
  5. send_key …&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — normalizes every phone to home page one.
  6. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<ids> — clears the stuck-click state before anything tap-critical.
  7. click — opens app, composer and gallery picker, selects the newest clip; an optional time= gives a long press.
  8. click — opens the sticker tray, chooses the link or mention sticker, focuses its text field; fn_key=OPENKeyboard is a fallback if focus does not take.
  9. send_key …&fn_key=WIN+v — pastes the sticker text; requires Full Keyboard Access on, with no completion signal.
  10. mouse_down → mouse_move (repeated) → mouse_up — places the sticker with a real drag. Move onto the sticker first: /mouse/down takes no coordinates and presses wherever the pointer already is.
  11. click — Publish. Irreversible; screenshot and inspect first, since one coordinate set is only valid within a single app build and experiment bucket.
  12. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<single id>&binary=true — per-phone verify.
  13. shortcut#3 POST /api {"fun":"/shortcut/album/del", "data":{"id", "list":[{"album_name","name","ext"}]}} — cleans up the staged media so the next run's "newest item" coordinate stays true; album/clear wipes a whole album and is destructive.

Needs

  • iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-edited and hotkey-bound on every phone, with Shortcuts > Advanced set to allow running scripts, sharing large data, and deleting (with and without confirmation).
  • Phone-to-kernel LAN path in both directions; the API is unauthenticated, so firewall 9911 and 17000 to trusted hosts.
  • iOS accessibility settings invisible to the API: AssistiveTouch max, Full Keyboard Access, Trackpad & Mouse speed max, Auto-Lock never, portrait lock, StandBy off.
  • Board bound and physically connected (state 1 then 2) with the vendor cable; location_crc non-empty.
  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in; every target phone on the same app build and A/B bucket if one coordinate set is shared.
  • Accounts the operator owns or is authorized for, checked against each platform's automation terms.
  • OCR and image-search plug-ins strongly advised, but not installed on this rig.

Watch out

  • Every call in the chain exists on the installed XP kernel with the stated parameters — verification, not availability, is the limiting factor.
  • With no OCR or image-search, the chain runs blind on fixed coordinates plus mean pixel diff: it cannot confirm which thumbnail was tapped, that the tray opened, or where the sticker landed.
  • /pic/screenshot and /shortcut/album/get are single-id, so confirm and verify are per-phone loops while input stays one comma-list call.
  • No success callback exists for the Shortcut path on XP; a 15 s timeout (code 30) looks identical to a slow response.
  • XP's swipe table documents no start or end randomization (that behavior appears only in the Phonefarm sibling doc); use down/move/up for the drag regardless, since it is deterministic and matches the vendor console.
  • An interrupted drag leaves the button held; /mouse/up releases it but does not clear the separate stuck-click state — only /mouse/reset does.
  • Portrait lock still matters on XP, but for a different reason than a borrowed Phonefarm error code suggests: rotation swaps imgw/imgh and fires dev_rotate, invalidating every stored coordinate.
  • Uploading to N phones is N separate LAN transfers, not a broadcast, even though it is one request.
  • There is no documented bandwidth figure for the album-upload channel itself; the vendor's AirPlay energy-mode Mbps figures describe outbound mirroring, not this inbound file path, and should not be reused to estimate video-upload time.
  • Only 2 of 19 boards have ever mirrored simultaneously here, so the frame-rate figures behind the screenshot-gate wait logic are unproven at full rack scale.

Trap A down-press has no confirmation

The only available check after a drag is a post-move pixel diff, which cannot tell "the sticker moved" from "the pointer moved and the sticker stayed put." Diff a small box around the sticker's start position, in addition to its destination, to catch a grab that missed.

Scale

Every input step takes a comma id list and costs one request regardless of N; a 400 px sticker drag is about 250 ms of board time whether the list holds one phone or nineteen. Only the screenshot and album-listing checks are per-phone, and pollers do not bottleneck each other (measured 512 req/s across ten concurrent pollers). The real cost center is the video transfer: each phone receives its own copy of the MP4 over Wi-Fi through the Shortcut with no documented bandwidth budget for that channel, so a typical 15-30 s clip (10-40 MB) plausibly runs low tens of seconds to a few minutes per phone, and a 19-phone batch upload is plausibly several minutes even largely in parallel. Realistic throughput for the full upload-confirm-normalize-paste-drag-publish-verify cycle, human-gated at the publish step, is on the order of one full-rack cycle every 5-10 minutes, or 6-12 cycles per hour run back to back — a shared wall-clock rate, not a per-phone-independent one. Keep per-account posting frequency well below this ceiling for the same coordinated-content reasons as the feed post above.

Launching composers by URL instead of hunting for icons

Cross-post one asset by launching each app's composer via URL scheme

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Push one asset into every camera roll, put the caption on every clipboard, then open each target app's composer directly with a URL scheme or universal link instead of finding its home-screen icon. Finish with mirrored taps and a WIN+v paste, and confirm each stage with a screenshot. On this rig the two XRs have entirely different home screens and wallpapers, so the same mirror coordinate is Clock on one phone and Reminders on the other; a URL scheme sidesteps that entirely because it puts every phone on the same composer screen at once, after which one mirrored coordinate is legitimately fair across the whole set.

How

  1. get_device_list + get_usb_list + mouse_reset_pos GET /api/device/get?id=<ids> | GET /api/config/usb/get | GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<ids> — confirms video and control are both up and clears the stuck-click state before anything tap-critical.
  2. shortcut#7 POST /api {"fun":"/shortcut/album/upload", …} — pushes the asset into every camera roll once per campaign.
  3. shortcut#10 POST /api {"fun":"/shortcut/clipboard/set", …} — pushes the caption once.
  4. shortcut#13 POST /api {"fun":"/shortcut/exec/url", "data":{"id","url","outtime"}} — launches each target app's composer by URL scheme or universal link, one call per app, all phones at once. The API places no constraint on the URL string; no scheme for any specific app is documented anywhere in this project — confirm each by hand before scripting it.
  5. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true — per phone, confirms the composer (not Safari, not a permission sheet) actually opened before any tap.
  6. click / swipe / down-move-up — drives the composer with mirrored taps, now that every phone shares one screen.
  7. send_key …&fn_key=WIN+v — pastes the caption into the focused field.
  8. click + get_device_screenshot + send_key …&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — submits, verifies per phone, then normalizes before the next app's launch.

Needs

  • Account authorization for every account involved — the precondition for the whole use case, not a footnote.
  • iMouse Shortcut installed and hotkey-bound on every phone; unverified on this rig, iOS 15+ for the file-family shortcut functions.
  • Board bound and at /config/usb/get state 2; mirroring live with a matching air_pid; IMConsole.exe running and logged in.
  • iOS accessibility settings invisible to the API (AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, Trackpad & Mouse speed, Auto-Lock, portrait lock, StandBy) and location_crc non-empty.
  • Target app already installed and signed in on every phone — nothing in this chain authenticates; a launch into a logged-out app lands on a login screen.
  • The URL scheme or universal link for each target app, confirmed by hand on the installed app version — not documented anywhere in this project or by the platforms.
  • A client-side frame comparator, since the server-side OCR and image-search plug-ins are unavailable here.

Watch out

  • The API hands iOS whatever URL string it is given; whether that string opens a composer is entirely a platform matter, undocumented and version-dependent. A retired scheme leaves the phone on the home screen or in Safari, and every mirrored tap after that lands on something unintended.
  • Universal links fall back to Safari if the app is not installed or the association is broken — the verifier must distinguish "app opened" from "Safari opened."
  • Opening a URL scheme from an automation context can surface a one-time "Open in [App]?" confirmation sheet distinct from the composer itself, especially the first time a scheme runs after install or an OS update. A tap sequence written only for the composer lands on this sheet instead, on an unpredictable subset of phones. Positive-match the sheet's shape, or dismiss it with a known fixed tap, rather than gating only on how much the screen changed.
  • No server-side recognition (code 28): verification is client-side pixel diff or template matching on raw BMP, never an MD5 comparison, since the AirPlay encoder changes every frame regardless of phone activity.
  • Mirrored taps are only fair once every phone is genuinely on the same screen; drop any phone whose launch failed from the id list for the rest of the sequence rather than tapping it blind.
  • Phones with different imgw/imgh must never share a coordinate; both XRs here happen to match at 500x1080.
  • Caption text with emoji or CJK must travel by clipboard, never /key/sendkey, which is ASCII-only on both editions.
  • App updates commonly retire or alter custom URL schemes, and auto-update timing varies per phone, so a scheme validated today can succeed on seventeen phones and silently fail on two in the same run.
  • Rapid app-open-close cycling across several target apps is itself a pattern some platforms' client-side heuristics can flag; keep the number of apps cross-posted per run small and paced, the same discipline as phone count.
  • Licensing is per device through the vendor account; confirm /config/user/info shows coverage for the device count before a large run.

Trap A stale URL scheme fails silently into whatever is foreground

The post-launch screenshot check is the only thing standing between a retired scheme and a blind tap storm across every phone in the set. Treat it as mandatory, and fail the whole batch closed rather than continuing with partial confirmation.

Scale

The write-side shortcut calls plus click and sendkey all take a comma id list, so N phones cost one request per step, not N; the board walks every listed phone in parallel. Per app the cost is one exec/url call, a handful of mirrored clicks, and one paste, with outtime defaulting to 15000 ms on XP and needing headroom for the hotkey-to-Shortcut round trip. Verification is the per-phone cost: single-id screenshots at 2 ms each, but the real ceiling is the phone's own AirPlay source rate, roughly 220 ms per new frame on the slower of the two XRs here. Practically, one app cycle runs 5-15 seconds of enforced screenshot-gate waiting plus whatever the app itself takes to load after the URL fires, which this API does not bound and which often runs several seconds on its own. Across M target apps sharing one asset and caption push, a full cross-post run is roughly M times 10-20 seconds of mechanics — five apps in one to two minutes, a technical ceiling near 30-60 cross-app runs per hour. Mandatory per-step screenshot review and a human approval before each submit tap will realistically cut sustained throughput to a handful of full cross-post runs per hour.

Scheduling campaigns across device groups

Campaign calendar: external scheduler fires posting jobs at device groups

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

The kernel has no timer of any kind, so the calendar lives outside it: Windows Task Scheduler, cron, or an n8n/Airflow job fires a posting run at the planned minute against a named device group. Groups give real tenant isolation, since group membership is the resolver a job trusts, so a mistyped device id resolves to nothing rather than to the wrong client's phones. A per-slot preflight on two independent channels plus a per-slot screenshot turns an unattended overnight run into an auditable evidence row per phone instead of a silent no-op — which matters, because this rig has a measured failure mode where a phone follows moves and hardware keys perfectly while ignoring every click.

How

  1. set_group /device/group/set?id=0&name=ClientA — one-time: creates a group per client or campaign; id=0 creates, any other id renames.
  2. set_dev /device/set?id=<id1,id2>&gid=<gid>&name=Slot-01 — assigns phones to the group and names each slot. gid/name take a comma list; vid/pid hardware binding is one device per call.
  3. get_group_list + get_group_dev /device/group/get then /device/group/get-dev?id=<gid> — resolves live group membership at fire time. XP-only endpoint; single group id per call; returns full device records, so no second lookup is needed.
  4. get_device_list /device/get?id=<ids> — preflight the video channel (state != 0, a live air_pid) and read imgw/imgh per phone.
  5. get_usb_list /config/usb/get — preflight the control channel (state 2, vid/pid/uid bound), independently of video.
  6. mouse_reset_pos /mouse/reset?id=<members> — clears the stuck-click state across the whole target set at the start of every run.
  7. shortcut#7 /shortcut/album/upload?id=<members>&files=[…]&zip=1&outtime=60000 — pushes the campaign asset; zip=1 for many small images, outtime in milliseconds.
  8. shortcut#10 + send_key /shortcut/clipboard/set?id=<members>&text=… then /key/sendkey?id=<members>&fn_key=WIN+v — delivers a Unicode caption, then pastes it into the focused field.
  9. click /mouse/click?id=<members>&x=&y=&button=1&time= — drives the in-app posting flow in mirror-pixel coordinates.
  10. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true — evidence frame per slot; single-id fan-out.
  11. callbacks ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api — dev_connect, dev_disconnect, usb_change, error_push — optional async watch; error_push carries the failed call and message for a board-level input failure.
  12. the scheduler itself none — no timer, cron, or scheduled-job endpoint exists in either doc set — the load-bearing external dependency; Task Scheduler, cron, n8n or a LAN service does the actual firing.

Needs

  • An external scheduler on the LAN — the kernel has no timers; this is the mechanism, not garnish.
  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in; a scheduled run should gate on board count greater than zero before firing.
  • Every phone bound (vid+pid) with non-empty location_crc.
  • Auto-Lock Never plus no pending passcode prompt — a phone that rebooted overnight sits on the lock screen with no API path to unlock it.
  • iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-edited and hotkey-bound on every phone, with the same Shortcuts > Advanced permissions as the other entries.
  • Asset files readable by the kernel process at the given PC paths, with Windows backslashes JSON-escaped.
  • Coordinates authored per phone layout, plus a known starting state (two WIN+h presses) before any shared coordinate is used.
  • Cheapest proof the Shortcut path is alive before a campaign night: GET /shortcut/device/ip returning code 0 with a matching ip field.

Watch out

  • Calling this "native" is wrong on two counts: there is no scheduler anywhere in either doc set, so the calendar is entirely external tooling, and asset and caption delivery both run through the per-phone Shortcut install. Only grouping, gating, reset, tapping and screenshot are native.
  • Group device listing, screenshots, album listing and clipboard reads are all single-id; input endpoints and the write-side shortcut endpoints take comma lists — do not assume every call fans out the same way.
  • With no OCR or image-search plug-in, the job cannot read "Posted" or find a moved Share button; verification is pixel diff plus human review of saved frames, and UI navigation must stay coordinate-based.
  • outtime is milliseconds on XP and seconds on Phonefarm; clipboard's sleep is seconds either way — mixing units silently truncates a video upload.
  • /device/set binds vid+pid for one device per call even on a comma list, so per-slot hardware binding is one call per phone.
  • Group deletion refuses while members remain (code 34); device deletion refuses online devices (code 7) — move phones to gid 0 first for teardown.
  • No completion callback exists for the Shortcut path on XP; the screenshot is the only proof that pasted text actually landed.
  • None of the iOS accessibility prerequisites are queryable over the API; the per-slot preflight is a proxy, not a guarantee, and a phone can show board state 2 with a stale air_pid while actually sitting on a lock screen with mirroring paused.
  • No per-phone locking exists: two scheduled jobs, or a job and a manual console session, can target the same board at once and interleave taps with no error from either side.
  • Binding a new phone into a group is two non-atomic calls (bind, then add to group); a crash between them leaves it bound but ungrouped and silently excluded from that night's run.
  • The two Shortcut calls were never exercised on this rig — if the Shortcut is not bound, both simply time out (code 30) and the run posts nothing while every other preflight gate reports fine.
  • An evidence frame only shows the screen changed near the expected coordinate, not that a post succeeded; treat it as requiring a human spot-check, not as an auditable pass or fail.
  • A coordinate-based Share or Post tap has no re-verification available; a silently moved button gets tapped wrong indefinitely until a human reviews saved frames.
  • The 15,000 ms default timeout for both Shortcut calls has no measured round-trip time on this rig; treat "minutes, not seconds" as an assumption pending that measurement, not a fact.

Trap A silent Shortcut failure looks identical to success

If the iMouse Shortcut is not installed or bound on a phone, album upload and clipboard set both simply time out while /mouse/reset and every other preflight gate reports fine. Add GET /shortcut/device/ip as a hard canary check at the start of every scheduled run, not an optional aside.

Scale

Group resolution and gating cost two GETs regardless of rack size, and input fans out for free: one click or sendkey call with a comma id list drives every listed board in parallel at about 0.6 ms per pixel, so a 20-phone group costs roughly what one phone costs on the input side. Evidence capture does not fan out, but phones are independent (measured 512 req/s across ten concurrent pollers), so a 20-shot evidence sweep is noise next to everything else. The real per-phone budget is the two Shortcut round trips, each capped at a 15 s timeout with no measured typical latency on this rig; budget minutes, not seconds, for a group of any size, more for video. On the slower of the two XRs (about 4.5 new AirPlay frames per second against its twin's 29), any screen-state wait must budget 220 ms or more per frame and use a pixel-difference threshold rather than a frame counter. Mechanically the rig could plausibly sustain 2-4 scheduled posting rounds per minute with shared content, or 2-4 phones per minute with per-phone content, but that ceiling is irrelevant in practice: a marketing calendar fires a handful of posts per day per account, and each platform's own posting-frequency policy is the real limit long before this API is stressed.

Direct messaging and replies

Unicode comment and DM replies pasted from the phone clipboard

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

/key/sendkey is documented ASCII-only in both editions, and the XP kernel has no send_text function at all. The only documented route to emoji, accents, CJK or Arabic text anywhere in this API is to set the phone's clipboard from the PC and paste it in: /shortcut/clipboard/set followed by a WIN+v hotkey. The same route serves comment replies, DM replies, captions, bios and search queries. Identical text to a group is one clipboard call with a comma id list; per-recipient text costs one clipboard call per phone.

How

  1. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<ids> — clear any silent stuck-click state on the target set before the tap-critical steps that follow.
  2. shortcut#10 POST {"fun":"/shortcut/clipboard/set","data":{"id":"<ids>","text":"<reply>","sleep":1,"outtime":15000}} — push the reply text to each phone's clipboard; one call per distinct reply, one comma-id call when the text is identical.
  3. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=&y= — focus the comment or DM field (or fn_key=OPENKeyboard to raise the on-screen keyboard).
  4. send_key GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+v — paste. One request covers the whole target set.
  5. send_key / click GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=ENTER or GET /api/mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=&y= — submit. ENTER's behaviour is app-specific and undocumented; the Send-button tap is the safer default.
  6. shortcut#11 (canary) GET /api/shortcut/clipboard/get?id=<one id>&outtime=15000 — read back the clipboard on one phone before a batch, to byte-compare the Unicode round trip and confirm the Shortcut path is alive at all.
  7. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true — confirm the text landed and the field cleared after send, by mean-pixel-difference against the pre-paste frame.

Needs

  • iMouse iOS Shortcut installed on every phone, kernel IP edited in, run once with every permission allowed, and bound to an AssistiveTouch custom key. Not exercised on this rig; prove it with the clipboard-get canary before building anything larger.
  • Full Keyboard Access on (so WIN+v and ENTER are interpreted), AssistiveTouch on with tracking sensitivity maxed, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock.
  • Board bound and cabled (/config/usb/get state 2) with a non-empty location_crc, or every mouse call fails with code 11.
  • Phone reachable to the kernel over Wi-Fi on 9911, since the Shortcut posts its result back that way even though the hotkey that triggers it arrives over USB.
  • The target text field already focused before WIN+v fires — a paste into nothing returns code 0 with no error.
  • Reply text authored upstream. This rig has no server-side OCR to read the inbound comment or DM (/pic/ocr answers code 28, plug-in not connected).

Watch out

  • Nothing under /shortcut/* was exercised in the 10 September probe. /mouse/*, /key/sendkey and /pic/screenshot are confirmed; the Unicode half of this chain rests on an unverified assumption.
  • Unit trap: XP's outtime is milliseconds (default 15000), sleep is seconds. The Phonefarm sibling doc uses seconds for both. Passing a Phonefarm value gives a 15 ms timeout and a guaranteed code 30.
  • A timed-out clipboard/set (code 30) leaves the clipboard holding the previous phone's text — a blind WIN+v afterwards pastes the wrong reply into this phone's field. Treat any non-zero data.code as a hard stop for that phone, not something to retry.
  • With no OCR plug-in there is no server-side way to confirm the reply text rendered correctly or to catch an in-app error banner; verification is limited to a raw-BMP mean-pixel-difference check, or client-side OCR you run yourself against the frame.
  • Coordinates are per phone: the two XRs on this rig have different home screens, so a comma-id click is only valid when the Send control sits at the identical mirror-pixel position on every listed phone.
  • fn_key=ENTER submitting the reply is app-dependent and undocumented — in many apps it inserts a newline instead. Verify per app before trusting it; default to clicking Send.
  • Phonefarm-style calls (bare {"fun":"send_text"}) return HTTP 500 on this kernel. There is no send_text and no send_text_ok callback on XP.
  • The clipboard-get canary proves the round trip for one phone at that moment; it does not prove every other phone in a batch has the Shortcut installed and bound. A 19-phone batch needs 19 canary checks, or a one-time setup audit, not one canary standing in for the group.

Trap A stale clipboard publishes on the wrong account

Because a timed-out clipboard/set leaves the old text in place with nothing visibly wrong, an orchestration wrapper that checks HTTP status instead of the JSON data.code field can paste and submit one phone's reply under a different phone's account. Hard-fail on any non-zero code before the paste step ever fires.

Scale

The shortcut round trip (HID hotkey → Shortcut launches → phone calls back over Wi-Fi to 9911) has never been timed on this rig; the documented bound is the 15,000 ms outtime ceiling, not a measured latency. Until it is timed, plan on up to 15 s per distinct reply, sequential across phones needing different text — identical text to a whole group is a single call regardless of group size. Steps that take a comma-id list (reset, click, paste, submit) cost one request for the whole target set either way, at roughly 0.6 ms/px of pointer travel. Verification screenshots are cheap and fully parallel across phones (~2 ms raw BMP each, phones independent, ten concurrent pollers measured 512 req/s aggregate), so they add negligible time. The slower of the two XRs on this rig delivers only ~4.5 new frames/s versus ~29 on its twin, so any screen-change check on it needs a longer wait budget, not a fixed 30 fps assumption.

Prefilled messaging deep links (wa.me, tg://, sms:) opened per phone, with a batched Send tap

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Instead of typing into a composer, hand each phone a URL that already carries the recipient and the message body: a wa.me or whatsapp://send link, an sms: body, or a tg://msg share. /shortcut/exec/url opens it and the app lands in the chat with the text already in the box, including emoji and CJK, so neither the ASCII-only hotkey path nor the clipboard round trip is needed. Nothing sends silently: every scheme still requires a visible composer and one real tap, and XP has no SMS-send endpoint at all.

How

  1. send_key GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — normalise every target phone to home screen page one.
  2. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<ids> — clear stuck-click state before the batched Send tap later in the chain.
  3. shortcut#13 POST {"fun":"/shortcut/exec/url","data":{"id":"<deviceid>","url":"https://wa.me/<number>?text=<url-encoded>","outtime":15000}} — open the prefilled chat; one call per distinct URL, since only an identical URL can share a comma id list. Use the JSON POST form so the URL's own ? and & don't collide with query-string encoding.
  4. alternative bodies — whatsapp://send?phone=&text= (no Safari bounce) · sms:<number>&body= (inconsistent across iOS builds) · tg://msg?text= (opens Telegram's share sheet, not a direct chat — no recipient in the scheme).
  5. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<deviceid>&binary=true — confirm the chat actually opened with the text in the box before anything is tapped.
  6. client-side check (preferred) or find_multi_color POST /api/pic/find-multi-color {...} — decide from that frame whether the Send control is present. The colour-probe endpoint exists as documented but is unprobed on this rig.
  7. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=&y=&button=1 — Send, one request for the whole batch, only once every phone in the list has independently confirmed its own composer is populated.
  8. send_key (alternative) GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=ENTER — app- and setting-dependent; test before trusting it over the tap.
  9. shortcut#10 + send_key (Unicode fallback) /shortcut/clipboard/set then fn_key=WIN+v — for a scheme that refuses to prefill.
  10. shortcut#7 (optional media) POST {"fun":"/shortcut/album/upload", ...} — stage an attachment into the phone's own album first, since a deep link cannot carry one; picking it into the chat is then ordinary tap automation.

Needs

  • iMouse iOS Shortcut installed, IP-edited, permissioned and hotkey-bound on every phone — unverified here; cheapest proof is GET /api/shortcut/device/ip?id=<id>&state=0 matched against /device/get's ip field.
  • WhatsApp, Telegram or Messages installed and registered on that phone's own SIM or Apple ID — a link to a non-user lands on an error page, which is exactly what the confirmation screenshot is for.
  • Documented consent for every recipient, and a message template and volume that comply with the target platform's terms and applicable marketing law, established before any of this touches real numbers.
  • Send-button coordinate captured per app version from a real screenshot, re-captured after any update.

Watch out

  • This is a hard, binary gate, not one caveat among several: every path to opening a URL scheme on iOS from this API goes through /shortcut/exec/url, and XP has no way to type a URL into Safari's address bar as a fallback. If the Shortcut isn't installed and bound on a given phone, there is no automation path to this use case on that phone at all.
  • Deep-link prefill is a property of the receiving app, not of this API; the vendor's own examples pass a bare hostname, so a long query-carrying URL is untested territory. Probe the length ceiling once and keep bodies well under roughly 1,500 characters.
  • tg://msg?text= opens a share-sheet chooser, not a one-tap send — it does not have the parity with wa.me an early draft implied.
  • sms: body prefill is inconsistent across iOS builds; verify per device before trusting it.
  • Server-side screen verification is weak here: /pic/ocr answers code 28 and image search is presumed the same, so confirm the composer client-side on the raw BMP with a mean-pixel-difference threshold, never MD5.
  • The batched Send tap is only safe once every phone's own confirmation frame has independently landed. Given a measured ~29 fps vs ~4.5 fps gap between the two XRs on this rig, firing the batch on a shared timer risks tapping Send on the slow phone before its composer is actually populated, sending a blank or partial message. Gate the batch on a per-phone confirmed flag, not a shared wait.
  • wa.me bounces through Safari before handing off (allow ~2 s); whatsapp:// avoids the bounce.
  • XP's outtime is milliseconds, default 15000; copying a Phonefarm example verbatim (seconds) gives a 15 ms timeout.
  • The Shortcut's triggering hotkey rides the same USB/HID control channel that can silently stop honouring /mouse/click. There's no evidence /mouse/reset also un-sticks a hotkey path — verify hotkey delivery per run rather than assuming the existing reset step covers it.

Open Platform limits, not hardware, set the real ceiling

WhatsApp, Telegram and carrier SMS all throttle and review accounts sending patterned, scripted messages, well below anything this rack can mechanically produce. Treat rack capacity as headroom for reliability, never as a sending target, and stop on any block or rate-limit notice rather than retrying.

Scale

Per-recipient personalisation makes the URL-open step one request per phone; only an identical URL can share a comma id list. The dominant cost is on-phone, not on the wire — hotkey fire, Shortcut launch, app render — budget roughly 2-4 s per phone before the confirmation frame means anything, against a 15 s default timeout ceiling. The normalise, reset and Send steps each collapse to a single request for the whole batch regardless of size. Verification is cheap and parallel (~2 ms raw BMP per phone, ten concurrent pollers measured 512 req/s aggregate). With only two phones currently attached and mirroring, a realistic round is on the order of N messages per 5-8 s of wall clock; scaled to all 19 boards the mechanical ceiling would be roughly 1,000-1,800 messages/hour, but the actual safe rate is set by per-number platform limits and by how many recipients have consented — realistically tens to low hundreds of messages per day per number, not per hour.

Engagement loops

Engagement loops (like, follow, story view) with a colour-check de-duplication probe before each toggle tap

PartialWith caveats

Drive a social feed on your own signed-in accounts through the pointer channel alone: normalise home, open the app, swipe the feed, and — before tapping a like or Follow toggle — read the control's own pixels first so the loop never un-likes a post it already liked or unfollows an account it already followed. The interesting part is that read-before-write probe: a colour check against the filled heart or Follow-button pixels, done either through the documented find-multi-color endpoint or, since this rig's plug-ins aren't confirmed present, by sampling the raw screenshot bytes directly. The same pattern generalises to any stateful control whose state shows as colour — mute, saved, subscribed, dark-mode — with no OCR and no accessibility tree.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get?id=<deviceid> — read imgw/imgh (500x1080 on these XRs) as the coordinate space for every later call, and confirm the phone is live.
  2. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<ids> — clear stuck-click state on the whole target set before any tap-critical pass; a stuck phone measured 0.09 mean pixel diff on a click, 141.96 after reset, and /mouse/up did not fix it.
  3. send_key GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — normalise to home screen page one.
  4. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=&y= — open the app, at a coordinate read from that phone's own screenshot.
  5. shortcut#13 (optional) GET /api/shortcut/exec/url?id=<ids>&url=&outtime= — deep-link entry instead of an icon tap; needs the Shortcut chain, not confirmed here.
  6. swipe GET /api/mouse/swipe?id=<ids>&direction=up&len=0.5 — advance the feed. XP's swipe is deterministic given the same parameters; there is no randomisation in the XP table (that claim exists only in the Phonefarm doc).
  7. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true — grab the frame the probe will read, cropped with rect to the heart/Follow strip.
  8. find_multi_color POST /api/pic/find-multi-color {id, list:[{first_color, rect, similarity}]} — the de-duplication probe: documented with exactly this absolute-colour syntax, but not confirmed working through the plug-in layer on this rig.
  9. fallback probe (client-side) GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true&rect= + your own pixel sampling — reproduces the same check in a few lines of code at 2 ms per frame, with no plug-in dependency. Build this path first.
  10. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=<one id>&x=&y=&time=80 — tap the control only when the probe says it is un-actioned. There is no native double-click; compose one from two calls roughly 100 ms apart.
  11. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=&y= — story view: tap the frame's right edge to advance, with a dwell before the next tap.
  12. ocr / find_image (not usable here) /pic/find-text or /pic/find-image-cv — the documented way to detect a rate-limit or "Action Blocked" interstitial; both are plug-in-gated and unavailable on this rig. Substitute a whole-frame mean-pixel-difference spike and halt the pass rather than retry.
  13. mouse_reset_pos / error_push GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<ids>; WebSocket ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api — recovery and async failure signal; error_push is the only way to learn an input call failed at the board.

Needs

  • Accounts you own or are authorised to operate, already signed in by hand on each phone. This describes driving your own logged-in sessions, not creating or disguising accounts.
  • Vendor console running and logged in, board state 2 per phone, vid/pid bound, and a non-empty location_crc, or every mouse call fails with code 11.
  • iOS accessibility set invisible to the API: AssistiveTouch on at max tracking sensitivity, Full Keyboard Access on, Trackpad & Mouse speed maxed, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock.
  • All coordinates in that device's imgw x imgh (500x1080), read per phone — the two XRs have different home screens and share nothing without measurement.
  • For the server-side colour probe: the image-search plug-in installed and enabled, unverified on this rig.
