  • The API on 9911 has no authentication of any kind; firewall it to trusted hosts before running anything unattended.

Watch out

  • The colour-check de-duplication — the whole point of this entry — is not confirmed working via the API on this rig. The only recognition endpoint actually probed, /pic/ocr, returned code 28 (plug-in not connected). Probe find-multi-color before designing around it; the client-side raw-BMP fallback is the safe path to build first.
  • No text recognition at all is available here — any "read the counter" or "read the dialog" step must be done client-side or not at all.
  • Every /pic/* observation call is single-device; input mirrors to N phones in one request, observation never does. After the first personalised feed load, the realistic shape is one independent loop per phone, not one mirrored loop.
  • No native double-click or double-tap: compose it from two /mouse/click calls, and note this is asserted, not measured, to register as an iOS double-tap gesture — if the two clicks land outside the recognition window it can silently degrade to two independent taps that toggle the like state twice, defeating the idempotency design.
  • /mouse/click can silently stop working on a phone while move and hotkeys still succeed; only /mouse/reset clears it, and every call still returns success while it's stuck.
  • Frame-based verification is bounded by the phone: one XR delivers ~29 new frames/s under motion, its twin ~4.5, and a still screen produces almost no new frames — any "did it fill in?" check must threshold mean pixel difference and budget hundreds of ms on the slow phone. Do not derive the poll interval from observed frame gaps; that decayed 23 fps to 16.5 in testing.
  • Reference colours are coupled to the phone's mirror resolution and app/iOS version; an app update that restyles the heart icon invalidates the table silently, with no drift detection available without OCR or image search.
  • The probe and the tap are two separate round trips with no atomicity — the control's state could change between the read and the write on any account with more than one active client.
  • Story-view and heart coordinates must be measured per app per phone from a real screenshot; illustrative coordinates are not safe to ship.

Tip The idempotency pattern is the reusable part

Reading a control's pixels before writing to it is what turns a screen-automation loop from a demo into something re-runnable on a schedule. It applies to any visibly-stateful toggle, well beyond likes and follows.

Trap Unattended engagement automation is a platform-policy problem, not a technical one

Unattended like, follow and story-view automation is prohibited by the terms of service of essentially every major social platform; follow/unfollow churn is separately covered by spam policies. The action rate and pattern are fully visible to the platform regardless of how the input is generated. Run this only on accounts you own or are contractually authorised to operate, and treat any rate-limit or "Action Blocked" interstitial as a hard stop for the session, not something to retry on a timer.

Scale

Input is cheap and parallel: click, swipe, reset and hotkeys all take a comma id list and cost the same for one phone or N. Observation is the bottleneck by design, since every /pic/* call is single-id — two phones polled flat out measured 83 and 85 req/s at p50 3 ms, ten concurrent pollers 512 req/s, and input traffic measurably did not slow polling. Per post, budget roughly 300-600 ms of swipe or scroll travel, ~2 ms for the screenshot, a sub-millisecond client colour probe, the tap itself, and a render-settle dwell bounded by the phone's own frame rate — about 1-3 s/action on the fast phone and 2-5 s on the slow one, a mechanical ceiling on the order of 700-3,600 actions/hour/phone. That mechanical number is not the meaningful one: any real deployment must throttle far below it, since the platform's own anti-abuse thresholds, not the rig, set the sustainable rate.

Monitoring and inbox alerts

Badge-polling watcher for new DMs, offers and mentions

PartialWith caveats

Park every managed account on its inbox or notifications tab, then poll each phone's raw mirror frame at a fixed 1-2 s cadence and watch a small fixed box — the tab-bar badge — for change against a per-phone baseline crop. The detection itself is a client-side mean-absolute-pixel-difference on a 2 ms raw BMP, no plug-in and no OCR required. iOS push notifications are invisible to the PC, but the AirPlay mirror is not, so a rack that already has every account logged in and open doubles as a real-time monitor with no platform API and no scraping — a human still does all the replying.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get — enumerate targets, filter to state non-zero with a live air_pid, and read each phone's own imgw/imgh.
  2. send_key GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — normalise each phone to a known state.
  3. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<ids> — clear stuck-click state before any tap.
  4. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=&y= — park each phone on its inbox or notifications tab. A shared coordinate is only fair when every phone in the list actually has that tab at that position.
  5. shortcut#13 (optional) GET /api/shortcut/exec/url?id=<ids>&url=&outtime= — deep-link straight into the inbox instead of tapping; needs the Shortcut chain, unverified here.
  6. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<single id>&binary=true — poll the raw frame per phone at a fixed cadence, one request per phone, concurrent pollers.
  7. client-side detection none — your own code on the decoded BMP — the load-bearing step: mean absolute pixel difference of the badge box against baseline. Idle noise floor measured 0.02-0.03; a real change measures 20-160. Never MD5 or whole-frame diff.
  8. find_multi_color (optional hardening, unverified) POST /api/pic/find-multi-color {...} — confirm the iOS red-badge colour. Documented but never probed on this rig; treat as optional, not the detection mechanism.
  9. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true&jpg=true — on trigger, capture a full-frame JPEG thumbnail for the alert (cheap since it fires once per event, not per poll).
  10. none (external) — deliver the alert via Slack, Teams, webhook or console UI. No iMouse function of either edition sends anything off-box.
  11. mouse_reset_pos + send_key + click — re-baseline and re-park after a human clears the badge, or after any /device/airplay/set change (which alters mirror geometry and invalidates every stored box).
  12. shortcut#15 (optional) GET /api/shortcut/switch/bril?id=<ids>&state=0.1&outtime= — dim the phone's own panel to cut thermal/power load on a permanently-lit rack; needs the Shortcut chain.

Needs

  • Vendor console running and logged in, every watched phone mirroring with a live air_pid, board state 2, and the iOS accessibility set (AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access) for the parking taps only.
  • Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock, brightness and Night Shift frozen — any drift decays both the pixel baseline and any colour table.
  • A per-phone baseline crop captured right after the inbox is cleared, and per-app badge-box coordinates in that phone's own mirror-pixel space.
  • An alerting sink entirely outside the iMouse API — Slack/Teams webhook, console UI, pager. Nothing in either edition sends a notification off-box.
  • Written authorisation to automate the accounts watched, and confirmation the platform's terms permit this kind of automated, read-only access.

Watch out

  • The detection mechanism is entirely client-side image processing; the API's whole contribution is a 2 ms frame grab. Don't describe this as native detection.
  • find-multi-color being plug-in-free is an inference from the doc naming no plug-in, not a documented fact — it sits on the same page as the confirmed plug-in-gated OCR call. Probe it before designing around it; if it returns code 28, drop that step.
  • No OCR means you get "something changed in the badge box," never "a DM from X about Y." Triage still requires a human opening the phone.
  • Badge coordinates and colour tables are brittle across app updates and are not portable between phones with different home screens — recut boxes after every update, and validate a new box for an hour against an idle phone before trusting it (a box overlapping a scrolling region, animated avatar or timestamp will false-trigger continuously).
  • Only two phones are currently online; every throughput figure is measured on two, and the aggregate model at full rack scale is untested.
  • Changing air_ratio disconnects the cast and alters mirror geometry on reconnect, invalidating every baseline, box and colour table.
  • A badge dot downscales from native resolution to roughly 12 px in this rig's 500x1080 mirror — well above the measured noise floor here, but this margin should not be assumed to hold on a higher-resolution phone model.
  • Continuous multi-hour foreground mirroring is only validated by short benchmark runs; a watcher meant to run for hours needs its own reconnection and staleness handling for AirPlay drops or the app being evicted by iOS memory pressure, not just a startup check.

Trap A silent watcher failure looks identical to no news

A phone whose mirror has dropped (state 0, no air_pid) produces no diffs and therefore no alerts — indistinguishable from zero new messages. Subscribe to the dev_disconnect and error_push WebSocket callbacks and surface per-phone video liveness alongside the badge state, or the system fails closed without telling anyone.

Wrong Unauthenticated read of customer conversations

The API has no authentication, so a watcher pulling frames of logged-in seller and DM inboxes turns port 9911 into an unauthenticated read of private customer conversations for any host on the subnet. Screenshots saved to disk or pushed into a Slack channel are a personal-data store; set retention, restrict membership, and prefer holding frames in memory. Firewall 9911 and 17000 to trusted hosts.

Scale

One raw BMP grab per phone at a 1 s cadence measures p50 2.0 ms and 1,620,054 bytes. Nineteen phones would be roughly 19 req/s and 31 MB/s on loopback against a measured ceiling of 84 req/s for a single flat-out poller and 512 req/s aggregate for ten concurrent pollers — about 4% of demonstrated capacity, needing no throttling. Phones are independent, and input traffic measurably does not slow polling. Each 1.6 MB frame exceeds the .NET Large Object Heap threshold: without buffer reuse, measured allocation was 488 MB/s with 496 gen-2 GCs per 8 s, fixed to 2.9 MB/s by reusing one buffer per poller. Today only two phones are actually online, so real current throughput is 2 req/s at a 1 s cadence — trivially sustainable, with headroom for a sub-500 ms cadence if faster badge detection is later wanted.

Ad account operations at agency scale

Mobile-only ad platform operations across client accounts (TikTok Ads, Meta Ads Manager, Snapchat approvals)

PartialWith caveats

Give each client's ad account its own phone in the rack, permanently signed in to the mobile ads app, and run a daily supervised routine: normalise home, open the app, capture a proof frame per client, scroll the campaign list, and tap Pause or Approve only on the narrow subset that needs it. Navigation and capture are fully native on this rig; reading the spend and delivery numbers off the screen is not, since the OCR plug-in is absent, so figures must be read client-side or by a human. Several ad-platform surfaces are mobile-first or mobile-only, and a phone per client keeps each authorised session isolated with its own notifications, turning a multi-minute daily check per client into one scripted pass plus a dated proof frame.

How

  1. set_group + set_dev GET /api/device/group/set?id=0&name= then GET /api/device/set?id=&gid=&name= — partition the rack by client: create a group, then name and assign each phone to it.
  2. get_device_list GET /api/device/get — read each phone's coordinate space (imgw/imgh) and cross-check readiness against /api/config/usb/get (state 2 confirms the control channel, not just video).
  3. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<ids> — clear stuck-click state across the whole target set.
  4. send_key GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — normalise to home screen page one.
  5. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=&y= — open the ads app on each phone; only mirror one coordinate to a group after confirming every phone in it has the app at that position.
  6. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<single id>&binary=true — capture the overview proof frame, one request per phone, optionally cropped with rect.
  7. mouse_wheel GET /api/mouse/wheel?id=<ids>&direction=down&len=100&number=2, then repeat capture — walk the campaign list. Wheel is preferable to swipe here since a full-height swipe costs ~580 ms of pointer travel and iOS may read it as a slow drag.
  8. client-side match / OCR (both server-side paths plug-in-gated) — verify the screen against a stored golden frame by mean absolute pixel difference before any state-changing tap. This is the gate that makes the whole use case safe; only proceed once the frame matches the expected screen.
  9. click + get_device_screenshot GET /api/mouse/click?id=<verified subset>&x=&y= then GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true&rect= — tap Pause/Approve only on the verified subset, then crop-diff around the control to prove the toggle actually moved.
  10. ocr / ocr_ex (unavailable on this rig) GET /api/pic/ocr?id=&rect= — lift spend and delivery figures into a sheet; currently answers code 28. Options are installing the plug-in, running client-side OCR against the raw BMP, or the Shortcut-based OCR fallback.
  11. send_key + shortcut#1/#2 (optional) fn_key=shift+win+3 then /shortcut/album/get / /shortcut/album/down — pull a native-resolution screenshot when the 500x1080 mirror is too small to read per-row figures; needs the Shortcut chain.

Needs

  • Vendor console running and logged in, with /config/user/info showing an active license before any run.
  • Per phone, the invisible iOS accessibility set: AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, Trackpad & Mouse speed maxed, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock, vendor cable only.
  • Each client's ad account already authenticated on its assigned phone by a person, under that client's authorisation and the platform's own terms for its mobile app — credentials are never typed by the automation.
  • Identical ads-app version and icon position across any phone group driven by a shared coordinate, or per-phone coordinate maps otherwise.
  • Either the vendor OCR plug-in, an external client-side OCR engine, or a human reader for figure extraction.
  • The Shortcut chain (installed, IP-edited, permissioned, hotkey-bound) for the native-resolution capture path only.

Watch out

  • Navigation and capture are fully native and doc-verified; reading the numbers is not — /pic/ocr answers code 28 and image search is presumed the same until proven otherwise.
  • The 500x1080 mirror is a pixel-exact downscale of the phone's own render, not a lossy copy — large headline figures are usually legible, per-row campaign metrics often are not. That's what the native-resolution capture path is for.
  • Mirroring a Pause/Approve tap to a whole group is the sharpest edge here. Send state-changing taps only to an explicitly verified subset, with a per-phone screen check and an after-tap frame diff, and exclude any phone whose imgw/imgh differs from the master.
  • The idle-floor mean-diff constant (0.02-0.03) assumes a static screen. Ads-manager feeds routinely contain autoplaying creative previews and live spend counters, which will sit well above that floor even with zero input — capture a per-app-screen baseline over a few idle frames, don't borrow the home-screen number.
  • An immediate screenshot after opening the app can capture a splash or blank frame rather than the campaign list — the verification gate needs a wait-for-target-screen loop, not a single capture.
  • A Pause/Approve toggle produces its own UI transition (switch animation, confirmation sheet), a different and unmeasured signature from a tap landing on an idle home screen — capture that app's own before/after pair rather than assuming the same numeric range confirms it.
  • 2FA and identity challenges are only partly automatable: a code arriving on the same phone can be entered via a tap plus ASCII /key/sendkey; a code on another device, an app-approval prompt, or a Face ID re-authentication all require a person, and the last one blocks the whole daily run for that client until unlocked in person — the API has no camera or biometric interface at all.
  • Non-ASCII client or campaign names need the clipboard-plus-paste route, which needs the Shortcut chain; there is no other text-entry path.
  • The claimed time savings is about request count, not wall time — the bottleneck is UI settle and app-launch time, unmeasured and app-version-dependent, not the kernel's 2 ms screenshot. Budget seconds, not milliseconds, per client for each navigate-and-verify leg.

Trap Mechanically identical timing reads as automation to the platform

Mobile ad-management apps commonly run client-side anti-automation heuristics — impossible-precision tap timing, absence of the sensor noise a hand-held phone produces, identical inter-action intervals every day. A HID board driving AssistiveTouch produces exactly that signature, so expect a materially higher chance of forced re-auth or session flags than a human operator would see, independent of anything this API can observe or control. Log and escalate to a human rather than retrying — this is a platform fraud-detection outcome, not a bug in the chain.

Wrong A mis-timed tap can pause a live campaign or approve the wrong spend

A mirrored tap on a stale or mis-positioned screen is a money risk, not a cosmetic one. The mitigations are structural: reset before every tap-critical sequence, a golden-frame diff check per phone before the tap, per-phone coordinates unless the group is provably identical, and an after-frame diff proving the control moved. Treat Pause/Approve as needing a human in the loop until the verification gate has a track record.

Scale

Navigation fans out for free — one comma-id request drives every listed phone in parallel, so a 20-client group costs the same wall time as one phone for the shared steps. Capture does not fan out (screenshot is single-id) but phones are fully independent: measured 83-85 req/s for two concurrent pollers and 512 req/s aggregate for ten, with input traffic not slowing polling. A daily pass over roughly 20 clients is dominated by unmeasured app behaviour — cold launch, list-scroll settle, toggle-confirmation animation — rather than by the kernel's sub-5 ms operations; a conservative 8-15 s per client, run concurrently across the rack's boards, puts a full daily pass at roughly 1-3 minutes of wall time end to end. Because this is a once-per-day-per-client design, the meaningful throughput ceiling is the client-account count — bounded by the 19 populated board slots, one phone per client — not requests per second.

Campaign quality assurance

Landing page render check against a golden frame

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Open your own campaign URL, with UTMs, on every mirrored phone in one call, capture the mirror frame at t+0.5 s, t+3 s and t+10 s, and compare the settled frame against a golden render captured earlier on a known-good phone at the same mirror resolution. It is read-only against your own property: nothing is clicked, nothing is posted, and there is no cross-account or geo-fabrication exposure, which makes it the strongest candidate of this group to build first.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get — read imgw/imgh per phone (500×1080 on both XRs); every later rect and coordinate is in that mirror-pixel space, not the 414×896 logical points. Exclude any phone whose imgw/imgh does not match the golden-frame phone.
  2. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<list> — clears the measured silent stuck-click state before the Safari-driving fallback; harmless when the Shortcut path is used.
  3. shortcut#12 open URL GET /api/shortcut/exec/url?id=<list>&url=<campaign URL>&outtime=<ms> — one comma-id call opens the URL on the whole set; outtime is milliseconds (default 15000), not the Phonefarm seconds. Needs the iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-configured and AssistiveTouch-bound on every phone.
  4. click + send_key POST /api/mouse/click then GET /api/key/sendkey?key=<ascii url> then fn_key=ENTER — fallback when the Shortcut is not installed: tap Safari, type the URL, hit Enter. key= is ASCII-only, so no Unicode or IDN URLs, and the two XRs have Safari at different home-screen coordinates, so this fallback cannot be mirrored across phones that differ.
  5. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true — one capture per phone per timestamp; single-id only. Raw BMP measured at 2 ms / 1,620,054 bytes versus 40.5 ms and a ~21 req/s cap for jpg=true.
  6. none client-side diff — compare the settled frame to the golden render and the t+3 frame to the t+10 frame by mean absolute pixel difference; no comparison endpoint exists in either edition.
  7. find_multi_color POST /api/pic/find-multi-color {id, list:[{first_color:'x|y|RRGGBB-101010,...', rect:[l,t,r,b], similarity}]} — optional CTA-colour presence check; XP's anchor syntax is absolute points, not the Phonefarm offset/dir scheme, and plug-in gating is unverified (probe for data.code 28 first).
  8. shortcut#19 GET /api/shortcut/device/ip?id=<one id>&state=1 — optional: record the egress IP each phone actually used, for a geo-verification audit trail.
  9. callback WS ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api — error_push — the only asynchronous signal that an input call failed at the board, separate from what the screenshot shows.

Needs

  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in — with only IMService.exe up, both phones showed state 0 and an empty board list.
  • iMouse Shortcut installed on each phone, kernel IP configured, run once with prompts allowed, bound to an AssistiveTouch key — required for /shortcut/exec/url and /shortcut/device/ip; unverified on this rig.
  • For the Safari fallback: board bound and state 2, non-empty location_crc, AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock — none queryable over the API.
  • A golden frame per page captured on a known-good phone at matching imgw×imgh, with brightness, True Tone, Night Shift and text size frozen afterward.
  • Masks defined for dynamic regions (carousels, countdown timers, personalized blocks, the status-bar clock) before any diff is meaningful.
  • UTMs tagged internal, or the rig's egress IP filtered out of analytics, so the pre-flight does not pollute campaign reporting.

Watch out

  • The Shortcut is not installed on this rig today, so the one-call open step is currently unavailable and the Safari fallback is what actually runs.
  • No text assertion is possible here: /api/pic/ocr answers data.code 28 (plug-in not connected), so headline or price copy cannot be checked server-side; everything is pixel- or colour-based until the OCR plug-in is installed.
  • /pic/find-multi-color's plug-in independence is not stated in the docs and should be assumed gated, the same as OCR, until a live probe proves otherwise.
  • This rig has 19 boards but only two phones mirroring, and one delivers ~4.5 new AirPlay frames/s against ~29 on its twin — a t+0.5 s capture on the slow phone may still show the previous screen (at most ~2 source frames land in that window); push its first checkpoint to at least t+1.5 s.
  • A consent or cookie wall should be photographed and flagged, not auto-dismissed — clicking Accept is a consent action and also destroys the regression being tested for.
  • The "air_play_ratio" field some drafts cite for matching golden and target phones does not appear in the documented /device/get response; match on imgw/imgh instead, which is confirmed and is the constraint that actually governs pixel-diff comparability.
  • Licence state can still gate phones coming online per device (/config/user/info, user_state, total_license) even though the XP docs carry no per-endpoint shortcut edition note.

Scale

One /shortcut/exec/url call covers the whole fleet regardless of size; capture is one request per phone per timestamp, and raw BMP at a measured p50 of 2 ms (phones proven independent up to ten concurrent pollers at 512 req/s aggregate) keeps three timestamps across the live phones to single-digit milliseconds of kernel time. The wall-clock cost is the 10-second observation window itself: a full three-shot pre-flight completes in roughly 11-15 seconds whether run against 2 phones or a hypothetical 19, because the window dominates, not the request count. Budget 1.6 MB per raw frame with a reused buffer. A monitoring cadence of one pre-flight run every few minutes per URL is easily sustainable; the ceiling is operator-chosen polling frequency, not the rig.

Coordinated publishing and guardrails

Synchronized drop: one multi-id click publishes every account at once

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Stage the composer on every phone up to but not including the Share button, park each pointer directly on the Share coordinate, verify per-phone readiness from a raw mirror frame, then fire a single click carrying the whole comma-separated id list at T0. Because every mouse endpoint accepts a device list and the boards walk it in parallel, N phones tap together in one request instead of N sequential ones — a pure-native variant (assets pre-loaded by hand, ASCII caption) needs no Shortcut at all.

How

  1. get_device_list / get_usb_list GET /api/device/get and GET /api/config/usb/get — build the drop list from records with a live state, air_pid, non-empty location_crc, and identical imgw/imgh; a phone with different mirror geometry cannot share a coordinate.
  2. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<list> — clears the measured stuck-click state (0.09 mean pixel diff before reset, 141.96 after) whenever the target set changes.
  3. shortcut#7 POST /api/shortcut/album/upload {id, files, album_name, zip, outtime} — puts the media on each phone; requires the Shortcut installed and hotkey-bound, none of which is verified here.
  4. send_key / click / swipe GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+h then /api/mouse/click and /api/mouse/swipe — drives the composer to the screen before Share; a mirrored coordinate is only fair when every phone has the same app build and the same element at that point.
  5. shortcut#10 + send_key POST /api/shortcut/clipboard/set then GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+v — the only documented non-ASCII caption route; a pure-ASCII caption can instead go straight in with /key/sendkey?key=.
  6. mouse_move GET /api/mouse/move?id=<list>&x=&y= — parks every pointer on Share ahead of T0. The board walks at ~0.6 ms/px, so pre-positioning removes the dominant cost of the T0 tap itself.
  7. get_device_screenshot (+ find_multi_color) GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true — per-phone readiness check; single-id only, so this is N requests, acceptable because phones are independent.
  8. click POST /api/mouse/click {id:'<a,b,c,...>', x, y, button:'1'} — the T0 tap: one HTTP request for the whole ready set. Button is numeric on XP ('1' left, '2' right), not the Phonefarm 'left'/'right' strings.
  9. get_device_screenshot (+ callbacks) GET /api/pic/screenshot per phone; WS error_push — records what actually happened per account; error_push is the only asynchronous board-failure signal and is invisible to an HTTP-only client.

Needs

  • Every target phone bound to its own board, state 2, non-empty location_crc, and identical imgw×imgh across the set.
  • iOS accessibility settings on every phone (AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, tracking speed, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock) — none queryable over the API.
  • Identical app build and composer layout across the set, so one Share coordinate is correct everywhere.
  • For media and non-ASCII captions: the iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-configured and hotkey-bound on each phone, reaching the kernel on TCP 9911.
  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in; a WebSocket client on the callback path for asynchronous failure signals.
  • Accounts the operator legitimately owns or is authorized to post from, on a platform whose terms permit automated posting.

Watch out

  • Simultaneity is at the tap, not at publication: /mouse/click returning code 0 only means the kernel accepted the request, and upload time, server-side queuing and per-phone network conditions afterward are outside the API's visibility. This should be described as synchronized initiation, not synchronized publication.
  • Parallel board dispatch is measured for two phones only; whether 19 simultaneous HID writes serialize inside the driver stack is unverified and is the single biggest open question for this use case at rack scale.
  • The rig's own AirPlay measurements show a 6× throughput gap between two identical XRs on the same Wi-Fi — direct evidence that per-phone link quality already differs enough to spread real publish times by whole seconds even given a perfectly simultaneous click.
  • A readiness check via /pic/find-multi-color should be assumed plug-in gated, like OCR, until proven otherwise; the dependable path is a client-side pixel test on the already-fetched raw frame.
  • Every /pic/* endpoint is single-id, so verify-before and verify-after are N requests each, unlike the input phase.
  • Simultaneous multi-megabyte media uploads from many phones sharing one access point can saturate its uplink, adding queuing delay that further desynchronizes real publish times — a Wi-Fi capacity constraint, not a software bug, and it scales with fleet size.
  • No Phonefarm function name works on this kernel, and the API has no authentication and listens on all interfaces — firewall 9911 to trusted hosts before wiring a scheduled drop to it.
  • Coordinated, identically-timed publication across many accounts is a strong and visible signal to platform anti-abuse systems regardless of intent; restrict this to accounts the operator owns or administers, on platforms whose terms permit it, with a stop-on-rate-limit policy rather than any attempt to soften the timing signature.

Scale

The T0 action is exactly one HTTP request regardless of set size; with pointers pre-parked, its own pointer travel is near zero, against a measured board-walk cost of ~0.6 ms/px that would otherwise add hundreds of milliseconds per phone. That parallelism is verified for two phones only — 19-phone parallelism is untested. Staging is the real budget: media upload via the Shortcut path is bounded by its 15-60 second outtime per phone and is serialized by the hotkey trigger, while readiness screenshots are single-id at ~2 ms each and phones poll independently (512 req/s aggregate across ten concurrent pollers, input and screenshot traffic proven not to interfere). For the two phones actually live here, a full stage-verify-fire-confirm cycle is plausibly 10-30 seconds; for a hypothetical 19-phone drop, budget tens of seconds of staging before T0 and expect several seconds of real publish-time spread across accounts even though the tap lands in one request.

Throttle and block detector: stop the loop when the app pushes back

PartialWith caveats

After every scripted action, pull a cropped raw frame for that phone and test it for a rate-limit dialog: a dimmed background plus an app-drawn card and button fill. On a hit, the controller stops issuing actions for that device, writes a full-frame evidence screenshot, dismisses the dialog, drops the id from the active list and stamps a cool-down timestamp entirely in controller-side state. This is the backstop that distinguishes a genuine platform refusal from the rig's own measured stuck-click state, and it is designed to halt on the platform's own stop signal, not to retry past it.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get — read imgw/imgh per device before the loop starts; every rect and coordinate below is in that mirror-pixel space.
  2. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<list> — pre-flight on the whole target set; without it a "no dialog, no reaction" reading is ambiguous between a block and a stuck pointer.
  3. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true&rect=[0,300,500,800] — captures the post-action frame cropped to the alert band; single-id only.
  4. none client-side decode — the only detection path proven available here: test fixed anchor pixels with per-channel tolerance plus mean-absolute-pixel-difference against the pre-action frame (idle floor 0.02-0.03, real reaction 20-160). Never compare by MD5.
  5. find_multi_color GET/POST /api/pic/find-multi-color — kernel-side alternative, unverified here; treat as plug-in gated like OCR until probed.
  6. ocr / ocr_ex /api/pic/ocr, /pic/find-text — NOT available on this rig: data.code 28, plug-in not connected. Would otherwise be the robust way to match dialog text.
  7. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&save_path=... — on a hit, write a full-frame evidence screenshot, timestamped and paired with the device's user_name and ip.
  8. click / send_key GET /api/mouse/click?id=<id>&x=&y= or /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=TAB+b — dismisses the dialog; TAB+b ("Return, not supported by all apps") is a fallback, not the primary path, and needs its own before/after diff verification.
  9. none controller-side state — remove the id from the active list and stamp a cool-down; optionally move it into a visible device group via /device/group/set and /device/set.
  10. (no equivalent) WS ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api — error_push, dev_disconnect, usb_change — the only asynchronous board-level failure signal; not proven to fire for a purely UI-level app refusal, only hardware/link failures.
  11. send_key + mouse_reset_pos GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+h (twice) then /api/mouse/reset — renormalises the active set before any resumed batch.
  12. none controller-side, human in the loop — nothing in either edition's API says the limit has lifted; resuming a specific account is an operator decision.

Needs

  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in, with the board bound, connected and location_crc non-empty for every monitored phone.
  • Colour anchors and the crop rect captured from a real rate-limit dialog on this app version at this mirror resolution — anchors are resolution-specific and invalidated by any air_play_ratio change.
  • Per-phone baselines rather than shared ones: the two XRs have different home screens, so a shared coordinate and a shared "idle" frame do not hold across phones.
  • A client-side BMP decoder with a reused frame buffer — each raw frame is 1.62 MB, well over the .NET Large Object Heap threshold.
  • Only for the kernel-side variant: the vendor image-search and/or OCR plug-ins, neither installed on this rig.
  • Accounts the loop drives must be ones the operator owns and is permitted to automate under the target platform's terms.

Watch out

  • The dependable detection path is client-side pixel testing; assume /pic/find-multi-color is plug-in gated like OCR (data.code 28) until a live probe proves otherwise, and build the pixel-anchor test as the primary detector, not a fallback bolted on after a failed probe.
  • Colour-anchor detection breaks on an app redesign, a dark/light mode switch, a different-width locale dialog, a Dynamic Type change, or a continuous server-side A/B test of dialog copy or layout — it needs a frequent (hours, not weeks) self-test against a stored reference crop.
  • A missed detection is not neutral: fail closed. If a post-action frame cannot be classified with confidence, including "no new frame arrived," stop that phone and flag it for a human rather than assuming all clear.
  • On the slow XR (~4.5 new frames/s versus ~29 on its twin) the post-action frame may be stale by ~220 ms or more; wait for a frame that actually differs from the pre-action frame rather than polling on a 30 fps assumption.
  • A "no dialog, no reaction" reading has at least three indistinguishable causes: the app ignored the tap, the pointer is stuck, or the tap landed off target. Reset before every batch and before every dismiss tap, not only at batch boundaries — the stuck state can appear mid-session on a previously working phone.
  • Automated dismissal taps a coordinate based on a colour match; a false positive taps whatever is actually there. Derive the dismiss point from the matched card's own geometry and require two consecutive positive frames before acting.
  • This design catches only the app's own explicit modal. A platform that throttles silently (delayed delivery, quiet feed reordering) will not trip it, and the loop keeps running at full rate against a service that is discarding the extra actions.
  • The cool-down table, timestamps, pacing and resume decision are all controller-side code; neither edition has a scheduler, a rate limiter or any notion of an account.

Scale

The detector is not the bottleneck: a cropped raw frame is a few milliseconds, the client-side anchor test on a small crop is sub-millisecond, and input traffic and screenshot traffic measured no interference with each other. But /pic/screenshot, /pic/find-multi-color and /pic/ocr all reject multiple ids, so capture and detection are strictly one request per phone; only reset and hotkey recovery calls fan out over a comma list. The real ceiling is each phone's own AirPlay source rate (measured ~29 fps versus ~4.5 fps on two identical XRs), so on a slow link the post-action frame wait dominates the per-action budget, pushing worst-case overhead to roughly 0.3-1 second per check. In practice, throughput is dictated by the target app's own action cadence and the rate limit this detector exists to respect: treat anything above the low hundreds of actions per hour per phone as almost certain to trip the very dialog being watched for, which is the design's point, not a rig limitation.

Creative testing at panel scale

A/B creative split across device groups with an insights harvest

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Partition the rack into two named groups, push creative A to one group's camera roll and creative B to the other, drive one identical posting flow across the union of both id lists, then hours later re-drive each phone to the post's Insights screen and capture the frame per phone into VariantA/ and VariantB/ folders. The grouping primitives exist precisely so a controller can address "the A half" and "the B half" as stable id lists across runs, but the harvest returns pixels only: with the OCR plug-in gated on this rig, nothing in the API turns an Insights screen into numbers.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get — confirm state, air_pid, vid/pid/uid and location_crc per phone, and record imgw×imgh (500×1080 on both XRs); exclude any phone whose mirror geometry differs.
  2. get_usb_list GET /api/config/usb/get — confirms board enumerated and phone attached (state 2); says nothing about the video channel, which is independent.
  3. set_group GET /api/device/group/set?id=0&name=VariantA then ?id=0&name=VariantB — id '0' creates a new group; capture the returned numeric ids.
  4. set_dev GET /api/device/set?id=<idsA>&gid=<gidA> and ?id=<idsB>&gid=<gidB> — assigns phones to their group; id accepts a comma list, re-readable via /device/group/get-dev.
  5. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<idsA,idsB> — clears the stuck-click state on the whole target set before any tap-critical sequence.
  6. shortcut#7 POST /api/shortcut/album/upload {id:'<idsA>', files:[...], outtime:60000} — two calls, each fanning out over a comma id list; response returns the 10 newest album records as confirmation the variant landed. Raise outtime well above the 15 s default for video.
  7. shortcut#10 POST /api/shortcut/clipboard/set then GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+v — optional per-phone caption; the only documented non-ASCII text route on XP.
  8. send_key / click / swipe GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+h (twice) then /api/mouse/click and /api/mouse/swipe — normalises every phone to a known screen, then drives the posting flow once over the union id list.
  9. shortcut#1 GET /api/shortcut/album/get?id=<one id>&num=10 — verifies the variant is the item the picker will select, one request per phone; XP has no date filter, so sort on create_time.
  10. mouse_reset_pos + click GET /api/mouse/reset then /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+h then /api/mouse/click — hours later, re-normalises and drives each phone to Insights on blind fixed coordinates; no scheduler exists in either edition.
  11. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true — captures the Insights frame per phone into VariantA/VariantB folders; single-id, run pollers concurrently.
  12. shortcut#3 POST /api/shortcut/album/del or /api/shortcut/album/clear — housekeeping so the next run's "newest item" is unambiguous; irreversible and needs Shortcuts delete permissions.

Needs

  • Accounts owned or authorized, one per phone, with a creator/business account type if the platform gates Insights behind that.
  • iMouse Shortcut installed on every phone, kernel IP configured, run once with prompts allowed, bound to an AssistiveTouch key — unverified on this rig; test with /shortcut/device/ip?state=0 first.
  • Shortcuts > Advanced permissions on each phone (run scripts, share large data, and delete permissions if album/del or album/clear is used).
  • Standard iOS input prerequisites (AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, tracking speed, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock) — none queryable over the API.
  • Board bound and cabled per phone, IMConsole.exe running and logged in, and every phone in a mirrored id list sharing the same imgw×imgh and the same element at the same coordinate once the app is open.
  • A controller process of your own to hold the delay between post and harvest — neither edition has a scheduling primitive.

Watch out

  • The harvest returns pixels, not metrics: /api/pic/ocr answers data.code 28, so reading impression and view counts off an Insights screenshot is a human job, a client-side OCR job on the raw frame, or requires the vendor plug-ins.
  • The navigation to Insights is blind: with no server-side element location, the harvest runs on fixed coordinates captured once and re-verified by frame diffing, which breaks on any app update that moves the control, and equally on the post scrolling off position, being removed, or still processing — none of which is observable from the API, and a wrong-screen capture returns the same status 200/code 0 as a correct one.
  • The group split is pure metadata: nothing in the kernel enforces that group A only ever receives file A; that discipline lives entirely in the controller.
  • /shortcut/album/upload fans out over a comma id list, but the read-back paths (album/get, album/down, clipboard/get, pic/screenshot) do not — the harvest is N requests, not one.
  • The "most recent project" grouping is a real strength here (each phone's Recents naturally holds only its assigned variant), but the shared picker-grid assumption is fragile: housekeeping (album/del) must run before each upload, not only after, or a phone with leftover items from a prior run has a different grid offset than a freshly cleared one.
  • The stuck-click trap is silent: a phone can ignore every /mouse/click while /mouse/move and hardware keys keep working, and it returns status 200, code 0 regardless. Verify by frame diff, never by return code.
  • Verification timing is per-phone: one XR delivers ~29 new frames/s under motion, its twin ~4.5, so a check on the slow phone must allow ~220 ms per new frame and compare by mean absolute pixel difference, never MD5.
  • Whether the shortcut dispatcher is licence-gated on this edition is undetermined; check user_state and total_license before planning around it.
  • Coordinated near-simultaneous posting of near-identical creative from multiple accounts is a pattern platform anti-abuse systems are specifically built to catch, independent of account ownership; this should stay a hard caveat rather than something the design tries to soften.
  • The single WebSocket failure watch catches board- and mirroring-level failures but has no signal for "the post failed to publish" or a content-policy interstitial — the posting leg's own verification is thin, confirming the media landed in the album, not that the post published.
  • Every album/clipboard/shortcut step depends on the Shortcut being installed, configured and bound on every phone, which is unverified here; until /shortcut/device/ip round-trips successfully per phone, roughly two-thirds of this chain, everything after group assignment, cannot run at all.

Scale

The split is nearly free: two upload calls instead of one, and the posting flow is a single mirrored request per tap over the union id list, since the board walks all listed phones in parallel at the cost of one. The read side does not scale the same way: screenshot, album/get, album/down and clipboard/get are all single-id, so a 20-phone harvest is 20-plus requests per stage, run concurrently since phones are measurably independent (ten pollers sustained 512 req/s aggregate). Use raw BMP for every capture (2 ms, 1.6 MB) rather than jpg (40 ms, ~21 req/s cap). The real wall-clock cost of the posting leg is pointer travel at ~0.6 ms/px, so a full-height swipe runs ~580 ms and may register as a drag; the slowest link of all is the Shortcut round trip, bounded by its outtime (default 15 s) and involving a hotkey, an iOS Shortcuts run and a LAN callback — a video upload can take far longer and needs outtime raised accordingly. A full A/B cycle across roughly 10 phones per side completes in low single-digit minutes for posting plus 10-30 seconds for a concurrent harvest sweep, well under the hours-long gap between posting and harvest, which is idle time, not compute time.

Ad-verification, outside the box

Geo/carrier ad-serving audit from a cellular-routed phone

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Exploit the rig's two-channel design, video over Wi-Fi, app traffic over the SIM, to audit your own geo- or carrier-targeted campaigns on a genuine carrier-located iPhone. Read each phone's LAN and public IP through the Shortcut, switch on cellular data, open the placement, and capture the served creative with the phone's Wi-Fi still associated (so mirroring keeps working) but its routed traffic on the carrier. The evidence artifact is a timestamped, IP-attributed frame of the real ad on a real handset on a real carrier IP, which is exactly the population geo/carrier targeting was bought against and which a datacentre VPN or emulator cannot reproduce.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get — gate the audit on a live state and air_pid, and read imgw/imgh and the LAN ip field, which is free and needs no Shortcut round trip.
  2. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<list> — clears the stuck-click state before any tap-critical sequence.
  3. shortcut#24 GET /api/shortcut/device/ip?id=<id>&state=0 — reads the LAN IP; single-id only. A match against step 1's ip field is the cheapest end-to-end proof the Shortcut path works; data.code 30 means the hotkey never fired or the phone cannot reach the kernel.
  4. shortcut#24 GET /api/shortcut/device/ip?id=<id>&state=1 — records the baseline public egress IP before the cellular flip, archived with deviceid and timestamp.
  5. none manual, on the phone: Settings > Wi-Fi > Edit > IPv4 > Manual — enter an IP address and subnet mask and leave the router/gateway field empty, per the vendor's own settings-page instructions; the phone stays associated to Wi-Fi (mirroring and the Shortcut callback keep working) while routed traffic moves to cellular.
  6. shortcut#20 GET /api/shortcut/switch/cdpd?id=<list>&state=1&outtime=20000 — turns cellular data on across the whole audit set in one fan-out request.
  7. shortcut#24 GET /api/shortcut/device/ip?id=<id>&state=1 — re-reads the public IP and asserts it changed to the carrier's pool; a renewed timeout here means the manual IPv4 config broke the LAN return path.
  8. shortcut#13 GET /api/shortcut/exec/url?id=<list>&url=<placement-url> — opens the placement; a tap into an installed app's feed is the alternative when the placement is not a bare URL.
  9. swipe GET /api/mouse/swipe?id=<list>&direction=up&len=0.5 — scrolls the ad slot into view; keep len modest, since the board walks at ~0.6 ms/px and a full-height stroke may read as a drag.
  10. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true — captures the served creative; single-id, raw BMP measured at 2 ms.
  11. shortcut#21 GET /api/shortcut/switch/cdpd?id=<list>&state=0 — ends the cellular session and stops metered data accruing between runs.
  12. NOT USED /api/shortcut/switch/wlan?state=0 — deliberately excluded: it kills both the AirPlay channel and the Shortcut's return path, leaving the phone controllable but blind and every later call timing out.
  13. NOT AVAILABLE /api/pic/ocr, /pic/find-image — the kernel cannot identify the advertiser or read the creative's text on this rig (data.code 28); classification happens off-box on the archived frames.

Needs

  • A SIM with an active data plan in each audit handset — neither XR on this rig is documented as having one, so this is unproven hardware, not a software gap.
  • The iMouse Shortcut installed on each phone, kernel IP configured, run once with prompts allowed, and bound to an AssistiveTouch key — unverified here and load-bearing for the whole workflow, unlike the optional Shortcut use in the other entries in this section.
  • The board bound and connected (state 2), since every Shortcut call is triggered by the board sending the hotkey.
  • The manual Wi-Fi IPv4 configuration on every audit phone, per-phone, surviving reboots but redone if the LAN is re-addressed.
  • Standard input prerequisites (AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, tracking speed, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock) and IMConsole.exe running and logged in.
  • A licensed account, and authorization to audit the campaigns and properties in question, plus awareness of the publisher's automated-access terms.

Watch out

  • Every function in this chain is documented and correctly named for this edition; nothing is invented. The caveats are all prerequisite and observability, not API existence.
  • Two prerequisites are unverified and either one blocks the workflow entirely: whether the handsets have SIMs with data, and whether the Shortcut is installed and hotkey-bound. This should be read as "achievable once two unconfirmed hardware/software prerequisites are separately verified," not as ready to run today.
  • /shortcut/device/ip and /pic/screenshot are single-device; only the cellular toggle, URL open and swipe/reset fan out over a comma list.
  • No server-side recognition is available: the kernel hands you pixels, not an advertiser identity. All creative identification happens off-box.
  • The no-gateway trick forces cellular egress at the IP-routing layer, but many ad exchanges use device location services for geo-targeting, not only IP geolocation. If the campaign's targeting is location-services-driven, this rig's fixed physical location keeps reporting that location regardless of which network carries the traffic, and the audit would silently validate the wrong geo dimension while looking successful end to end. State explicitly which signal is being audited, carrier/IP, and flag that location-based targeting needs physically relocating the handset, which this rig cannot do.
  • iOS's behaviour when a Wi-Fi interface has no gateway but stays associated is not guaranteed to route every app's traffic over cellular equally; an app already running before the IPv4 change can hold stale sockets. Force-quit and relaunch the target app after the change, and verify egress IP with the Shortcut round trip before trusting a capture.
  • Repeatedly loading ad placements, even passively for screenshot capture with no click, generates billable impressions and may be scored as invalid traffic by verification vendors; this is a hard constraint on run frequency and volume, not a tuning knob.
  • The technique rests on a vendor settings-page instruction that could not be independently cross-checked against this rig's own measured hardware record, which is silent on cellular/SIM capability entirely.
  • The stuck-click trap and the mirror-pixel coordinate space apply here exactly as elsewhere, and the slow-phone framerate (~4.5 fps versus ~29 fps) lengthens, but does not break, each placement's render confirmation if the carrier-routed phone happens to be the weak-link handset.

Scale

Per phone per placement, the fixed costs are two single-id IP round trips (seconds each, bounded by the 15 s default outtime), one URL open or tap, one or two short swipes, and a settle wait for the ad to render. Capture itself is negligible at 2 ms for raw BMP. Fan-out is asymmetric: the cellular toggle, URL open, click, swipe and reset all take a comma id list and cost the same for one phone or many, while the IP reads and screenshot are single-id loops. Phones do not contend, ten concurrent pollers sustained 512 req/s aggregate, so a rack scales close to linearly with one poller per phone; the binding constraint is cellular data volume and per-SIM plan cost, not API throughput. The realistic per-placement budget is 15-30 seconds end to end, dominated by app and ad-server latency rather than the kernel, and the number of SIM-equipped, Shortcut-bound handsets available is the actual ceiling on this rig, currently unconfirmed and possibly zero.

MARK-PLATFORMS-MARK

Section 4 · Platform-by-platform playbook

Platform-by-platform playbook

Every entry below is built from the same eight or nine XP primitives: a device read, an album upload, a key send, a mouse click, a clipboard set-and-paste, a mouse drag or wheel, and a screenshot. What changes per platform is the composer layout, whether the text needs Unicode, whether the platform itself offers scheduling, and how much the missing OCR and image-search plug-ins cost you at the verification step. Every entry needs the iMouse iOS Shortcut for anything beyond ASCII typing or a PC-to-phone file transfer, and every entry's proof of success is a pixel comparison, because this rig's OCR reports data.code 28, plug-in not connected, and the image-search plug-in should be assumed absent until proven otherwise.

Short-form video: TikTok, Instagram, YouTube Shorts

TikTok: album push to a verified post

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

One /shortcut/album/upload call with a comma-separated id list lands an mp4 in Recents on every phone at once and returns the ten newest album records as proof it arrived. From there the TikTok composer is driven by taps in each phone's own mirror-pixel space, an ASCII caption goes in through /key/sendkey, and an emoji or CJK caption goes in through the clipboard-and-paste route. This is the workload the rack exists for, and it is also the clearest demonstration of its blind spot: with the OCR plug-in reporting code 28 on this rig, a raw pixel difference is the only success signal available, and it cannot tell a successful post from a guideline rejection.

How

  1. get_device_list /device/get?id=<a,b,c>, reads state, air_pid and imgw/imgh (500x1080 on these XRs, not the 414x896 iOS point space); exclude any phone whose imgw/imgh differs from the master.
  2. shortcut#7 /shortcut/album/upload, pushes the clip into Recents on every listed phone in one call. The response's ten newest album records confirm the clip landed before any tile is tapped; raise outtime well past the 15000 ms default for a 30 MB clip.
  3. send_key + mouse_reset_pos /key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+h (x2) then /mouse/reset, two Home presses return every phone to page one, then the reset clears the silent stuck-click state that /mouse/up cannot fix.
  4. click / shortcut#13 /mouse/click or /shortcut/exec/url, opens TikTok. Coordinates are captured per phone: the two XRs on this rig have different home screens, so one coordinate hits a different app on each.
  5. click /mouse/click, walks the composer: plus tab, Upload, first Recents tile, Next, Next. Each tap costs about 0.6 ms per pixel of pointer travel.
  6. send_key /key/sendkey?key=%23fyp+%23unboxing, types the ASCII hashtags directly; ASCII punctuation including # is supported, but typing speed and maximum length are undocumented.
  7. shortcut#10 + send_key /shortcut/clipboard/set then WIN+v, the only Unicode path on XP, carries the emoji or CJK half of the caption. sleep is in seconds, outtime in milliseconds.
  8. click + get_device_screenshot /mouse/click then /pic/screenshot?binary=true, taps Post, then verifies by mean absolute pixel difference (idle floor 0.02-0.03, real reaction 20-160) with a rect crop on the Post button, since MD5 always reports a false "reacted."
  9. click + shortcut#10 + send_key comment sheet: /mouse/click, /shortcut/clipboard/set, WIN+v, the same clipboard pattern for replies, addressed purely by screen position, since there is no OCR to read comment text.

Needs

  • iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-edited, run once with all permissions, and bound to an AssistiveTouch key on every phone; not verified as done on this rig.
  • Board bound and connected (state 2 in /config/usb/get) with mouse parameters present (location_crc non-empty).
  • Phone accessibility settings the API cannot query: AssistiveTouch on, Full Keyboard Access on, max tracking speed, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock.
  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in; with only IMService.exe up, both phones read state 0 and the board list is empty.
  • TikTok already signed in on each phone, on an account you own, with composer coordinates captured per phone and per app version.

Watch out

  • Verification is pixel-diff only: a guideline rejection, a duplicate-content warning and a successful post are indistinguishable at whole-frame level, and a rect-cropped check on the Post button narrows this without closing it.
  • Every coordinate is app-version and phone specific; nothing in the API finds a UI element without a plug-in, so the macro breaks silently on a TikTok update.
  • The two XRs deliver new frames at very different rates, about 29/s versus about 4.5/s under motion; a verification poll tuned to the fast phone will read a stale frame on the slow one as evidence nothing happened.
  • Distinct captions per phone cost a full clipboard round trip each, adding 1-3 s per phone rather than folding into a flat post-time estimate.
  • /mouse/reset must be resent whenever the batch's id list changes, including when a run is split into smaller posting groups.
  • Album-upload outtime should scale with clip size and each phone's Wi-Fi energy-mode cap (roughly 5, 10 or 20 Mbps); a 30 MB clip can take 12-48 s depending on which cap applies.

Trap A pixel match is not a success signal

Driving many phones from one comma-separated id list produces byte-identical actions at the same millisecond, which is exactly the signature integrity systems are built to find. That is a mechanical fact about the transport, not something to engineer around. Treat a rate-limit or "Action Blocked" dialog as a stop signal for that phone's queue, and capture its pixel-diff signature in advance, since there is no OCR to read the dialog text.

Scale

About 20 taps per post, dominated by pointer travel at roughly 0.6 ms per pixel (a corner-to-corner tap on the 500x1080 mirror is about 600 ms). A shared caption across N identically laid-out phones costs the same wall time as one, since the board walks a comma-separated id list in parallel: call it 40-60 s per post, up to roughly 60-90 batch-cycles an hour run back to back. Distinct captions serialize the clipboard step, so a 19-phone batch with distinct captions runs closer to 80-160 s per cycle, around 22-45 cycles an hour for the whole rack. Verification is about 2 ms per phone per check on a reused BMP buffer. These are transport ceilings; TikTok's own rate limits and detection will very likely force a lower real cadence.

Instagram: Reel, Story, DM reply and Follow

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Instagram's four short-loop actions map onto the same primitives as the TikTok flow but lean harder on Unicode: the reel and story assets go to Recents in one album-upload call, captions and DM text arrive via clipboard-and-paste since /key/sendkey is ASCII-only, and a two-tap Follow is confirmed by reading the button's own pixels out of a raw screenshot. It is the platform where operators want the most non-Latin text and the shortest loops, and both are covered, the hard part is verification, not the action.

How

  1. get_device_list /device/get?id=<a,b,c>, confirms mirroring is live and reads imgw/imgh for the coordinate space; excludes any follower whose mirror geometry differs from the master.
  2. shortcut#7 /shortcut/album/upload, pushes the reel mp4 and the story jpg in one call, since files is a string array. Read the response's newest-record list rather than assuming "first tile" ordering.
  3. shortcut#1 /shortcut/album/get, optionally re-reads the album (single id only) to disambiguate which upload is which by create_time.
  4. send_key + mouse_reset_pos WIN+h (x2) then /mouse/reset, normalises state and clears the stuck-click trap.
  5. click /mouse/click, drives the Reel composer: open app, plus, Reel, first tile, Next, Next, caption field. Coordinates are per phone, since the two XRs share no home-screen layout.
  6. shortcut#10 + send_key /shortcut/clipboard/set then WIN+v, the only Unicode caption route; prove the round trip once per phone with /shortcut/clipboard/get.
  7. shortcut#13 / click /shortcut/exec/url?url=instagram://camera (unverified) or tap-through, opens the Story camera. The URL scheme is documented in neither vendor doc and may fall through to Safari.
  8. click + shortcut#10 + send_key DM reply: click, clipboard/set, WIN+v, ENTER, the same clipboard pattern, addressed purely by position, with no way to confirm which thread is open.
  9. click + get_device_screenshot + find_multi_color /mouse/click then /pic/screenshot?binary=true, optionally /pic/find-multi-color, taps Follow, then reads the button's own pixels (blue before, grey after) out of the raw BMP; treat the color-search endpoint as a bonus, not the primary method.
  10. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?binary=true&rect=[l,t,r,b], verifies every write step by mean absolute pixel difference against the pre-tap frame, cropped to the button or dialog region.

Needs

  • iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-edited and bound to an AssistiveTouch key on every phone; album upload and every clipboard call depend on it.
  • Board bound and connected with mouse parameters present; Full Keyboard Access on for WIN+v and ENTER; AssistiveTouch, max tracking speed, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock.
  • Instagram signed in on each phone on accounts you own; Reels composer, camera, DM and profile coordinates captured per phone and per app version.
  • A Follow-button color reference sampled at the phone's current settings, with brightness, True Tone, Night Shift and Dark Mode fixed and matching across phones.

Watch out

  • No OCR on this rig, so the DM step cannot confirm which thread is open and the Follow step cannot read the button label; both are positional or color-based guesses, and both should sit behind a screenshot review gate before running unattended.
  • /pic/find-multi-color's plug-in status here is unverified; treat client-side pixel reading of the raw BMP as the primary method.
  • Gallery ordering is app behavior, not an API guarantee; confirm the intended asset from the album-upload or album-get response rather than trusting "first tile."
  • Only the input and clipboard-set calls fan out; screenshot, find-multi-color, and album-get are all single-id.
  • Identical-timing Follow actions fanned out to many accounts via one comma-separated id list is one of the most heavily policed automation signatures on the platform, independent of any attempt to look human; that is a direct, factual consequence of the transport.
  • Video upload duration is unbounded and unmeasured on this rig; raise outtime for album upload well past 120 s for a video and poll /shortcut/album/get rather than using a fixed sleep.
  • Only 2 of the rack's 19 boards currently have a phone bound and mirroring, so every fan-out claim is proven at n=2, not at rack scale.

Trap Reel trims need two fingers, this rig has one

Instagram's Reels composer can require a pinch-to-zoom or a two-finger trim-handle drag when a source clip's aspect ratio does not already match 9:16. The rig drives exactly one HID pointer per phone, with no multi-touch, so any step needing two simultaneous contact points cannot be automated at all. Restrict the chain to source video already cropped to 9:16 before upload, or do that step by hand.

Scale

A Reel post is roughly 15 taps (30-45 s), a Story about 6 taps (about 15 s), a DM reply 4 taps plus one clipboard round trip (about 5 s), a Follow 2 taps (about 3 s); shared inputs fan out at no extra cost, per-phone captions add one clipboard call each. The board-time ceiling is tens of such actions an hour per phone, but real throughput is capped lower by video-ingest wall time on a shared Wi-Fi link, by the mandatory human review of blind DM and Follow steps, and by Instagram's own throttling on Follow and DM, which is the real ceiling regardless of rig speed. A realistic sustained rate is low single digits of Reels an hour per phone and tens of Stories or Follows an hour per phone at most before platform-side risk dominates.

YouTube Shorts: album upload with in-app scheduling

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

The YouTube app's upload flow ends on a Visibility screen that includes Schedule, so a Short can be posted or scheduled entirely on the phone: push the mp4 into the album, normalise with two Home presses and a pointer reset, walk plus, Create a Short, gallery, Next with taps, paste the caption via clipboard, set the schedule with short drags, tap Upload. A clip already staged for another platform is reused with no second PC-to-phone transfer, and because Visibility carries Schedule, the rack does not have to be awake at publish time.

How

  1. shortcut#7 /shortcut/album/upload?files=[...]&outtime=180000, pushes the clip (skip if already staged for another platform); the response's ten newest album records confirm arrival before the UI walk begins.
  2. send_key + mouse_reset_pos WIN+h (x2) then /mouse/reset, normalises state and clears the stuck-click trap; budget this before every Short, not once per session, since the trap has been observed to reappear.
  3. click / shortcut#13 /mouse/click or /shortcut/exec/url?url=youtube://, opens YouTube; the custom URL scheme is unverified, and the icon-tap route cannot be mirrored across phones with different home screens.
  4. click /mouse/click, walks plus, Create a Short, gallery icon, first tile, Next; coordinates are mirror-pixel (500x1080), not iOS points, and cannot be located at runtime without OCR.
  5. shortcut#10 + send_key /shortcut/clipboard/set then WIN+v, sets the caption for any non-ASCII text, since key= is English/numbers only.
  6. mouse_down / mouse_move / mouse_up /mouse/down, repeated /mouse/move, /mouse/up (or /mouse/swipe), drives Visibility, Schedule, and the date/time wheel; keep strokes to 100-200 px given the roughly 0.6 ms/px board walk.
  7. click /mouse/click, taps Done then Upload Short; the transfer continues in the background, so Auto-Lock must be Never or the phone sleeping mid-upload both stalls it and drops the mirror.
  8. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?binary=true&rect=[l,t,r,b], verifies the upload started and, later, completed, by mean absolute pixel difference on the banner region.

Needs

  • iMouse Shortcut installed and IP-edited, with Allow Sharing Large Amounts of Data on for the video transfer; never probed on this rig.
  • YouTube app logged in to a channel the operator owns, on each phone.
  • Board bound, location_crc non-empty, AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, max tracking speed, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock.
  • Composer, gallery and Visibility coordinates captured per app version in 500x1080 mirror-pixel space.

Watch out

  • Video transfer duration is undocumented and unmeasured; a timeout returns code 30 with no partial-progress signal, so raise outtime well past the 15000 ms default.
  • The "Create a Short" entry point and the Visibility screen move between app versions, and nothing in the API can find them at runtime while OCR and image search are unavailable.
  • Upload completion cannot be read as text on this rig; a pixel diff on the banner region tells you something changed, not whether it says success or failure, since "Uploading," "Processing," and "Upload failed" look similar in a region diff without OCR.
  • Two separate transfers are involved (PC to phone, then phone to YouTube over its own Wi-Fi), each with its own unmeasured bottleneck; a 50-100 MB clip can add tens of seconds to minutes before the UI walk can even begin.
  • iOS can suspend background network activity depending on Background App Refresh permission, which is not queryable through this API and is a silent failure mode beyond Auto-Lock.

Tip The schedule wheel tracks the finger, it does not need a flick

YouTube's Visibility date/time control is a position-driven wheel, not a velocity-gated gesture like a swipe-to-dismiss list. A slow board-driven drag that ends at the correct offset should land the right value even at 0.6 ms/px, because the wheel tracks finger position continuously. Budget for the cost of the drag itself (a 200 px scroll is about 120 ms of board time, done once), not for extra retries against an assumed flick threshold.

Scale

About 14 taps plus one clipboard round trip and one picker drag per Short, roughly 40-60 s per phone excluding file transfer, and the same whether one phone or N are listed since the driving calls fan out across a comma-separated id list. That is a physics ceiling of roughly 60-80 Shorts an hour per phone if content and transfer time were free. Real throughput is dominated by two things the chain-only number leaves out: per-clip file transfer time, likely tens of seconds to minutes, and YouTube's own upload-processing wall time before Visibility can be reached reliably. A defensible planning number is 10-20 Shorts an hour per phone sustained, not 60-80; the network and app are the bottleneck, not the API.

Text-first and native-scheduling platforms: Threads and Facebook

Threads: text posting and replies via clipboard fan-out

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Threads needs no media pipeline; the whole value is text. Normalise every phone, tap into the composer, push the post body onto the phone clipboard with /shortcut/clipboard/set, which takes a comma-separated id list so identical copy reaches N phones in one request, paste with WIN+v, tap Post. Replies are the same six taps on a reply sheet. This is the cheapest platform per post on the rack and the cleanest template for any text-only surface, but the whole text path rides on an iMouse Shortcut round trip that has never been exercised on this rig.

How

  1. send_key /key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+h (x2), presses Home twice; the first leaves the app, the second returns to page one, and it doubles as a liveness probe since a Home press produces a whole-frame diff around 142.
  2. mouse_reset_pos /mouse/reset?id=<ids>, clears the silent stuck-click state before any tap-critical sequence; send it whenever the target set changes.
  3. click /mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=&y=, opens Threads. Button is numeric on XP ('1' left), not the Phonefarm strings; the two XRs have different home screens, so one coordinate is not valid across both.
  4. click /mouse/click, taps the compose control in the bottom tab bar; the position is an app-UI fact absent from any vendor doc and must be re-captured per app version.
  5. shortcut#10 /shortcut/clipboard/set?id=<ids>&text=&sleep=1&outtime=15000, pushes the post body, emoji included; sleep is seconds, outtime is milliseconds; POST JSON in UTF-8 rather than a query string.
  6. send_key /key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+v, pastes into the focused field; if the field was never focused the paste silently does nothing, and fn_key=OPENKeyboard can force the keyboard up as a focus check.
  7. click /mouse/click, taps Post.
  8. shortcut#10 + send_key + click reply sheet: clipboard/set, WIN+v, click, the reply chain is the same three calls on the post's reply sheet, serialised per phone since the Shortcut is triggered by a HID hotkey through the board.
  9. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<single id>&binary=true, verifies the post landed by mean absolute pixel difference; single-id only, so run one poller per phone.

Needs

  • iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-edited and bound to a custom AssistiveTouch key on every phone; not yet verified present on this rig, no shortcut endpoint has ever been probed here.
  • Shortcuts > Advanced: Allow Running Scripts, Allow Sharing Large Amounts of Data; phone must reach the kernel on TCP 9911 to post the Shortcut's result back.
  • Board bound (state 2), location_crc non-empty; AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, max tracking speed, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock.
  • Threads app logged in on accounts the operator owns; composer and Post coordinates captured per app version in 500x1080 space.
  • Licence headroom checked via /config/user/info: unlicensed phones are refused.

Watch out

  • The whole text path depends on the iMouse Shortcut, a per-phone manual install never verified on this rig; without it, posting is limited to ASCII via /key/sendkey, no emoji, no non-Latin script.
  • XP has no send_text and no asynchronous completion signal for text delivery; the only confirmation is /shortcut/clipboard/set returning code 0 within outtime, optionally cross-checked with clipboard/get.
  • Mirrored icon taps are invalid across phones with different home screens; fan-out is only safe for phones with identical layouts and identical imgw/imgh.
  • No OCR on this rig, so a rate-limit or "Action Blocked" dialog cannot be read by the kernel; detecting it requires client-side template matching on raw frames.
  • A positive pixel diff on the Post button region is necessary, not sufficient, evidence of success: a rate-limit interstitial or an error toast also changes enough pixels to register as a reaction.
  • The 10-20 s per-post figure is an explicit guess; the Shortcut round trip has never been exercised end to end on this rig, so the whole text-posting path is unproven, not just slow by an unknown amount.
  • Posting identical text from several accounts via one comma-id fan-out is a direct, mechanical consequence of the transport and is already treated as spam behavior by platform policy; that is a factual risk to name, not a detection problem to solve technically.

Scale

Roughly six taps plus one clipboard round trip per post, about 2-4 s of pure board time; the clipboard call is bounded by outtime (default 15 s) and in practice is the long pole, so call it 10-20 s per post per phone with that figure unverified. Identical copy to N phones costs the same wall time as one, since input calls fan out; distinct copy costs one clipboard call per id. Verification does not fan out (single-id) but is nearly free, raw BMP p50 2 ms; the real ceiling on it is the AirPlay source rate, about 29 new frames/s on the fast phone against about 4.5 on its identical twin. If the unverified figure holds, the chain-only ceiling is roughly 150-350 posts an hour per phone, but Threads' own automated-posting throttling will cap real throughput long before the API or board time does.

Facebook: Business Suite scheduling, Marketplace listings, comment hiding

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Facebook is the one large surface with first-class in-app scheduling, so the rack only has to drive the Meta Business Suite composer and its date picker. Photos arrive in bulk through album upload, the caption comes from clipboard-and-paste, ASCII fields like price and title are typed directly, the date picker is driven with a real down-move-up drag, and hiding a comment is a long press expressed as a click with time=800. Because Business Suite schedules natively, a single supervised sitting can front-load a week of Page posts per phone instead of requiring the rack to be awake at each publish time.

How

  1. shortcut#7 /shortcut/album/upload?files=[...]&zip=0&outtime=120000, seeds listing or post photos from the PC; the response returns the 10 newest album records to confirm arrival, so a batch of more than 10 images cannot be fully confirmed from that one response alone.
  2. send_key + mouse_reset_pos WIN+h (x2) then /mouse/reset, normalises state and clears the stuck-click trap.
  3. click /mouse/click, opens Meta Business Suite, taps Create post, taps the text area; positions are app-UI facts absent from every vendor doc.
  4. shortcut#10 + send_key /shortcut/clipboard/set then WIN+v, sets a caption with emoji; required for anything outside ASCII.
  5. click /mouse/click, taps Add photo and the Recents tiles; the freshly uploaded files are the newest items, checked against the upload response before tapping.
  6. mouse_down / mouse_move / mouse_up /mouse/down, repeated /mouse/move, /mouse/up (or /mouse/swipe, /mouse/wheel), toggles Schedule and sets the date/time wheel; keep strokes to 100-200 px given the 0.6 ms/px board walk.
  7. click /mouse/click, taps Schedule to commit the Page post.
  8. click /mouse/click, walks the Marketplace path: Marketplace tab, Sell, Item, Add photos, select; coordinates differ per region and account type.
  9. send_key + shortcut#10 /key/sendkey for Title and Price, clipboard/set + WIN+v for Description, types ASCII fields directly and pastes anything with a currency symbol, accent or emoji.
  10. click /mouse/click, taps Next then Publish.
  11. click (with time) /mouse/click?time=800, hides a comment via a long press, no separate API call needed; 800 ms is a starting value and more likely to over-fire than under-fire, tune downward first.
  12. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<single id>&binary=true&rect=[l,t,r,b], verifies each stage by mean absolute pixel difference, single-id only.

Needs

  • iMouse Shortcut installed and IP-edited on every phone, with Allow Sharing Large Amounts of Data on; never probed on this rig.
  • Meta Business Suite and Facebook logged in with Page admin rights per phone, since scheduling is per Page.
  • Board bound and connected, location_crc non-empty, AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, max tracking speed, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock.
  • Date-picker behavior tested on one phone before any fan-out.
  • Coordinate sets captured per app version for Business Suite, Marketplace and the comment sheet.

Watch out

  • Media upload timing is unbounded in the docs and unmeasured here; a timeout returns code 30 with no partial-progress signal.
  • Business Suite and Marketplace coordinates are per app version, region and account type, and nothing in the API can locate them at runtime without OCR or image search.
  • /key/sendkey cannot type a currency symbol, accent or emoji; anything outside ASCII must go through the clipboard.
