  • A rate-limit or "Action Blocked" interstitial cannot be distinguished from a successful publish by pixel diff alone, both change the screen well above the noise floor; this is a real, currently unclosed gap, not just a documented limitation.
  • Marketplace listing fan-out across phones is generally unsafe: identical listings from several accounts is exactly what commerce policy restricts, and an accepted offer is a real transaction the operator must fulfil, unlike reversible Page-post scheduling.
  • Photo attachment relies on the uploaded file being the newest item in Recents; check the album-upload response's newest records rather than assuming the first tile.
  • Only 2 of 19 boards currently have a phone bound and mirroring; fan-out and rack-scale framing are unverified beyond that.

Tip The date picker is a wheel, not a flick gesture

iOS's native picker tracks the finger 1:1 while pressed rather than requiring an inertial flick, so it is a direct-manipulation control, not a velocity-gated one. A short drag of roughly one row height, about 40-50 px, repeated a few times should move the wheel deterministically. Treat it as moderately risky and cheaply testable in a handful of short attempts before committing to fan-out, not as an unknowable step.

Scale

A scheduled Business Suite post is roughly 15 taps plus one picker interaction, about 45-60 s per phone, dominated by app response and the picker, not the API; a Marketplace listing is about 20 taps plus ASCII typing, roughly 60-90 s. The composer half of this playbook mirrors for free across phones with identical app versions, layouts and imgw/imgh. For Page scheduling this gives a technical ceiling of about 40-70 scheduled posts an hour per phone. Marketplace listings imply a similar per-phone ceiling, but each one is a real binding commercial listing, so the meaningful constraint is how many genuine, deliverable items and prices a human can source and verify per hour, not board time. Comment hiding is a few seconds each, bounded by comment volume and by keeping a human in the moderation decision.

Niche surfaces: Pinterest and Snapchat

Pinterest: catalogue pins with native publish-later

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Pinterest is the most automation-friendly of the platforms covered here. The composer takes an album photo, an ASCII destination link and title typed directly, a Unicode description delivered by clipboard-and-paste, a board pick, and on business accounts a publish-at-a-later-date toggle. Saves from the feed are a three-tap macro. A whole day's catalogue can be pushed to N phones in one album-upload call with zip=1, after which each pin is a per-phone script; it is also the only platform here whose own product offers scheduling.

How

  1. get_device_list + get_usb_list /device/get and /config/usb/get, reads imgw/imgh for the coordinate space, requires a live air_pid for video and board state 2 for control; excludes any phone whose imgw/imgh differs from the master.
  2. shortcut#7 /shortcut/album/upload?zip=1, pushes the day's catalogue images in one call; the doc recommends zip=1 for many small images. The response's 10 newest records confirm arrival, but a catalogue larger than 10 needs spot checks or a split batch, since one timeout covers the whole request with no per-file granularity.
  3. send_key + mouse_reset_pos WIN+h (x2) then /mouse/reset, normalises state and clears the stuck-click trap.
  4. click /mouse/click, opens Pinterest and starts a Pin: icon, plus, Pin, image tile, Next; no label-based fallback exists without OCR.
  5. send_key /key/sendkey?key=... for title and URL, types the title and destination link directly, since both qualify as ASCII and need no Shortcut round trip, the real efficiency of this playbook.
  6. shortcut#10 + send_key /shortcut/clipboard/set then WIN+v, delivers a Unicode description; use the documented sleep parameter rather than a blind delay, and prove the round trip with clipboard/get.
  7. click + mouse_wheel /mouse/click plus /mouse/wheel?direction=down&len=1-127, picks the board and sets publish-at-a-later-date; whether an iOS native picker wheel honors HID scroll is unverified, with a down-move-up drag as the fallback if it does not.
  8. click + get_device_screenshot /mouse/click then /pic/screenshot?binary=true[&rect=[l,t,r,b]], creates the pin and verifies by mean absolute pixel difference, cropped to the composer chrome if the page animates.
  9. click + mouse_wheel /mouse/click, /mouse/wheel?direction=down, saves from the feed, three taps; this cannot be comma-id mirrored even though the endpoint accepts a list, since each phone's feed shows different pins at the same coordinate.
  10. shortcut#3 /shortcut/album/del or /shortcut/album/clear, optional album cleanup after the run; /shortcut/album/clear is XP-only and deletes every item in the named album with no undo.

Needs

  • iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-edited and bound to an AssistiveTouch key on every phone, for both album upload and clipboard set.
  • Full Keyboard Access on, AssistiveTouch on with max tracking sensitivity, max tracking speed, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock.
  • Board bound (vid and pid set together), location_crc non-empty.
  • Pinterest logged in per phone on an account the operator owns, a business account if native publish-later is wanted.
  • Composer coordinates captured per phone and per app version, in 500x1080 mirror-pixel space.

Watch out

  • Without the Shortcut, only content already on the phone can be pinned and only ASCII text typed; no file can be delivered from the PC.
  • No OCR or image search on this rig, so every composer control is a captured coordinate that breaks on a Pinterest UI update.
  • Clipboard paste can lag the write on some handsets; use the documented sleep parameter rather than a blind delay.
  • The two text-entry paths have different verification stories: /key/sendkey has no read-back, while /shortcut/clipboard/set has a documented get-back-and-compare round trip; use the round trip for the description and accept the title and URL fields are otherwise unverifiable except by re-reading the screen.
  • Pushing many distinct catalogue images with distinct destination links at a mechanical per-phone cadence is the shape of activity spam classifiers key on for velocity and content-similarity; nothing in this chain should be tuned to vary timing or cadence to evade that.
  • Claims about what volume of distinct pins a platform "rewards" are policy framing, not a physics constraint the rig can rely on; the real limiting factor is Pinterest's own anti-spam thresholds, not anything measured here.

Trap Album clear has no undo and no per-caller gate

/shortcut/album/clear deletes an entire named album in one call, with no confirmation, and once the phone-side deletion permission is granted it stays armed for any future call from any LAN host, since the API has no authentication. Require an explicit human decision before wiring this to anything automatic, and treat it as a standing rack-level risk, not just a caveat for this one flow.

Scale

One album-upload call with zip=1 delivers the whole catalogue to every phone; from there each pin is roughly 16 taps plus two ASCII typing bursts and one clipboard round trip, realistically 45-60 s per pin per phone with taps dominated by pointer travel and the clipboard call bounded by its 15 s default outtime. Ten concurrent frame pollers measured 512 req/s total with no input/polling cross-talk, so throughput scales with handset count, not the kernel. Saves are about 3 taps and 5 s but strictly per-phone. The chain-only ceiling is 60-80 pins an hour per phone if the wheel-scroll step works, add 5-15 s per pin if it must fall back to an explicit drag; a defensible planning number once Pinterest's own spam-velocity limits are respected is 15-30 pins an hour per phone, not 60-80.

Snapchat: Memories Story post and per-phone streak keeper

PartialWith caveats

Snapchat exposes no share-sheet upload and no deep-linked composer, so the whole flow runs through the camera screen: push the day's image into the phone album, swipe up to Memories, pick the Camera Roll tile, Send To, then either My Story or a multi-select of friend rows. Streaks and Stories run on a 24-hour clock, so keeping them alive on accounts you own is otherwise a daily manual pass over every handset; every call in the chain exists on this kernel, but the blocking dependencies are the iMouse Shortcut and per-phone captured coordinates, since there is no label-based fallback without OCR.

How

  1. get_device_list + get_usb_list /device/get and /config/usb/get, reads imgw/imgh (500x1080), requires state != 0 with a live air_pid for video and board state 2 for control; video and control are independent channels, so a phone that mirrors perfectly can still ignore every tap.
  2. shortcut#7 /shortcut/album/upload, pushes the day's image from the PC in one call for all N phones; the response's newest album records are non-visual confirmation the file landed.
  3. send_key + mouse_reset_pos WIN+h (x2) then /mouse/reset, normalises every phone and clears the stuck-click trap; re-verify board state 2 per target each run, since a board can silently drop to state 1 between runs with no visible symptom until a tap fails.
  4. click / shortcut#13 /mouse/click or /shortcut/exec/url?url=snapchat://, launches Snapchat; whether the scheme resolves to the app is Snapchat and iOS behavior, not anything the API documents.
  5. swipe or mouse_down/move/up /mouse/swipe?direction=up&len=0-1&brake=1, opens Memories from the camera screen; XP's len is a percentage of the axis, not pixels, so a roughly 300 px stroke on a 1080 px axis is len around 0.28. Test both the swipe endpoint and a longer explicit drag before committing, with an icon-tap fallback if the drawer never opens.
  6. click /mouse/click, taps the Camera Roll tab, the newest tile, then Send To; positions are captured coordinates with no layout-independent alternative on this rig.
  7. click /mouse/click, taps My Story then the send arrow for a Story post; this can fan out to phones with matching imgw/imgh and matching app state, which a scrollable Send To list will not have.
  8. click + send_key / shortcut#10 /mouse/click plus /key/sendkey?key=... or clipboard/set + WIN+v, selects friends on the Send To screen for the streak keeper; ASCII names go through /key/sendkey, non-ASCII names need the clipboard route, since there is no send_text on XP.
  9. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<single id>&binary=true[&rect=[l,t,r,b]], verifies the send landed by mean absolute pixel difference; single-id only, one poller per phone.
  10. mouse_reset_pos / key_release_all / restart_usb /mouse/reset, /key/upall, /device/usb/restart?id=VID|PID, recovers a step that did not land; the WebSocket error_push callback is the only asynchronous signal that an input call failed at the board.

Needs

  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in; with only IMService.exe up, both phones read state 0 and the board list is empty.
  • iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-edited and bound to an AssistiveTouch key on every phone, for album upload and clipboard set.
  • Shortcuts > Advanced: Allow Running Scripts, Allow Sharing Large Amounts of Data.
  • AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, max tracking speed, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock; none queryable over the API.
  • Board bound to the phone, location_crc non-empty.
  • Snapchat installed and logged in per phone on an account the operator owns; coordinates captured for Memories, the newest tile, Send To, My Story and the send arrow; friend-row coordinates or ASCII-only friend names for search.

Watch out

  • Every function name written in Phonefarm style fails on this kernel: a bare {"fun":"click"} to 9911 returns HTTP 500, and 9912 is closed. Use the XP paths shown here.
  • No OCR and no image search on this rig; every tap is a captured coordinate that breaks when Snapchat moves its UI, and the streak step cannot resolve a friend by name from the screen.
  • Coordinates are mirror pixels (500x1080), not iOS logical points (414x896); screenshot-derived coordinates are already in the right space.
  • The Shortcut round trip is itself unverified on this rig; prove it first with /api/shortcut/device/ip before relying on it, a code 30 timeout means the AssistiveTouch hotkey never fired.
  • The Camera Roll "newest tile" coordinate is only stable if every phone's roll has exactly one new item since the last run; a phone that missed a prior push shifts its newest tile, so every step after image pick, not only friend selection, must run per-phone.
  • Camera viewfinder screens produce a hot whole-frame diff by nature, since it is a live preview; a rect crop for verification needs to be confirmed empirically per app version, since chrome elements like a send checkmark can themselves animate and register as noise.
  • A daily streak-keeping loop is a recurring, scheduled, low-variance automated action against a social app, exactly the shape of activity abuse detection is built to catch over time, independent of whether any single run's chain is technically correct; nothing here should be tuned to vary timing or behavior to evade that.

Trap Opening Memories may need a faster hand than the board has

Snapchat's camera-screen navigation drawer is commonly a gesture-recognizer paging control, gated on distance and velocity, unlike a position-tracked picker wheel. A roughly 300 px stroke at the board's fixed 0.6 ms/px walk is only about 180 ms of travel, and the open-or-not decision may need a faster hand than the board's HID walking speed can deliver, since that speed is fixed by firmware and not adjustable per gesture. Test the swipe endpoint and a longer explicit drag before committing to either, and keep an icon-tap fallback route to Memories.

Scale

The album push is one request for all N phones; everything after it is per-phone. A Story is roughly 8-10 taps and the streak keeper adds about 3 taps per friend, dominated by pointer travel at roughly 0.6 ms per pixel: budget 20-40 s per phone for the Story, more for a multi-friend send. Because friend-row order differs per account and cannot be comma-id mirrored, the streak keeper is inherently one script per account per day, not a batchable macro; the correct throughput unit is friends kept per run per phone, likely tens per phone per day, rather than a sustained hourly rate. Treating it as a high-frequency loop would itself be the kind of activity pattern that risks detection, so the physics-correct answer here is also the risk-correct one.

Commerce and seller-app forms

Shopify and TikTok Shop seller apps: album-fed listing forms and tap-through fulfilment

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Seller apps are plain forms driven blind by coordinates: product photos land in the phone album via one /shortcut/album/upload call, title and price go in as ASCII with /key/sendkey, the Unicode description arrives by clipboard plus a paste, and Save is a tap. Fulfilment is a fixed tap path from Orders through to a typed tracking number. A rack can keep several owned seller accounts' catalogues current from one content folder on the PC, for stores where only the phone app is available to the operator. Nothing in the chain needs the OCR or image-search plug-ins, which is exactly why it survives on this rig, and exactly why nothing in it can read a field back to confirm what landed there.

How

  1. send_key /key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — normalize every target phone to home page one; hardware keys still fire even when taps are silently dead, so this alone proves nothing about the tap path.
  2. mouse_reset_pos /mouse/reset?id=<ids> — clear the silent stuck-click state (measured: 0.09 mean pixel diff on a click vs. 141.96 after reset) before any tap-critical run.
  3. shortcut#7 /shortcut/album/upload (id list, files array of PC paths, album_name, zip, outtime ms) — push SKU photos into the phone album in one call across the whole id list; the response's newest album records confirm the file arrived before the picker taps begin.
  4. click /mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=<px>&y=<py>&button=1 — walk Products > + > Add images > Photo Library > newest tiles > Add, then Save/Submit and the Active toggle; coordinates are mirror pixels (500x1080 here), never iOS points.
  5. send_key key= /key/sendkey?id=<id>&key=<ascii text> — type title, price and later the tracking number; ASCII only, no Unicode.
  6. shortcut#10 + send_key fn_key /shortcut/clipboard/set then /key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+v — paste the Unicode/emoji description, since send_key cannot carry it.
  7. mouse_wheel /mouse/wheel?id=<ids>&direction=down&len=30&number=1 — scroll the category picker or a long form; expect this to fail, since an iOS picker is normally a drag-driven control, and keep a swipe or a real down/move/up drag as the actual default.
  8. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true — crop-diff each field's box right after typing it, before moving to the next field, not just the whole form after Save.

Needs

  • Seller apps installed and signed in on each phone with product-edit rights, on accounts the operator owns; this flow logs into nothing and creates no accounts.
  • iMouse Shortcut installed per phone, kernel IP edited in, run once with every permission allowed, bound to an AssistiveTouch custom key; album/upload and clipboard/set both travel that path and time out with code 30 if the binding never fires.
  • Shortcuts > Advanced: Allow Running Scripts and Allow Sharing Large Amounts of Data.
  • Board bound and physically attached (state 2), phone mirroring live with an air_pid.
  • Full Keyboard Access, AssistiveTouch, max tracking speed, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock — none of it visible over the API.
  • A per-app-version coordinate set captured per phone, fields tapped top-down so the keyboard never covers the next target.
  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in; with only IMService.exe up, phones showed state 0 and an empty board list.

Watch out

  • The Shortcut dependency was never probed live on this rig; a guessed /shortcut/get 404 is not evidence either way. Prove it first with /shortcut/device/ip?id=<id>&state=0 and expect data.text to equal the device's own IP.
  • Tapping is blind: there is no way to assert "the price field now reads 49.90," only that the frame changed, and a value typed into the wrong field because the keyboard covered it will pass a naive whole-frame diff.
  • If the Shortcut binding is absent, album/upload and clipboard/set fail with code 30, killing photos and any Unicode description, while the ASCII-only steps (title, price, tracking number, Save) still fire — a partial failure that produces a live listing with no photos and no description unless the upload response is checked first.
  • Mirroring one tap to several phones only holds when every listed phone shares app version, layout and imgw/imgh; typed content is always one call per phone.
  • No character-set limit is documented for the clipboard route; confirm with a set/get round trip per phone before trusting emoji or non-Latin descriptions.
  • Typing speed and inter-key delay for send_key are undocumented in either edition; chunk long strings and prefer the clipboard set/get round trip over trusting send_key for anything past short values.
  • The Photo Library multi-select step assumes a fixed tile position after upload; if the album defaults to single-select or re-sorts by capture time instead of import time, a blind coordinate can attach the wrong image to the wrong listing — a materially worse failure than a blank field.
  • Running many SKUs unattended with no field-level verification risks a batch of live, mispriced or mis-titled listings before a human notices; spot-check a sample rather than trusting a whole-form diff.

Scale

One listing is roughly 25 taps plus three or four typed strings, 60-90 seconds per phone, dominated by app latency and pointer-walk time (~0.6 ms/px) rather than the API. Fulfilment is about six taps and a tracking number, ~15 seconds. The album upload fans out to every phone in one request regardless of count; verification does not fan out, one screenshot per phone at 2 ms per raw BMP frame, gated by each phone's AirPlay source rate (measured ~29 new frames/s on one XR, ~4.5 on its twin — budget 220 ms or more per fresh frame on the slow one). That works out to roughly 40-60 listings/hour/phone if every blind tap lands correctly; discount for whatever spot-check rate is needed to catch a mis-tap, since nothing here verifies field content.

Messaging and community broadcast

Telegram: near-coordinate-free channel broadcast by deep link, clipboard paste and ENTER

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Telegram is the platform where this rack comes closest to layout-independent posting: a tg://resolve deep link opens the exact chat, the clipboard carries the message (emoji and CJK included), and paste plus ENTER sends it. All four calls in the chain accept a comma-separated id list, so a broadcast to N phones is four requests. One caveat survives scrutiny that an early draft missed: nothing guarantees the composer is focused after a deep link, so one /mouse/click on the input bar stays in the chain — exactly one coordinate per phone rather than a dozen, not zero.

How

  1. send_key /key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — normalize to the home screen; requires Full Keyboard Access ON.
  2. mouse_reset_pos /mouse/reset?id=<ids> — clear the stuck-click state; cheap insurance since the one remaining tap is the flow's single point of failure.
  3. shortcut#13 /shortcut/exec/url?id=<ids>&url=tg://resolve?domain=<channel> — open the exact channel on every phone at once; both vendor doc examples are bare web domains, so a custom scheme resolving is an inference to probe once per app build, not a guarantee.
  4. click /mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=<x>&y=<y>&button=1 — focus the message input; the input bar sits at a fixed y near the bottom of the mirror frame, so this one coordinate mirrors safely across same-geometry phones.
  5. shortcut#10 /shortcut/clipboard/set (id list, text, sleep seconds, outtime ms) — load the message onto every clipboard; the documented XP route for non-ASCII text, since XP has no send_text and no completion callback.
  6. send_key fn_key=WIN+v then fn_key=ENTER /key/sendkey — paste and send; whether Telegram iOS treats ENTER as send or as a newline is app behavior outside any document here, verify once and keep a send-button tap as fallback.
  7. shortcut#7 /shortcut/album/upload then click — push a media file to the album, then paperclip > newest tile > send; the upload response's newest album records are the only step in this flow the kernel can actually confirm server-side.
  8. click time=700 /mouse/click?id=<id>&x=<x>&y=<y>&time=700 — forward an existing message via long press, Forward, select, send; the message's y depends on scroll state, which differs per phone, so this branch is per-phone coordinate work.
  9. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true&rect=[0,820,500,1080] — crop the bottom bubble region and threshold a mean absolute pixel difference (idle floor 0.02-0.03, real change 20-160); never MD5.

Needs

  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in, reachable at 127.0.0.1:9911.
  • Board bound at state 2 per phone, non-empty location_crc, Full Keyboard Access ON.
  • iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-edited and bound to an AssistiveTouch custom key on each phone — never exercised on this rig.
  • Telegram installed, logged in, with posting rights on the target channel.
  • A one-time probe per app build that tg:// resolves through the Shortcut's Open URLs action, and that hardware ENTER sends rather than inserting a newline.
  • The input-bar coordinate captured once in mirror-pixel space; phones with differing imgw/imgh excluded from the mirrored id list.

Watch out

  • No /shortcut/* endpoint has ever been called on this rig; the whole flow rests on a manual Shortcut install and AssistiveTouch binding. Probe with /shortcut/device/ip?state=0 first — code 0 with the right LAN IP proves install, binding and return path in one call.
  • Custom URL schemes are outside what the vendor documents for exec/url; if the scheme isn't handled, the Shortcut may hand it to Safari instead, which shows nothing useful and leaves the subsequent paste and ENTER landing somewhere unintended, possibly the Shortcuts app or the home screen. Capture a screenshot after the exec/url call itself, not just the shortcut's return code — a success code only proves the Shortcut ran, not that the URL resolved to Telegram.
  • No OCR or image-search plug-in (code 28), so nothing in the chat can be located on screen; screenshot diffing on raw BMP frames is the only verification channel, one request per phone.
  • The clipboard is global phone state: a mirrored set overwrites whatever was there, and distinct per-phone texts need one call per phone, which removes the constant-cost property.
  • Whether ENTER sends or inserts a newline is Telegram-iOS-version behavior that can change with any app update, with no signal from any endpoint here; re-probe after every Telegram update, not once per "build."
  • The claimed "5-10 s end to end largely independent of N" figure only holds if the composer-focus click is issued as one mirrored call across the whole id list, not one call per phone — say so explicitly when building the flow.

Scale

Identical text to N phones is four requests plus one mirrored click, roughly 5-10 seconds end to end regardless of N, since the board drives every listed id in parallel. Distinct texts or distinct chats collapse this to one clipboard call and one exec/url per phone, ~2-4 seconds each — linear in N. That yields on the order of 350-700 identical broadcasts/hour with only per-broadcast crop-and-diff verification, or roughly 900-1800 distinct sends/hour aggregate across many phones run concurrently. Verification is the serial tail: 2 ms per raw BMP fetch, gated by AirPlay source rate to roughly 35 ms per new frame on the fast phone and 220 ms on the slow one.

Discord: channel deep-link posting, long-press reactions and moderation from a member account

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

The same four-call pattern as Telegram applies: a deep link opens the channel, clipboard plus paste fills the composer, ENTER sends. Reactions and moderation hang off a long press, which needs no dedicated API since /mouse/click carries a time parameter — a click with time=700 is a press-and-hold, and the sheet it raises holds the quick-reaction row alongside Delete Message and Pin Message. The technical chain is sound; the honest framing is that everything it does to a channel, a bot can do through Discord's own API with no phones involved.

How

  1. send_key /key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — normalize to home; hardware keys work even when taps are silently dead, so this alone is not proof of a live tap path.
  2. mouse_reset_pos /mouse/reset?id=<ids> — mandatory here rather than optional: this flow is tap-heavy (composer, long-press, sheet item, confirm), and a stuck phone follows every move and hotkey while silently swallowing every tap.
  3. shortcut#13 /shortcut/exec/url?id=<ids>&url=https://discord.com/channels/<guild>/<channel> — open the target channel; the https universal link is the safer primary form over discord://, since a universal link degrades to the web app rather than to nothing if the app is missing, but this is still an inference outside the doc's bare-http examples.
  4. click /mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=<x>&y=<y>&button=1 — focus the message bar; button is numeric on XP, not the string form. Its y is stable near the bottom of the frame across same-geometry phones.
  5. shortcut#10 then send_key fn_key=WIN+v /shortcut/clipboard/set — load and paste the message; emoji is exactly why the clipboard route is required over ASCII-only send_key.
  6. send_key fn_key=ENTER /key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=ENTER — send; whether Discord iOS sends on hardware ENTER is undocumented app behavior, verify once and keep a send-button tap as fallback, treated as the primary path rather than a rarely-needed backup.
  7. click time=700 then click /mouse/click?id=<id>&x=<x>&y=<y>&time=700 — react to a message; re-send the deep link first so every phone is scrolled to the bottom and the newest message sits at a predictable y, which mitigates but does not guarantee the target.
  8. click time=700 then two more clicks — moderation: Delete Message / Pin Message from the same long-press sheet; irreversible, gate behind explicit human confirmation or route through Discord's own API where the target is addressed by id.
  9. shortcut#7 then click x3 /shortcut/album/upload — attach media; the response's newest album records confirm the file landed before the blind picker taps.
  10. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true&rect=[0,700,500,1000] — confirm the post appeared, mean absolute pixel diff on the crop, never MD5.

Needs

  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in; boards bound at state 2; non-empty location_crc per phone.
  • Full Keyboard Access, AssistiveTouch, max tracking speed, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock — none visible to the API.
  • iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-edited and bound to an AssistiveTouch custom key per phone — never exercised on this rig.
  • Discord installed and logged in per phone, a member of the target guild, with Manage Messages permission for the moderation branch.
  • One-time probes: channel link opens the app rather than Safari, hardware ENTER sends, and a 700-800 ms click registers as a long press on this Discord build.
  • Per-phone message-bar and sheet coordinates captured in mirror pixels.

Watch out

  • The entire /shortcut/* dependency (clipboard for the caption, exec/url for the deep link) is completely unverified on this rig; a 404 on a guessed /shortcut/get path is not evidence either way. Run /shortcut/device/ip?id=<id>&state=0 per phone first — if it fails, the flow degrades to ASCII-only typed text and manual app navigation with no deep link.
  • A 700 ms click registering as a long press is a vendor-documented parameter, not a fact confirmed against this Discord build; probe once per app/iOS version, since press-duration thresholds vary by app.
  • The https link opening the app rather than Safari's web view is an assumption, not documented kernel behavior; if it degrades to Safari, every downstream coordinate targets a browser, not the app.
  • Reaction and moderation coordinates depend on scroll position and message height; with no OCR or image-search plug-in, nothing confirms what is under the pointer before the tap. A reply-preview banner, mention autocomplete strip, or sticker tray above the composer shifts the message-bar y in a way the API cannot detect — re-verify it is truly static for the accounts and servers actually used.
  • Re-issue /mouse/reset before each tap-critical phase (composer focus, long-press, sheet tap, confirm), not only once at the top — the stuck-click state was observed to appear mid-session, and a hardware key press still works while stuck, giving no signal that a later tap silently failed.
  • Because 9911 has no authentication, any other LAN host can fire the same moderation, reaction or post calls against these logged-in accounts concurrently with your automation, racing on the same coordinates this flow assumes are stable.
  • Delete and Pin reach a variable-height sheet by blind tap and are irreversible; keep human confirmation on every destructive tap, or route moderation through Discord's own API where the target is addressed by message id.

Scale

A text post to N phones with identical content is four comma-id requests plus one mirrored composer click, roughly 5-8 seconds regardless of N. Distinct channels or text make it linear, one exec/url and one clipboard/set per phone at 2-4 seconds each. Reactions and moderation are inherently per-phone, 2-3 taps plus the 700 ms hold and pointer-walk time (~0.6 ms/px), budget 3-5 seconds per phone per action. That is a theoretical hardware ceiling of roughly 200-400 posts/hour/phone or 700-1000 reaction/moderation actions/hour/phone; it is irrelevant in practice, since Discord's own anti-automation heuristics will trigger account action long before hardware limits bind. Treat this as a manual, occasional capability rather than a throughput target.

Feature-gap workarounds on the composer surface

X: media post and poll in the app, bookmarks, and scheduling through the mobile web composer

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

The X iOS app posts text, media and polls but exposes no schedule control; x.com in mobile Safari does. The rack opens the web composer, pastes text through the Shortcut clipboard, attaches media pushed earlier by /shortcut/album/upload, and drives the web schedule picker — giving scheduled posts from real handsets with no new API capability, only a change of surface. Scheduling is the capability operators most often assume is unavailable on mobile, and the fix costs nothing beyond pointing the same primitives at Safari instead of the app.

How

  1. get_device_list + get_usb_list /device/get and /config/usb/get — take imgw/imgh per phone as the tap space (500x1080 here); require state != 0 with a live air_pid and board state 2, since a phone can mirror perfectly and ignore every tap.
  2. shortcut#7 /shortcut/album/upload — push the promo image into the album for every phone in one request; the newest album records confirm arrival before the composer opens Photos.
  3. send_key fn_key=WIN+h (x2) then mouse_reset_pos /key/sendkey then /mouse/reset?id=<ids> — normalize and clear the stuck-click state.
  4. shortcut#13 /shortcut/exec/url?id=<ids>&url=https://x.com/compose/post — open the web composer, the surface with the schedule control. A universal link to x.com may instead be claimed by the installed app, which has no schedule control; that is iOS link routing, not an API fault, and must be resolved on the handset. Confirm with a screenshot (App Store back button vs. Safari chrome) before trusting the schedule steps ran in a browser.
  5. shortcut#10 + send_key fn_key=WIN+v /shortcut/clipboard/set — put the post text in place; send_key key= is ASCII-only, so emoji and non-Latin text must take the clipboard route, and there is no completion callback to confirm delivery.
  6. click + send_key /mouse/click + /key/sendkey?key=Yes|No — attach media and build the poll: media icon > Photo Library > newest tile > Choose; poll icon > option fields; all positional, since OCR is unavailable.
  7. click + mouse_wheel /mouse/click + /mouse/wheel?id=<id>&direction=up|down&len=1-127&number=n — set the schedule; treat a wheel attempt as opportunistic and a real down/move/up drag as the primary path, since a picker wheel is normally drag-driven, not scroll-driven, and picker drags travel well under 1080 px so the pointer-walk cost is trivial regardless.
  8. click /mouse/click — bookmark a post: open it, tap share, tap Bookmark. Per-phone even under a mirrored id, since two timelines don't show the same post at the same coordinate.
  9. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<single id>&binary=true[&rect=[l,t,r,b]] — verify each post or schedule landed with a cropped mean-absolute-pixel-diff against an idle control; no step can be confirmed by the kernel as "posted" vs. "scheduled" vs. "drafted," only as a pixel change in the region that actually differs between those outcomes.
  10. mouse_reset_pos / key_release_all /mouse/reset, /key/upall — recovery; watch the WS error_push callback for hardware-level failures.

Needs

  • XP kernel on 9911 with IMConsole.exe running and logged in.
  • Logged in to x.com in Safari on each phone (persistent session) for the web route; the app logged in for immediate posts, on accounts the operator owns.
  • iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-edited, run once with all permissions allowed, bound to an AssistiveTouch custom key.
  • Full Keyboard Access ON, AssistiveTouch at max sensitivity, max tracking speed, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock.
  • Board bound with a non-empty location_crc.
  • Web composer coordinates captured in mirror-pixel space with Safari zoom left at default.

Watch out

  • Prove the Shortcut round trip first with /shortcut/device/ip?id=<id>&state=0; code 0 with the device's own IP means installed and reachable, code 30 after roughly 15 s means the hotkey never launched it.
  • If the X app claims the universal link — normal iOS behavior when the app is installed — /shortcut/exec/url never reaches Safari, and the whole schedule-from-mobile-web premise collapses silently with a 200 status and no error signal from the kernel.
  • No OCR or image search on this rig, so every composer control is a captured coordinate; a Safari zoom change or layout update invalidates the capture silently. Coordinates are mirror pixels, not logical points.
  • Whether the web date/time pickers honor HID wheel events is unverified; budget the drag as the primary mechanism, not a rarely-needed fallback — the earlier full-height-swipe timing cost from the hardware measurements does not apply to a picker drag, which travels far less distance.
  • XP gives no completion callback for text delivery, so confirmation is a clipboard read-back plus a frame diff, not an event.
  • AssistiveTouch and Full Keyboard Access being ON is invisible to the API; a phone with either silently OFF accepts /mouse/move but ignores taps or paste, indistinguishable from the stuck-click state without a post-reset verification tap.
  • The API has no authentication on the LAN; firewall 9911 and 17000.

Scale

An immediate in-app post is roughly 8 taps (~20 s/phone); a scheduled web post is roughly 14 taps plus the picker steps (~50 s), with pointer travel dominant at ~0.6 ms/px (a 400 px move is 250 ms, a full-height traverse ~592 ms). The media push fans out to every phone in one request; composer work is per-phone but phones run fully independently (two concurrent frame pollers measured 83 and 85 req/s at p50 3 ms, ten pollers 512 req/s total). Verification is capped by AirPlay source rate — roughly 29 new frames/s on one XR versus 4.5 on its twin, so budget 220 ms or more per fresh frame on the slow handset. Mechanically this allows on the order of 50-70 scheduled posts/hour/phone run back to back, but a rate-limit or challenge interstitial on the real account is the actual ceiling, set by the platform, not the rig — treat the mechanical number as a limit, not a target.

LinkedIn: PDF carousel pushed into Files, composed and scheduled by blind coordinates

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

A PDF document carousel is the one LinkedIn format that normally cannot be produced on a phone, because the file has to reach the device first. /shortcut/file/upload puts the PDF into a fixed Files-app folder on every bound phone in one comma-id call; everything after that is /mouse/click at mirror-pixel coordinates through Add a document, Choose from Files, the upload folder and the composer, ending in Post or LinkedIn's own clock-icon scheduler. Getting a multi-page PDF onto twenty phones is the actual bottleneck for carousel posting, and that file transfer is the one part genuinely enabled by this rack rather than by a person holding a phone.

How

  1. shortcut id=8 /shortcut/file/upload?id=<ids>&path=/iMouse/&files=[...]&zip=0&outtime=120000 — push the PDF into a fixed Files folder on every target phone at once; iOS 15+ only, verified in the shortcuts documentation.
  2. send_key fn_key=WIN+h (x2) /key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+h — normalize every phone to home page one; requires Full Keyboard Access ON.
  3. mouse_reset_pos /mouse/reset?id=<ids> — clear the stuck-click state before any tap-critical sequence.
  4. click /mouse/click?id=<id>&x=<x>&y=<y>&button=1 — open LinkedIn, tap Post, tap the text area; the two XRs have different home screens and wallpapers, so this app-icon tap is per-phone even though later in-app coordinates can be mirrored.
  5. shortcut id=10 then send_key fn_key=WIN+v /shortcut/clipboard/set — put the post copy, emoji included, on the clipboard and paste it; the only documented Unicode path, since send_key key= is English-only.
  6. click (x5-7) /mouse/click?id=<id>&x=<x>&y=<y> — attach the document through Add a document > Choose from Files > Browse > On My iPhone > the upload folder > the PDF; purely coordinate-driven since the kernel cannot locate the file row for you. Keep the upload folder holding exactly one file so the row's y is deterministic, and re-verify the picker screenshot rather than trusting a hardcoded y after any prior run.
  7. send_key key= /key/sendkey?id=<ids>&key=<ascii title> then click Done — type the ASCII document title; use the clipboard route instead for a CJK or emoji title.
  8. mouse_wheel, or down/move/up drag /mouse/wheel?id=<ids>&direction=up&len=30&number=1 — schedule: tap the clock icon, set date and time, Next; treat the wheel as a cheap first attempt and the drag as the primary mechanism, since nothing in the measured facts supports a picker wheel responding to HID scroll in either direction.
  9. click /mouse/click?id=<id>&x=<x>&y=<y> — publish or leave it scheduled; irreversible, gate behind explicit human confirmation since no step above can be visually confirmed by the kernel.
  10. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<single id>&binary=true[&rect=[l,t,r,b]] — verify each stage by mean-absolute-pixel-diff frame comparison; one request per phone, ten concurrent pollers measured 512 req/s.
  11. shortcut id=6 /shortcut/file/del?id=<ids>&path=/iMouse/&list=[{name,ext}] — delete the uploaded PDF afterward so the picker row stays deterministic for the next run; needs the Shortcuts "allow deleting without confirmation" permission or the call hangs on an unanswered prompt.
  12. shortcut id=13 then click + clipboard + WIN+v + click Send /shortcut/exec/url?url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/<slug> — connection request with a note; one exec/url mirrored to N phones opens the same profile on all of them, so distinct targets need one call per phone.

Needs

  • XP kernel on 127.0.0.1:9911 (path-style API); Phonefarm function names return HTTP 500 on this rig, 9912 closed.
  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in — with only IMService.exe up, both phones showed state 0 and an empty board list.
  • Per phone: board bound at state 2, location_crc non-empty, or every mouse call returns an error code.
  • Per-phone iOS settings invisible to the API: AssistiveTouch at max sensitivity, Full Keyboard Access ON, max tracking speed, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock.
  • iMouse Shortcut v1.3+ installed, kernel IP edited in, run once with every permission allowed, bound via Send Binding Key; Shortcuts > Advanced allowing scripts, large-data sharing and deletion without confirmation — not verified present on this rig.
  • iOS 15+ for all /shortcut/file/* calls (the XRs qualify at 18.7.10).
  • The /iMouse/ folder created once in Files on each phone.
  • LinkedIn logged in on each phone; composer and Files-picker coordinates captured per phone in mirror pixels.

Watch out

  • No /shortcut/* call has actually been exercised on this rig; the 10 Sep probe only touched device, USB, group, OCR and mouse/key paths. Prove the Shortcut round trip first with /shortcut/device/ip?id=<id>&state=0.
  • No OCR and no image-search plug-in (code 28); nothing in the composer or the Files picker can be located by the kernel, only asserted and checked with a client-side pixel diff.
  • The two XRs have entirely different home screens, so only in-app coordinates mirror, and only between phones whose imgw/imgh match.
  • Verification is per-phone and one at a time, and one XR delivers only ~4.5 new frames/s — budget 220 ms or more per expected frame there rather than assuming 30 fps.
  • The date/time picker is the one unverified mechanism in both directions, not merely unverified for this app version; plan the drag fallback as the primary path.
  • A substituted USB cable leaves the board at state 1 with a phone plugged in and the whole chain silently dead.
  • The 120000 ms upload outtime is fine for a single file, but a 20 MB carousel PDF at the rig's worst-case ~5 Mbps Wi-Fi mode takes roughly 32 seconds for the transfer alone; margin shrinks if the id list carries many phones sharing the same access point, since the upload call has no documented per-phone parallelism guarantee the way mouse and key calls do.
  • A previous run leaving the Files folder in a different view state (list vs. grid, a stale cached row from before a delete) shifts the picker row's y even with the folder empty; re-verify the screenshot, don't just trust an empty folder.
  • If this flow and the Telegram flow share phones in the same session, the phone's clipboard is single-slot shared state — serialize clipboard-dependent steps across use cases, not just within one.
  • Stay inside LinkedIn's own published invite and posting limits and halt on the first restriction screen; keep a human in the loop on the final Post or Send tap, since a blind tap on a shifted layout can publish or send the wrong thing irreversibly.

Scale

The file upload is O(1) in phone count, one call with a comma-id list, outtime raised to ~120 s for a multi-MB PDF. Everything else is roughly 18-22 taps plus one clipboard round trip, dominated by pointer-walk at ~0.6 ms/px (a 1000 px traverse measured 592 ms); a move mirrored to N phones costs the same as one, so a mirrored carousel post is ~45-70 seconds regardless of N when every phone shares layout. Screenshot verification is the only per-phone serial cost, 2 ms per raw BMP frame at 84 req/s per phone, gated by AirPlay source rate (29 fps vs. 4.5 fps between the two XRs). Connection requests run ~10-15 seconds each and cannot be mirrored when the target profile differs per phone. That supports on the order of 40-60 mirrored carousel-post cycles/hour across an arbitrary phone count, bounded by the composer walk rather than by phone count — but LinkedIn's own connection-request and posting caps bind well before the rig does for the connection-request branch specifically.

Cross-platform posting patterns

Share-sheet-first cross-platform posting from Photos

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Push one clip to every phone with a single upload call, then start every post from the same place: Photos, newest item, Share, pick the target app in the share sheet. The first six taps are identical for every platform and every phone, so only the tail (caption, Post) is app-specific, which roughly halves the number of coordinate sets to maintain. A single entry path is what makes a many-platform playbook maintainable on a rack of phones; on iOS the share sheet is that path, removing the need to learn each app's own composer navigation.

How

  1. shortcut#7 /shortcut/album/upload?id=<all ids>&files=[...]&zip=0&outtime=180000 — push the clip to every phone in one call; zip=0 is right for a single large file, and the response's newest album records confirm it actually arrived.
  2. send_key fn_key=WIN+h (x2) then mouse_reset_pos /key/sendkey then /mouse/reset?id=<all> — normalize every phone to home page one and clear the stuck-click state.
  3. click /mouse/click?id=<same-layout group>&x=<px>&y=<py>&button=1 — Photos icon, Recents, newest tile, Share button; the newest-tile corner depends on the phone's own Photos sort order and must be captured per phone, standardized once per phone before it can be trusted at all.
  4. mouse_wheel /mouse/wheel?id=<ids>&direction=right&len=60&number=1 — scroll the share sheet's app row; expect this to fail, since the row is a touch-driven UIScrollView with no general scroll-wheel support, and build the horizontal swipe or drag as the default rather than a contingency.
  5. click /mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=<px>&y=<py> — tap the target app's icon; its composer opens with the video already attached. Making icon order identical across phones is a one-time manual per-phone edit to share-sheet Favourites, with no API equivalent, and it is not permanently stable — iOS can reshuffle these suggestions after an OS update, so re-verify periodically rather than treating the one-time edit as durable.
  6. shortcut#10 then send_key fn_key=WIN+v /shortcut/clipboard/set — put the caption on the clipboard and paste it into the composer; the only documented Unicode text route on this edition.
  7. click /mouse/click?id=<id>&x=<px>&y=<py> — tap Post/Share; the irreversible step, and share-sheet composers often use different coordinates from the in-app composer, so keep the two sets separate.
  8. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true — verify per phone that the post went out, mean-absolute-pixel-diff, never MD5.
  9. shortcut#3 /shortcut/album/del?id=<ids>&list=[{album_name,name,ext}]&outtime=30000 — delete the clip from the album afterward so the next run's newest-tile coordinate stays valid; confirm the deleted filename matches exactly what the upload step returned before issuing this, the one destructive call in the chain, and never reach for the album-wide clear.

Needs

  • All target apps installed and signed in on each phone, on accounts the operator owns.
  • iMouse Shortcut installed per phone, kernel IP edited in, bound to an AssistiveTouch custom key; Shortcuts > Advanced must allow running scripts, sharing large data, and deleting without confirmation, since the last two are what album deletion needs.
  • Share-sheet Favourites edited once per phone so app icons sit in the same order — a manual, one-time human step with no API equivalent.
  • Board bound and attached, phone mirroring live with an air_pid.
  • Full Keyboard Access, AssistiveTouch at max sensitivity, max tracking speed, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock.
  • Two coordinate sets per platform where the share-sheet extension opens a reduced composer that differs from the in-app one.
  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in.

Watch out

  • The three Shortcut-backed steps (upload, clipboard, delete) were never probed on this rig; prove the round trip per phone with /shortcut/device/ip?id=<id>&state=0 before assuming any of this runs.
  • Newest-tile determinism depends on the phone's Photos sort-order setting, a per-phone toggle invisible to the API; standardize it once per phone as a precondition, not just something the deletion step manages after the fact.
  • Deleting the clip afterward only keeps the next run's coordinate valid under strictly serial upload-post-delete per phone; two pieces of content in flight for the same phone (a retry, or two campaigns queued back to back) makes newest tile ambiguous again even with deletion in place — serialize per phone.
  • A single wrong coordinate anywhere in this long chain compounds: a wrong share-sheet tap can open the wrong app's composer, receive the pasted caption, and land a subsequent tap on that wrong app's own Post control, publishing to an unintended surface with nothing here to detect it.
  • Publishing is irreversible and unverifiable beyond a pixel diff on this rig, since there is no OCR to read a success or error toast; budget a human review pass.
  • The comma id list mirrors taps but not state — phones with a different app version, share-sheet order or imgw/imgh must be excluded from the fan-out group.

Scale

The upload is one request for the whole rack (a 30 MB clip takes tens of seconds, give outtime ~180000 ms). After that, each platform is roughly 10-14 taps, so six platforms from one clip is under six minutes per phone, and the taps mirror across identical phones at no extra wall time since the board walks all listed phones in parallel. Captions and verification do not fan out, since both the clipboard read-back and the screenshot call are single-id. Screenshot verification is cheap (2 ms raw BMP, 84 req/s per phone, ten concurrent pollers measured 512 req/s total) but is gated by AirPlay source rate, roughly 29 new frames/s on one XR and 4.5 on its twin — the slower phone, not the API, sets the real pace of a multi-platform run.

Composers prefilled through URL schemes: one exec/url call instead of clipboard plus paste

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Where a platform accepts the message or caption as a URL parameter, /shortcut/exec/url alone delivers full Unicode straight into the composer with no keyboard and no clipboard, and it fans out to the whole rack in one comma-id request. Where a platform ignores the parameter, the fallback is the ordinary clipboard route. The valuable artifact is the matrix itself — which apps honor a prefill on which version — and that matrix is an external, app-version-dependent fact the vendor documentation cannot confirm and that has to be measured on this rack, then re-measured after every app update.

How

  1. Host-side only, no call — build the URL on the PC with UTF-8 percent-encoding; send it as POST JSON to /api rather than a GET query string, since XP accepts POST application/json and encoding is easy to mangle in a query string.
  2. send_key fn_key=WIN+h (x2) then mouse_reset_pos /key/sendkey then /mouse/reset?id=<ids> — normalize the phones and clear the stuck-click state.
  3. shortcut#13 /shortcut/exec/url?id=<ids>&url=<prefilled link>&outtime=15000 — open the prefilled URL on every target phone in one request; both vendor doc examples are bare web domains, so custom schemes or universal links honoring the parameter is unverified, the load-bearing assumption of the whole idea.
  4. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true&rect=[l,t,r,b] — confirm the composer is on screen before touching Send; with no OCR this can only prove the screen is not the home screen, not that the correct app or composer opened, nor that the injected text arrived complete and correctly encoded. A login wall, paywall or rate-limit interstitial produces the same pixel delta as a successful open.
  5. click / send_key fn_key=ENTER /mouse/click or /key/sendkey?fn_key=ENTER — send, one tap or ENTER where the app sends on Enter; the irreversible step.
  6. shortcut#10 then send_key fn_key=WIN+v /shortcut/clipboard/set — fallback for platforms that ignore the text parameter; the only documented Unicode route on this edition, verify per phone with a clipboard read-back.
  7. Measurement, not a call — record and re-verify the apps-that-honor-prefill matrix per app version; it is an external platform behavior, not documented or probeable from the API, and it changes with every app update.

Needs

  • iMouse Shortcut installed on each phone, kernel IP edited in, bound to an AssistiveTouch custom key — exec/url fires through that hotkey path and times out with code 30 if the binding doesn't fire.
  • Target apps installed and signed in on accounts the operator owns, with one manual test per app of whether the text parameter is honored on the current version, repeated after each app update.
  • Full Keyboard Access ON for ENTER and for the clipboard fallback's paste.
  • Board bound and attached, phone mirroring live, on the LAN so the Shortcut can reach the kernel.
  • Portrait lock, Auto-Lock Never, AssistiveTouch at max sensitivity.
  • A one-time probe of exec/url with a custom URL scheme and with a long URL, since neither is documented.
  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in.

Watch out

  • The apps-that-honor-prefill matrix is an external claim about third-party apps, not a vendor-documented fact; treat any specific list as a hypothesis to measure on this rack, not a finding, and schedule a re-probe rather than hard-coding it into a production flow.
  • Neither vendor doc's examples go beyond bare web domains; if only http(s) works, platforms whose prefill lives behind a custom scheme fall back to the web composer or the clipboard route. Probe this first, since it is the assumption everything else depends on.
  • exec/url fires through the same single hardware-key-to-AssistiveTouch-to-Shortcut trigger path as every other /shortcut/* call; that binding is a manual, console-only, per-phone setup step with no API, and a failure there (unanswered permission dialog, unedited kernel IP, wrong board bound) returns code 30 after the full outtime window, not a quick failure — budget worst case up to the default 15 s per phone per attempt, not an optimistic happy path.
  • No maximum URL length is documented; Safari handles several thousand characters but the Shortcut layer's own limit is unknown and should be found by bisection before a long caption is trusted.
  • A universal link may open Safari or the app depending on the phone's prior per-domain choice, a state the API cannot read, making resulting coordinates non-deterministic across a fan-out group.
  • The fan-out is only safe for identical messages; a per-recipient message is one call per phone.
  • Since exec/url and clipboard/set share the same single trigger channel, concurrent use from a different script against the same phone races on outtime and clipboard state — there is no isolation between two automations sharing a rig.
  • Treat any "Action Blocked" or rate-limit response as a hard stop per phone rather than a retry condition, and keep volumes within the platform's own published limits; the platform's anti-spam systems, not the kernel, set the real ceiling.

Scale

One exec/url call per distinct message fans out to every phone in the id list, plus one tap or ENTER — roughly 2-4 seconds per message end to end, with the shortcut round trip (hotkey, iOS Shortcut, kernel over Wi-Fi) dominating rather than the HTTP call itself, versus three round trips for the clipboard route. Verification does not fan out, 2 ms per raw BMP frame per phone, gated by AirPlay source rate to roughly 35 ms on the fast phone and 220 ms on the slow one. That is a kernel-only ceiling on the order of 900-1800 messages/hour/phone with no relationship to a sustainable real-world send rate: a binding failure costs up to the full 15 s outtime per attempt, and target-platform rate limiting and anti-spam detection will bind well below that ceiling for any real messaging app, a platform-policy question this rig's telemetry cannot answer.

Also worth knowing

Domain index: where else these primitives apply

Every card above is built on the same five moves: an album push (/shortcut/album/upload), a clipboard fan-out (/shortcut/clipboard/set plus WIN+v), a composer deep link (/mouse/click on a captured icon, or the unverified /shortcut/exec/url), a golden-frame diff (/pic/screenshot?binary=true, mean absolute pixel difference against an idle floor of 0.02-0.03), and group targeting (/device/group/get-dev, XP path style; the Phonefarm edition calls the same idea get_group_list and set_group, function-name style, and neither name works against this XP kernel). None of that changes when the app on screen is a job board instead of TikTok. The table below is a map, not fifteen new cards: it says which of the five primitives a domain family actually needs and names the one thing that stops the chain short of full automation there. Two mechanical facts apply to every row. First, this rig's own device records report group 未分组 (ungrouped) and a live call to /device/group/get returns an empty list, so "group targeting" below is a documented, callable primitive, not something already configured here; a real group has to be created with /device/group/set before /device/group/get-dev has anything to return. Second, with OCR reporting data.code 28 (plug-in not connected) and image search unverified, every "confirms" in the chain column means a pixel region changed, not that the rack read what it says.

Domain familyReused chainFeasibilityOne blocker that bites this family
Recruiting/HR, job boards /device/group/get-dev picks a QA cohort; /mouse/click opens the ATS or job app; /shortcut/clipboard/set pastes cover-letter or screening-answer text; /pic/screenshot diff confirms the apply step advanced. Needs ShortcutWith caveats No OCR to read multi-field application or screening forms, and identical text pasted from many device-bound accounts into one job board is the duplicate-application signature ATS anti-spam already screens for. Stays at one account per phone testing your own listing's apply funnel, not scaled applying.
Dating and marketplace trust-and-safety review /shortcut/album/upload stages a reported image on a review phone; /mouse/click opens the moderation queue; /pic/screenshot diff confirms an action registered; /device/group/get-dev routes report categories to separate phones once a real group exists. Needs ShortcutWith caveats No OCR to read the report reason or a chat transcript off screen, so a human still reads every screenshot before an action is taken. This is a queue router and evidence-capture aid, not an automated moderation decision-maker.
Gig and field-service operator apps /mouse/click or /shortcut/exec/url opens the driver or technician app; /pic/screenshot diff watches the job-offer screen for a state change (idle floor 0.02-0.03 vs. a real reaction 20-160); /device/group/get-dev fans a status toggle to a fleet-test group; /shortcut/clipboard/set sends a canned customer reply. Needs ShortcutWith caveats A pixel diff says the offer screen changed, not what job or pay it shows, since there is no OCR. Accepting or declining a live gig offer is a real dispatch commitment, so this stays at online/offline status checks and canned-reply QA on accounts you operate.
Real estate listing apps /shortcut/album/upload seeds listing photos; /mouse/click walks the listing composer; /shortcut/clipboard/set pastes the description; /pic/screenshot diff confirms the Published banner. Needs ShortcutWith caveats Same rule as the Facebook Marketplace card above: a published listing and any resulting lead are real. Fanning identical listings across many device-bound accounts is exactly what duplicate-listing detection is built to catch, so this stays to one account publishing per phone.
Travel and hospitality (OTA, airline, hotel apps) /mouse/click or /shortcut/exec/url opens the booking app; /pic/screenshot diff confirms a fare-search screen loaded; /device/group/get-dev, once populated, lets N phones poll N routes or dates in parallel. PartialWith caveats No OCR to read a fare or price number off the screen, only that the screen changed, so this is availability-presence monitoring and booking-flow UI QA, not fare scraping. The Prohibited-actions list also keeps this pipeline off any "Book" tap; that is a real purchase the operator has to make themselves.
Education (LMS and course apps) /mouse/click opens the LMS app; /shortcut/clipboard/set posts identical announcement or feedback text to an instructor or TA cohort; /pic/screenshot diff confirms the post landed; /device/group/get-dev separates a student-view group from an instructor-view group. Needs ShortcutWith caveats No OCR to read or grade free-text student submissions, so the reused mechanics cover posting and UI QA only. Auto-grading or scraping submitted work is out of reach on this rig.
Mobile gaming (regression testing on your own title) /mouse/click launches the build and drives an input sequence; /pic/screenshot diff checks whether a menu or dialog advanced; /device/group/get-dev replays the same sequence across identical devices. PartialWith caveats No OCR or image search to read a score, currency count or dialog text, only that pixels changed. That limits this to input-replay regression testing on a build you own, not reading or farming a live in-game economy.
Healthcare and telehealth apps /mouse/click or /shortcut/exec/url opens the portal app for a UI smoke test; /pic/screenshot diff confirms a screen transition; /device/group/get-dev repeats the check across every phone on the same build. PartialWith caveats Real content here is PHI, and the control API is plaintext and unauthenticated on the LAN, with no OCR to verify what is actually rendered. Stays to UI smoke-testing with synthetic test accounts and test data, never live patient data.
Finance and banking apps as targets, not as the account heartbeat /mouse/click opens the app for its own UI regression test; /pic/screenshot diff confirms a post-tap screen change; /device/group/get-dev runs the same smoke test across a device bank. PartialWith caveats The Prohibited-actions list bars this pipeline from executing any trade or transfer, and from entering financial credentials through it. Even short of that, there is no OCR to verify a balance or confirmation screen, so this narrows to pre-login launch and navigation checks on a test build.
Government and e-ID apps /mouse/click or /shortcut/exec/url opens the portal or wallet app; /pic/screenshot diff confirms a known screen rendered. PartialWith caveats e-ID and government apps sit behind device-bound biometric or hardware-backed key attestation the rack cannot see or replay: the API is a mouse-and-keyboard emulator plus a mirrored screen, with no camera, no biometric injection and no Bluetooth. This reduces to confirming an app opens and a known screen renders, nothing that touches the credential itself.
IoT/smart-home and wearable companion apps /mouse/click opens the companion app once a device is already paired by hand; /pic/screenshot diff confirms a control tap (a toggle, a scene) changed the phone-side UI. PartialWith caveats The rack has no Bluetooth radio and no BLE peripheral role. Pairing a phone to a smart-home hub or wearable is a system-level Bluetooth prompt, Settings or a first-run pairing sheet, that nothing in this API can originate or answer. Onboarding a new accessory is not possible through the rack; only driving an app whose accessory is already paired is.
Media and streaming (video/OTT apps) /mouse/click or /shortcut/exec/url launches the app and drives playback controls; /pic/screenshot diff confirms a play/pause state change. Needs ShortcutWith caveats No OCR to read a title, an episode name or an ad-countdown timer, so this confirms that something is playing, not which asset or whether an ad slot served. Inflating watch time or view counts across the fleet is an ad-fraud pattern this document will not detail as a technique; keep this to your own app build's playback-path smoke test.
Podcasts and music streaming apps Same playback pattern as media and streaming, plus /shortcut/clipboard/set to post a caption when sharing an episode or track from a single account. Needs ShortcutWith caveats Identical share, follow or like actions timed to the same millisecond across many device-bound accounts is stream-count or engagement manipulation, the reward-farming loop this document excludes. The legitimate remainder is single-account posting and playback QA, not fleet-wide engagement.
Internal enterprise apps (MDM-managed line-of-business tools) /shortcut/exec/url or /mouse/click opens the internal tool; /shortcut/clipboard/set delivers identical or per-phone form text; /pic/screenshot diff confirms a submit or sync screen changed; /device/group/get-dev runs the same check across a cohort once /device/group/set has actually populated one. Needs ShortcutWith caveats None of the external platform-policy risks above apply, since there is no outside platform to violate. The remaining blocker is entirely local: no OCR to read back a confirmation banner or a validation error, so a human still reads the final screenshot to confirm the workflow actually completed.

Open Group targeting is a real primitive with nothing in it yet

/device/group/get-dev takes a group id and returns the phones in it, and the doc shows it working with a populated group on a different install. On this rig every phone's gname reads 未分组 and a live call to /device/group/get returns an empty list, so any row above that leans on group targeting first needs a one-time /device/group/set call per cohort (Marketplace phones, LMS student-view phones, a fleet-test lane) before it does anything. That setup step is unverified on this rig, same status as the Shortcut round trip itself.

MARK-ACCOUNTS-MARK

Section 5 · Account management

Account management

Logging in, logging out and rotating credentials on accounts you own reduces to the same mouse, key and screenshot primitives already proven on this rig, with the clipboard and the iMouse Shortcut picking up wherever /key/sendkey's ASCII limit stops. The harder half is not driving the UI, it is knowing what happened afterward: with the OCR and image-search plug-ins both dark here (code 28), every login result, every OTP arrival and every signed-in check has to be read off a raw frame by your own pixel-diff code, not the vendor's recognition endpoints.

Login, logout and credential rotation

Credential vault to keystrokes: login, logout and session rotation

PartialWith caveats

Keep every credential on the PC and never on the phone. A login job taps the username and password fields, types them through the HID keyboard path, submits, and classifies the result against stored crops for a signed-in state, a wrong-password state and a 2FA challenge. Logout and slot relabeling follow the same pattern, so one vault can own many accounts across many slots without a human touching a screen, as long as the passwords stay ASCII and every result stays auditable.

How

  1. get_device_list + get_usb_list GET /api/device/get?id=<id> and GET /api/config/usb/get — confirm video (state != 0, live air_pid) and control (board state 2) are both up, and read imgw/imgh (500x1080) as the coordinate space.
  2. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<id> — clear the silent stuck-click state before any tap-critical run.
  3. send_key fn_key + click GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+h (twice), then GET /api/mouse/click — go Home twice, then navigate to the login screen.
  4. click then send_key POST /api/mouse/click, then POST /api/key/sendkey {key: username} — focus and type the username, ASCII only, POST JSON never GET.
  5. click then send_key POST /api/mouse/click, then POST /api/key/sendkey {key: password} — same for the password field, one device id at a time.
  6. shortcut#10 → send_key WIN+v → shortcut#10 → shortcut#11 POST /api/shortcut/clipboard/set, GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+v, verify with GET /api/shortcut/clipboard/get — non-ASCII secrets go through the clipboard instead.
  7. send_key fn_key POST /api/key/sendkey {fn_key: ENTER} — submit.
  8. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true — capture a raw BMP and classify the outcome client-side.
  9. send_key POST /api/mouse/click (code field), then POST /api/key/sendkey {key: <TOTP>} — type a PC-generated TOTP if the classifier sees a 2FA screen; an SMS code stops the job for a human.
  10. click + get_device_screenshot GET /api/mouse/click (Log out → confirm), then GET /api/pic/screenshot?binary=true — log out and confirm the login wall is back before marking the slot closed.
  11. set_dev GET /api/device/set?id=<id>&name=Rack1-Slot07 — label the slot, never the account, in the device record.

Needs

  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in; with only IMService.exe up, both phones showed state 0 and no boards on this rig.
  • AssistiveTouch on with maximum tracking sensitivity, Full Keyboard Access on, Trackpad & Mouse speed maxed, Auto-Lock never, portrait lock; none of this is queryable over the API.
  • Board bound (vid and pid together) and at USB state 2, location_crc non-empty (B0DBD800 shared-library profile here).
  • Per-app, per-version golden crops for signed-in, wrong-password and 2FA states, captured per phone since the two XRs have different wallpapers.
  • A PC-side secret store; no password manager or notes app on the handsets.
  • iMouse Shortcut installed and AssistiveTouch-bound, only for the Unicode clipboard path.
  • Authorization to administer every account the vault holds.

Watch out

  • OCR is dead on this rig (code 28), so every outcome classification is client-side pixel work on raw BMP frames, not a vendor recognition call.
  • The Unicode clipboard path is Shortcut-gated, and the Phonefarm sibling doc marks its whole shortcut dispatcher professional-only; ASCII typing needs neither.
  • XP has no send_text; clipboard/set plus WIN+v is the substitute, and outtime is milliseconds on XP versus seconds in the Phonefarm doc.
  • Clipboard scrubbing is a documented write, not a documented erase: overwrite with a placeholder and read it back, do not try to blank the pasteboard.
  • The ASCII claim on /key/sendkey does not enumerate which punctuation survives; validate the vault's character set once per board generation rather than assume full ASCII.
  • /mouse/click can silently stop responding while /mouse/move and hotkeys keep working. Reset before every tap-critical run, or a password can be typed into nothing while the job reports success.
  • /mouse/* and /key/* take comma-separated id lists; a stray comma mirrors one account's password to every listed phone.
  • SMS-delivered 2FA is out of reach in both editions: no SMS endpoint, and reading a banner needs the missing OCR plug-in. TOTP typed from the vault works; SMS needs a human or an out-of-band feed.
  • iOS can interpose a "Save Password to Keychain?" sheet or an autofill bar after submit that none of the three golden crops account for; add a fourth crop and a dismiss step.
  • Nothing re-verifies that the username or password focus click actually landed before typing. Add a keyboard-visible or pointer-box check after each focus tap, not just at final classification, or a masked field can receive zero characters while step 8 reports success against a generic "try again" screen.
  • No inter-keystroke wait or pre-submit check of the masked-dot count is built in; ENTER could fire before typing finishes if key injection lags the HTTP response.
  • Only two phones are confirmed live and control-bound on this rig; a 19-phone claim is a capacity projection, not a measured result.
  • The API has no authentication on the LAN, so a credential sent to /key/sendkey crosses as plaintext HTTP any host on the segment can read. POST JSON, never GET, and firewall 9911 and 17000 to trusted hosts. Treat a rate-limit or "too many attempts" response as a stop signal, not something to retry through.

Scale

Logins run one phone at a time because the values differ per slot, but phones do not contend: two pollers held 83 and 85 req/s, ten held 512 req/s, and input traffic did not slow frame polling. Per-call cost is small (screenshot p50 2 ms raw BMP; never JPEG here, it is 40 ms with a roughly 21 req/s cap), but pointer travel and the target app's own response time dominate wall-clock: roughly 10 to 20 seconds per phone for a full login-verify-logout-verify cycle. That caps a sane cadence at tens of rotations per hour per phone, not hundreds, since backoff between attempts matters more than raw API throughput. Scaling past the two confirmed live phones to the rack's 19 boards is unverified.

Unicode-safe password rotation campaign across the rack

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Rotate the passwords of accounts you own, fleet-wide, from the PC: push the new secret to each phone's clipboard through the iMouse Shortcut, drive the change-password screen with the pointer, paste with WIN+v, submit, verify on a captured frame, and only then commit the new secret to the vault. This is what makes long Unicode or emoji passphrases possible at all, since /key/sendkey is ASCII-only in both editions.

Trap Some apps paste-block the new-password field

Secure text-entry fields on banking-grade or security-conscious apps can refuse a paste specifically to defeat clipboard-based credential tools. The rig cannot see or override that at the HID layer, and the ASCII fallback does not cover the non-ASCII passphrases this workflow exists for. Probe paste-acceptance on a given app (paste a known string, read it back from a frame) before committing to the clipboard path for it.

How

  1. get_device_list + get_usb_list GET /api/device/get?id=<id> and GET /api/config/usb/get — confirm control and video, read imgw/imgh.
  2. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<id> — clear the stuck-click state before touching the password screen.
  3. shortcut#10 POST /api/shortcut/clipboard/set {id, text: <new password>, sleep, outtime} — push the new secret to that phone's clipboard.
  4. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=<id>&x=&y= — navigate to the app's change-password screen.
  5. send_key / shortcut#10 + paste GET /api/key/sendkey?key=<old password> or clipboard/set + fn_key=WIN+v — fill the old-password field.
  6. send_key fn_key GET /api/mouse/click (focus), then GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+v (twice) — paste the new secret into the new and confirm fields.
  7. send_key fn_key / click GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=ENTER or GET /api/mouse/click (Save) — submit.
  8. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true&rect=[l,t,r,b] — capture the result banner and verify client-side.
  9. shortcut#10 then shortcut#11 POST clipboard/set {text: decoy}, then GET clipboard/get — scrub the pasteboard and prove the scrub took.
  10. (no API call) client-side bookkeeping — commit to the vault only after the previous step passed; queue re-login for every other device holding that account.

Needs

  • Accounts you own, with the right to change their credentials.
  • iMouse Shortcut installed on every phone (Advanced settings: allow running scripts, allow sharing large amounts of data), IP edited to the kernel PC, run once with every prompt allowed.
  • Shortcut bound to an AssistiveTouch custom key via IMConsole's "Send Binding Key".
  • Phone able to reach the kernel on TCP 9911 over the LAN, since the Shortcut posts its result back through the kernel.
  • Board bound and at USB state 2, location_crc non-empty.
  • Full Keyboard Access on with a 1 s auto-hide, AssistiveTouch on, Trackpad & Mouse speed maxed, Auto-Lock never, portrait lock.
  • Per-app, per-version change-password screen coordinates and a success-state crop, captured per phone.
  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in.
  • A vault that supports staged, propose-then-commit secrets so a failed verification does not overwrite the working password.

Watch out

  • Unicode entirely depends on the Shortcut. No Shortcut, no non-ASCII password, and the Phonefarm sibling gates its whole shortcut dispatcher behind a professional licence.
  • Phonefarm-style bare function POSTs return HTTP 500 on this rig; use XP paths only, and remember outtime is milliseconds here, seconds in the Phonefarm doc. Code 30 means the hotkey never launched the Shortcut.
  • Verification is unassisted. OCR and image-search are both effectively unavailable (code 28), so template matching happens in your own process; /shortcut/other/ocr and /shortcut/other/find-image exist but are documented by path name only, so probe before relying on them.
  • /pic/screenshot and /shortcut/clipboard/get are single-id only; only the mouse, key and clipboard-set calls fan out over a comma list.
  • Real change-password flows often demand a second factor or an out-of-band confirmation the rig cannot complete, and the SMS route is absent in both editions. Expect a human step on those apps.
  • A full-height swipe is roughly 580 ms of pointer walk and iOS may read it as a drag rather than a flick; scroll long settings pages with /mouse/wheel instead.
  • iOS's own "Save Password to Keychain?" sheet or an autofill bar is not one of the golden-crop states and reads as ambiguous. That correctly blocks the commit, but budget for the extra dismiss-and-reclassify step it forces.
