  • Per-phone Shortcut setup (install, edit the IP, grant prompts, bind an AssistiveTouch key) is manual, one-time labor per phone. For onboarding a real fleet this setup cost, not API throughput, is the actual bottleneck.
  • The 19-phone throughput projection in the source draft was extrapolated from board count; only two phones were confirmed mirroring and bound in this rig's evidence. Re-probe all 19 before promising that scale.
  • The password crosses the LAN as plaintext HTTP to an unauthenticated API, then briefly sits on the iOS pasteboard where any foreground app can read it. Firewall 9911 and 17000, and treat a failed verification as "keep the old secret, flag a human," never as a reason to commit on faith. A password change normally invalidates other sessions, so expect a re-login wave, and keep the automation's cadence sane against the platform's terms.

Scale

Dominated by the Shortcut round trip, not the API: each clipboard call is a HID hotkey plus a Wi-Fi callback bounded by a 15 s outtime, with real completion usually 1 to 3 seconds, and this flow makes two to four of them per account. Pointer travel and verification screenshots add low hundreds of milliseconds. Budget roughly 10 to 25 seconds per phone end to end, so a 19-phone campaign is 3 to 8 minutes sequential, faster in parallel since phones do not contend (ten concurrent screenshot pollers held 512 req/s). Only /pic/screenshot and /shortcut/clipboard/get force one-at-a-time handling; give each phone its own worker. Real safe cadence is far below the theoretical 150 to 350 rotations/hour/phone, because password changes trigger re-authentication waves and confirmation emails; plan for single digits to low tens per hour per phone with backoff, and treat the 19-phone figure as unverified beyond the two confirmed live phones.

Knowing which slots are actually signed in

Session-state sweep: classify signed-in, login wall, captcha or ban from the mirror frame

Native APIWith caveats

On a fixed interval, bring every mirroring phone to a known state, open the target app, grab one raw frame per phone, and classify it as signed-in, login wall, captcha, account-restricted, or an unexpected dialog. A rack's real inventory is accounts still signed in and unrestricted, not just phones that happen to be mirroring; without this sensor a scheduler can drive taps into a login wall or a captcha for hours and produce silent, zero-yield work.

How

  1. get_device_list / get_usb_list GET /api/device/get (optional id=a,b) and GET /api/config/usb/get — enumerate targets with live video and control state, read imgw/imgh per phone.
  2. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<list> — clear the stuck-click state on the whole sweep set in one call.
  3. send_key fn_key=WIN+h GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<list>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice, with a settle wait) — normalize the whole set to Home in one request.
  4. click / swipe / send_key / shortcut#13 GET /api/mouse/click, /api/mouse/swipe, /api/key/sendkey, or /api/shortcut/exec/url — open the target app by icon tap, home-screen search, or Shortcut deep link.
  5. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<single>&binary=true — one raw BMP per phone, one request each, run concurrently.
  6. (none, client-side) your own code on the returned bytes — mean-absolute-pixel-diff fixed regions against golden crops for each state; the only classifier that works here today.
  7. find_multi_color POST /api/pic/find-multi-color — optional distinctive-colour-block classifier, for example a restriction banner. Probe once for plug-in gating before relying on it.
  8. ocr / ocr_ex GET /api/pic/ocr, POST /api/pic/find-text — optional text classifier, only once the OCR plug-in is actually installed; it answers code 28 today.
  9. get_device_screenshot (save) / send_key GET /api/pic/screenshot?save_path=..., GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=TAB+b — act on the verdict: capture forensic evidence and pause the queue, or best-effort dismiss a benign dialog and re-check.

Needs

  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in.
  • Phones mirroring with a live air_pid matching AirplayMirroring.exe and an established socket on TCP 17000.
  • Per-phone imgw/imgh (500x1080 here, not the 414x896 logical size); golden crops and coordinates cannot cross phones with different values.
  • Your own bottom-up BMP decoder and mean-absolute-difference comparator; nothing in the API does this.
  • Golden crops per app, per app version and per phone, at fixed display settings (lowest brightness, Standard view, no True Tone or Night Shift drift).
  • AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, Trackpad & Mouse speed, Auto-Lock never; all unqueryable input prerequisites.
  • Board bound and at USB state 2, location_crc non-empty.
  • OCR plug-in (installed, ocr_num set) and OpenCV plug-in (opencv_num ≥ 1) only for the optional recognition legs; both are effectively absent here.
  • iMouse Shortcut, only for the deep-link app-opening route.
  • Authorization to operate the swept accounts under the platform's terms.

Watch out

  • Recognition is not native here: /pic/ocr answers code 28, so ocr, ocr-ex, find-text and find-text-ex are all unusable. Assume the image-search plug-in is in the same state until probed.
  • /pic/find-multi-color sits on the same plug-in-gated page and has a Shortcut fallback, the same pattern OCR follows, so probe its data.code before designing a classifier around it.
  • Screenshot-family endpoints are single-id only; navigation fans out with a comma list but capture is one request per phone.
  • Frame freshness, not request latency, is the real constraint: one XR delivers roughly 29 new frames/s under motion, its identical twin roughly 4.5. Settle at least 220 ms on the slow phone and never assume 30 fps.
  • Never compare frames by hash. MD5 or byte equality reports "changed" on an untouched phone every time from clock drift and encoder noise. Use mean-abs-diff (idle 0.02 to 0.03, real change 20 to 160).
  • Golden crops are the real maintenance burden. They break on every app update and per-phone display drift, and cannot be shared across phones with different home screens or imgw/imgh.
  • Getting to the app's home view is the weakest link, not the capture. The two XRs' different home screens mean shared coordinates are wrong by construction, and the only layout-independent route, a Shortcut deep link, pulls in the whole Shortcut prerequisite chain.
  • A cached view can look signed-in while the session is dead. Classify a screen that cannot render without a valid session, not a feed that may be served from cache.
  • Nothing here solves a captcha or a restriction notice. Both are terminal states: capture evidence, pause the queue, escalate to a person, and treat repeated notices as a signal to reduce or stop the automation, not to route around it.
  • iOS system sheets (Keychain autofill or save prompts, "Allow Paste from X?" banners, low-power-mode banners) can look identical to an app dialog to a fixed-region diff classifier unless a golden crop exists for each, and these can shift wording or position across iOS point releases even on the same hardware. Crops need to be per-iOS-version, not just per-app-version.
  • TAB+b is documented as "not supported by all apps," and on iOS a Tab-family key more plausibly moves focus than dismisses a sheet. A mis-fire could shift focus into an unintended field that gets typed over on the next sweep cycle.
  • The frame-rate asymmetry between phones means a sweep interval tuned to the fast phone will more often catch the slow one mid-transition, systematically biasing which phone's states get misclassified. Settle-wait budgets need to be per-phone.
  • A 19-phone throughput claim was extrapolated from board and hub count; only two phones showed a live device state and air_pid in this rig's evidence, and per-frame classifier CPU at higher concurrency is untested.
  • An unrecognized frame, from a failed navigation or a swallowed keystroke, does not cleanly fall into any of the four semantic buckets. Define an explicit "navigation failed / unrecognized" bucket rather than forcing a low-confidence match; reporting a banned phone as healthy is the worse failure mode.
  • Forensic frames are full screenshots of a signed-in account and contain personal data. Store them encrypted with a short retention window and off any shared or version-controlled path. The API has no authentication on the LAN, so firewall 9911 and 17000 to trusted hosts.

Scale

Capture is cheap and embarrassingly parallel: two pollers held 83 and 85 req/s, ten held 512 req/s at p50 3 ms, and input traffic did not slow frame polling. A full 19-phone raw-BMP capture is well under a second of wall time and is bounded by your own decode and compare cost, not the kernel; reuse one buffer per poller, since naive allocation measured 488 MB/s and 496 gen-2 GCs per 8 s, versus 2.9 MB/s with reuse. Never switch to JPEG on loopback, it is 40 ms against 2 ms with a roughly 21 req/s cap. Navigation legs are one request each regardless of fleet size since /mouse/* and /key/* fan out over comma lists; the real ceilings are per-phone settle time, pointer travel at roughly 0.6 ms/px (prefer short strokes over full-height swipes), and your classifier's per-frame CPU, untested above two concurrent phones. A realistic sweep round lands in the tens of seconds for a rack this size, fine for a cadence measured in minutes, but treat the 19-phone figure as a capacity projection until all 19 boards are confirmed live.

Capturing one-time codes

Copy OTP and email codes out of Messages/Mail via the phone clipboard

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

For codes that never reach the QuickType strip, such as email codes, in-app messages or untagged SMS formats, drive the phone's own UI to copy the code, read it off the phone with /shortcut/clipboard/get, and type it back with /key/sendkey. This is the only supported text-extraction channel on this rig: there is no message-reading API in either edition, and the server-side OCR fallback is dead here.

Trap Messages and Mail are not the same gesture

iOS's context-sensitive "Copy Code" long-press menu is a Messages behavior. Mail has no equivalent auto-detection, so pulling a code from an email needs a manual drag-handle text selection (tap to place a cursor, then drag the handle to bracket the code) before Copy appears. As written, a single long-press-then-tap only works for Messages; treat Mail as a separate, harder sub-case with its own calibrated sequence.

How

  1. get_device_list + get_usb_list GET /api/device/get?id=<id> and GET /api/config/usb/get — confirm control and video are up, read imgw/imgh.
  2. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<id> — clear the stuck-click state before the sequence.
  3. send_key fn_key=WIN+h GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — normalize to Home.
  4. get_device_screenshot → click GET /api/pic/screenshot?binary=true, then GET /api/mouse/click — open Messages or Mail and tap the newest thread from a live frame.
  5. click time=800 GET /api/mouse/click?id=<id>&x=&y=&time=800 — long-press the code text to raise the iOS context menu (Messages) or place a cursor (Mail).
  6. click GET /api/mouse/click — tap Copy or Copy Code, using the frame taken after the long-press, not a cached coordinate.
  7. shortcut#11 GET /api/shortcut/clipboard/get?id=<single>&outtime=<ms> — read the code off the phone; validate data.text against a 4 to 8 digit regex.
  8. send_key fn_key=AppSwitch, then send_key key=<digits> GET /api/key/sendkey — return to the app and type the digits, ASCII, no paste needed.
  9. shortcut#10 GET /api/shortcut/clipboard/set?id=<list>&text=<placeholder> — overwrite the pasteboard afterward; this is a scrub, not an erase.
  10. get_device_screenshot + ocr GET /api/pic/screenshot?binary=true&rect=[...] then client-side OCR — plug-in-free fallback when the clipboard path is unavailable; server-side OCR answers code 28 here.

Needs

  • iMouse Shortcut installed on every phone (Advanced: allow running scripts, allow sharing large amounts of data), IP edited in, run once with every "Allow" granted.
  • Shortcut bound to an AssistiveTouch custom key; board bound and at USB state 2.
  • Phone able to reach the kernel on 9911 for the Shortcut's Wi-Fi callback, alongside the USB trigger channel.
  • AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, Trackpad & Mouse speed, Auto-Lock never, portrait lock.
  • location_crc non-empty on the device record.
  • Thread and menu coordinates read live per phone, never hard-coded or shared between the two XRs.
  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in.
  • Only phones and accounts the operator owns.

Watch out

  • The whole chain hinges on one Shortcut-gated call; without it, harvesting degrades to screenshot plus external OCR, since /pic/ocr answers code 28 here.
  • /shortcut/clipboard/get, /pic/screenshot, /pic/ocr, /pic/find-image and /pic/find-text are all single-id only; only clipboard/set and the mouse, key and switch endpoints take a comma list. There is no way to harvest N phones in one request.
  • The Phonefarm sibling gates its whole shortcut function family behind a professional licence; XP states no edition gate on /shortcut/*, but licensing is enforced per device through login, so treat it as licence-dependent.
  • Phonefarm-style bare function POSTs return HTTP 500 on 9911, and 9912 is closed. Use XP paths only, and note outtime is milliseconds on XP, seconds in the Phonefarm doc.
  • The long-press depends on iOS's "Copy Code" context menu, which neither vendor doc describes. Verify each frame rather than replaying coordinates, since a different app, iOS version or link-detected code can change the menu layout.
  • A silent tap failure is invisible here too: /mouse/click can stop working while /mouse/move and hardware keys keep succeeding, returning code 0 throughout. Verify with mean-abs-pixel-diff, never MD5 equality.
  • Overwriting the pasteboard is cosmetic. It does not clear iOS pasteboard history, does not un-send a Universal Clipboard sync to a paired Mac or iPad, and does not stop any app that already read the pasteboard in the interval. Disable Handoff on rack phones if that matters.
  • No message-read API exists in either edition; Phonefarm's SMS-send and read-aloud shortcut ids are struck through and absent from XP, so the clipboard is the channel, not a convenience.
  • This rig has no Shortcut installed on either phone today, so the install-and-bind procedure, itself manual and on-phone, outside the HTTP API, is a blocking one-time setup cost, not a background assumption.
  • Bubble geometry shifts with message length and wrapping, so a coordinate calibrated on one test message can miss a differently-worded real one. The per-frame verify step is necessary, not optional, and adds a round trip the throughput math should include.
  • Typing digits back in after an AppSwitch round trip assumes the code field still has focus. If the OS backgrounds or reloads the app, the digits could land in the wrong field with no error, since /key/sendkey returns one code with no per-keystroke confirmation of where it went.
  • The harvested code is a live authentication factor sitting briefly in PC memory and the kernel's HTTP response. Scope it to the single attempt, never log or persist it, and firewall 9911 and 17000 since any LAN host can otherwise call clipboard/get on any phone.

Scale

Two costs dominate per phone: pointer travel at roughly 0.6 ms/px, so home to thread to code to menu is several hundred milliseconds of board time regardless of whether one phone or a comma-listed many is targeted, and the Shortcut round trip itself, a USB hotkey plus a Wi-Fi callback bounded by a 15 s outtime, so expect seconds, not milliseconds, and code 30 if the Shortcut never fired. Verification frames are cheap (2 ms p50 raw BMP) and phones are fully independent, two pollers ran 83 and 85 req/s with no interference, ten ran 512 req/s total, so run one worker per phone rather than serializing. The real ceiling is AirPlay source rate, roughly 29 fps on one XR and 4.5 on its twin, so a "wait for the menu" step on the slow phone needs 220 ms or more per frame, not a 30 fps assumption. Realistic figure: roughly 5 to 20 s per code per phone if messages are already present, on the order of 100 to 500 codes/hour/phone at best, dropping sharply once message-arrival latency or app-side rate limiting becomes the actual gate rather than the rig.

One-tap OTP from the iOS QuickType suggestion strip

Native APIWith caveats

When a code field is tagged as a one-time-code field, iOS itself offers the SMS code in the QuickType suggestion strip above the keyboard. Tapping it inserts the code without the rig ever reading the message. The chain is entirely XP-native, reset, click, force the keyboard open, poll a cropped frame, tap, ENTER, and the code never transits the PC. The premise, though, is iOS behavior no vendor document covers and this rig has not verified.

Trap A hardware keyboard usually suppresses the software one

The control board presents to iOS as a HID keyboard, and iOS's normal behavior with an external keyboard attached is to suppress the full software keyboard for a thin predictive-text bar instead. OPENKeyboard is documented to force the on-screen keyboard up, but whether that produces a full keyboard with a QuickType row, the thin bar, or no visible change at all is exactly what the one-time manual calibration has to establish, not just the strip's coordinates within an assumed layout.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get?id=<id> — confirm the phone is mirroring and read imgw/imgh (500x1080 here).
  2. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<id> — clear the stuck-click state first.
  3. click GET /api/mouse/click?button=1&x=&y= — tap the code field so it takes focus.
  4. send_key (fn_key) GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=OPENKeyboard — force the on-screen keyboard up so the suggestion strip sits at a repeatable height.
  5. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true — one-time manual step: trigger a real code, diff two frames, and record the strip band and tap point for this model and iOS build.
  6. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true — baseline capture of the strip band before the code arrives.
  7. get_device_screenshot (poll) GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true, polled — poll the same crop every roughly 500 ms for up to 60 s; mean-abs-diff over the band (idle 0.02 to 0.03, real change 20 to 160).
  8. find_multi_color POST /api/pic/find-multi-color — optional discriminator to confirm the band holds the AutoFill suggestion, not ordinary predictive text; its own plug-in gating is unverified.
  9. click GET /api/mouse/click?x=&y= — tap the suggestion; iOS inserts the code, and the PC never learns it.
  10. get_device_screenshot + send_key GET /api/pic/screenshot?binary=true, then GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=ENTER — confirm the field region changed and submit; verification is blind, without OCR.
  11. shortcut#11 (fallback) GET /api/shortcut/clipboard/get?id=<id> — if the strip never appears, long-press-copy on the phone instead and read the pasteboard; needs the Shortcut installed.

Needs

  • Only appropriate for accounts you own or your own app under QA; the codes are authentication material.
  • An active SIM and cellular service on the handset; unverified on this rig, neither the probe nor HARDWARE.md confirms cellular service on either XR.
  • The field must be declared a one-time-code field by the app (iOS textContentType oneTimeCode, or autocomplete="one-time-code" in Safari); nothing in the API can tell you whether it is.
  • Messages notifications enabled and the phone unlocked; the suggestion does not appear on a locked screen.
  • Board bound and at USB state 2, location_crc non-empty.
  • AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, Trackpad & Mouse speed, Auto-Lock never, portrait lock.
  • Strip band and tap point measured once per model and iOS build, stored in that device's own mirror pixels.
  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in.
  • The fallback path additionally needs the iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-edited, run once, and AssistiveTouch-bound.

Watch out

  • Every call in the core chain is verified on this kernel, but the premise, that the QuickType strip appears and a tap inserts the code, is iOS behavior no vendor document covers and this rig has not tested.
  • Detection is blind: without OCR, a diff-triggered tap cannot distinguish an AutoFill code suggestion from an ordinary predictive-text candidate, so it can insert a wrong word. /pic/find-multi-color is the only plug-in-free discriminator, and its own plug-in gating is unverified.
  • You cannot verify the inserted digits. Confirmation is limited to "the field region changed" and "the next screen appeared," so a wrong insert looks identical to a right one until submit fails.
  • Strip geometry is model-, iOS- and layout-specific and will drift across iOS updates; treat it as a per-model-and-build calibration, never a hardcoded constant.
  • Coordinates must come from that device's imgw/imgh (500x1080), not its logical width/height (414x896).
  • XP has no push-stream screenshot, so this must be a poll, and XP's rect is a flat [left, top, right, bottom], not Phonefarm's four corner points.
  • /mouse/reset is not optional housekeeping; the measured stuck-click state returns code 0 on every click while doing nothing.
  • Nothing confirms the code was accepted by the app, only that the region changed and the next screen appeared. A masked field, a validation delay, or a second confirmation screen all read as identical to success or failure.
  • AssistiveTouch and Full Keyboard Access being simultaneously required can themselves change where or whether a QuickType bar renders versus an AssistiveTouch floating menu intercepting the tap; an interaction this rig has not tested.
  • Cellular and SIM presence on these two XRs is unconfirmed by any document. Without an active SIM, no SMS ever arrives and the whole premise cannot be exercised on this rig regardless of how well the pixel-diff logic is built.
  • Automating OTP entry only makes sense on accounts you own or your own app under QA; against third-party accounts it is account takeover regardless of how the code was obtained. The API is unauthenticated on the LAN, so firewall 9911 and 17000 even though the code itself never touches the PC in this design.

Scale

Per-phone by nature: each handset waits on its own SMS, and /pic/screenshot is single-id, so it is one poller per phone. Cost is trivial against measured headroom: a 500 ms poll is 2 req/s, against a measured 84 req/s per phone alone and 512 req/s across ten pollers. Input traffic and frame polling do not interfere. The real limiter is the AirPlay source rate, roughly 29 new frames/s on one XR under motion and roughly 4.5 on its twin, so allow 220 ms or more for the slow phone's crop to refresh, and discard identical polls as "no suggestion yet" rather than treating a still screen as a failure. Wall-clock is dominated by SMS delivery, seconds to a minute, not the rig; realistic planning figure is well under 60 to 100 OTP attempts/hour per phone even with a perfect rig, and zero if the phone has no active SIM.

Account provisioning

Apple ID sign-in on a fresh phone with same-device 2FA

Plus external toolingWith caveats

Sign a phone into an Apple ID entirely from the PC: tap the Settings fields with /mouse/click, type the Apple ID and password with /key/sendkey (ASCII only), then handle the six-digit verification code. An Apple ID gates every App Store install, TestFlight join, iCloud backup and iMessage/FaceTime identity on a phone, so this is the first commissioning step for any handset entering the rack. It is also the clearest test of this stack's ceiling: it exercises typing, tapping and screen-reading in one flow and shows exactly which links, the code read and the Keychain sheet, still need a person.

How

  1. get_device_list / get_usb_list GET /api/device/get?id=<id>, GET /api/config/usb/get — confirm the phone is control-ready (board state 2, bound, non-empty location_crc) and video-ready (state != 0, live air_pid), and read imgw/imgh (500x1080) as the coordinate space.
  2. mouse_reset_pos / send_key GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<id> then GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<id>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — clear the stuck-click state and return to home page one.
  3. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=<id>&x=&y= — open Settings by tapping its per-phone icon; there is no Spotlight hotkey in the XP fn_key table.
  4. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=<id>&x=&y= — tap "Sign in to your iPhone" at the top of the Settings root list.
  5. send_key POST /api {"fun":"/key/sendkey","data":{"id":"<id>","key":"<apple id>"}} then fn_key=ENTER — type the Apple ID; the key parameter is documented ASCII-only.
  6. send_key (ASCII) or shortcut#10 + paste POST /mouse/click then /key/sendkey key=<password>; non-ASCII: POST /shortcut/clipboard/set then fn_key=WIN+v — tap the password field and enter the password.
  7. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true&rect=[l,t,r,b] — capture the 2FA prompt region; rect is XP's flat array, single-id only.
  8. ocr / ocr_ex GET /api/pic/ocr?id=<id>&rect=[l,t,r,b] — not usable on this rig (code 28, plug-in not connected); digits must be read client-side or by a human.
  9. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=<id>&x=&y= — prefer the QuickType "From Messages" autofill chip when the code lands by SMS on this phone's own SIM; one tap fills all six boxes and sidesteps OCR.
  10. send_key POST /api/key/sendkey {"id":"<id>","key":"123456"} — type the code manually if no chip appears.
  11. send_key (unverified) POST /api/key/sendkey key=<digits> — the Keychain "enter the passcode of <device>" sheet; whether HID input reaches this secure field on iOS 18.7.10 is unproven and must be tested by hand first.
  12. get_device_screenshot + compare GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true&rect=[Settings header band] — verify sign-in visually; no field anywhere in the device record reports Apple ID state.

Needs

  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in; with only IMService.exe up, this rig showed both phones at state 0 and an empty board list.
  • Board bound (vid+pid together, single device per call) at /config/usb/get state 2, location_crc non-empty, or every tap lands offset with code 11.
  • iOS accessibility settings unreadable over the API: AssistiveTouch on at max sensitivity, Full Keyboard Access on with 1 s auto-hide, Trackpad & Mouse speed max, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock.
  • An Apple ID the operator owns, with this phone's SIM as the trusted number if the 2FA code is to land on-device at all.
  • Client-side OCR or a human reading the mirror; the vendor OCR plug-in is not connected (code 28) on this rig.
  • For non-ASCII passwords: iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-edited, hotkey-bound via AssistiveTouch; unconfirmed here, probe with /shortcut/device/ip first.
  • A one-off manual test establishing whether the Keychain passcode sheet accepts hardware-keyboard digits on this iOS build.
  • Per-phone stored coordinates for Settings, the sign-in banner, the credential fields and the QuickType chip; the two XRs have different home screens.

Watch out

  • "Same-device 2FA" only holds when this phone's SIM is already the trusted number. A fresh phone typically has Apple push the code to an already-trusted device instead of SMS here, so budget for the push-to-other-device case as the default, not the QuickType happy path this chain leans on.
  • No OCR on this rig: /pic/ocr, /pic/ocr-ex, /pic/find-text and /pic/find-text-ex share the same absent plug-in, so any digit read is client-side or manual work.
  • XP's rect on /pic/screenshot, /pic/ocr, /pic/find-image and /pic/find-text is a flat [left,top,right,bottom] array, not the Phonefarm four-corner form.
  • /key/sendkey key is ASCII-only by the vendor's own wording; a non-Latin password needs the clipboard+paste route, which drags in the whole Shortcut prerequisite chain and leaves the password sitting in the phone's pasteboard until overwritten.
  • XP has no send_text or send_text_ok callback; those are Phonefarm-only and this kernel rejects Phonefarm function names with HTTP 500.
  • Secure-input behavior is undocumented in both editions. A field may silently discard keystrokes while /key/sendkey still returns code 0 — an API success is not evidence the phone accepted the input.
  • No account-state readout exists anywhere in /device/get, /config/user/info (the kernel's own vendor license, not the Apple ID) or any callback; success detection is pixel-diff or client-side OCR only.
  • /mouse/click can silently stop working while /mouse/move and hardware keys keep responding; only /mouse/reset clears it. Send it before the sequence and treat a near-zero frame diff as a stuck pointer, not a wrong coordinate.
  • Screenshots are single-id ("Multiple is not allowed"), so the read side of this flow cannot be fanned out even though click and sendkey accept comma lists.
  • Any Face ID or biometric prompt is unreachable through the API; the run becomes attended at that point.
  • A byte-for-byte identical, machine-fast keystroke cadence across many phones is itself a signal Apple's sign-in risk engine can key on. That is a detection-risk fact to disclose, not something to engineer around.
  • Apple ID sign-in commonly interposes an "unusual activity" check or a forced delay after a few sign-ins from the same PC/IP; do not plan a same-day multi-phone batch and expect it to run unattended.
  • This flow is single-phone-at-a-time in practice: credentials differ per account, so the comma-id support on /mouse/click and /key/sendkey does not make parallel sign-ins as cheap as parallel screenshot polling.
  • The API is unauthenticated on the LAN; the Apple ID, password, 2FA code and any device passcode travel in the clear to any host that can reach port 9911. Use POST JSON, never a query string, firewall 9911 and 17000 to trusted hosts, and have the operator supply credentials at run time rather than storing them.
  • Only for accounts the operator owns; not a route to fabricate or bulk-provision identities.

Scale

One phone at a time per PC, roughly 1-2 minutes each, dominated by Apple's server round trips rather than the API — the rig itself imposes no shared bottleneck (ten independent screenshot pollers sustain 512 req/s at 3 ms p50). /mouse/click, /key/sendkey and /mouse/reset accept comma id lists, but /pic/screenshot is single-id and credentials differ per account, so typing cannot be mirrored across the rack in practice. Expect on the order of 20-40 sign-ins/hour if the SMS-to-this-device path holds, dropping to roughly 5-15/hour when the code must route to another trusted device or be read by a human, and expect Apple's risk engine to slow or halt a same-IP batch well under 40/hour sustained after the first few accounts.

Profile setup

Profile completion: avatar from the album plus pasted Unicode bio

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Push an avatar PNG from the PC into the phone's album via the iMouse Shortcut, tap through the app's photo picker and crop screen with mirror-pixel taps, then set a Unicode bio by pasting from the clipboard, since /key/sendkey types ASCII only. The shortcut album transfer is the only documented way to get an arbitrary file onto a phone in this stack, and the clipboard-paste route is the only way to put non-Latin text on screen, so this one chain covers both media and Unicode text entry for any profile-editing job.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get?id=<id> — read imgw/imgh (500x1080) and require state != 0 with a live air_pid plus non-empty location_crc.
  2. get_usb_list GET /api/config/usb/get — confirm the board is enumerated and the phone is cabled (state 2), independent of video-readiness.
  3. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<id1,id2,...> — clear the stuck-click state before any tap-critical sequence.
  4. send_key (fn_key WIN+h) GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — normalize to a known home screen before the first scripted tap.
  5. shortcut#7 POST /api {"fun":"/shortcut/album/upload","data":{"id":"<id1,id2>","files":["C:\\farm\\avatars\\0421.png"],"album_name":"","zip":0,"outtime":60000}} — push the avatar file from the PC into the phone's Recents album.
  6. shortcut#1 the upload response's data.list, or GET /api/shortcut/album/get?id=<id>&num=5 — read back the name iOS actually gave the imported photo (never the PC filename).
  7. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=&y= — open the app's profile editor and reach "Choose from library".
  8. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=&y= — tap the target tile in the picker grid, then confirm the crop.
  9. shortcut#10 POST /api {"fun":"/shortcut/clipboard/set","data":{"id":"<id1,id2>","text":"<bio>","sleep":1,"outtime":15000}} — put the Unicode bio on the phone clipboard.
  10. send_key (fn_key) GET /api/mouse/click?id=<ids> then GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+v — focus the bio field and paste.
  11. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=&y= — save the profile; the irreversible step of the flow.
  12. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true[&rect=[l,t,r,b]] — verify the result client-side against a known-good reference frame.
  13. shortcut#3 POST /api {"fun":"/shortcut/album/del","data":{"id":"<id1,id2>","list":[{"album_name":"","name":"<name from upload>","ext":"png"}],"outtime":15000}} — delete the uploaded image by its exact returned name+ext.
  14. shortcut#10 POST /api {"fun":"/shortcut/clipboard/set","data":{"id":"<ids>","text":" "}} — optional clipboard scrub, cheap and reversible.

Needs

  • iMouse Shortcut installed on every phone (Settings > Shortcuts > Advanced, all permissions allowed), IP-edited to the kernel, and bound to an AssistiveTouch custom key; the shortcut launches by a HID hotkey, so the board must be bound and working for any /shortcut/* call to fire.
  • Phone reachable from the kernel on TCP 9911 over the LAN; Wi-Fi off or airplane mode breaks every shortcut call and mirroring, while USB control survives.
  • USB board bound (/device/set with vid+pid together) at /config/usb/get state 2; mouse parameters present (location_crc non-empty).
  • iOS accessibility settings unreadable over the API: AssistiveTouch on at max sensitivity, Full Keyboard Access on (required for WIN+v), Trackpad & Mouse speed max, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock, phone unlocked.
  • Photo-library permission granted to the target app once by hand, and its photo picker reached manually so tile coordinates can be measured from a raw BMP frame.
  • A per-app, per-version coordinate profile in 500x1080 mirror pixels for every screen in the flow; no OCR or image-search plug-in on this rig, so nothing can be located at runtime.
  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in; with only IMService.exe up, both phones showed state 0 and an empty board list.
  • iOS 15+ as the safe floor for the file/album functions; these XRs run 18.7.10.

Watch out

  • Every /shortcut/* call in this chain is untested on this rig. Probe first with GET /api/shortcut/device/ip?id=<id>&state=0: code 0 echoing the phone's own IP proves the Shortcut is installed, hotkey-bound and reachable; a code 30 timeout after ~15 s means the hotkey never launched it.
  • The Phonefarm doc marks the entire shortcut dispatcher "professional version only." XP gates no endpoint by edition and licenses per device instead, so whether this rig's license covers shortcut calls is unresolved until that probe runs.
  • No runtime vision: without the OCR and image-search plug-ins, the flow is entirely open-loop on hard-coded coordinates, and a layout change in an app update silently taps the wrong thing.
  • Picker tile order ("top-left is newest") is an app-specific claim, not an API guarantee, and it differs between the system picker and an in-app album grid; measure it per app before wiring it in.
  • /shortcut/album/upload gives no progress signal, and the slow XR here delivers only ~4.5 new frames/s versus ~29 on its twin, so any screen-verification during the picker must not assume 30 fps.
  • /mouse/click can silently stop working while moves and hardware keys still succeed; only /mouse/reset clears it, and skipping it is the likeliest cause of a run that reports success and does nothing.
  • A shared coordinate is only safe across phones with identical imgw/imgh AND an identical app layout; the two XRs here have different home screens.
  • outtime is milliseconds on XP (default 15000) and seconds on Phonefarm; a value copied across editions is wrong by 1000x, and a large avatar over Wi-Fi can exceed the 15 s default.
  • The album name iOS assigns is not the PC filename; delete by the name+ext the upload response returns, never by the original filename.
  • Saving the profile is an irreversible, published account change; gate the Save tap behind an explicit go-ahead rather than fanning it across the rack unattended.
  • /shortcut/album/clear wipes an entire album on every listed phone with no undo; never wire it into automated cleanup — the targeted /shortcut/album/del does the job.
  • A raw-BMP diff only proves the cropped region's pixels changed, not that the correct avatar was applied and saved; compare against a known-good post-save reference captured once by hand, not just an idle-floor threshold.
  • AssistiveTouch emulates one simulated touch point per phone; a picker or crop sheet that needs a gesture beyond a plain tap (drag-to-resize) will not be satisfied by a coalesced click, and needs per-iOS-version validation.
  • The API is unauthenticated on the LAN; firewall 9911 and 17000 to trusted hosts. Only use this against accounts the operator owns and is authorized to administer.
  • Images carry EXIF and container metadata that travels with the upload, and the same file uploaded to multiple accounts is, factually, a linkage signal platforms act on.
  • Automating profile edits with hardware input sits outside most platforms' automation terms even on owned accounts, and a profile edit is a visible account-level change that can trigger re-review; if the app surfaces a rate-limit or "action blocked" interstitial, stop that phone's run rather than retry.

Scale

The media and text steps fan out cheaply: /shortcut/album/upload, /shortcut/album/del, /shortcut/clipboard/set and every /mouse and /key call take a comma id list, so mirroring a tap to N phones costs the same wall time as one. The per-phone cost is the shortcut round trip itself (outtime default 15000 ms; budget 30-60 s for a real image over Wi-Fi) plus verification, which is single-id but cheap and independent per phone (measured up to 512 req/s across ten pollers). A shared avatar and bio across a same-layout group costs roughly a minute per batch, dominated by the two shortcut round trips; unique avatars per phone force the upload into a per-phone loop, at which point plan on roughly 40-70 unique profile completions per hour per PC run serially, or 2-4x that pipelined.

Fleet app version management

TestFlight and App Store install/update rollout across the rack

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Fan a TestFlight join link or an App Store product URL out to every bound phone in one /shortcut/exec/url call, tap Accept/Install/Get/Update at a measured coordinate, then poll a cropped screenshot band over the button until the label changes to Open. Version state can be carried in each device's custom name via /device/set, turning "which phones are stale" from a manual audit into a query. As written this is really an update or relaunch flow for phones that already have TestFlight and an Apple ID configured, not an install-from-scratch flow: there is no App Store install endpoint, and account sign-in cannot be scripted.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get — build the rollout id list from devices with state != 0, a bound board and imgw/imgh identical to the reference phone; cross-check /config/usb/get for board state 2.
  2. send_key (fn_key WIN+h) GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<a,b,c>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — normalize every phone to a known screen.
  3. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<a,b,c> — clear the stuck-click state before any install tap sequence.
  4. shortcut#13 (Open URL) GET /api/shortcut/exec/url?id=<a,b,c>&url=https://testflight.apple.com/join/XXXXXXXX&outtime=20000 — open the TestFlight or App Store URL on every phone at once.
  5. send_key + click /api/mouse/click, then /api/key/sendkey?key=<url>, then fn_key=ENTER — fallback when the Shortcut is not installed: type the URL into Safari (per-phone icon coordinate).
  6. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=<a,b,c>&x=&y=&button=1 — tap Accept / Install / Get / Update; button is numeric on XP, coordinates are mirror pixels (500x1080), not iOS logical points.
  7. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true&rect=[l,t,r,b] — poll a cropped band over the button until it reads Open; single-id only.
  8. ocr / find_image GET /api/pic/find-text?id=<id>&text=["Open","Update","Get"] — not available on this rig (code 28); would read the button label server-side once the plug-in exists.
  9. set_dev GET /api/device/set?id=<one id>&name=Slot07-v3.2 — record the installed version per device, persisted in DeviceList.json and broadcast as a dev_change callback.
  10. callbacks (dev_connect / dev_disconnect / error_push) ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api — watch the run asynchronously for a phone that lost its mirror mid-install.

Needs

  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in; with only IMService.exe up, the live probe showed both phones at state 0 and an empty board list.
  • Per phone: board bound at /config/usb/get state 2, location_crc non-empty.
  • iOS settings invisible to the API: AssistiveTouch on at max sensitivity, Full Keyboard Access on, Trackpad & Mouse speed max, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock.
  • iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-edited and hotkey-bound on each phone for /shortcut/exec/url to fire; phone reachable to the kernel on 9911.
  • TestFlight already installed and the Apple ID already signed in on each phone; neither is achievable through this API.
  • Apple ID purchase/download authentication settings (Face ID for downloads, password prompts) configured by hand; the board has no path to satisfy a biometric prompt.
  • Button coordinates measured once per iOS build and app, plus a stored crop of the settled "Open" state.
  • A client-side comparator on raw BMP frames, since the OCR plug-in is not connected (code 28) — a hard prerequisite for verification, not an optimization.

Watch out

  • Nothing in this workflow is a vendor feature; TestFlight and the App Store appear nowhere in either API doc, so this is blind coordinate tapping with a screenshot diff as the only feedback, and any iOS or App Store UI revision breaks it silently.
  • Only /shortcut/exec/url, /key/sendkey, /mouse/click and /mouse/reset fan out on one request; /pic/screenshot is documented "Multiple is not allowed," so confirmation is strictly per phone.
  • A shared coordinate is only safe when every listed phone shows the same layout at the same imgw/imgh; the two XRs here have different home screens, so the Safari-fallback path in particular cannot be mirrored.
  • Credential entry is out of scope by design: if the App Store asks for the Apple ID password, or a Face ID/passcode prompt appears, stop the run, flag the device, and hand it to a person.
  • /shortcut/exec/url outtime is milliseconds on XP (default 15000) but seconds on the Phonefarm sibling; copying 15 across editions yields a 15 ms timeout.
  • A code 30 "call timeout" from any /shortcut/* call usually means the hotkey never launched the Shortcut (check the AssistiveTouch binding and that the phone is unlocked), not that the URL failed.
  • Install progress is invisible for long stretches on the slow phone (~4.5 new frames/s versus ~29 on its twin); do not treat frame scarcity as a stalled install.
  • The device record's custom name is a convenient version tag but unvalidated free text with no schema; it is a label, not a source of truth for what is actually installed.
  • A phone that loses Wi-Fi mid-install goes state 0 and disappears from the mirror while the install continues over cellular; USB control survives, so the run is blind rather than stopped.
  • A cropped-button pixel diff cannot distinguish "install finished, button now reads Open" from a different system sheet or crash dialog occupying the same region; corroborate with a secondary check, such as relaunching the app via Spotlight, rather than trusting the button region alone.
  • Apple enforces a device-association limit and a cooldown on associating new devices with one Apple ID, and TestFlight builds expire 90 days after upload with capped public tester slots; a 19-phone rack under one Apple ID hits that account-side wall well before any rig-side limit — a hard scaling ceiling, not just a background risk.
  • The API is unauthenticated; firewall 9911 and 17000 to trusted hosts, and never print or copy the vendor password stored as reversible hex in C:\iMouseXP\IMService.json.
  • An interrupted install leaves a phone in an unknown UI state; always re-normalize with two Home presses plus /mouse/reset at the start of each run rather than assuming where the previous run left off.
  • Scripted redemption and installation across many devices likely sits outside what Apple's App Store and TestFlight terms contemplate; that legal exposure is the operator's to assess for accounts and builds they own.

Scale

Link fan-out, taps and resets are one request regardless of fleet size, since /shortcut/exec/url, /key/sendkey, /mouse/click and /mouse/reset all take comma id lists and the boards walk in parallel; even a 500 px reposition costs about 300 ms. Confirmation is the only per-phone cost, at p50 2 ms and roughly 84 req/s per phone independently (ten pollers measured 512 req/s aggregate), so a 0.5 Hz poll across 19 phones is a small fraction of measured capacity. The real ceiling is external: per-phone Wi-Fi bandwidth and Apple's own servers, plus Apple ID device-association and tester-slot limits, not the rig. Realistic throughput is on the order of tens of phones per hour per PC across several legitimately owned Apple IDs on a reasonable uplink; an API-requests-per-second figure would misrepresent the actual bottleneck here.

Session hygiene

Lock between sessions, unlock by typed passcode

PartialWith caveats

Put each phone on its lock screen between account sessions with the documented hotkey TAB+l, so no logged-in feed sits visible on the mirror wall or in a captured frame, then wake it, raise the passcode pad with a swipe, type the passcode, and confirm with a screenshot diff. The lock leg is fully native and needs no plug-in or Shortcut; the unlock leg depends on undocumented iOS behavior, whether mirroring survives a lock, whether the USB accessory path stays live while locked, whether the passcode field accepts HID digits, that must be proven once per phone model before this is trusted. It also runs opposite to the vendor's own documented rack setting of Auto-Lock Never.

How

  1. get_usb_list + get_device_list GET /api/config/usb/get ; GET /api/device/get?id=<id> — confirm control-ready (board state 2, bound, non-empty location_crc) and video-ready (state != 0, live air_pid); read imgw/imgh.
  2. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true — capture a pre-lock reference frame and a small crop that differs between lock screen and app content.
  3. send_key (fn_key TAB+l) GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<id1,id2>&fn_key=TAB+l — lock the whole target set in one request; TAB+l is documented on XP and has no Phonefarm counterpart.
  4. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true — confirm the lock landed via mean-absolute-pixel-diff against the reference, budgeting for the phone's own frame rate (never MD5-compare frames).
  5. send_key (fn_key WIN+h) GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<id>&fn_key=WIN+h — wake the phone; whether this wakes a locked screen is unverified, fall back to a tap or fn_key=ControlBar.
  6. mouse_reset_pos then swipe GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<id> ; GET /api/mouse/swipe?id=<id>&direction=up&sx=250&sy=1000&ex=250&ey=500 — clear the stuck-click state, then raise the passcode pad with an explicit-coordinate swipe (single id).
  7. send_key (key) POST /api/key/sendkey {"id":"<id>","key":"<digits>"} — type the passcode for that one phone; follow with fn_key=ENTER only for a custom alphanumeric passcode. Never comma-list this call.
  8. get_device_screenshot + send_key GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true ; GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — verify the unlock against a home-screen reference, then normalize before any coordinate-based work.
  9. n/a (client-side policy) n/a — on failure, stop; do not retry the passcode. Raise it to a human and leave the phone locked.

Needs

  • Phones the operator owns and administers, with passcodes held legitimately.
  • Full Keyboard Access on with 1 s auto-hide; TAB+l, WIN+h and WIN+v are all HID hotkeys and are inert without it.
  • AssistiveTouch on at max sensitivity, Trackpad & Mouse speed max; none of this is queryable over the API.
  • Board bound and physically connected: /config/usb/get state 2 for that board and vid/pid/uid set together on the device record.
  • location_crc non-empty (B0DBD800 shared-library profile on this rig), or every mouse call returns code 11.
  • Mirroring live for verification: /device/get state != 0 with a live air_pid, and IMConsole.exe running and logged in.
  • A one-time manual acceptance test per model and iOS build on an expendable phone: does mirroring survive TAB+l, does the swipe raise the passcode pad, does the pad accept typed digits, does it need ENTER.
  • Per-phone stored reference crops for lock screen and home screen; the two XRs have different wallpapers, so references never transfer between phones.
  • Explicit acceptance that this contradicts the vendor's own documented rack prerequisite of Auto-Lock Never.

Watch out

  • The observation channel may vanish exactly when needed: no reference file says whether AirPlay mirroring survives a lock. If it drops outright, /device/get goes state 0 and /pic/screenshot returns code 25. A more likely outcome is that mirroring stays up but every frame is frozen or blanked (iOS's own content-privacy behavior on a locked device), so a flat pixel diff after TAB+l is not proof the lock command failed, only that content may be suppressed.
  • iOS can block Lightning/USB-C accessory data after a device has been locked for a period (Settings > Face ID & Passcode > Accessories, off by default). If that fires, the board cannot deliver the wake, swipe or digits and the phone needs hands on the rack; the exposure window is small for a between-job lock (minutes) but not zero for an overnight one.
  • Never use this as a restart-recovery plan: a rebooted phone is in a before-first-unlock state that refuses accessory input until a human unlocks it. Do not combine it with /device/restart or a switch/device-state call.
  • Face ID will attempt and fail in a rack with no face presented, which is what drops to the passcode pad, but a failed attempt still counts toward iOS's own retry accounting.
  • No OCR on this rig (code 28 confirmed live); every check is a mean-pixel-diff against a stored crop, not a read of "Enter Passcode" or "iPhone Unavailable."
  • A passcode sent as a GET query parameter is a plaintext secret on an unauthenticated LAN; use the POST JSON form, keep it out of logs, and firewall 9911 to trusted hosts regardless of verb.
  • /mouse/reset and /mouse/swipe both assume the control channel survived the lock; if accessory access is blocked, /mouse/reset itself silently no-ops, so check for a state change after every step, not only after the final digit entry, or three no-ops in a row look identical to three successes.
  • The claim that a standard 6-digit passcode submits without ENTER is unverified over a HID/AssistiveTouch path and should carry the same unverified flag as the rig's other unproven iOS behaviors, not read as settled.
  • The single most destructive failure mode is a wrong-passcode retry loop: iOS escalates lockout delays on consecutive failures and can render a device unusable or erased depending on configuration. Hard-code one attempt, then escalate to a human; never retry.
  • Never lock a phone you cannot reach to unlock; if any of the open unknowns resolves unfavorably for a given phone, that phone needs a human touch for that cycle, not an API retry.
  • This is administration of devices and passcodes the operator already owns and holds; it carries no anti-abuse-evasion content, but reference crops and screenshots are real account-screen images and should be stored like the account data they are.
  • The setup deviates from the vendor's documented Auto-Lock Never prerequisite, so any misbehavior traced to a locked phone falls outside supported configuration.

Scale

Locking is effectively free: /key/sendkey with a comma id list locks the entire rack in one request with the board walking phones in parallel. Unlocking does not scale the same way, since /pic/screenshot is single-id and a passcode must be typed per phone and never comma-listed, but concurrency across phones is cheap (measured up to 512 req/s across ten independent pollers), so N unlock workers can run in parallel. Per-phone wall time is roughly 1-4 s of API-visible work on a healthy link (about 300 ms of pointer travel for the swipe plus one or more frame waits, worse on the slow XR at ~220 ms per frame), but the real throughput driver is the failure rate on the three unproven legs: any phone where mirroring, accessory access or passcode-field acceptance resolves unfavorably falls out of automation entirely for that cycle rather than costing extra time.

Navigation infrastructure

Layout-independent app launch through Spotlight typing

PartialWith caveats

The rack's phones have different home screens and wallpapers, so a shared icon coordinate is not a fair multi-id target. Spotlight is layout-invariant: a mid-screen pull-down opens search on every iPhone, the search field accepts hardware-keyboard text, and ENTER opens the top hit, so one fan-out sequence launches the same app on every bound phone by name rather than by pixel. This turns "open the app," the first step of nearly every account job, from N per-phone coordinate lookups into a single request per step; what remains unsolved is confirming which app actually opened, since there is no OCR on this rig.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get (optionally ?id=a,b) — read imgw/imgh, state, vid/pid and location_crc; drop any phone whose mirror geometry differs from the master.
  2. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<a,b,c> — clear the stuck-click state on the whole target set before anything tap-critical.
  3. send_key (fn_key WIN+h) GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<a,b,c>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — normalize every phone to home page one.
  4. swipe GET /api/mouse/swipe?id=<list>&direction=down&sx=250&sy=400&ex=250&ey=600 — open Spotlight with a short mid-screen pull-down, not from the top edge (Notification Center).
  5. send_key (key) GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<list>&key=instagram — type the app name into the focused search field (ASCII only).
  6. send_key (fn_key) GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<list>&fn_key=ENTER — wait roughly 1 s for the result list to settle, then open the top hit.
  7. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=<list>&x=&y= — fallback when the top hit is a web or App Store suggestion: tap the first result row at its fixed, layout-independent coordinate.
  8. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<single id>&binary=true — verify per phone by mean-absolute-pixel-diff against the pre-launch frame; single-id only.
  9. ocr / find_image GET /api/pic/find-text?id=<single>&text=["Instagram"]&contain=true&similarity=0.8 or /api/pic/ocr — blocked on this rig (code 28); would confirm which app opened and pre-check the top hit before ENTER.
  10. shortcut#13 (open URL) GET /api/shortcut/exec/url?id=<list>&url=<scheme://...>&outtime=<ms> — deterministic alternative worth benchmarking: deep-link the app instead of searching for it.

Needs

  • Full Keyboard Access on with 1 s auto-hide; not queryable over the API.
  • AssistiveTouch on at max sensitivity, and Trackpad & Mouse speed max; the menu only appears while the board is cabled, itself a diagnostic that control is alive.
  • Each phone bound to its board (/device/set with vid+pid together) at /config/usb/get state 2.
  • location_crc non-empty on every target, or /mouse/* returns code 11.
  • Every phone in the id list sharing the same imgw/imgh as the master (500x1080 here); a different-sized model needs its own coordinate set.
  • Portrait lock on, Auto-Lock Never, StandBy off.
  • Siri Suggestions in Search turned off per phone, once, by hand, so the top hit is deterministic rather than usage-ranked; invisible to the API.
  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in; with only IMService.exe up, both phones reported state 0 and an empty board list.
  • For non-ASCII app names, and for the /shortcut/exec/url alternative: iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-edited, run once with all prompts allowed, and hotkey-bound; not verified present on this rig.
  • For confirming which app opened: the OCR plug-in installed and connected, plus the image-search plug-in if used; currently absent, /pic/ocr returns code 28.

Watch out

  • The launch half is native and fully multi-id; the verification half is not. Without OCR you get "the screen changed by N pixel units," not "Instagram is open."
  • Whether a board-driven pointer drag actually triggers iOS's Spotlight pull-down gesture is unverified on this rig. It is more likely to work than an even-odds guess, since the home-screen reveal is a distance-threshold gesture rather than the velocity-gated edge-swipe app switcher, but that raises confidence without removing the need to verify once against real hardware, since AssistiveTouch's synthesized touch path is not guaranteed identical to a finger's.
  • Do not pass len together with explicit sx/sy/ex/ey on /mouse/swipe; the doc only auto-derives coordinates from the percentage when they are 0. The XP swipe table also mislabels sx/ex as "y coordinate," confirmed a copy-paste error; they are start/end x,y.
  • /key/sendkey key is ASCII only in both editions; an app whose Spotlight-searchable name is not Latin cannot be typed this way and needs the clipboard+paste route instead.
  • Spotlight ranking is suggestion-driven per phone; until Siri Suggestions in Search is off everywhere, ENTER can open a web result or an App Store card instead of the app, and without OCR you will not know which happened.
  • /mouse/reset must run first: a phone in the stuck-click state still accepts every typed step and hotkey, so the sequence looks healthy right up to the fallback tap, which silently does nothing.
  • Do not use fn_key=Home in place of WIN+h here; Home needs kernel 2026.2.27+ and targets the iOS 26.1+ fix, while these phones run 18.7.10.
  • Timing is undocumented at three points, Spotlight's open animation, typing rate and query latency; the slow XR cannot be observed faster than ~220 ms per frame, so no timeout should assume 30 fps.
  • /shortcut/exec/url is more deterministic than Spotlight ranking, but the Phonefarm sibling marks the whole shortcut dispatcher "professional version only" and the Shortcut install is unverified here; prove it with /shortcut/device/ip?state=0 before designing around it.
  • Full Keyboard Access's on-screen affordances could race with the injected keystrokes; if the phone briefly shows its own predictive-text bar, the typed string could be autocorrected before ENTER, with no server-side way to detect this without OCR.
  • A truncated search string, the field losing focus mid-stream, could still return a plausible top hit and open the wrong app silently; there is no way to detect a partial type without full-screen OCR.
  • This is ordinary device automation on phones the operator owns and controls; it does not touch any platform's anti-abuse surface. The real risks are local: an open-loop launch can leave a phone sitting in Spotlight, Notification Center or Safari while later steps run against the wrong screen, so gate the next step on a frame diff; the stuck-click state makes a broken phone look healthy, so distinguish control-ready from video-ready rather than inferring either from "the app appeared to open"; and the API has no authentication at all, so firewall 9911 and 17000 to trusted hosts.

Scale

Steps that move the pointer or type are one request for the entire rack regardless of size, since /mouse/reset, /key/sendkey, /mouse/swipe and /mouse/click all take comma id lists and the boards walk in parallel; a 200 px pull-down costs about 120 ms whether it drives 2 phones or 19. Verification is the only per-phone cost, at p50 2 ms for a raw BMP frame with pollers measured fully independent of the input stream (up to 512 req/s across ten pollers). The real ceiling is the phone's own AirPlay source rate, not the kernel: about 29 new frames/s on one XR here versus 4.5 on its identical twin. The full normalize-search-launch cycle is roughly 2-4 seconds of pointer/API time for the entire bound id list, implying on the order of 900-1500 launch cycles per hour run back-to-back, with that aggregate figure essentially unchanged whether it targets 1 phone or 19, since fan-out cost does not scale with device count.

SMS and OTP retrieval

OTP and SMS relay by cropping the Messages or Notification Center screen for an external recogniser

Plus external toolingWith caveats

iOS hands SMS content to no API, and this rig has no server-side OCR, so the mirror frame is the only extraction surface: drive the phone to the message, crop the bubble or banner, run OCR client-side on the raw bitmap, and pattern-match the code out. This closes the one gap the API cannot close by design: Phonefarm's shortcut id 12 "Send SMS" is struck through in the vendor's own table, and XP has no SMS function in either direction. Scope this to SIMs and accounts you own, such as signing in to your own services, receiving your own 2FA codes across the rack, or QA-ing your own SMS delivery and message rendering.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get?id=<deviceid> — confirm the phone is live (state non-0, air_pid set) and read imgw/imgh, 500 x 1080 on these XRs, for every rect and tap that follows.
  2. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<id> — clear a stuck-click state before any tap-critical sequence; measured on this rig, a tap can otherwise silently do nothing (0.09 mean pixel diff) while moves and hardware keys keep working.
  3. none GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<id>&fn_key=NoticeBar — preferred, layout-independent route: open Notification Center by hotkey rather than hunting for the Messages icon, since the two XRs have different home screens and wallpapers.
  4. send_key WIN+h x2, then click GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<id>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice), then GET /api/mouse/click?id=<id>&x=<x>&y=<y>&button=1 — fallback route: two Home presses normalize to page one, then tap the Messages icon at coordinates mapped by hand for that specific phone. No OCR or image search is available to find the icon automatically, so this map is per device.
  5. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true&rect=[l,t,r,b] — crop the frame to the bubble or banner. rect is a flat [Left, Up, Right, Down] array in XP, not Phonefarm's four corner points. binary=true returns raw bottom-up BMP bytes with no JSON envelope, 2 ms for a full frame.
  6. ocr / ocr_ex none usable — /pic/ocr, /pic/ocr-ex, /pic/find-text and /pic/find-text-ex all return data.code 28 — recognition has to run client-side on the decoded bitmap; the server plug-in is not connected on this rig, and there is no verified fallback.
  7. none none — pattern-match the expected code shape (length, charset) rather than grabbing any digits, and reject a low-confidence or wrong-shaped read instead of guessing.
  8. send_text / shortcut#10 + paste POST /api/shortcut/clipboard/set {id, text, sleep}, then GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<id>&fn_key=WIN+v — optional: hand the code back into a field on a device you own. id takes a comma list. ASCII-only codes can skip the clipboard entirely and go straight in with /api/key/sendkey?key=<digits>.
  9. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true — confirm the new screen arrived by thresholding mean absolute pixel difference above roughly 1 (idle floor 0.02-0.03, a real reaction 20-160); never MD5-compare, since an untouched mirrored phone never repeats a frame.

Needs

  • An external OCR engine running client-side on the decoded bitmap; the server plug-in answers data.code 28, and the /shortcut/other/ocr fallback is undocumented beyond its path name and needs iMouse Shortcut v1.3+
  • A SIM in the phone receiving the SMS, and ownership of both the SIM and the account the code belongs to
  • Mirroring live for the read, and a bound working board for the navigation taps
  • A per-phone coordinate map for the Messages icon if using the hand-mapped route; none is shared across the two XRs
  • Notification previews enabled on that phone (Settings > Notifications > Messages > Show Previews set to "Always") if using the NoticeBar route; the API cannot read that setting, and "When Unlocked" or "Never" leaves NoticeBar blank
  • iMouse Shortcut installed and bound only if relaying via the clipboard; typing an ASCII code with /key/sendkey needs no Shortcut

Watch out

  • Every step except recognition is documented XP, already verified elsewhere on this rig; only OCR is off-rig, and there is no server-side fallback while the plug-in is missing, so "achievable" rests on an unverified external component with no measured accuracy or error rate
  • rect on /pic/screenshot is written with literal brackets, [l,t,r,b], unlike every other multi-value XP parameter in this doc set which uses bare comma-separation; confirm the kernel actually parses it rather than silently returning the full frame, which would still work for OCR but destroy the throughput benefit of cropping
  • rect combined with binary=true is documented as two independent flags but was not probed on this rig; check the returned byte count against the expected crop size before trusting it
  • Fully per-device on the read side: /pic/screenshot is single-id, so navigation can fan out over a comma id list but every screenshot is one phone at a time
  • Small text on a 500 x 1080 mirror is the weak link; crop tightly and treat a low-confidence read as a failure rather than a guess
  • Sending SMS is not available in any form, Phonefarm shortcut id 12 is struck through and XP has no SMS endpoint at all, so this chain is read-only
  • Codes expire in seconds while the slower XR yields only ~4.5 new frames/s; budget navigation and settle time, and gate the wait on a real change-detection threshold rather than a fixed sleep, or the frame you OCR was captured before the banner rendered
  • Automating login or OTP retrieval through the UI, rather than an official API, is a pattern many services' fraud and bot-detection systems flag regardless of whether the account is self-owned; repeated automated app opens plus screen scraping around auth flows is a real operational cost to weigh, not just a legal footnote
  • Some banking and 2FA apps suppress lock-screen and notification-center previews for security-sensitive codes by design; when that is the case, NoticeBar returns nothing and the hand-mapped Messages-app fallback, with its own per-device coordinate map, is mandatory rather than optional
  • Reading SMS or relaying codes for a SIM or account you do not own, or without the holder's consent, breaks the terms of service of essentially every service that sends them and may be unlawful depending on jurisdiction; confine this to your own devices, SIMs and accounts
  • Codes are short-lived secrets: do not write them to logs, on-disk screenshots or a shared queue, and delete the cropped frames after use
  • The API is unauthenticated on port 9911; anything on the LAN can drive these phones and pull the same frames, so firewall it
  • Crops of a Messages screen also capture unrelated content from real correspondents, a privacy decision to make before turning the capture on, not after

Scale

Strictly serial on the read side: /pic/screenshot is single-device only, and recognition is per-frame and per-phone. Navigation is cheap and fans out, since /key/sendkey and /mouse/click take comma-separated id lists and a board walks every listed phone in parallel, but the sequence is dominated by pointer travel (about 0.6 ms/px) plus the settle wait for a fresh frame, roughly 35 ms on the faster XR and 220 ms on the slower one. End to end that is a few seconds per code on one phone. For a single OTP, external wait (SMS or carrier delivery, typically 3-30 s) dominates over the API calls themselves, and the realistic ceiling is tens of retrievals per hour per phone, set by upstream resend cooldowns rather than rig throughput. Screenshot polling itself scales linearly per phone (84 req/s/phone measured), so across the rack aggregate throughput tracks phone count up to the number of accounts and SIMs available; the API is not the bottleneck anywhere in this chain.

MARK-ECOMMERCE-MARK

Section 6 · Commerce, customer and business operations

Commerce, customer and business operations

This is where the rack earns its keep on a resale or storefront operation: listing, restocking, price sweeps, support replies, live-shopping control and pre-launch verification. Every one of these builds on the same three primitives from Section 3 — /mouse/*, /key/sendkey and /pic/screenshot — plus, for anything that needs Unicode text or file transfer, the iMouse Shortcut app installed and hotkey-bound on each phone. Two facts shape almost every card below: the OCR and image-search plug-ins are not connected on this rig (every call returns data.code 28), so verification is client-side pixel comparison rather than reading text off the screen; and none of this makes a platform's anti-automation detection or its terms of service go away, so each card states the risk plainly and stops there.

Listing and catalog operations

Photo-to-listing publisher for mobile-only seller apps

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Turns a folder of edited photos plus a CSV of titles, descriptions and prices into draft or published listings inside apps that expose no listing API to ordinary sellers — Depop, Poshmark, Vinted, Etsy Seller and similar. The PC pushes photos into the phone's album, opens the app, taps through the Sell flow, pastes title and description, types the price, taps Publish and checks the result, all in mirror-pixel coordinates. This is the single largest labour cost in a resale operation, and it is the most demanding card in this section to stand up.

How

  1. get_device_list /device/get — read imgw/imgh per phone (500x1080 on this rig); every coordinate below is in that space, not the 414x896 logical size.
  2. mouse_reset_pos /mouse/reset?id=a,b,c — clear the silent stuck-click state before any tap-critical run; /mouse/up does not clear it.
  3. send_key /key/sendkey?id=a,b,c&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — normalise every phone to home page one.
  4. shortcut#7 /shortcut/album/upload?id=<ids>&files=[...]&zip=1&outtime=60000 — push this SKU's photos; the response's newest-10 album records are the documented proof they landed.
  5. shortcut#13 /shortcut/exec/url?id=<ids>&url=<scheme> — open the app at its Sell screen, if the app publishes a URL scheme; otherwise tap its icon.
  6. click /mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=&y= — tap Sell/+, select album cells, tap Done. Do not assume the newest photos are the first grid cells; confirm from the /shortcut/album/upload response before proceeding.
  7. send_text /shortcut/clipboard/set?id=<ids>&text=<title> then /key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+v — paste Unicode-safe title and description; XP has no async Chinese-text path, so clipboard+paste is the only route.
  8. send_key /key/sendkey?id=<ids>&key=1999 — type the ASCII price directly, after fn_key=WIN+a to select the pre-filled default.
  9. swipe /mouse/swipe?id=<ids>&direction=up&len=0.5 — scroll to category, size and condition pickers.
  10. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true — tap Publish, then compare a crop against a golden crop by mean absolute pixel difference (idle floor 0.02–0.03, a real reaction 20–160). Single id only, so one request per phone.
  11. shortcut#3 /shortcut/album/del?id=<ids>&list=[...] — remove the pushed photos so the next SKU's are again the newest. Irreversible once granted.

Needs

  • iMouse Shortcut installed on every phone, IP-configured, run once with all permissions, and bound to an AssistiveTouch custom key via the console's Send Binding Key — a one-time per-phone setup, not something a comma-separated id list gives you for free.
  • Board bound and connected (/config/usb/get state 2, non-empty vid/pid/uid) and a live control channel, since the Shortcut is launched by a HID hotkey through the board.
  • Phone-side accessibility settings invisible to the API: AssistiveTouch on with tracking sensitivity max, Full Keyboard Access on, Trackpad & Mouse tracking speed max, Auto-Lock never, portrait lock.
  • Seller app already logged in, on a version whose coordinate map you have captured from a raw BMP — per phone, since the two XRs on this rig have different home screens.
  • IMConsole.exe running and the kernel licensed; with only IMService.exe up, the board list comes back empty.

Watch out

  • A mean-pixel-diff proves the screen changed, not that the listing published: a validation-error toast changes the screen by the same 20–160 magnitude as a real publish. With OCR unavailable, there is no way to read a "Listed successfully" string, so treat pixel-diff as "detects that something happened" and have a human review a sampled subset of listings before trusting a batch.
  • Coordinate maps are captured per app version and per phone layout — the two XRs already differ, so the tap sequence must be authored and dry-run twice, not written once and mirrored across the fleet.
  • App URL schemes are undocumented by the vendor and change between app versions; budget a tap-the-icon fallback.
  • Full Keyboard Access must be on for the price keystrokes to register; there is no API signal if it is off, so a mis-configured phone silently leaves the price at its prefilled default while the console reports success for every keystroke.
  • Automating listing creation on accounts you do not own or are not permitted to operate, or in a way built to evade a platform's anti-automation detection, is a terms violation; this card is scoped to owned, permitted accounts and includes no pacing or human-mimicry logic by design.

Trap Pixel-diff is not proof of a correct publish

Because the change-detection threshold (20–160) does not distinguish "listed" from "rejected with an error banner," never let a passing diff alone trigger /shortcut/album/del. Delete only after a sampled human check, at least until the OCR plug-in is installed and can read the confirmation text.

Scale

About 25 taps, 2–3 clipboard pastes and one album upload per listing, dominated by the board's ~0.6 ms/px pointer walk plus app settle time: 60–120 s per listing per phone is realistic. Content is per-phone (unique photos and text per listing), so the comma-separated id fan-out does not help the tap sequence itself — only the shared normalisation steps (/mouse/reset, WIN+h) batch. Phones are genuinely independent (measured 98.8 req/s while streaming moves and polling versus 78.7 idle), so N phones run N listings concurrently: roughly 30–60 listings/hour per phone, times phones in the rack, with a human sampling published listings as the real ceiling rather than the API.

Inventory photo round-trip: harvest camera roll, edit on PC, push back

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Staff photograph stock on any iPhone, dock it in a rack slot, and the PC pulls the new photos off with /shortcut/album/get plus /shortcut/album/down, runs background removal and colour correction externally, then pushes the finished set back with /shortcut/album/upload — to that same phone or fanned out to every seller phone in one request. The rack becomes the sync layer between camera roll and editing queue, replacing AirDrop-by-hand.

How

  1. dev_connect callback or get_device_list WS /api — dev_connect; or poll /device/get — notice a freshly docked phone. A non-zero state only proves the video channel; control readiness is a separate check via /config/usb/get.
  2. shortcut#1 /shortcut/album/get?id=<one id>&album_name=&num=200 — list the camera roll. Single id only, and XP has no date filter (unlike Phonefarm), so track "already seen" on the PC by name and create_time.
  3. shortcut#2 /shortcut/album/down?id=<one id>&list=[...]&zip=1&outtime=120000 — pull new photos to the PC. Files land in <install>\Shortcut\Media; the response carries no file list, so poll that folder for arrivals.
  4. External tooling — edit on the PC. The kernel neither transforms nor inspects images.
  5. shortcut#7 /shortcut/album/upload?id=<a,b,c>&files=[...]&album_name=Ready to list&zip=1 — push the finished set back, to one phone or many; id is comma-separated here, so one request fans the set to every seller phone.
  6. shortcut#3 / shortcut#5 /shortcut/album/del or /shortcut/album/clear — clean up originals once the PC copy is verified. Both irreversible once granted.
  7. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true — optional, weak spot-check only; the upload response's newest-album list is the real proof of arrival.

Needs

  • iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-edited, run once with all permissions and hotkey-bound on every phone that ever docks — including ad-hoc camera phones, which is the real friction here.
  • Shortcuts > Advanced set to allow sharing large amounts of data and deleting without confirmation.
  • Both channels up per docked phone: cabled to a bound board for the hotkey trigger, and on rack Wi-Fi for the byte transfer; airplane mode kills the transfer while leaving USB control alive.
  • A stable slot-to-role map (/device/group/set, /device/set gid+name, /device/group/get-dev) so the PC knows which uid is a camera drop-box versus a seller phone.

Watch out

  • The harvest side is single-id only, so pulling from several docked phones is serialized one request per phone; only the push-back direction actually batches. State this asymmetry up front rather than reading "harvest camera roll... push back" as symmetric.
  • The default outtime is 15000 ms — far too short for a hundred photos at once; raise it and poll the Media folder for arrivals rather than trusting the response.
  • Comparing file size between the phone's record and the PC copy is a weak integrity check: a truncated transfer or a HEIC-to-processed transcode can coincidentally match on size. Prefer a hash check, or at minimum require a human confirmation before the first several deletes.
  • Camera-roll harvesting pulls in whatever is on the roll, not just intentional stock photos — personal images and geotagged EXIF metadata included.
