With no server-side content filtering available, scope the harvest to a dedicated album rather than Recents, and strip metadata before anything downstream is published; this is a staff privacy matter, not just data hygiene.

Scale

Three to five API round trips per phone; everything else is photo bytes moving over that phone's own Wi-Fi through the Shortcut, so tens of seconds to a few minutes per hundred photos depending on link quality (the two XRs on this rig already differ 6x in AirPlay throughput, so expect similar variance here). Harvest is serialized per phone by the single-id rule, but N docked phones harvest concurrently via N connections since phones are independent at the API layer (512 req/s measured across ten concurrent pollers). Push-back is genuinely O(1) in phone count. The true bottleneck is the external editing step and Wi-Fi transfer time, not the kernel API.

Fleet-wide storefront maintenance

Fleet price-drop and relist sweep with mirrored taps

Native APIWith caveats

Runs the same open-item, edit-price, save (or relist) sequence across a group of seller phones. Every XP input endpoint takes a comma-separated id list and the board walks all listed phones in parallel, so the taps themselves cost the same wall time for nineteen phones as for one. Prices are ASCII digits typed straight through /key/sendkey, so this is the one card in the set whose input half needs no Shortcut anywhere in the loop.

How

  1. get_group_list / get_device_list /device/group/get → /device/group/get-dev?id=<gid> → /device/get?id=a,b,c — build the target id list. Exclude any phone with state 0, empty vid/pid, empty location_crc, or imgw/imgh different from the master.
  2. mouse_reset_pos /mouse/reset?id=a,b,c — clear stuck-click state across the whole target set; the load-bearing step (a stuck phone measured 0.09 mean diff on click versus 141.96 after reset).
  3. send_key /key/sendkey?id=a,b,c&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — normalise to home page one; confirm per phone with a whole-frame mean diff since layouts differ.
  4. click /mouse/click?id=a,b,c&x=&y=&button=1 — open the seller app, its listings tab and the first item. button is numeric (1–8), not the "left"/"right" strings from Phonefarm.
  5. send_key /mouse/click on price field → /key/sendkey fn_key=WIN+a → /key/sendkey key=1799 → /mouse/click Save — edit the price. Requires Full Keyboard Access on; there is no error signal if it is off.
  6. click /mouse/click?id=a,b,c&x=&y= — relist / renew / share variants; ordinary taps, no dedicated marketplace-action API exists in either edition.
  7. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true&rect=[l,t,r,b] — verify per phone before moving on; single id, so cheap but not batched.
  8. swipe / wheel /mouse/swipe?id=a,b,c&direction=up&len=0.4 or /mouse/wheel?id=a,b,c&direction=down&len=30&number=3 — advance to the next row; prefer wheel for list traversal since it skips the ~0.6 ms/px pointer walk entirely.

Needs

  • Every phone in the target set on the same seller-app version with the same list ordering and identical imgw/imgh — a coordinate is only a fair shared target if the same element sits there on all of them.
  • Boards bound at state 2, non-empty location_crc, and the full iOS accessibility checklist (AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, tracking speeds max, Auto-Lock never, portrait lock), proven per phone with /mouse/reset + /mouse/move and a pointer-box diff before trusting the sweep.
  • Groups created and populated first via /device/group/set and /device/set.

Watch out

  • The fan-out is real for input but not for observation: /pic/screenshot is single-id, so verification is one request per phone even though the taps are O(1). Split the framing: input is fully kernel-native and O(1); verification is kernel-native but O(N) and only proves pixels changed.
  • A /mouse/click response of data.code 0 only means the kernel accepted the call — the stuck-click state returns the same code while doing nothing, so the sweep must verify by frame and /mouse/reset must precede every tap-critical run.
  • Insert a screenshot check of the price field itself between typing and tapping Save, not only after Save — by the time a post-Save screenshot runs, a wrong or unregistered keystroke has already been committed.
  • A stable, identical listing-tab layout across every phone in the id list is a strong and fragile assumption for a real operation where sellers may have different listing counts, sort orders or app versions; a mismatch produces silent wrong-price edits across the whole batch with no server-side catch.
  • error_push is scoped to hardware/board failures and will not fire for a logically wrong outcome (wrong item selected, unfocused field) — it complements but cannot replace per-phone pixel-diff verification.

Trap One bad coordinate, N wrong edits

The same fan-out that makes this cheap makes mistakes expensive: a mirrored id list replicates one wrong coordinate or wrong price string instantly across every phone in the sweep. Dry-run each new app version on a single phone before enabling the id list, and keep an explicit human confirmation before any sweep that writes prices.

Scale

Input is genuinely O(1) in phone count: a click or move with nineteen ids costs the same wall time as one, since latency is a function of pointer distance (~0.6 ms/px), not fan-out. Verification is O(N) but cheap and independent (2 ms per raw BMP, no shared bottleneck). A 10-item sweep at ~6 taps per item runs to roughly 100–300 price edits/hour across the whole rack if verification checkpoints stay light — the real driver is the app's own settle time between taps, dropping sharply if a human reviews every screenshot before advancing, which the fragility of the shared-coordinate assumption argues for on any new app version.

Customer messaging and live commerce

Human-in-the-loop support reply desk over live mirrors

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

An agent works a console showing the live mirror of each support phone — WhatsApp Business, Instagram DMs, marketplace chat — picks a conversation and a reply, and the console taps and types on the phone in mirror-pixel space. ASCII replies go straight through /key/sendkey; anything with emoji, accents or non-Latin text goes through the phone clipboard. A cropped screenshot confirms the bubble appeared. Every reply stays human-composed or human-approved and human-triggered.

How

  1. get_device_list /device/get — read imgw/imgh per phone, the coordinate space for every tap below.
  2. mouse_reset_pos /mouse/reset?id=<comma list> — clear stuck-click state whenever the agent switches phone or before any tap-critical reply.
  3. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<one>&binary=true — live mirror in the console; XP has no push-video stream, so this is a poller per phone on a fixed period, not a broadcast.
  4. click /mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=&y=&button=1 — tap the conversation row, then the compose field.
  5. send_key /key/sendkey?id=<ids>&key=<ascii> — ASCII fast path, including a quick-reply trigger the app itself matches; the API only delivers characters.
  6. shortcut#10 /shortcut/clipboard/set?id=<comma list>&text=<utf8>&sleep=1&outtime=15000 — Unicode/emoji/RTL reply text to the clipboard; one broadcast can reach many phones since id is comma-separated, but serialise per phone since the clipboard is a single shared slot.
  7. send_key fn_key /key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+v — paste into the focused field.
  8. click /mouse/click — tap the app's own Send control, kept bound to an explicit agent action; do not rely on fn_key=ENTER, since hardware Return behaves differently per app.
  9. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<one>&binary=true&rect=[l,t,r,b] — confirm the bubble appeared by mean absolute pixel difference; no text verification is possible on this rig.
  10. shortcut#10 /shortcut/clipboard/set?id=<ids>&text= — clear the clipboard after each reply so customer PII does not sit there.
  11. shortcut#24 /shortcut/device/ip?id=<one>&state=0 — cheapest proof the Shortcut path is alive on a phone; run before the desk opens, not per reply.

Needs

  • Board bound per phone at state 2 with non-empty location_crc, and the full iOS accessibility checklist, none of it queryable over the API.
  • iMouse Shortcut installed and bound (Send Binding Key) on every phone for the Unicode path, with Shortcuts > Advanced allowing scripts and large data.
  • A per-app coordinate map (thread row, compose field, Send, attachment picker), refreshed after app updates and per phone layout.
  • Agent accounts and business profiles the operator legitimately owns.

Watch out

  • One HID pointer per phone means one agent can drive a given handset at a time; two agents cannot work the same phone's thread list concurrently without racing the pointer and the single clipboard slot — enforce an explicit per-phone lock in the desk UI.
  • No server-side verification exists: the mean-pixel-diff bubble check catches gross failures (nothing sent) but not a reply sent with wrong or garbled text from a stale clipboard, and it cannot read a "message not delivered" banner.
  • A timed-out Shortcut launch (data.code 30, "Call timeout") pastes stale or empty clipboard content into a live reply; check the Shortcut's liveness before treating a paste as safe to send.
  • /key/sendkey has no documented per-key timing, rate limit or maximum length — it has not been measured on this rig the way pointer movement has. Measure typed-length versus latency before relying on it for long templated replies.
  • Platform terms forbid automated bulk or unsolicited messaging; this design is defensible only because a human composes or approves and triggers every send — never wire the Send tap to a scheduler.

Tip Blank the clipboard after every reply

Customer names, addresses and order numbers otherwise sit on the phone clipboard until overwritten, and every clipboard call crosses an unauthenticated LAN endpoint. Fold the clear-clipboard step into the send action itself rather than treating it as optional cleanup.

Scale

Per-reply API overhead is small next to human read/compose time: ASCII path roughly 200–500 ms, Unicode/clipboard path 1–5 s bounded by outtime. Ten concurrent pollers sustained 512 req/s at p50 3 ms with no interference between input traffic and frame polling, so the mirror wall itself costs nothing. Realistic agent throughput is roughly 60–150 replies/hour across several multiplexed phones, gated by the human and by serialising the clipboard and pointer per phone, not by the rig.

Live-commerce control room: product pinning and comment replies

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

A dedicated "producer" phone per live stream runs the seller's LIVE control surface — product showcase panel and comments — while the host streams from a separate handset outside the rack. A scheduled script rotates the pinned product by tapping captured coordinates; operator-approved comment replies go through the clipboard-and-paste path; a moderator watches every stream on a wall of screenshot pollers, one per producer phone.

How

  1. get_device_list /device/get — read imgw/imgh, state and rotate per producer phone; exclude any whose imgw/imgh differs from the phone the coordinate map was captured on.
  2. set_group / set_dev /device/group/set?id=0&name=live-producers then /device/set?id=<list>&gid=<gid>&name=Slot-01 — create the producer group and assign slots.
  3. mouse_reset_pos /mouse/reset?id=<list> — clear stuck-click state before each scheduled pin; a pin that silently never happened is invisible unless you verify.
  4. click /mouse/click?id=<one>&x=&y=&button=1 — tap the shopping-bag icon, the product row, then Pin; drive each phone with its own coordinate set since row counts can differ.
  5. swipe /mouse/swipe?id=<ids>&direction=up&len=0.3 — scroll the product list between pins.
  6. shortcut#10 /shortcut/clipboard/set?id=<list>&text=<utf8>&sleep=1&outtime=15000 then send_key fn_key /key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+v and click Send — operator-approved comment reply, kept human-triggered.
  7. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<one>&binary=true — moderator wall, one poller per phone; measured a 30 fps wall costs the master view nothing.
  8. send_key fn_key /key/sendkey?id=<list>&fn_key=MuteSoundSwitch — keep the rack silent without dropping the cast, unlike /device/airplay/set air_audio which disconnects and reconnects.
  9. dev_rotate callback ws://<pc>:9911/api — react to orientation changes; every stored coordinate must be re-derived when imgw/imgh swap meaning.
  10. auto_connect_screen /device/airplay/connect (disconnect first, XP has no force flag) — recover a producer phone that lost its mirror; may fail with code 15 or 28 since the plug-ins the vendor's own navigation relies on are absent here.

Needs

  • Producer phones signed into the seller's own account with LIVE shopping enabled; the host stream runs on a separate handset that need not be in the rack.
  • A coordinate map of the LIVE control layout per app version and per phone layout, with a re-capture routine after app updates.
  • iMouse Shortcut installed and bound on each producer phone for non-ASCII replies.
  • A persistent WebSocket connection for dev_rotate, dev_disconnect, error_push and airplay_connect_log, with its own reconnect logic — a dropped socket produces silence, not an event.
  • Licence headroom: dev_online_num within total_license, or phones are refused with "not logged in, not allowed online."

Watch out

  • Every pin is fire-and-forget unless verified: with OCR absent, there is no way to read "Pinned" back, only a mean-pixel-diff against a golden frame — and a silently failed pin looks identical to a working one. Gate the next scheduled pin on that diff succeeding, not just alert after the fact, or a stuck-click phone will silently skip every future pin in the run.
  • Only two of nineteen boards were ever observed mirroring simultaneously on this rig. Treat concurrent producer-phone streams as validated at n=2, single digits pending a real multi-phone test, not the board count.
  • A pinned-product rotation script that fires on a fixed schedule regardless of what is on screen (a checkout modal, an ad interstitial, a permission prompt) taps blind — nothing in the chain checks current screen state before the next scheduled sequence.
  • Per-phone AirPlay source rate varies enormously on identical hardware; some tiles will look laggy for reasons no setting fixes.

Trap A muted tile is a dropped tile

/device/airplay/set air_audio disconnects and reconnects the cast to mute, which drops that moderator tile for the reconnect duration during a live. Default to the hardware fn_key=MuteSoundSwitch, which does not touch the cast, and treat air_audio as a fallback only.

Scale

Pinning is a handful of taps per minute per phone, negligible against the board's parallel id-list dispatch. The moderator wall scales for free per this rig's own numbers (512 req/s at ten concurrent pollers, p50 3 ms), and streaming input alongside polling measured no interference. The binding limits are per-phone AirPlay production (4.5–29 fps observed on identical hardware), LAN bandwidth per mirrored stream, and the licence's online-device count — not the rack's board count. Comment replies through the clipboard are seconds-scale round trips bounded by outtime, so they stay operator-paced by design.

Verification, compliance and monitoring

Coupon, loyalty and promo discount verification in the app

Plus external toolingWith caveats

Before a campaign goes out, drives a rack phone through the store app's cart, types the promo code, taps Apply, and captures a cropped screenshot of the totals box as evidence the advertised discount actually lands in the iOS app — catching the gap between a web-only discount and one that silently fails on mobile. Every input and capture step is proven on this rig; only turning the crop into a number has no working path today.

How

  1. send_key fn_key /key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — normalise to home page one; doubles as a liveness probe since it works even while the pointer is stuck.
  2. mouse_reset_pos /mouse/reset?id=<ids> — clear stuck-click state on the whole target set; skipping this is the single most likely cause of a false "coupon failed."
  3. click /mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=&y=&button=1 — open the app, open a known product, add to cart, open Cart, then tap the promo-code field to focus it.
  4. send_key /key/sendkey?id=<ids>&key=SAVE20 — type the ASCII coupon code; a non-ASCII code needs the clipboard-and-paste path instead.
  5. click /mouse/click — tap Apply.
  6. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true — poll at a fixed period until the totals area settles (mean-diff falling back toward the idle floor).
  7. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true&rect=[l,t,r,b] — capture just the totals box, in the same mirror-pixel space as the clicks.
  8. ocr / ocr-ex /pic/ocr, /pic/ocr-ex, /pic/find-text, /pic/find-text-ex — ALL UNAVAILABLE ON THIS RIG (data.code 28) — the intended way to read the discount amount; not usable until the plug-in is installed.
  9. Client-side mean-pixel-diff, or find_image/find_image_cv /pic/find-image or /pic/find-image-cv (plug-in status unverified here) — alternative assertion needing no OCR: compare the totals crop against its own prior value from a known-good run.
  10. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<id>&save_path=D:\iMouseXP\Screenshot\ — archive the full frame as the campaign record; the kernel writes the file and returns the path.
  11. click, send_key /mouse/click ... then /key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+h — remove cart lines and go Home for the next code; cart state is not queryable, so another screenshot is the only proof it is empty.

Needs

  • Store app signed in with a TEST account and a single-use test coupon code — a live code on a production account can consume a real redemption.
  • A coordinate map in mirror pixels per app version and per phone.
  • Control and video channels both ready (board state 2, phone bound; /device/get state non-zero with a live air_pid), plus the full iOS accessibility checklist.
  • For server-side reading only: the vendor OCR plug-in installed and connected, or a PC-side OCR library — external tooling this rig does not currently have.

Watch out

  • The read-the-number step does not work on this rig today: /pic/ocr returns data.code 28, and find-text, ocr-ex and find-text-ex sit behind the same plug-in.
  • A rejected code often re-renders the same totals with a small error toast, which can register as a real change (diff 20–160) even though the discount did not apply — diff the specific totals-number crop against its own prior value, not just "something changed" on the page.
  • Applying a promo code is a security-sensitive cart action in most storefronts, often gated by bot-detection or fraud SDKs. A code that fails only under automation looks, in the API's eyes, identical to a genuinely broken coupon (data.code 0 on every call) — the rig cannot distinguish "coupon broken" from "automation detected and silently blocked."
  • Only two of nineteen boards have a phone actually mirroring on this rig, so checks are serialized across those two devices today, not parallel across a fleet.

Trap "It worked" and "automation was blocked" look the same

Because every call still returns data.code 0 whether the coupon applied or a fraud filter silently intervened, a passing pixel-diff cannot separate a genuinely broken promo from one that platform defenses quietly suppressed. Treat a failed check as "investigate," not as proof the coupon itself is broken.

Scale

About 8–10 taps plus one settle-wait and one crop per code per phone: 15–30 s realistically, dominated by app response time, not the API. Input and capture do not contend (98.8 req/s with streaming input versus 78.7 idle). Tap steps batch across phones sharing a layout; screenshots do not (single-id, 2 ms each). Practical parallelism today is the two mirroring phones, giving roughly 240–480 checks/hour combined — not the 19 the board count implies.

Banking and PSP app availability heartbeat

Native APIWith caveats

A dedicated monitoring phone opens a merchant's banking, PSP or payout app on a schedule and confirms it reaches its expected login or dashboard screen, timing the launch and archiving a frame, so payout-day outages and forced-update walls are caught hours before someone notices a blank screen. Scope is deliberately "does the app open and render the expected screen" — no automated login, no credential entry, ever.

How

  1. send_key fn_key, mouse_reset_pos /key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+h (twice), then /mouse/reset?id=<ids> — normalise and clear stuck-click state; WIN+h works even while the pointer is stuck, so it doubles as a board-liveness probe.
  2. click /mouse/click?id=<id>&x=&y=&button=1 — record t0 and tap the app icon.
  3. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true — poll frames at a fixed period until launch settles, recording elapsed time; no server-push frame stream exists on XP.
  4. Client-side mean-pixel-diff, or find_image/find_image_cv server-side equivalents plug-in-gated and unverified here — compare the settled frame's stable crop against a golden crop, and diff the banner region to flag a forced-update or maintenance wall.
  5. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true — detect capture-protected apps (near-uniform histogram on an otherwise-fresh frame) and report "renders but capture-protected," never "down."
  6. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<id>&save_path=D:\iMouseXP\Screenshot\ — archive the evidence frame.
  7. send_key fn_key, swipe /key/sendkey?fn_key=AppSwitch then /mouse/swipe, or fn_key=WIN+h — leave the phone clean for the next check.
  8. get_device_list, get_usb_list, callbacks /device/get, /config/usb/get, dev_connect/dev_disconnect/usb_change on ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api — watch control and video channels independently rather than inferring health from one; a phone can be controllable with no picture, or visible with no control.

Needs

  • A dedicated monitoring phone that holds no real funds and is not anyone's primary banking device, signed in only as far as the screen you intend to assert on.
  • Golden crops per app per app version, captured at the same air_ratio, since crops are resolution-specific.
  • Board bound and connected, the full iOS accessibility checklist, and a PC-side scheduler — the kernel has no cron of its own.

Watch out

  • Never automate login. This is a launch/render probe, not a session driver; Face ID, a passcode prompt or an SMS one-time code end the probe at that screen, full stop.
  • Banking and PSP terms typically prohibit third-party automation and, often, screen mirroring of the app — confirm terms per app before wiring it into a schedule; this is a legal risk, not a technical one.
  • Capture protection is real and unverified here: an app that blanks its content while the screen is captured yields a flat frame that the heartbeat must distinguish from "down," or it pages someone every run. Banking apps are among the likeliest to implement this or to detect the AssistiveTouch pointer outright, degrading the probe to "launched, no evidence" for every run — verify this once per app before trusting it long-term.
  • A forced iOS update (Auto-Lock Never does not block it) can change the exact screen layout a golden crop was captured against, producing a false "down" alert that is really just a UI refresh; golden crops need a version-pinned refresh process.
  • IMConsole.exe is a GUI app whose absence silently zeroes out /device/get and /config/usb/get with no API-level alert — the heartbeat needs its own external process watchdog on IMConsole.exe, or a false "all apps down" page-out is inevitable the first time the console crashes.
  • A dropped WebSocket connection produces silence, not a callback; a heartbeat relying on dev_disconnect or error_push needs its own liveness ping and reconnect logic, since there is no documented WS heartbeat frame in the protocol.

Trap A reboot looks exactly like every app being down

A restart of the phone or kernel drops mirroring and leaves the phone at the lock screen; the probe must re-cast, and a passcode-protected phone will simply sit there with Full Keyboard Access still on but no board-driven way past the lock — which correctly cannot be automated. Without a distinct "stuck at lock screen" state, this reads as every monitored app failing at once.

Scale

A launch-and-capture cycle is a few seconds of wall time, almost all of it the app's own launch, so one monitoring phone can rotate through a dozen apps every 10 minutes comfortably. Raw BMP is 2 ms per frame at 84 req/s per phone, and input traffic does not slow polling or vice versa. Roughly 60–120 checks/hour on the one dedicated phone, bottlenecked by app launch time and by keeping the fleet to a single monitoring device, not by the API.

Automated video production

On-device video render farm driving CapCut/InShot templates

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Push raw clips and stills into each phone's album, drive a pre-favourited CapCut or InShot template with taps and drags, paste text overlays through the clipboard, wait out the export by polling a cropped progress bar, then pull the finished MP4 back and clean up. Every step routes through the iMouse iOS Shortcut, so the phones become a batch renderer for template styles that exist only inside the iOS apps, with no cloud render cost. TikTok Shop and Reels listings need many short vertical videos, and this is the only way to reach templates a desktop editor cannot reproduce.

How

  1. shortcut#7 (album upload) POST /api/shortcut/album/upload — seed raw clips and stills into every target phone's album in one call; id is a comma list, files is an array of PC paths, blank album_name means Recents, outtime is milliseconds (15 s default, raise it for large files).
  2. send_key, mouse_reset_pos, click, shortcut#13 /api/key/sendkey (WIN+h); /api/mouse/reset; /api/mouse/click; or POST /api/shortcut/exec/url — return Home, clear any stuck click, then open the editor app, either by icon tap or by URL scheme if the app publishes a usable one (unverified here).
  3. click, swipe, mouse_down/move/up /api/mouse/click, /api/mouse/swipe, /api/mouse/down+move+up — walk the template flow: pick the template, place media cells in order, preview, export. Coordinates are mirror pixels (500x1080 on the XRs); use a down-move-up drag for timeline scrubs rather than the canned swipe.
  4. shortcut#10 + send_key POST /api/shortcut/clipboard/set then GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+v — fill a text overlay, including non-ASCII, by setting the clipboard (comma id list, sleep in seconds) then pasting. XP has no async send_text/send_text_ok, so this two-call sequence is the only documented Unicode path.
  5. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?binary=true&rect=[l,t,r,b] — poll a crop of the progress bar, single-id only, and judge completion by mean absolute pixel difference against the prior crop, not by hash; poll every 250-500 ms since exports run minutes.
  6. click, shortcut#1 (album get) /api/mouse/click then GET /api/shortcut/album/get?num=1 — tap Save/Done, then read back the exported file's name, extension and create_time; single-id, and there is no date filter on XP so the newest item must be inferred from create_time, not position.
  7. shortcut#2 (album down) POST /api/shortcut/album/down {id, list:[{album_name,name,ext}], zip, outtime} — pull the MP4 back to the PC; single-id, name and extension are split fields, lands in <install dir>\Shortcut\Media, and the response carries no file manifest.
  8. shortcut#3 (album del) + send_key POST /api/shortcut/album/del then /api/key/sendkey (WIN+h) — delete the raw inputs and export, comma id list, then return the phone Home. /shortcut/album/clear wipes an entire album and has no Phonefarm counterpart; treat it as destructive.
  9. shortcut#4/#5 (file get/down) GET /api/shortcut/file/get then POST /api/shortcut/file/down — alternate route when the app exports to Files instead of the album; iOS 15+ only (fine on the 18.7.10 XRs), single-id, lands in <install dir>\Shortcut\File.
  10. find_image / find_image_ex / ocr /api/pic/find-image-cv, /api/pic/ocr, /api/pic/find-multi-color — the intended version-proof way to detect app state instead of tapping blind; OCR returns code 28 (unavailable) on this rig and the image-match plug-ins are unprobed, so this step does not work today.

Needs

  • iMouse iOS Shortcut installed on every phone, kernel IP edited in, run once with all permissions allowed, and bound to an AssistiveTouch key. Not evidenced on this rig; prove it first with GET /api/shortcut/device/ip returning code 0 and the expected IP before building anything on top.
  • Shortcuts > Advanced enabled per phone: allow running scripts, allow sharing large data, allow deleting without confirmation, allow deleting large data.
  • iOS 15+ for the file endpoints (18.7.10 on the XRs qualifies); board bound and connected, since the Shortcut launches via a HID hotkey; mirroring live to see and drive the editor UI.
  • CapCut or InShot installed, signed in, target templates pre-favourited, and a coordinate map per app version in 500x1080 mirror pixels.
  • Free storage for raw inputs plus export on each phone; Full Keyboard Access on for WIN+v paste; Auto-Lock set to Never so a multi-minute export does not sleep the phone.
  • Per-device licensing headroom: devices are refused online when unlicensed, so check dev_online_num against total_license via /config/user/info, not an edition gate.

Watch out

  • Until /shortcut/device/ip returns code 0, the upload, clipboard, album-get, album-down and album-del steps do not function at all. That is most of what makes this a render farm rather than plain template navigation, so treat those specific steps as not achievable, not merely caveated, until that one proof call succeeds.
  • XP has no generic shortcut dispatcher: each function is its own path with typed parameters. Phonefarm's double-encoded parameter JSON, devlist array and string retdata do not exist here, and outtime is milliseconds on XP versus seconds on Phonefarm.
  • album/get, album/down, file/get, file/down, clipboard/get and every /pic/* call are single-id; only upload/del/clear/clipboard-set/exec-url fan out to a comma list. Pull-backs and screen verification are per phone, so wall-clock scaling with phone count is much worse than the fan-out steps alone suggest.
  • "Newest album item = first in the picker" is app behavior that breaks the moment anything else writes to the album, including a prior run's own export. Sequence runs so only the intended assets are recent, or select by create_time from album/get.
  • No working server-side state detection exists today: OCR returns code 28 and the image-match plug-ins are unprobed. Every tap returns code 0 even when it lands on nothing, so a blind coordinate chain fails silently; the actual working method is client-side pixel-diff against a golden crop, which still breaks on layout drift between app versions.
  • CapCut/InShot template editing routinely uses pinch-to-zoom and two-finger trims. The rig has one HID pointer per phone with no native multi-touch; AssistiveTouch's gesture menu can simulate a pinch only through its own on-screen menu, which is slower and less reliable than the single-pointer drag this chain otherwise uses, so not every template interaction is covered.
  • Transfers and the phone's own encoder dominate wall clock, and they share Wi-Fi with AirPlay mirroring. Plan outtime and timing against the low end of the measured bandwidth range (roughly 5 Mbps), not an average, since mirroring runs concurrently and is not controllable through the API; a slow phone's mirroring also degrades further during a transfer storm.
  • The album/down response carries only code, id and message, no file manifest; verify the file actually landed in <install dir>\Shortcut\Media rather than trusting code 0.
  • Watermarks, template licensing and app subscription tier are phone-local facts the API cannot see or change. CapCut and InShot terms of service may restrict automated use; check before running this at volume, and never point a delete-without-confirmation cleanup step at a phone's Recents if it holds anything a person cares about.
  • The API is unauthenticated on the LAN, so any host on the network can upload into, or download out of, any phone's album. Firewall port 9911 and treat the kernel's IP as a trust boundary.

Scale

Taps are cheap; transfers and the phone's own encoder dominate. A roughly 100 MB clip in and 50 MB out per phone means outtime needs to be in the minutes (180000 ms upload, 300000 ms download are reasonable starting points, counted in milliseconds on XP). Upload, delete and clipboard-set fan out to a comma id list in one call; album/get and album/down do not, so pull-backs run sequentially per phone though concurrently across phones. Progress-bar polling is independent per phone and does not contend with input traffic (measured at 83-512 req/s across 2-10 pollers, p50 3 ms). With the Shortcut verified and working, expect on the order of a few videos per hour per phone once transfer and export time are counted, roughly 2 to 6 videos/hour across the two phones actually online today. A 19-phone, 300-video/hour figure is a projection only; this rig has 19 boards but two phones mirroring, the wall has never been tested past two, and Wi-Fi bandwidth is the first thing likely to break above that.

Also worth knowing

Content and asset production

Store, documentation and marketing asset harvest across locales

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Producing App Store screenshots, support and documentation screenshots, and app-preview or marketing video clips is recurring, scheduled work, done again for every release and every locale. This card treats it as its own production line rather than a one-off QA check, reusing the deep-link and hardware-hotkey chain from the cross-device and localization QA card and the Control Center recording chain from the QA screen-recording card, but running them for design and marketing deliverables instead of a layout diff. The rack's advantage over a person with one phone is repeatability across locales and screens, not resolution or device coverage, both of which stay bounded by whatever is physically docked.

How

  1. set_dev / get_device_list GET /api/device/set?id=<id>&name=xr-de-DE then GET /api/device/get. Label one phone per locale, and per device model if more than the two XRs ever join the rack, so harvested files can be filed correctly. Read imgw/imgh, 500 x 1080 on this rig, before any capture.
  2. shortcut#13 GET /api/shortcut/exec/url?id=<id1>,<id2>,...&url=myapp://screen/onboarding&outtime=15000. Land every locale phone on the target screen in one fan-out request, the same deep-link approach as the QA card.
  3. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<one>&rect=[l,t,r,b]&save_path=D:\Assets\<locale>\. For documentation and support screenshots, the mirror frame is good enough for a help article, so capture and crop straight to disk with no Shortcut hop and no album round trip at all. This is the cheap path, and it does not need the Shortcut app installed.
  4. send_key (shift+win+3) GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<id1>,<id2>,...&fn_key=shift+win+3. For App Store screenshots, fire the phone's own hardware screenshot into Photos at native resolution, 828 x 1792 on this rig's XRs, above anything the AirPlay mirror can produce. Needs Full Keyboard Access on. The fan-out is free since fn_key takes a comma list.
  5. shortcut#1 then shortcut#2 then shortcut#3 GET /api/shortcut/album/get?id=<one>&num=1, then POST /api/shortcut/album/down {id, list, zip:1, outtime:60000}, then POST /api/shortcut/album/del {id, list}. Find the new still by create_time, pull it to <install dir>\Shortcut\Media, then delete it off the phone so the next locale's capture is unambiguous. All three are single-id, so a still harvest is strictly one phone at a time.
  6. send_key (fn_key=ControlBar) + click GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=ControlBar then GET /api/mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=<tile x>&y=<tile y>. For app-preview and marketing clips, open Control Center and tap the Screen Recording tile to start, run the scripted flow, then repeat the same tap to stop. This is the QA card's chain, reused for a deliverable instead of a bug report.
  7. shortcut#1 / shortcut#2 / shortcut#3 as above, ext "mp4". Pull the RPReplay clip the same way as a still, with a generous outtime since a clip is tens of megabytes.
  8. none (manual) none. Switch each phone's display language by hand for the next locale. There is no API for this on either edition, and it restarts SpringBoard, so schedule the switch outside the automated run and re-cast AirPlay afterward before capturing again.

Needs

  • iMouse Shortcut installed on every phone used for stills or video, IP-edited, run once with all permissions, bound to an AssistiveTouch key; Shortcuts > Advanced set to allow large data and deleting without confirmation.
  • One physical phone per locale to capture concurrently, and one physical phone per required App Store size class to cover more than a single size. Both boards mirroring on this rig carry the same model, iPhone XR, so today this pipeline can produce exactly one size class.
  • Full Keyboard Access on, AssistiveTouch on, Auto-Lock never, portrait lock, the same accessibility checklist as every other Shortcut-dependent card in this document.
  • Deep links for every screen that needs an asset, since nothing in the vendor docs describes how the Shortcut chain would navigate there without one.
  • A naming and tracking scheme kept entirely on the PC: the kernel does not tag a captured file with locale, screen, or device model, and /shortcut/album/get returns only name, extension, size, and create_time.

Watch out

  • shift+win+4 ("screenshot and edit") opens the Markup editor on the captured frame instead of saving it, which needs further blind taps to dismiss. Use shift+win+3 for any unattended batch run; it saves to Photos on its own after the usual on-device thumbnail timeout.
  • /shortcut/other/screenshot exists on shortcut v1.3 and later as a stated fallback for "special cases," but the vendor page gives it no parameter table of its own; it just reuses /pic/screenshot's table under that heading. Whether it returns the AirPlay mirror frame or a native-resolution capture through the Shortcut app is not documented and was not probed on this rig; treat it as an unverified secondary route if AirPlay mirroring itself is down, not as a substitute for the confirmed shift+win+3 hotkey.
  • get_devicemodel_list is a static reference table of models the kernel recognizes, not a way to provision a size the rack does not physically have. Coverage of "every device size" is bounded by which phones are docked to a board, not by any API call.
  • Album functions are single-id for get, down, and del alike, so both the still and the video harvest serialize per phone even though landing on the screen and firing the hotkey are free fan-outs. A ten-locale, six-screen still harvest is 180 serial Shortcut round trips before any video is pulled.
  • A language switch drops the AirPlay session and needs a re-cast before the next capture; running it inside the same script as the capture loop, instead of as a separate manual step between locales, is what breaks a batch run silently.
  • Nothing in the chain confirms a captured asset actually shows the intended screen in the intended language: with no OCR plug-in connected, a wrong deep link or a locale that silently fell back to English produces a file that looks correct to every check available here. Budget a human pass over the harvested batch before it goes into a listing or a help article.
  • Video clips inherit the same caveats as the QA screen-recording card: a persistent AssistiveTouch overlay in the frame, a three-second start countdown to trim, and no report if an app blocks screen capture and records black.

Open What does the shortcut screenshot fallback actually capture

/shortcut/other/screenshot is named as one of the functions behind this card, but the documentation does not say whether it is a second route to the same 500 x 1080 mirror frame or a native-resolution capture taken through the Shortcut app itself. That distinction matters for App Store assets specifically. Confirm it against a real device before building a pipeline around it, and until then treat shift+win+3 as the only proven native-resolution route.

Scale

Landing on a screen is free per locale, one fan-out request regardless of count. Stills cost one Shortcut round trip per phone for get, down, and del each, on the order of 3 to 10 seconds per file measured elsewhere on this rig's Wi-Fi, so ten locales across six screens for stills alone is on the order of tens of minutes serial, not the minute a naive per-request estimate gives. A full-rack video pull runs 5 to 15 minutes serially at a generous 120-second outtime, per phone, for one clip apiece, since a one-minute recording is tens of megabytes. Documentation screenshots taken straight off the mirror with save_path are the fast path, at 2 milliseconds a frame with no Shortcut involved, and are the only piece of this card that scales the way the rest of the document's screenshot numbers do. Today's real ceiling is two phones, both iPhone XR, so a full store-asset refresh across many locales and multiple size classes needs more docked hardware, not a faster script.

MARK-DATA-MARK

Section 7 · Data collection, monitoring and verification

Data collection, monitoring and verification

Everything in this section answers one question: how do you get exact information off a phone's screen and back onto the PC. On this rig the answer is narrower than the vendor docs suggest, because the OCR plug-in is not connected (/pic/ocr answers data.code 28, "插件未连接") and the image-search plug-in has never been probed. That removes every server-side recognition path and leaves three native channels: the mirror frame itself (compared by pixels, never by hash), the iOS clipboard (exact text, no plug-in needed), and the iMouse Shortcut's own photo album (native-resolution files). All three are documented XP-native endpoints; none of the Shortcut-dependent ones have actually been exercised on this rig's two phones, so every card below is gated on a one-call smoke test before it earns any throughput number.

Tip One call proves the whole Shortcut channel is alive

Every card in this section that depends on the iMouse Shortcut (album, clipboard, custom probes, deep links) rides the same install-and-binding chain, and none of it has been probed on this rig. The cheapest possible proof is GET /api/shortcut/device/ip?id=<id>&state=0: a data.code 0 whose data.text equals the ip field from /device/get confirms the Shortcut is installed, IP-edited, hotkey-bound, and can reach the kernel on port 9911, all in one round trip. A 15 second wait ending in data.code 30 means the AssistiveTouch binding never fired the Shortcut, and nothing downstream in this section will work until that is fixed. Run it once per phone before building anything on top.

Reading on-screen text and numbers without OCR

Region OCR of prices and counters inside native apps

Needs plug-inWith caveats

When a number lives inside a native app and is not selectable text (in-app pricing, follower counts, creator dashboards), deep-link to the screen, let the mirror settle, then crop a fixed rectangle and OCR it. On this rig the kernel OCR plug-in reports data.code 28, so /pic/ocr and /pic/find-text are dead code today; the only path that actually works is fetching the raw mirror frame and running OCR client-side on the PC against that same rectangle.

How

  1. shortcut#13 /shortcut/exec/url?id=<ids>&url=<deep link> — jump straight to the product/profile/dashboard screen, skipping in-app navigation
  2. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true — fetch two raw frames ~300 ms apart, require mean absolute pixel difference under ~1 before trusting the screen has settled
  3. ocr /pic/ocr?id=<id>&rect=[l,t,r,b] — read the number from a fixed rectangle (flat four-integer array, not Phonefarm's four-corner-point form); confirmed dead on this rig, code 28
  4. — /pic/find-text?id=<id>&text=[…]&contain=true&similarity=0.8 — boolean check instead of parsing (e.g. "Out of stock" vs "Add to Cart"); same plug-in dependency, same dead result here
  5. — /shortcut/other/ocr — named as a Shortcut-side "special case" fallback (v1.3+) but has no parameter table in the docs; probe once before designing around it
  6. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true&rect=[l,t,r,b] — the only path that works today: kernel crops server-side, PC runs Windows.Media.Ocr or Tesseract on the strip
  7. mouse_reset_pos + click /mouse/reset?id=<ids> then /mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=<centre.x>&y=<centre.y> — optional: act on what was read, since OCR centres are already in mirror-pixel space

Needs

  • OCR plug-in installed and connected — not satisfied here; ocr_num in the kernel config is GPU-build only and a change needs /imserver/restart
  • For the deep-link and Shortcut-side fallback: the full iMouse Shortcut install/bind chain, plus Shortcut v1.3+
  • Stable air_ratio per device — rects live in imgw×imgh mirror pixels (500×1080 here), never the iOS logical 414×896
  • For the client-side fallback: an OCR engine on the PC plus a reused frame buffer (each 1.6 MB frame crosses the .NET Large Object Heap threshold)

Watch out

  • Treat steps 3-4 as dead code on this rig and build against the client-side fallback first; the kernel path is a drop-in once the plug-in is actually installed and a call returns code 0
  • rect here is a flat [left, top, right, bottom] array that must be JSON-then-URL-encoded in GET mode — a Phonefarm-shaped four-corner rect is a parameter error on this kernel
  • /pic/ocr, /pic/find-text and /pic/screenshot are all single-device — a rack sweep is one serialized round trip per phone at both capture and (once unblocked) recognition
  • The mirror is roughly 60% of the XR's linear panel resolution (~36% of the area); small captions sit at the edge of reliable OCR cap-height once downscaled. Raising air_ratio helps but invalidates every stored rect and disconnects the cast — a real design fork, not a footnote
  • similarity is the engine's own score, not a validated confidence figure — range-check the parsed value and require two consecutive settled frames to agree
  • Settle timing is per phone: the rig's two otherwise-identical XRs deliver roughly 29 and 4.5 new frames per second under motion, so a fixed settle window is generous on one and starved on the other
  • Many consumer apps only support top-level or category deep links, not item-level ones — those need an added in-app navigation phase (taps guided by earlier-frame template matching) before the rect read is valid, which reintroduces pointer-walk cost and mistap risk
  • Reading numbers out of a third-party app's screens is still scraping that app; its terms of service apply regardless of the capture mechanism

Scale

Capture is cheap and phones are independent: measured 84 requests/second per phone flat out, 512 req/s aggregate across ten concurrent pollers, no interference from input traffic. Recognition, not capture, is the ceiling — kernel-plug-in OCR latency is undocumented, and client-side OCR on a 500×1080 crop is an unmeasured estimate of tens to a few hundred milliseconds per call, so budget a handful of region reads per second per PC core and crop tight. Realistically that is roughly 200-800 region-reads per hour per phone for a workflow that navigates before every read, versus several thousand per hour for a fixed screen that never needs re-navigation. Only two phones are mirroring on this rig today; the 19 count is boards, not live devices.

Retail price watch by copying page text out of Safari

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Open a product URL in mobile Safari, select-all and copy the page with the board's hardware hotkeys, then read the clipboard back and regex the price, stock line and delivery promise out of plain text. It gets the mobile-personalized page the retailer actually serves (geo, app-vs-web pricing, member pricing) as exact characters, not an OCR guess. The whole approach rests on one unverified assumption: that iOS Safari treats Cmd+A as select-all-page on a non-editable web document, not just inside form fields.

How

  1. get_device_list /api/device/get — enumerate targets, read each phone's imgw×imgh mirror geometry
  2. mouse_reset_pos /api/mouse/reset?id=<a,b> — clear the stuck-click state before any tap-critical sequence
  3. shortcut#13 /api/shortcut/exec/url?id=<a,b,c>&url=<product url> — open the page on every listed phone in one request
  4. get_device_screenshot /api/pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true — poll and diff by mean absolute pixel difference to detect settle, never a fixed sleep
  5. click /api/mouse/click?id=<id>&x=250&y=600 — give the web view keyboard focus, picking a known-blank region so the tap can't land on a link or ad
  6. send_key (fn_key) /api/key/sendkey?id=<a,b,c>&fn_key=WIN+a — select all page text; the untested assumption the whole chain rests on
  7. send_key (fn_key) /api/key/sendkey?id=<a,b,c>&fn_key=WIN+c — copy the selection
  8. shortcut#11 /api/shortcut/clipboard/get?id=<one id>&outtime=<ms> — read and parse; guard with a sentinel written before step 6
  9. get_device_screenshot /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&save_path=D:\evidence\ — optional evidence frame (kernel names the file itself, not timestamped)
  10. ocr / ocr_ex / find_image /api/pic/ocr, /pic/find-text, /pic/find-image — not available on this rig, code 28; listed so no fallback is designed around a dead endpoint

Needs

  • Full iMouse Shortcut install/IP-edit/AssistiveTouch-binding chain, verified with the /shortcut/device/ip smoke test before relying on anything past step 6
  • Full Keyboard Access ON with 1 second auto-hide — without it WIN+a/WIN+c/WIN+v are not interpreted at all
  • Board bound at state 2 with mouse parameters present, phone unlocked and mirroring, reachable to the kernel on 9911

Watch out

  • The core assumption is genuinely unverified: if Cmd+A only selects inside fields, the clipboard comes back empty or stale and the approach collapses to "open URL and screenshot." Test on one phone before building a pipeline
  • /key/sendkey returns code 0 once the hotkey was transmitted, not once iOS acted on it — without the sentinel guard a failed select-all silently reports last hour's price as this hour's
  • WIN+a copies the entire page: navigation, cookie banner, recommendation carousels, footer. Anchor parsing on labels and currency symbols, never on line offsets, and expect Reader mode to reorder the copy
  • Many retail sites render the price as an image, canvas element, or a lazy-loaded node that only materializes on scroll — select-all captures the DOM at copy time regardless of scroll position, so a price that only appears on intersection can be silently missing from the clipboard even though a screenshot would show it. That is a distinct failure from a cookie wall and needs its own handling
  • Consent and cookie walls in several jurisdictions mean the first copy is the banner, not the product; accepting one automatically is a policy decision, not something to do silently
  • A mistap that lands on a link or ad navigates away and the clipboard captures the wrong page with no distinguishing signal beyond the sentinel check — pick the tap point from the current frame, not a constant
  • This rig has two phones mirroring, not 19 boards — every throughput figure below scales from that, not from board count

Scale

Per page per phone: the URL open and both hotkeys fan out free over a comma id list; settle polling is cheap (raw BMP fetch measured at 2 ms, phones independent); the clipboard read is the one serial, single-id cost, bounded by outtime. Realistic estimate is 5-10 seconds per page per phone, dominated by real page load and the Shortcut round trip — roughly 8-15 pages/hour/phone sustained once retail load variance is accounted for, so 16-30 pages/hour across the rig's two live phones today. Whether the kernel serializes concurrent Shortcut calls to different phones is undocumented; measure with two simultaneous clipboard reads before promising a rack-wide number.

Change detection without recognition

Competitor profile monitoring by post-grid image diff

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Drive a logged-in phone to a competitor's profile on a schedule, grab the mirrored frame, crop the top row of the post grid, and compare it to a stored baseline by mean absolute pixel difference. A score above threshold means the grid changed; archive the frame and re-baseline. The detection core is entirely native to this rig: a raw frame fetch and client-side arithmetic, no OCR plug-in and no platform API, so it survives the missing recognizer completely. Only navigation wants the Shortcut, and only an optional creative-tagging step wants the (unverified) image-search plug-in.

How

  1. get_device_list /api/device/get — read geometry, mirroring state and board binding; exclude any phone whose imgw/imgh differs from the one the baseline was measured on
  2. mouse_reset_pos /api/mouse/reset?id=<a,b,…> — clear stuck-click state before tapping
  3. send_key (fn_key WIN+h) /api/key/sendkey?id=<a,b,…>&fn_key=WIN+h — press twice to normalize every phone to home page one
  4. shortcut#13 /api/shortcut/exec/url?id=<a,b,…>&url=https://…/<handle>/ — deep-link straight to the profile, one request for every phone
  5. get_device_screenshot /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true — fetch two frames ~500 ms apart, require mean absolute pixel difference under ~1 before treating the profile as loaded
  6. mouse_wheel /api/mouse/wheel?id=<ids>&direction=down&len=<1-127>&number=<n> — scroll the grid into view; identical every run or the crop misaligns
  7. get_device_screenshot (rect) /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true&rect=[l,t,r,b] — capture and crop the top grid row (flat array, JSON-then-URL-encoded)
  8. local (client-side) — score the crop against the stored baseline by mean absolute pixel difference; idle measured 0.02-0.03, real change measured 20-160
  9. get_device_screenshot (save_path) /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&jpg=true&save_path=D:\social\<handle>\ — on a hit, archive the frame and set it as the new baseline
  10. find_image_ex /api/pic/find-image-cv — optional: tag which of your own known creatives appeared; plug-in gated, unverified on this rig
  11. ocr / ocr_ex /api/pic/ocr, /pic/find-text — not available: follower counts, post counts and captions stay out of reach; the design must stay purely diff-based

Needs

  • Kernel reachable with IMConsole.exe logged in; each phone mirroring with a live air_pid
  • A logged-in account you own or are authorized to operate — logged-out sessions typically hide or degrade profile grids
  • AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock, StandBy off and Do Not Disturb, none of which are queryable over the API
  • The grid rectangle measured by hand once per app per phone, re-measured after every app update
  • For deep-linking, the full Shortcut install/bind chain; for creative tagging, the image-search plug-in and a kernel restart

Watch out

  • A diff only proves the grid changed, never what changed or whether it was a post at all: stories rings, live badges, view counters, an avatar change, an A/B-tested layout and a reordered pin all cross the same threshold. Treat every hit as "review the archived frame," never as a confirmed new post
  • A diff below threshold is equally ambiguous: it can mean no change, or that the app never loaded, hit a login wall, or served an error screen. Pair the diff with a positive-anchor rectangle over a known-stable element that must never disappear
  • Repeated automated profile views on a real logged-in account routinely trigger a re-authentication prompt, an OTP challenge, a "suspicious activity" interstitial, or a rate-limit wall — this rig has no OCR to read any of them, so without the positive-anchor check a challenge screen either mis-scores as a grid change or silently stalls the schedule for that handle indefinitely
  • Universal-link behavior is unverified per app: first-run "Open in app?" interstitials or signed-out mobile-web routing can serve a different grid layout and crop coordinates than expected
  • Push and notification banners overlay exactly the profile-header/top-grid-row region and produce a diff spike unrelated to any post change; Do Not Disturb must be on for every monitoring phone
  • /pic/screenshot is single-id; only navigation and hotkey steps fan out — capture cost scales linearly with phone count
  • binary=true returns raw bytes with no JSON at all, so there is no data.code to read on that call; validate the body (BM magic, expected length) instead, and never mix binary=true with save_path

Scale

Frame fetches are cheap and phones are fully independent: measured 83 and 85 req/s per phone concurrently, 512 req/s aggregate across ten pollers, no interference from input traffic. A 19-phone rack checking 50 handles each every 10 minutes is roughly 1.6 screenshots/second rack-wide, under 1% of measured capacity — the rig is nowhere near the bottleneck. Reuse one frame buffer per poller; each 1.62 MB frame crosses the .NET Large Object Heap threshold (488 MB/s allocation and 496 gen-2 collections per 8 seconds without reuse, versus 2.9 MB/s with it). The real limits are app cold-start and profile load (2-5 seconds), pointer travel if scrolling by swipe, the weaker phone's slower settle window, and above all the platform's own tolerance for repeated views from one session — pace by handle-per-hour against that tolerance, not against the rig's request ceiling. Only two of 19 boards are actually mirroring today.

Native-resolution capture for evidence and QA

Native-resolution iOS screenshots pulled back as evidence

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

The AirPlay mirror is a re-encoded 500×1080 stream, the wrong artifact when a human, a client, or an OCR pass has to read small text. Firing the phone's own screenshot chord writes a native full-panel PNG into iOS Photos, which the Shortcut then pulls back to the PC. Unlike a mirror frame, the file is byte-stable and therefore hashable, with the iOS status-bar clock and EXIF creation time intact — the right input for ad-creative review, dispute and chargeback evidence, and anywhere font rendering or dark-mode contrast has to be judged at real pixels.

How

  1. click / shortcut#13 /mouse/click or /shortcut/exec/url — stage the page to capture; send /mouse/reset first, since taps can silently stop registering while moves and hotkeys keep working
  2. send_key fn_key WIN+h /key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+h — two Home presses to normalize state before a cross-phone sweep
  3. send_key fn_key WIN+SHIFT+3 /key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=shift+win+3 — fire the native iOS screenshot on every listed phone in one request; confirmed in the XP hotkey table
  4. shortcut#1 /shortcut/album/get?id=<single>&num=1&outtime=<ms> — read the newest album entry, one phone per call; sort order is undocumented
  5. shortcut#2 /shortcut/album/down?id=<single>&list=[{…}]&outtime=30000 — pull the PNG to <install dir>\Shortcut\Media
  6. local (local file handling) — rename with phone id and timestamp, hash the file, log the call (id, coordinates, fn_key, returned create_time) beside it
  7. shortcut#3 /shortcut/album/del?id=<single>&list=[{…}]&outtime=<ms> — clean the album so "newest entry" stays predictable for the next sweep
  8. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<single>&binary=true — optional paired mirror frame, taken in the same moment, to scale OCR coordinates into mirror-pixel space
  9. mouse_wheel /mouse/wheel?id=<ids>&direction=down&len=<1-127>&number=<n> — for long pages, scroll and repeat the chord rather than swiping

Needs

  • Full Shortcut install/IP-edit/AssistiveTouch-binding chain, plus Shortcuts > Advanced permissions for running scripts and deleting without confirmation
  • Full Keyboard Access ON — the screenshot chord is a hotkey iOS interprets, not a synthetic tap
  • Board bound and connected, phone and PC on the same LAN, free storage and Photos access on the phone

Watch out

  • /shortcut/album/get and /shortcut/album/down are single-id only ("Multiple is not allowed") — only the capture chord fans out
  • Native resolution is an iOS device property, not an API field: the API only exposes imgw/imgh (the mirror) and width/height (iOS logical points). Read the actual PNG dimensions from the downloaded file
  • No screenshot plug-in path is involved, which is why this works at all here; the vendor also lists /shortcut/other/screenshot (Shortcut v1.3+) as an alternative "in special cases" but with no parameter table — probe before relying on it
  • /shortcut/album/del is destructive and irreversible on the phone; run it per phone with that phone's own filenames, never with a rack-wide id list, and stay away from /shortcut/album/clear entirely
  • outtime is milliseconds on XP (15000 default) but seconds in the Phonefarm sibling doc — mixing the two silently breaks a timeout
  • Error codes to branch on: 30 call timeout (Shortcut never launched), 27 path does not exist, 35 file list empty, 2 device not bound, 3 hardware not connected, 25 device offline, 36 parameter error — match on data.code, never the (Chinese) message text
  • iOS surfaces a screenshot thumbnail for a few seconds; a stray tap on it opens the markup editor and derails the next step. Screenshots of DRM-protected views (some banking and video apps) can come back blank
  • This is fundamentally a serial-per-phone pipeline bookended by one free fan-out chord and one free fan-out cleanup precondition — describe it that way, not as rack-parallel

Trap A wrong assumption here fails silently

Whether num=1 returns the shot you just took is undocumented sort order. If it turns out to be oldest-first or unstable, the pipeline can archive an unrelated older photo as "evidence" with data.code 0 at every layer and no error anywhere. Verify once against the chord's own create_time before trusting a sweep on it; a smoke test alone is not enough.

Scale

The capture chord is a single request regardless of rack size — the board walks every listed phone for the same cost as one. Everything after that is serial per phone: one album read, one download, one optional delete, each a full hotkey-to-Shortcut-to-Wi-Fi round trip. No timing for this path has been measured on this rig; treat any per-shot figure (drafts suggest roughly 3-10 seconds, 1-2 minutes for a 19-phone sweep) as an unmeasured placeholder and instrument the first real run before quoting it. The rig's own AirPlay measurements already show a roughly 6x per-phone Wi-Fi asymmetry between two otherwise-identical XRs, which plausibly extends to the Shortcut's own file transfer.

The clipboard as a general data-exit channel

Select-all, copy, clipboard read: exact text without OCR

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

On any surface where iOS exposes selectable text (Safari pages, text fields, Notes, a caption or bio field) the board can send select-all then copy, and the Shortcut hands the clipboard back as a UTF-8 string in data.text — no transcription error, no font guessing, Unicode intact. The same channel captures a permalink after tapping an app's own "Copy link" share action, though without OCR that step reduces to fixed per-app coordinates rather than anything text-aware.

How

  1. mouse_reset_pos /mouse/reset?id=<id1,id2,…> — clear the stuck-click state before any tap-critical sequence
  2. shortcut#10 /shortcut/clipboard/set?id=<ids>&text=<sentinel> — write a per-phone sentinel first, so a stale read is detectable
  3. shortcut#13 /shortcut/exec/url?id=<ids>&url=<url> — Route A: push a URL onto the phone
  4. click /mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=<x>&y=<y> — Route B: tap the app's own "…" menu then "Copy link"; coordinates only, since there is no OCR to find the row
  5. click /mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=<x>&y=<y> — focus the field or page body (Route A only)
  6. send_key (fn_key) /key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+a — select all; documented only in the XP hotkey table, absent from the Phonefarm doc
  7. send_key (fn_key) /key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+c — copy
  8. shortcut#11 /shortcut/clipboard/get?id=<single id>&outtime=<ms> — read back, one phone per call; the only step that crosses Wi-Fi
  9. shortcut#10 /shortcut/clipboard/set?id=<ids>&text=<placeholder> — scrub the clipboard afterward, one request for the whole rack
  10. ocr / ocr_ex /pic/ocr, /pic/find-text, /pic/find-text-ex — fallback if the plug-in is ever installed; all return code 28 today

Needs

  • Full Shortcut install/IP-edit/AssistiveTouch-binding chain, Full Keyboard Access ON with 1 second auto-hide
  • A text surface that is actually selectable by iOS — Safari bodies, fields, Notes and search boxes are; native feed cells, comment lists and DM bubbles generally are not
  • Phone on the same LAN as the kernel, reachable on 9911; Handoff/Universal Clipboard turned off on rack phones

Watch out

  • Nothing in this chain has been exercised on this rig; run the /shortcut/device/ip smoke test before trusting anything past step 1
  • /shortcut/clipboard/get is single-id — the hotkeys fan out to the whole rack, the read does not, so N phones means N reads
  • Checking that a string "starts with https://" is not a sufficient staleness check, since a previous phone's permalink also starts that way — compare against the written sentinel, and pair it with a shape check: in a list-based UI, WIN+a can select objects or messages instead of text and still return a non-empty, URL-shaped clipboard payload
  • WIN+a and WIN+c are XP-only documented hotkeys; the Phonefarm doc's fn_key examples and named-key list omit them entirely — don't present that column as vendor-confirmed
  • Route B (tapping a share sheet's "Copy link") is exact-text only once a human already knows exactly where to tap; share sheets reorder by usage, so a fixed coordinate needs re-verification per app version
  • Apps can show a "pasted from" or clipboard-access banner that changes what's on screen and can break a concurrent frame-diff check
  • The API has no authentication and the clipboard text crosses the LAN as plain HTTP — never route credentials, one-time codes or payment details through it, and firewall 9911 to trusted hosts

Trap A success code proves delivery, never outcome

data.code 0 on the hotkey call means the keystroke reached the phone, not that iOS acted on it. A failed selection is silent — the read comes back with whatever was on the clipboard before. The sentinel-write-then-compare pattern in steps 2 and 8 is the only defense; a naive "non-empty string" check passes even when the wrong thing was copied.

Scale

The reset and both hotkeys fan out free over a comma id list — 19 phones cost the same three requests as one. The serial cost is the clipboard read: a full round trip out over the board, through iOS, back over Wi-Fi to 9911, bounded by outtime (15000 ms default), realistically 1-2 seconds per phone when healthy. With the two phones actually live on this rig today, a full capture cycle is roughly 3-5 seconds; extrapolating to the full 19-board inventory (unverified) at 1-2 seconds/phone serial reads gives roughly 20-40 seconds per full-rack capture.

Turning the phone into a queryable sensor

Custom Shortcut as an on-phone probe answering through the clipboard

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Neither the XP nor the Phonefarm device record carries battery level, free storage, SSID, carrier, lock state or GPS. A Shortcut authored by hand on each phone — Get Battery Level, Get Network Details, Get Current Location, ending in Copy to Clipboard — turns Shortcuts into a sensor API the vendor never exposed: fire it from the PC, read the answer with /shortcut/clipboard/get. This is the only documented mechanism on this stack that runs arbitrary phone-side code and hands a result back without a jailbreak. Both possible triggers are unproven on this rig, so feasibility here is binary, not a gradient, until one of them is confirmed.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get — enumerate the rack and build the join key every probe reading files under; confirms the absence of battery/storage/SSID/carrier fields that justifies this entry
  2. shortcut#24 GET /api/shortcut/device/ip?id=<one id>&state=0 — prove the vendor Shortcut round trip works before adding your own Shortcut to the picture
  3. local (manual, no API) — author the probe Shortcut on the phone by hand, run once with every permission prompt answered, ending in Copy to Clipboard
  4. shortcut#13 GET /api/shortcut/exec/url?id=<id1,id2,…>&url=shortcuts://run-shortcut?name=FarmProbe — preferred trigger; unverified whether iOS honors the scheme from the vendor Shortcut's Open URL action
  5. send_key (fn_key) GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<id1,id2,…>&fn_key=<chord> — fallback trigger via a spare AssistiveTouch binding; unverified whether the kernel forwards a chord absent from its published hotkey table
  6. local (client-side sleep) — wait roughly 2-3 seconds for a local-sensor Shortcut; there is no completion callback on XP
  7. shortcut#11 GET /api/shortcut/clipboard/get?id=<one id>&outtime=<ms> — read the answer, one phone per request
  8. shortcut#10 GET /api/shortcut/clipboard/set?id=<id1,id2,…>&text= — scrub the pasteboard, one request for the whole rack
  9. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true — optional visual confirmation of a Shortcuts banner or a stuck "Allow" prompt, since there's no OCR to read either

Needs

  • The vendor Shortcut fully installed, IP-edited and bound, confirmed by the /shortcut/device/ip round trip
  • A self-authored probe Shortcut per phone, run once by hand with the screen unlocked so permission prompts (Location especially) are answered
  • For the chord fallback only: a spare AssistiveTouch binding that does not collide with the vendor's own, plus Full Keyboard Access ON

Watch out

  • Until one trigger is confirmed, there is no third API-only path to run phone-side code — if neither fires, this collapses to reading the vendor's own shortcut functions, none of which expose battery, storage, SSID or GPS. Treat the whole idea as conditional on a same-day acceptance test on one phone, not something to schedule into production first
  • The chord fallback reasons by analogy from the Phonefarm edition's own send_text chord (CTRL+ALT+SHIFT+WIN+v) to argue the board emits 4-modifier chords at all — that only proves the vendor's own Shortcut consumes that specific chord on that edition, not that an arbitrary unpublished chord passes the XP kernel's dispatcher unfiltered. Weaker evidence than it sounds
  • Fan-out is asymmetric: both triggers and the scrub take a comma id list; the harvest is single-id, so one request starts the rack and N requests read it back
  • There is no completion callback on XP (no send_text, no send_text_ok) — a slow Shortcut and a dead one look identical until the read returns stale text or times out with code 30. Put a nonce or timestamp in the payload and reject answers that don't match the cycle just triggered
  • outtime is milliseconds (15000 default); clipboard/set's sleep is seconds — mixing the two silently gives a 15 ms or a 15,000 second timeout
  • The probe overwrites the same pasteboard the vendor's own Unicode-paste flow (clipboard/set then WIN+v) depends on — never run a probe cycle concurrently with a paste-driven script on the same phone
  • A rack-wide sweep with several stalled phones (unanswered prompt, no Wi-Fi) pays the full 15 second timeout per stalled phone if reads are issued serially; read concurrently across phones or the trigger's free cost is masked by a slow harvest
  • This is legitimate first-party device administration on hardware you own, not a platform-evasion technique — the genuine risk items are the unauthenticated LAN and retaining GPS, carrier or SSID as identifying data

Scale

Trigger cost is one request for the whole rack on either route, walking every listed phone in parallel. Harvest cost is one request per phone, each blocking up to outtime but typically returning in the Shortcut's own runtime — a local-sensor probe should complete in 2-3 seconds; anything using network or GPS is bounded by the phone's own connectivity, so raise outtime rather than assume a timeout means failure. Concurrency of the shortcut path itself has never been measured on this rig, only screenshot polling (512 req/s aggregate, no cross-interference) — read concurrently across phones, strictly serially per phone. A 10-15 minute sweep interval is comfortable; a per-minute sweep is not, since every cycle steals the pasteboard from anything else that pastes.

Ad and storefront verification

Ad verification and brand safety capture from real devices in real geos

Needs plug-inWith caveats

Turns the rack into an ad-verification panel: open a target app or deep link on each phone, step the feed with a single fan-out scroll request, and pull one raw-BMP frame per stop that captures the creative together with the content around it and your own timestamp. Ad-platform delivery reports confirm an impression was counted; they say nothing about what the creative looked like on a real iPhone, on a real carrier, in a real place, or what ran next to it, which is exactly what a mirror frame is. The rig's split network path, mirroring over Wi-Fi while the phone's own internet rides cellular, means the capture channel never contaminates the identity being tested. Recognition (matching the creative, reading a "Sponsored" label) is the gated half: the image-search plug-in is unconfirmed and the OCR plug-in is confirmed absent on this rig, so matching runs client-side on the decoded frame today.

How

  1. get_device_list + get_usb_list GET /api/device/get?id=<id> and GET /api/config/usb/get — confirm the phone is mirroring (air_pid) and controllable (board state 2), and read imgw/imgh (500x1080) for the coordinate space.
  2. shortcut#24 GET /api/shortcut/device/ip?id=<id>&state=1 — record the phone's public IP (state=0 for LAN, no Shortcut needed) and stamp it with your own clock.
  3. send_key WIN+h GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+h, sent twice — normalise to a known home screen before reusing a coordinate across phones.
  4. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<ids> — clear the silent stuck-click state that lets /mouse/move keep working while clicks do nothing.
  5. shortcut#13 / click GET /api/shortcut/exec/url?id=<ids>&url=<url> or GET /api/mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=&y= — open the app under test, by deep link or icon tap.
  6. mouse_wheel GET /api/mouse/wheel?id=<ids>&direction=down&len=60&number=2 — step the feed by a fixed increment in one request for the whole panel (iOS behaviour unverified, see Watch out).
  7. get_device_screenshot (polled) GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true — poll until mean absolute pixel difference exceeds the idle floor, not a fixed sleep, to confirm a genuinely new frame.
  8. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true (+ jpg&save_path for archive) — capture the evidence frame, one request per phone.
  9. find_image_ex / find_image POST /api/pic/find-image-cv {img_list, similarity:0.8} — locate the creative in the frame (plug-in gated).
  10. ocr / find_image_ex POST /api/pic/find-text {text:["Sponsored","Ad"]} or /api/pic/ocr — read the disclosure label (plug-in gated, unavailable on this rig).
  11. (orchestration) repeat steps 6-9 — loop stops then phones; screenshots are one request per phone, input is one request for the whole panel.

Needs

  • Vendor console (IMConsole.exe) running and logged in — without it phones show state 0 and the board list is empty.
  • Per-phone iOS accessibility settings none of this API can query: AssistiveTouch on, Full Keyboard Access on, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock.
  • Board bound and cabled with the vendor cable, phone attached only after the board enumerates.
  • Mouse parameters present (location_crc non-empty), or every mouse call returns data.code 11.
  • iMouse Shortcut installed and bound, for the public-IP read and the deep-link route only.
  • Image-search plug-in for in-API matching; the OCR plug-in is confirmed absent (code 28) on this rig.
  • A SIM per phone plus the static-IP-without-gateway Wi-Fi setting, for a genuine per-geo egress.
  • Accounts you own or are authorised to use, logged in normally.
  • A reused per-poller buffer: un-pooled 1.62 MB frames measured 488 MB/s of allocation and 496 gen-2 GCs in 8 s.

Watch out

  • The capture spine (steps 1-8, wheel behaviour aside) is fully native on this rig today; only recognition and public IP are gated.
  • /pic/ocr answers code 28 here; assume image-search is in the same state until probed. Decode the BMP and match client-side instead — the frame is already in the API's own coordinate space.
  • The public-IP call needs the Shortcut and a working USB board (the hotkey rides USB) and defaults to a 15 s timeout, making it the slowest call in the loop — read it once per session, not once per stop.
  • No carrier, SIM, locale or timezone field exists anywhere; geo is inferred from the public IP plus your own SIM-to-slot mapping. No server timestamp exists either — every time in the record is your controller's clock.
  • Whether /mouse/wheel actually scrolls an iOS feed through AssistiveTouch is unmeasured on this rig. A raw wheel HID event has no guaranteed mapping to a swipe gesture, so default to /mouse/swipe on the short axis (~0.6 ms/px, ~300-500 ms/stroke) until a probe proves the wheel path works, rather than building the throughput model on it.
  • Screenshots and recognition are single-id ("Multiple is not allowed"); only /mouse/*, /key/* and /shortcut/exec/url fan out to a comma-separated list.
  • Frame rate is per-phone and not fixable in software: one XR here delivers ~29 new frames/s under motion, its identical twin ~4.5 — settle waits must be frame-driven, not a fixed sleep.
  • Templates must be cropped from the mirror stream itself, since AirPlay re-compresses everything — match at similarity ~0.8, not ~0.95, and re-cut if the encoder ratio or display settings change.
  • save_path chooses the directory only; the kernel names the file. Rename client-side and keep a manifest or the archive is unattributable.
  • Ad platforms treat device-farm impressions as invalid traffic, a sharper risk than a plain ToS breach: take the minimum impressions needed to verify, never click the ad being verified, never run this as a volume loop, and pause on any block or rate-limit interstitial rather than working around it. Repeated automated scrolling from the same account can also simply reduce fresh ad delivery over time through ordinary frequency capping, a functional failure distinct from account risk. Get written authorisation naming accounts and campaigns before verifying on a client's behalf.
  • Captured frames contain other people's names, faces and message previews next to the creative — that is personal data; scope retention, restrict access and crop or redact before anything leaves the organisation.
