  • The iMouse Shortcut installed on every test phone, IP-edited to the kernel PC, all permissions granted, and bound to an AssistiveTouch key — the core group-wide launch step depends on it and it is not confirmed present on this rig.
  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in, and each phone's board bound (state 2 in /config/usb/get) with a non-empty location_crc.
  • iOS accessibility settings on every phone that the API cannot query: AssistiveTouch on, Full Keyboard Access on, Auto-Lock never, portrait lock.
  • A deliberately heterogeneous phone set (at least one without the app) and per-phone golden frames — home layouts differ, so coordinates and goldens are not shareable.
  • An apple-app-site-association file actually deployed on the domain under test, matching the build's associated-domains entitlement.

Watch out

  • The headline "one request reaches all 19 phones" economics rests entirely on the Shortcut channel. Confirm it first with a single /api/shortcut/device/ip probe before quoting the 20–30 minute matrix figure; without it, fall back to the per-phone typing path, serial and no longer flat with rack size.
  • Cold-start by swiping the app-switcher card is unlikely to work: the board walks the pointer at ~0.6 ms/px, so the stroke reads as a slow drag rather than a flick. Budget on /device/restart or /shortcut/switch/device state=1 instead, at a real cost of 60–90 seconds offline plus a re-cast.
  • outtime on XP is milliseconds (default 15000), not seconds as in the Phonefarm edition — a value of 15 times out instantly with code 30.
  • No OCR or image-search on this rig (code 28); every landing classification falls back to mean absolute pixel diff against a golden-frame library sized to (phone × app-state × destination) built before the run, not on the fly.
  • /pic/screenshot is single-id — there is no group screenshot on XP, only input and hotkey calls fan out over a comma id list.
  • Test traffic pollutes your own analytics unless links carry clearly-marked test parameters; scope the whole exercise to domains and apps you own or are authorised to test, and never let a run tap through a checkout or consent flow.

Scale

Launch fans out for free: one /shortcut/exec/url call reaches all 19 phones inside its outtime window. Frame capture is the real cost: raw BMP polls run flat out at 84 req/s per phone (p50 2 ms), and ten concurrent pollers sustain 512 req/s aggregate with no shared bottleneck, so bandwidth is never the limit. The ceiling is each phone's own AirPlay rate — about 4.5 new frames/s on the slow XR versus 29 on the fast one — which sets a 2–3 second settle window per cell. A 50-URL by 3-app-state matrix (150 cells) runs in roughly 20–30 minutes with the Shortcut confirmed live; without it, the step-13 fallback is serial and roughly 15–20x slower, no longer flat with rack size.

Trap The address bar is not a fallback

Typing a URL into Safari's address bar is specifically the context where iOS does not hand off to an installed app. Treating that as the "native fallback" and then reporting a universal-link failure against it produces a false negative — use auto-linked text in a note or message body instead.

Push-notification render, arrival-latency and tap-through testing

Plus external toolingWith caveats

Put each phone into the app state under test (foreground, backgrounded, or locked), start a cropped raw-BMP poller on the banner strip, fire a test push from your own backend or ESP with a unique marker in the title, and take the first frame that crosses a mean-diff threshold as the on-screen arrival moment. Long-press the banner to expand rich media, tap through, and screenshot the landing screen to confirm the deep link routed correctly. Every step of the observation loop is native XP API; the push itself must come from outside the rig, and reading the notification text server-side needs a plug-in that is not installed here.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get — enumerate targets and read each phone's coordinate space and liveness.
  2. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<ids> — clear the silent stuck-click state on the whole target set.
  3. send_key WIN+h GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+h — two presses, normalize each phone to a known state.
  4. send_key TAB+l / WIN+h GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=TAB+l|WIN+h — place the phone in the app state under test: locked, backgrounded, or leave the app open for foreground.
  5. get_device_screenshot, polled GET /api/pic/screenshot?binary=true&rect=[0,0,500,200] — start a cropped raw-frame poller per phone on the banner strip.
  6. none external — your backend, APNs sandbox, or ESP — fire the test push with a unique marker in the title; record the send timestamp on the PC clock.
  7. none (client-side) mean absolute pixel diff on consecutive raw BMP buffers — flag the first frame crossing ~20 as the arrival moment; keep one untouched phone as an idle control.
  8. ocr / ocr_ex (optional) GET /api/pic/ocr?rect=[l,t,r,b] — read the notification title/body text; not available on this rig, code 28.
  9. send_key NoticeBar GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=NoticeBar — open Notification Centre for grouping and thread-summary evidence.
  10. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?binary=true&save_path=<dir> — capture the full-frame render evidence.
  11. click with time GET /api/mouse/click?x=<cx>&y=<cy>&time=700 — long-press the banner to expand a rich notification; coordinates from that phone's own arrival frame, never a hard-coded constant.
  12. click GET /api/mouse/click?x=<cx>&y=<cy> — tap through to the deep-link destination.
  13. find_image / find_image_ex (optional) GET /api/pic/find-image-cv?img_list=[...]&similarity=0.85 — assert the landing screen against a golden, plug-in gated.
  14. send_key shift+win+3 + album (optional) GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=shift+win+3, GET /api/shortcut/album/get, GET /api/shortcut/album/down — pull a lossless native-resolution copy of the render; needs the Shortcut.
  15. send_key VolumeUp (optional) GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=VolumeUp — attempt to wake a dark screen before capture; unreliable, see watch-outs.
  16. swipe + send_key GET /api/mouse/swipe?direction=up, GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+h — dismiss and reset between cases.
  17. WS callbacks ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api — error_push, dev_disconnect, usb_change — subscribe for asynchronous failure signals so a board fault doesn't read as a push failure.

Needs

  • An external push sender you control — your own backend against APNs, or a test-only audience in the ESP. The rig cannot originate a push.
  • Board and mirror ready per phone, plus the iOS accessibility settings the API cannot query (AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, Auto-Lock never).
  • The test app installed with notification permission granted, its push token registered to a dedicated test segment, and its deep-link scheme wired up.
  • The OCR plug-in only for step 8's text read (confirmed absent, code 28); everything else in the chain is native.

Watch out

  • What you measure is on-screen arrival, not APNs delivery latency: the number is (first frame above threshold) minus (your send timestamp), inflated by that phone's AirPlay rate and poll period. Quote it as display-arrival latency with the per-phone frame rate attached, or it will be read as something it is not.
  • The locked-screen branch is likely not achievable at all: locking turns the physical display off, and AirPlay mirrors the rendered framebuffer, so frames may freeze on the last image or go black once the display sleeps. Auto-Lock Never only suppresses idle timeout, not a deliberate lock. Verify on one phone (check air_pid and whether frames keep changing) before building any part of the matrix on this branch.
  • VolumeUp does not wake a locked iPhone display on stock iOS with Face ID; drop that premise rather than relying on it.
  • A 700 ms pointer hold via /mouse/click time is not confirmed to trigger iOS's haptic-touch expand gesture — treat it as optional, not a required chain link.
  • /pic/screenshot, /pic/ocr and /pic/find-image are single-id; only /key/sendkey, /mouse/click, /mouse/swipe and /mouse/reset fan out over a comma id list.
  • A tap that produces no reaction is ambiguous between "the deep link is broken" and "the phone is in the silent stuck-click state" — /mouse/reset before every tap and error_push are what disambiguate it.

Scale

Hotkeys and taps fan out for free across the rack in one request each; frame capture does not, so budget one poller per phone. Measured headroom is large — 512 req/s aggregate at ten concurrent pollers, p50 3 ms — so the API is never the constraint. Foreground/background cases run at roughly 150–250 cases per hour for the whole rack, bounded by the slow phone's ~4.5 fps AirPlay rate and, more often, by the ESP or APNs sandbox's own send-rate limits. Locked-state throughput is 0 through this API pending the freeze/black-frame check above; if the mirror dies on lock, that branch has to be re-scoped to a physical camera rig and dropped from any automated figure.

Open Does the mirror survive a lock?

Whether the AirPlay mirror keeps streaming after a synthetic lock (TAB+l) is undocumented and untested on this rig. If it freezes or goes black, as it does on stock iOS lock behaviour, the entire locked-screen half of any test matrix has to be dropped or redone by camera, not fixed in software. Check this on one phone before designing anything around it.

Email campaign rendering sweep on real iOS mail clients

PartialWith caveats

Send the campaign to seed inboxes, then on each phone drive the real mail app (Apple Mail, Gmail, Outlook), open the newest message, and alternate raw-BMP frame grabs with mouse-wheel scrolls until the frame stops changing, stitching the tiles client-side into a full-height render. Because taps and scrolls take a comma id list, the identical sequence fans out to the whole rack in one request, so adding phones adds mail clients rather than wall-clock time. On this two-phone rig the sweep varies the client, not the device, since both are the same iPhone XR build.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get — preflight: read per-phone mirror geometry and liveness.
  2. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<ids> — clear the silent stuck-click state on the whole target set.
  3. send_key WIN+h GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+h — two presses, normalize every phone to home page one.
  4. click GET /api/mouse/click?x=<px>&y=<py> — launch the mail client; per-phone coordinates are mandatory, home layouts differ.
  5. shortcut#13 (optional) GET /api/shortcut/exec/url?url=<https url> — open a landing page or deep link instead of tapping; needs the Shortcut, and no mail-app URL scheme is documented in either edition.
  6. click GET /api/mouse/click — open the newest message; without OCR, pin the seed send as the only unread item and verify by whole-frame diff that the view changed.
  7. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true — capture one viewport tile.
  8. mouse_wheel GET /api/mouse/wheel?id=<ids>&direction=down&len=<1-127>&number=<n> — scroll one viewport; covers every phone in the id list at once, but whether webview-backed clients honour it is unverified.
  9. none (client-side) mean absolute pixel diff on consecutive frames — detect the bottom of the message; nothing under ~1 means nothing moved.
  10. click + get_device_screenshot GET /api/mouse/click, GET /api/pic/screenshot — tap the CTA and capture the landing page; locating it by label needs OCR, absent here.
  11. send_key shift+win+3 + album (optional) GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=shift+win+3, GET /api/shortcut/album/get, GET /api/shortcut/album/down — the only lossless native-resolution path for colour-critical QA; needs the Shortcut.
  12. none no API — blind /mouse/click through Settings > Display & Brightness > Dark — the dark-mode pass; no appearance switch exists anywhere in either API.

Needs

  • Seed addresses excluded from campaign reporting, with the test send delivered and unread before the run starts.
  • Mail apps installed and signed in per phone (Apple Mail is stock, Gmail and Outlook must be added by hand), one client per phone or per group.
  • Per-phone icon and message-row coordinate maps, and an empirical pixels-per-wheel-tick calibration per mail client before any stitch can be trusted.
  • The iMouse Shortcut, unconfirmed on this rig, for the deep-link-open and native-resolution steps only.

Watch out

  • The OCR plug-in is not connected (code 28), which removes every text assertion — no confirming the subject line, no finding the CTA by label. The sweep produces images for a human or a client-side vision model to judge, not automated text pass/fail.
  • Both phones here are the same model and iOS build, so the sweep currently tests mail-client rendering variance only, not device or OS variance; only 2 of 19 boards have a phone attached and mirroring.
  • /mouse/wheel's behaviour inside iOS Mail or Gmail's webview is unverified — calibrate pixels-per-tick per client and keep a down/move/up drag as a committed fallback, not an afterthought, or the stitched composite will silently duplicate or drop rows.
  • No dark-mode API exists in either edition — checked every /shortcut/switch/* path (device, brightness, torch, flight, cellular, Wi-Fi) and none touches appearance.
  • Tapping a CTA in a real inbox fires the campaign's genuine open and click tracking; confirm seed-address exclusion from ESP reporting before the first run, or the rack will quietly inflate engagement metrics.
  • The bottom-of-message stop condition proves the view changed, not that the right message opened — add a structural check (e.g. a fixed subject-line crop) before trusting the stitch, since there is no OCR to confirm it directly.

Scale

API time per tile is negligible — 2 ms capture, sub-millisecond wheel — so wall clock is set by waiting for a genuinely new AirPlay frame (as little as 34 ms on the fast XR, 220 ms or more on the slow one) plus the mail app's own layout settle. A six-tile email render runs roughly 3–8 seconds per phone on the fast XR and 10–20-plus seconds on the slow one. Scaling this use case means adding phones for more mail clients in parallel, not compressing per-email time; testing several clients on one phone is serial and multiplies wall time by the number of clients.

Visual regression and rig health

Golden-frame visual regression and screen-change detection

Native APIWith caveats

Drive each phone to a known screen, wait for the mirror frame to actually settle, pull the raw BMP off the AirPlay decoder in about 2 ms, and compare it to a stored golden with a masked mean-absolute-pixel-diff threshold. No plug-in, no on-phone agent, no app instrumentation: a screenshot call plus a client-side comparator is the whole pipeline, which matters because it is the one vision capability that works today given the OCR and image-search plug-ins are not connected. Every phone is independent, so the suite scales across the rack without scheduling.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get — build the target set and read each phone's coordinate space; require rotate == 0.
  2. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<ids> — clear the silent stuck-click state before any tap-critical walk.
  3. send_key WIN+h GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+h — two presses, normalize every phone to home page one.
  4. shortcut#13 (optional) GET /api/shortcut/exec/url — navigate to the screen under test by deep link; Shortcut-gated, unverified here.
  5. click / mouse_wheel GET /api/mouse/click, GET /api/mouse/wheel — navigate to the screen under test by tap; the no-dependency path.
  6. mouse_move + get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?binary=true — confirm the tap actually landed with a diff on a ~40 px box around the commanded coordinate, before judging the screen.
  7. get_device_screenshot, polled GET /api/pic/screenshot?binary=true — settle loop counted in new frames, not polls, at a fixed 33–50 ms period.
  8. none (client-side) mean absolute pixel diff, masked — compare the settled frame to the golden.
  9. get_device_screenshot, saved GET /api/pic/screenshot?jpg=true&save_path=<dir> — archive the live frame on a failure; the harness owns the golden and renders any side-by-side itself.
  10. find_image / find_image_ex (optional) POST /api/pic/find-image-cv — assert the expected widget is present; plug-in gated.
  11. ocr / ocr_ex (optional) GET /api/pic/ocr, POST /api/pic/find-text — assert the expected label text appears; plug-in gated, absent here.
  12. send_key TAB+b / WIN+h GET /api/key/sendkey — leave the screen and advance the suite; watch the dev_rotate callback, which invalidates goldens on rotation.

Needs

  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in, board bound per phone (state 2) with a non-empty location_crc, and the iOS accessibility settings the API cannot query.
  • Golden images stored per screen and per phone — home layouts differ between phones, so a golden is not portable.
  • A client-side BMP decoder and mean-abs-diff comparator with a reused buffer per poller, and masks maintained per screen for dynamic content (clocks, badges, carousels).
  • A pinned app version on the monitoring phone for change-monitoring use, since there is no installed-app-version signal in the API.

Watch out

  • Settle detection must gate on new frames plus a per-phone timeout, not a poll count: a still screen produces almost no new frames (4.5/s on the slow XR), so a poll-counted quiet window fires falsely early, while genuinely continuous motion (video, spinners) never goes quiet and always hits the timeout.
  • A tap that never landed looks identical to "nothing changed." The pointer-box diff is mandatory, and /mouse/reset, not /mouse/up, is the only documented recovery.
  • Rotation swaps imgw/imgh meaning and invalidates every golden for that phone — check rotate == 0 and subscribe to dev_rotate.
  • The assertion layer (OCR, image search) is plug-in gated and unavailable today, code 28 — keep it additive, never load-bearing.
  • /pic/screenshot is single-id and XP has no server-push frame stream, so polling is the only route; only 2 of 19 boards are actually mirroring, so any full-rack throughput figure is a projection.
  • Golden images and coordinate tables go stale together on any app or OS update, none of which the API can detect.

Scale

Frame capture is effectively free (2 ms paced, 84 req/s flat out) and the client-side diff costs about 1 ms; the real cost per screen is the settle wait, roughly 1–2 seconds on the fast XR and 2–4 seconds on the slow one, plus pointer-walk time at 0.6 ms per pixel. A 20-screen suite runs in about 30–60 seconds per phone, and phones scale independently up to at least ten concurrent pollers (512 req/s aggregate, p50 3 ms). On this rig that is roughly 300–600 verified screen-checks per phone per hour, or 600–1,200 across the two phones actually mirroring today — the 19 boards are control capacity, not video capacity, and do not by themselves multiply this figure.

Trap Never hash-compare frames

MD5 or byte-equality comparison reports "changed" on every single frame, because the AirPlay encoder, the clock, and wallpaper parallax vary from frame to frame even on an untouched phone. This project already reached a wrong conclusion that way once. Threshold on mean absolute pixel difference instead — measured idle floor 0.02–0.03, a real reaction 20–160 — on every use case in this section.

Crash-to-springboard and frozen-UI watchdog

Native APIWith caveats

A per-phone background watchdog that detects an app crash (the springboard dock reappears while the script expects to be in-app) and a hang (no frame change under a deliberate stimulus), and separates both from rig faults — a silent stuck-click pointer, a dropped AirPlay session, a failed board — using this rig's measured signatures. The core loop is native XP HTTP plus the WebSocket callback bus; no OCR or image-search plug-in is required, which matters because neither is connected here.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get?id=<id> — read imgw/imgh, state and air_pid once per watchdog start.
  2. send_key WIN+h GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+h — two presses, normalize before capturing the signature.
  3. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?binary=true — capture the per-phone dock-strip signature as the home-screen reference.
  4. find_multi_color (optional) POST /api/pic/find-multi-color — a plug-in-status-unconfirmed colour-table alternative to the pixel crop; probe for code 28 before relying on it.
  5. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?binary=true — the ~1 Hz crash poll, comparing the dock crop to the signature.
  6. mouse_wheel / mouse_move GET /api/mouse/wheel, GET /api/mouse/move — the hang check: apply a stimulus and require the screen to move; prefer a 2 px move over a wheel event when the app must not be perturbed.
  7. send_key + mouse_reset_pos GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+h, GET /api/mouse/reset — rule out the silent stuck-click state before declaring a hang.
  8. get_device_list GET /api/device/get?id=<id> — rule out a dropped video channel (state, air_pid) before blaming the app.
  9. WS callbacks ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api — error_push, usb_change, dev_disconnect — subscribe to the event bus so board- and session-level failures are logged next to app failures.
  10. shortcut#13 / click GET /api/shortcut/exec/url, GET /api/mouse/click — on a confirmed crash, harvest the last frame and relaunch; the plain click relaunch needs nothing beyond a bound board.

Needs

  • A per-phone dock/home signature and per-phone icon coordinates captured on that same phone during the same normalisation pass — the two XRs have different home screens.
  • A per-phone frame-rate baseline measured under driven motion, used to size the hang timeout.
  • Board and mirror ready per phone (state 2, non-empty location_crc), and the Shortcut only for the optional deep-link relaunch branch.

Watch out

  • A legitimate return to home — logout, deep-link bounce, user exit — looks identical to a crash by the dock signal alone. Gate the verdict on the script's own expected state, always.
  • The hang window must be sized per phone from its measured frame rate: a generic 500 ms window fails on the slow XR, where a still screen delivers almost no new frames as the normal case, not a symptom.
  • Crash-log harvesting through the Files-app shortcut path does not reach iOS's system crash-log store — only app-written, Files-visible containers are reachable.
  • XP has no server-push frame stream, so the watchdog's own poll cadence bounds its detection latency, and /pic/screenshot is single-id.
  • The two-Home-press normalisation itself takes non-zero time and counts as input — sequence it before, not during, an armed watch window, or a crash mid-normalisation is missed.
  • Do not report "mirroring broken" without checking /device/get state and air_pid first — diagnosing a silent phone as an app hang when it is really a dropped AirPlay session is the specific wrong conclusion this design exists to prevent.

Scale

A 1 Hz crash poll is under 1.2% of the measured per-phone capture ceiling (84 req/s), and hang checks at a several-second cadence add negligible load; the watchdog scales to at least ten phones concurrently at the same measured 512 req/s aggregate. The only real cost is memory — each frame is 1.62 MB, so reusing one buffer per poller matters, measured at 488 MB/s allocation and 496 gen-2 collections per 8 seconds without reuse, versus 2.9 MB/s with. Reset and relaunch actions are rare, triggered only on a confirmed fault, so they do not affect steady-state throughput.

Cross-device and localisation QA

Mobile web compatibility sweep in real Safari

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Drive Safari on every mirrored phone from one controller: open a URL with a comma-id /shortcut/exec/url call, or Shortcut-free by tapping the address bar and typing; capture raw BMP frames and compare renderings client-side, since no OCR or image-search plug-in is connected here. The API supports the whole flow cleanly, but the rig is the limiting factor: both phones are the same iPhone XR on iOS 18.7.10, so a sweep today produces one data point, not a version matrix. 19 is the count of USB control boards, not phones; 17 of those boards have nothing attached.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get (optional id=a,b) — enumerate targets, read imgw/imgh (500x1080, not the 414x896 logical points), and confirm each phone's iOS build; on this rig it returns exactly two iPhone11,8 / 18.7.10 records.
  2. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=a,b — clear the silent stuck-click state before any tap sequence.
  3. shortcut#13 GET /api/shortcut/exec/url?id=a,b,c&url=<url>&outtime=15000 — open the same URL on every phone in one request; needs the iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-edited and AssistiveTouch-bound on each phone.
  4. click + send_key POST /api/mouse/click, then GET /api/key/sendkey?id=a,b&key=<url>, then &fn_key=ENTER — Shortcut-free alternative: tap the address bar and type; ENTER belongs in fn_key, not key.
  5. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<single>&binary=true — capture the rendered page; single-id only, one poller per phone.
  6. mouse_wheel GET /api/mouse/wheel?id=a,b&direction=down&len=60&number=1 — scroll to stitch a full-page capture; avoids the ~0.6 ms/px pointer-walk cost a swipe would carry.
  7. send_key GET /api/key/sendkey?id=a,b&key=<ascii text> — fill a form field with ASCII.
  8. clipboard/set + fn_key WIN+v POST /api/shortcut/clipboard/set, then GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+v — the only route to Unicode/CJK text, since XP has no send_text function.
  9. find-image-cv / ocr / find-text POST /api/pic/find-image-cv, GET /api/pic/ocr, POST /api/pic/find-text — documented, but each answers data.code 28 on this rig; do template matching and text assertions client-side on the raw BMP instead.
  10. send_key shift+win+3 + shortcut album GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=shift+win+3, then /api/shortcut/album/get and /album/down — the only route to above-mirror, pixel-exact resolution.

Needs

  • XP kernel on 9911 logged in via IMConsole.exe (the Phonefarm 9912 path does not exist here)
  • AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, max tracking speed, Auto-Lock Never and portrait lock per phone
  • Board bound via vid+pid together
  • iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-edited and AssistiveTouch-bound, for exec/url, clipboard/set and album/down
  • Additional phones on different iOS builds for any real version-matrix claim — none present here

Watch out

  • No Safari-version coverage exists today: two identical iPhone XR on 18.7.10 prove nothing about version differences
  • Comma-id fan-out covers exec/url, /mouse/*, /key/sendkey and clipboard/set, but /pic/screenshot, /pic/ocr, /pic/find-image and /shortcut/album/* are single-id — frame capture is always one request per phone
  • The 500x1080 mirror is a downscale of the XR's native 828x1792; sub-pixel CSS defects and font-smoothing differences are invisible without the native-resolution harvest
  • No console errors, network waterfalls or HTTP status codes are observable through any API in either edition — only visible rendering is evidence
  • Whether Safari honours HID wheel scrolling through AssistiveTouch was not measured on this rig; verify per phone before trusting a stitched capture, and never compare frames by hash
  • Address-bar tap coordinates are state-dependent (tab count, keyboard state) and drift across phones and sessions; re-home to a known state before each URL
  • Full-page stitching needs an explicit overlap/dedupe step for sticky headers and lazy-loaded content, not naive frame concatenation
  • WIN+v paste into a WKWebView form field is plausible on iOS 18 but unverified here; probe per target site before relying on it for CJK data

Scale

Navigation, scroll and typing are one request regardless of phone count; screenshot capture is strictly one request per phone (2 ms, 1.6 MB raw, phones independent up to 512 req/s aggregate across ten pollers). Page-settle time of 1-3 s per URL dominates, so a 100-URL sweep runs in roughly 3-5 minutes of wall time across the two phones today — yielding two same-version data points, not a mixed-iOS matrix — or on the order of 1,200-2,000 URL-loads/hour combined, scaling close to linearly if more same-geometry phones were added.

Localisation QA and App Store screenshot harvesting

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

One phone per locale is driven by deep link to each marketing screen in a single multi-id request; the phone's own hardware screenshot hotkey (shift+win+3) writes a native-resolution PNG into Photos, which the Shortcut album functions pull back to the PC. The 500x1080 mirror frame is used only for a quick overflow and layout-shift check, since it sits far below native resolution. Every step that actually lands on a screen runs through the iMouse Shortcut, and per-locale language switching has no API at all — this rig has neither the Shortcut confirmed installed nor a way to verify the flow end to end.

How

  1. set_dev GET /api/device/set?id=<id>&name=xr-de-DE — label each locale phone once so the harvest files correctly; re-read /device/get to confirm, since the response only echoes the ids that were set.
  2. none (manual) none — set each phone's display language by hand; there is no XP or Phonefarm function for this, and a blind coordinate walk through Settings is unverifiable without OCR.
  3. shortcut#13 GET /api/shortcut/exec/url?id=<id1>,<id2>,...&url=myapp://screen/onboarding&outtime=15000 — land every locale phone on the same screen in one request; the multi-id fan-out is what makes this cheap.
  4. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true (poll until stable) — take the mirror frame as a layout-check artefact only, diffed against an en-US golden for overflow and wrapped buttons.
  5. send_key (shift+win+3) GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<id1>,<id2>,...&fn_key=shift+win+3 — take the phone's native-resolution screenshot into Photos; needs Full Keyboard Access ON.
  6. shortcut#1 GET /api/shortcut/album/get?id=<id>&num=1&outtime=20000 — find the new file; single-id, and ordering by num is undocumented, so match by create_time.
  7. shortcut#2 POST /api/shortcut/album/down {id, list:[{album_name,name,ext}], zip:1, outtime:60000} — pull the file to the PC; the response carries no file path, so locate it by name under <install dir>\Shortcut\Media.
  8. shortcut#3 POST /api/shortcut/album/del {id, list, outtime} — clean up so the next capture is unambiguous; /shortcut/album/clear empties an album entirely and is irreversible.
  9. find-text POST /api/pic/find-text {id, text:[...], contain:true, similarity:0.8} — optional text assertion on the mirror frame; unavailable here (OCR plug-in code 28).

Needs

  • iMouse Shortcut installed on every locale phone, IP-edited to the kernel, every permission allowed, bound to an AssistiveTouch custom key — none confirmed on this rig
  • Shortcuts > Advanced toggles for running scripts and deleting without confirmation
  • Full Keyboard Access, AssistiveTouch, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock; each phone bound to its board and on the kernel's LAN
  • Display language set by hand, per phone, outside the run
  • A per-locale en-US golden mirror frame; App Store frame composition done externally
  • OCR plug-in for the optional text assertion — absent here

Watch out

  • The entire pipeline from "land on the screen" onward is Shortcut-gated, not just the harvest half; only the mirror-frame diff and the hardware-hotkey screenshot are pure HID/HTTP
  • album/get, album/down and album/del are single-id, so a full harvest of N locales x M screens costs N x M x 3 serial Shortcut round trips; only the fan-out steps (exec/url, sendkey) are free
  • Any declined "Allow" prompt on the phone surfaces only as an undiagnostic code 30 "Call timeout"
  • Album ordering is undocumented; select by create_time, not by assuming num=1 is newest, since XP has no date filter
  • The hardware screenshot needs Full Keyboard Access ON as a standing accessibility toggle; if an iOS update silently resets it, the harvest fails at that step with no error surfaced, since /key/sendkey reports success regardless of whether iOS honoured the key combo
  • A language change restarts SpringBoard and drops the mirroring session; schedule it outside the run and re-cast afterward
  • Neither phone on this rig is confirmed to have the Shortcut installed, so this use case is unverified end to end here
  • Deep links must be static, vetted strings baked into the harness, never derived from anything a phone or webpage returns
  • Nothing in the vendor docs specifies how the Shortcut itself navigates to a screen before firing the deep link; if a locale's screen has no myapp:// route and instead relies on blind coordinate taps, the same per-locale layout risk that rules out the Settings-walk fallback resurfaces for in-app screens too

Scale

Fan-out steps are one request regardless of locale count. The harvest is the bottleneck: album/get and album/down are single-id Shortcut round trips over Wi-Fi, realistically 3-10 seconds each rather than the sub-millisecond kernel calls elsewhere in this API. Ten locales by eight screens by three calls is 240 round trips; if phones cannot be harvested concurrently — unverified on this rig, unlike the proven-independent /mouse/move and /pic/screenshot — that is 12-40 minutes wall clock, not the 5-10 minutes a naive estimate gives. Mirror-frame settle checks are effectively free (2 ms/frame, phones independent), but the settle dwell must respect each phone's own frame rate, several hundred milliseconds longer on the slow XR.

Release health: canaries, ad verification and flow recording

iOS update canary phones running rig preflight plus smoke suite

PartialWith caveats

Keep one or two rack phones ahead of the fleet on the newest iOS; a job watches /device/get for the version change, runs a preflight (calibration lookup, pointer accuracy at three corners, hotkeys, a real tap) and then an app smoke suite, so an iOS release that breaks the app is told apart from one that breaks the control path itself. The vendor's own docs record exactly this failure mode: the Home fn_key exists only to fix a malfunction introduced in iOS 26.1, requiring kernel 2026.2.27 or later.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get?id=<canary> — watch for the version change; a WebSocket client can get the same record pushed on dev_change / dev_connect for an event-driven trigger instead of polling.
  2. get_devicemodel_list GET /api/config/devicemodel/get — check the calibration library has a record for the new model+iOS pair; the response body is elided in the vendor doc, so probe the live shape before writing matching logic.
  3. mouse collection open/cfg/close GET /api/device/collection/mouse?id=<canary>&cmd=1 … &cmd=2 — collect mouse parameters if location_crc is empty or taps return code 11; progress arrives only on the collection_mouse WebSocket callback, and only one device can collect at a time.
  4. save_dev_location GET /api/device/collection/mouse/save?id=<canary>&describe=<note> — publish the collected profile so the fleet auto-matches after it updates; there is no delete, so a bad profile can only be superseded.
  5. mouse_reset_pos + mouse_move + get_device_screenshot /api/mouse/reset, then /api/mouse/move to three corners, each followed by /api/pic/screenshot?binary=true — pointer accuracy probe; detect the dot by mean pixel diff in a ~40 px box (measured 1.4-9.8 versus an idle floor of 0.02-0.03).
  6. send_key GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<canary>&fn_key=WIN+h (also TAB+b, AppSwitch, ControlBar) — hotkey path check, verified by a whole-frame mean diff.
  7. click (with stuck-click guard) two Home presses, then /api/mouse/click?id=<canary>&x=&y= — tap check; a click reading ~0.0 mean diff after a working move is the measured stuck-click state, cleared by /mouse/reset, not /mouse/up.
  8. shortcut#13 + get_device_screenshot GET /api/shortcut/exec/url?id=<canary>&url=<deep link> (or click-only navigation), then /api/pic/screenshot?binary=true — app smoke suite diffed against previous-iOS goldens with a loose threshold for OS-chrome changes.
  9. auto_connect_screen GET /api/device/airplay/connect?id=<canary>, or the global auto_connect flag via /api/config/imserver/set — recover the canary after the update reboot; progress on the airplay_connect_log callback.

Needs

  • A dedicated canary phone holding only test data, enrolled in beta or with automatic updates on
  • A human to enter the passcode after reboot and run the phone-side half of mouse-parameter collection (the console presents a QR code; no collection URL is published)
  • Board bound with /config/usb/get showing state 2
  • Stored goldens and icon-coordinate maps per phone
  • A WebSocket client for the kernel version and any collection/cast progress — none of this is available over plain HTTP
  • IMConsole.exe logged in with a license state that allows the device online; the full accessibility checklist re-verified after every update

Watch out

  • The version watch, pointer probe, hotkeys and tap check are fully native; calibration collection needs a manual phone-side step and the smoke suite's deep links need the Shortcut, so the job cannot run unattended end to end
  • The kernel version needed to know whether the Home-key fix is present is WebSocket-only; a purely HTTP job can detect that a phone updated but not whether the kernel already supports that iOS
  • Apple, not this API, controls when an enrolled device installs a downloaded update, typically overnight and only when idle; whether mirroring around the clock with Auto-Lock Never counts as idle to iOS's scheduler is unverified, so treat the job as event-driven off the version signal, not scheduled to a fixed nightly time
  • Only one device can collect mouse parameters at a time, and a published bad profile is permanent and auto-matches every same-model/same-iOS phone the moment it updates; gate publishing behind the corner-probe pass criteria and never run it unattended before that gate is confirmed
  • Whether the rig can type a passcode through the board after a reboot is unverified; plan for a manual unlock, and make the job fail loudly on a lock-screen frame rather than retry against it
  • The three-corner pointer thresholds were measured on iOS 18.7.10; a canary running ahead on a newer iOS could see AssistiveTouch pointer rendering shift in ways that move those thresholds — treat them as a starting point to re-validate per iOS version
  • Beta iOS can change AssistiveTouch or pointer behaviour in ways the vendor kernel has not caught up with; that is a genuine canary result, not a rig bug
  • Do not update the whole rack at once: a calibration miss puts every tap in the wrong place on every phone simultaneously

Scale

A preflight is roughly a dozen API calls and about ten raw-BMP screenshots per canary, seconds of kernel time; pointer travel for the three-corner probe is under 1.5 seconds at ~0.6 ms/px. The real costs sit outside the API: the reboot itself is 60-90 seconds offline plus an unbounded wait for a human to unlock, and mouse-parameter collection is one device at a time and human-operated, minutes not seconds. Screenshots must wait for a genuinely new AirPlay frame (up to ~220 ms on a slow phone) rather than assume 30 fps. This scales to one or two canaries per rig, run opportunistically rather than on a guaranteed cadence.

Ad slot fill, render and time-to-render measurement

Native APIWith caveats

Open each ad placement, poll the mirror frame and classify a fixed slot rectangle client-side from the decoded raw BMP: near-zero colour variance means no fill, a jump that stays stable for about a second means a creative painted, and the delta from the navigation timestamp to that first stable frame is time-to-render. The classification is pure arithmetic on pixels the kernel already returns, so it needs no plug-in — which matters, since none is connected on this rig. Repeated across sessions this builds fill-rate and render-time distributions from a real SDK on real iOS.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get?id=<id> — read the slot's coordinate space (imgw x imgh, 500x1080 here, not iOS points) and confirm state and air_pid before trusting any frame.
  2. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=a,b — clear the stuck-click state before the tap sequence.
  3. shortcut#13 / click GET /api/shortcut/exec/url?id=a,b&url=<deeplink>&outtime=15000, or POST /api/mouse/click {id,x,y} — navigate to the placement and record t0 as the PC's send timestamp.
  4. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<single>&binary=true — poll the frame containing the slot; whether rect combines with binary=true is undocumented and unprobed, so fetch the full frame and crop client-side.
  5. (client-side) none (arithmetic on the decoded BMP) — classify the crop by mean absolute pixel difference against a calibrated idle control (measured ~0.02-0.03 idle, 20-160 for real change); never use MD5 or byte equality.
  6. find_multi_color POST /api/pic/find-multi-color {id, list:[{first_color:'x|y|RRGGBB-tolerance,...', rect, similarity}], same:false, all:false} — detect the SDK's placeholder by colour signature; the plug-in dependency is unconfirmed on this rig, so treat this as an enhancement, not a foundation.
  7. find_image_ex POST /api/pic/find-image-cv {id, img_list, similarity} — confirm the AdChoices badge; unusable here (plug-in code 28), do the template match client-side on the crop already held.
  8. ocr GET /api/pic/ocr?id=<single>&rect=[l,t,r,b] — read ad copy or "no fill" text; probed 10 Sep 2026 and returns code 28.
  9. shortcut#23 / #18 GET /api/shortcut/switch/wlan?id=a,b&state=0 or /api/shortcut/switch/flight?id=a,b&state=1 — test the offline/late-fill path; this blanks the mirror on the same phone, since AirPlay runs over Wi-Fi, so the condition cannot actually be observed on this rig.

Needs

  • Test ad unit IDs with the device registered as a test device per network
  • IMConsole.exe logged in, phone state non-zero with a live air_pid
  • Board bound with location_crc non-empty for the tap-navigation route
  • Per-screen slot rectangles measured once in mirror pixels from a raw BMP
  • iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-edited and bound for exec/url and any switch/* call — not probed here
  • Fixed display settings (brightness, True Tone, Night Shift) if colour-signature matching is used

Watch out

  • Time-to-render is measured at the PC: the clock starts on send and stops on frame arrival, carrying AirPlay encode and Wi-Fi latency as an unknown positive bias; treat it as a same-phone relative metric only
  • Timing resolution is bounded by that phone's own AirPlay source rate — roughly 34 ms granularity on the fast XR, 220 ms on its identical twin — so a 100 ms poll on the slow phone mostly returns the same frame again
  • /pic/screenshot is single-id, so the slot is sampled with one poller per phone even though navigation and taps are multi-id
  • A video or animated creative can outrun the slow phone's mirror rate, making "stable for 1 s" an unsafe test there; run video placements on the fast phone or lengthen the window
  • The rack holds two phones on one iOS build, so there is no per-OS or per-device-class breakdown available today
  • The chain has no app-relaunch or ad-session-reset step: repeatedly re-navigating to the same placement can just redisplay a cached creative rather than trigger a fresh ad-server call, so a measured "fill rate" may really be a cache-hit rate — force a cold ad request (relaunch the host app) between samples to measure true fill
  • The variance classifier is vulnerable to false positives from system UI (a low-battery banner, an incoming-call banner, a keyboard) landing inside a poorly chosen crop, especially near the top or bottom of screen where ad slots often sit

Scale

A single poller sustains ~84 req/s at p50 2 ms and phones are independent, so sampling a slot at 10 Hz per phone is nearly free, though 10 Hz only buys real resolution on the fast phone. With two phones, an overnight run at roughly 50-100 placement loads per phone per hour — bounded by placement-load and settle time, not the API — yields on the order of 100-200 impressions per hour rack-wide today; that does not extrapolate to the 19-board count, since 17 boards have no phone attached. Keep only the crop and the classification, not the 1.6 MB frames, or storage becomes the real cost.

UX flow recording with a timestamped input log

Native APIWith caveats

While a script drives a task through an app, record two synchronised streams: raw mirror frames polled at a fixed period, and a timestamped log of every input call with its coordinates and id list. Discard duplicate frames by pixel diff, encode externally, and overlay each commanded coordinate against the pointer's own low-contrast dot visible in the frame. The output is a flow video with the exact input sequence attached, plus steps/taps/screens/time-to-complete metrics pulled from the log rather than a stopwatch, re-runnable whenever the app ships a change.

How

  1. set_dev GET /api/device/set?id=<id>&name=AppA-v3.2 — label each phone with what it is running; re-read /device/get afterward, since XP echoes only the ids that were set.
  2. get_device_list GET /api/device/get?id=<id> — establish imgw/imgh as the coordinate space and confirm a live air_pid.
  3. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=a,b — clear the stuck-click state before recording starts.
  4. send_key (fn_key WIN+h, twice) GET /api/key/sendkey?id=a,b&fn_key=WIN+h — normalise the starting state; the two XRs have different home screens, so an identical coordinate opens different apps.
  5. loop_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<single>&binary=true, polled on a fixed ~33 ms period — run the frame recorder, one per phone; XP has no server-push stream, so recording is client-side polling with a fixed period and a reused buffer.
  6. mouse_move / click / swipe / mouse_wheel / send_key the full input vocabulary, each call logged with its coordinate and id list — drive the task; a real drag is down, streamed moves, up.
  7. error_push (WebSocket) ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api — {data.message, data.call_fun} — catch input failures the HTTP reply does not report; the only asynchronous signal that an input actually failed at the board.
  8. (client-side) none — external ffmpeg or equivalent — deduplicate frames by mean absolute pixel diff and encode; never MD5-compare, since encoder noise changes every frame.
  9. shortcut#7 POST /api/shortcut/album/upload {id, files, album_name, zip, outtime} — give every phone identical input assets so upload flows are comparable; Shortcut-gated.
  10. (manual + shortcut) GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=ControlBar, tap the Screen Recording control, then /api/shortcut/album/get and /album/down — capture at native resolution instead of the 500 px mirror; there is no API that starts iOS Screen Recording, and the toggle's coordinate must be hand-calibrated per phone.

Needs

  • IMConsole.exe logged in, phone state non-zero with a live air_pid, board state 2 and location_crc non-empty
  • The full accessibility checklist per phone (AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, max tracking speed, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock, StandBy off), none of it queryable over the API
  • ffmpeg or an equivalent external encoder
  • Accounts with synthetic test data
  • iMouse Shortcut for album upload/download
  • A WebSocket client for error_push and dev_change/dev_disconnect events

Watch out

  • The slow phone (~4.5 fps) records as a slideshow; put teardowns on the fast phone (~29 fps) and report per-phone fps in the output
  • Recordings are a 500x1080 downscale of the XR's native 828x1792; native resolution needs the manual Control-Center recording toggle plus a Shortcut-gated harvest, and that toggle's tap coordinate is undocumented anywhere and must be hand-calibrated per phone, re-checked on every iOS update
  • Pre-dedupe data rate is ~47 MB/s per phone at 29 fps, far less on the slow phone (~7.3 MB/s); size ingest buffers per phone's own measured fps, not a shared constant, and dedupe/encode on the fly rather than buffering raw frames
  • /pic/screenshot is single-id, so N apps recorded means N pollers; the limit on parallel recordings is encoder CPU and disk, not the kernel
  • A whole-frame diff cannot see the pointer dot; verify a move landed by diffing a ~40 px box around the commanded coordinate, and treat "the app opened" as inference, not proof an input worked
  • A full-height swipe is ~580 ms of pointer travel, which iOS may read as a slow drag rather than a flick; prefer the short axis, /mouse/wheel, or a shorter length so velocity-dependent gestures still fire
  • The input log and frame poller run on independent loops, so the frame nearest an input timestamp is not guaranteed to show the pointer having arrived, especially on the slow phone; carry an explicit per-phone uncertainty window on any overlay, not a single frame index
  • A "flow video next month" diff is only valid if the app's layout has not shifted target coordinates; a layout change produces wrong taps with no error, which /mouse/reset discipline helps catch but does not eliminate
  • There is no audio capture, no touch-event ground truth and no accessibility-tree export; the log records what was sent and the video records what the mirror showed, nothing about what the app actually received

Scale

Frame capture is 2 ms per request and phones are fully independent (two pollers 83+85 req/s, ten pollers 512 req/s aggregate), and input traffic does not slow polling, so the API is never the bottleneck. The ceiling is each phone's own AirPlay source rate and PC-side encoding: today that means one fully usable smooth recording (fast phone, ~29 fps) plus one degraded recording (slow phone, ~4.5 fps) per PC, since only two phones exist and mirror. A monitoring wall of thumbnails alongside the recorder costs the master poller nothing (17.7 fps with it off versus 17.6 fps with it on at 30 fps). Scaling further is bounded by per-phone AirPlay fps and encoder/disk throughput, not by the kernel.

Outside-the-box measurement: latency, network transitions and accessibility

Tap-to-paint latency and scroll smoothness from frame arrival timing

PartialWith caveats

Use the flat-out raw-BMP frame poller as a sampling oscilloscope: timestamp every frame whose pixel difference from its predecessor exceeds the noise floor, measure the interval from an input call to the first changed frame in the target region and to the point that region goes still again, and count distinct frames per second during a scripted scroll to spot jank against the phone's own baseline. Every call is native HTTP and needs no plug-in, but the API supplies no server-side frame timestamp, so these are relative, same-phone A/B figures, never absolute device latencies. It is the only performance signal this API exposes at all, which makes it genuinely useful for build-over-build regression checks on one fixed phone.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get?id=<id> — confirm mirroring and read imgw/imgh (500x1080, not the 414x896 logical points); record air_pid so a mid-run reconnection can be detected and that run discarded.
  2. swipe + get_device_screenshot GET /api/mouse/swipe?id=<id>&direction=left&len=0.5 (loop), while polling GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true flat out for 5 s — baseline the phone's own frame production under continuous driven motion (measured 28.9 new frames/s on the fast XR).
  3. mouse_move GET /api/mouse/move?id=<id>&x=<bx>&y=<by> — pre-position the pointer so the measured click carries no pointer-walk cost (measured ~0.6 ms/px); the pre-move itself paints the pointer dot into the frame, so the stable baseline must be read after it settles, not before.
  4. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=<id>&x=<bx>&y=<by> (optionally &button=1&time=<ms>) — fire the input and timestamp the send; pin time to a fixed value across all A/B runs, since a changed press duration shifts when iOS registers the tap. Send /mouse/reset first, since a phone can silently stop honouring clicks while moves and hardware keys keep working.
  5. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true (poll flat out; optionally &rect=[l,t,r,b]) — detect first paint as the first polled frame whose mean diff in the target region exceeds the reaction threshold (idle floor 0.02-0.03, real reaction 20-160); raw BMP only, since jpg=true costs 40.5 ms and caps at ~21 req/s.
  6. mouse_wheel or swipe GET /api/mouse/wheel?id=<id>&direction=down&len=30&number=30, or GET /api/mouse/swipe?id=<id>&direction=up&len=0.5 — drive a scroll and count distinct frames per second; wheel avoids the pointer-walk cost that would make a full-height swipe read as a slow drag rather than a flick.
  7. get_device_list GET /api/device/get?id=<id> — repeat N times, take medians, and discard any run where air_pid or frame body size changed, or a dev_disconnect/dev_rotate/error_push callback arrived during the window.

Needs

  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in, phone mirroring with a live air_pid
  • Board bound (vid/pid/uid set, /config/usb/get state 2) and location_crc non-empty
  • A per-phone frame-rate baseline, re-measured whenever air_ratio/air_fps change
  • A fixed poll period with buffer reuse — never an adaptive interval fed by observed gaps
  • One dedicated poller thread per phone; Auto-Lock Never and orientation locked
  • A/B builds compared on the same phone only — cross-phone comparison is meaningless here

Watch out

  • The API exposes no server-side frame timestamp, so what is actually measured is time from issuing the input call to the client observing a changed frame, including HTTP round trip, poll interval and encoder pipeline delay; report it as a bound, never as device latency
  • Sampling resolution is bounded by the AirPlay source: ~33 ms on the fast XR, ~220 ms on the slow one, which makes the slow phone's numbers close to useless for latency work, though its scroll-smoothness figures remain valid against its own baseline
  • XP has no push stream; every sample is a poll, and the poll cadence is part of the measurement
  • The click's own execution includes the board walking the pointer to (x,y); the pre-move reduces that to near zero but does not remove the click's own board latency from the figure
  • Only relative, same-phone, same-session comparisons are defensible; any change to air_ratio, air_fps, air_img_fps, air_refresh, Wi-Fi conditions or a mirroring reconnect invalidates the comparison
  • /pic/screenshot accepts one id only, so there is no way to sample several phones from one request, and re-verifying air_pid/imgw/imgh/air_ratio between build swaps is easy to miss if done manually via the console
  • This is not read-only: the scroll pass moves app state and the tap opens whatever is under it, so run it only on a phone and build you are willing to perturb
  • The API is unauthenticated on the LAN, so another host, or the vendor console itself, can inject input mid-measurement; close IMConsole's own activity on the phone during a run

Scale

Each phone under test needs its own flat-out poller: 84 req/s at p50 12.7 ms, 1.62 MB per frame, with one reused buffer per poller — without reuse, measured 488 MB/s allocation and 496 gen-2 collections in 8 s, exactly the kind of periodic hitching that would corrupt timing work. Phones are independent (two concurrent pollers measured 83 and 85 req/s, ten measured 512 req/s aggregate at p50 3 ms, worst p95 142 ms), and input traffic does not slow polling nor vice versa, so stimulus and sampler run fully concurrently. Effective sampling resolution stays capped by the AirPlay source regardless: usable tap-to-paint samples on the slow phone top out around 16,000 per hour, far below the raw request ceiling. Never use jpg mode for this; it adds 40 ms of encode and caps the sampler at 21 req/s.

Offline and network-transition testing with the split-network trick

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Give each phone a static Wi-Fi IP with no gateway so Wi-Fi carries only the LAN — AirPlay video plus the Shortcut's return path — while the internet rides cellular. Toggling cellular data with /shortcut/switch/cdpd then takes the app fully offline and back without ever losing the mirror, so a golden frame can be captured before, during and after the outage. The airplane-mode variant is also reachable but blinds the rig entirely and needs a pre-recorded blind-HID recovery path.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get?id=<a,b,c> — confirm each phone is mirroring and read imgw/imgh (500x1080).
  2. none (manual) none — Wi-Fi > Configure IP > Manual, IP on the PC subnet, gateway left empty; a one-time per-phone setting with no API that takes effect immediately without dropping mirroring.
  3. shortcut#24 GET /api/shortcut/device/ip?id=<one id>&state=1 (and state=0) — verify the split holds, LAN vs. public IP; single-id, one round trip per phone; a code 30 here means the Shortcut isn't bound, not that the network is wrong.
  4. shortcut#13 / click GET /api/shortcut/exec/url?id=<a,b>&url=<deep link>, or /api/mouse/click?id=<a,b>&x=&y= — drive the app to the screen under test; send /mouse/reset to the whole target set first.
  5. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true — capture the golden online frame.
  6. shortcut#21 GET /api/shortcut/switch/cdpd?id=<a,b,c>&state=0 — cellular off, one request for the whole cohort; outtime is milliseconds on XP, not the seconds the Phonefarm doc uses.
  7. click / swipe / wheel + get_device_screenshot /api/mouse/click, /api/mouse/swipe, /api/mouse/wheel, /api/pic/screenshot?binary=true — exercise the app and observe the offline state; assertions must be client-side pixel diff or template match, since OCR answers code 28 here.
  8. shortcut#20 GET /api/shortcut/switch/cdpd?id=<a,b,c>&state=1 — cellular back on; time-to-first-refresh measured client-side by diffing the content region across polled frames.
  9. shortcut#18 / #19 GET /api/shortcut/switch/flight?id=<a,b>&state=1 then state=0 — airplane-mode variant; state=1 drops Wi-Fi too, so the Shortcut can no longer be reached and the recovery call cannot get through — plan the outage as one-way.
  10. send_key + click + auto_connect_screen GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<a>&fn_key=ControlBar, then /api/mouse/click on a pre-recorded tile coordinate, then /api/device/airplay/connect?id=<a> — blind recovery from airplane mode over pure HID; the coordinate must be recorded per phone before the outage, since Control Center layout is per-phone.
  11. shortcut#22 / #23 GET /api/shortcut/switch/wlan?id=<a,b>&state=0|1 — Wi-Fi toggle variant; severs both the video channel and the Shortcut's return path in one move, strictly worse than the cdpd route for this test.
  12. none none — no bandwidth-throttling or lossy-link function exists in either edition; apply it on the router or carrier side, upstream of the AirPlay/LAN hop this split deliberately keeps untouched.

Needs

  • A SIM with an active data plan in every phone under test — neither XR on this rig is documented as having one
  • Static-IP-without-gateway Wi-Fi configuration applied by hand on each phone
  • iMouse Shortcut installed, IP-edited and AssistiveTouch-bound — not verified on this rig
  • Board bound and physically attached (/config/usb/get state 2)
  • Control Center with two icon rows, portrait lock, Auto-Lock Never; IMConsole.exe running and logged in
  • A per-phone pre-recorded mirror-pixel coordinate of the Control Center airplane tile

Watch out

  • Every network-toggle step runs through the iMouse Shortcut, which is not confirmed installed or bound on this rig; a code 30 after ~15 s is the signature of an unbound Shortcut
  • outtime on XP is milliseconds, not the seconds the Phonefarm doc specifies — a value copied across editions is off by 1000x
  • /shortcut/device/ip is single-id, so verification is one round trip per phone even though the toggles fan out; count that cost for every phone in the cohort, both before and after each toggle, not just once
  • Airplane and Wi-Fi "off" are one-way over the API: the Shortcut's return path dies with the LAN, so only pre-recorded blind HID brings the phone back
  • No text recognition is available on this rig, so "assert the offline banner says X" must be a client-side pixel diff or template match, not OCR
  • The kernel exposes no throttling or packet-loss injection; that belongs on the router or carrier side
  • Neither phone on this rig is documented as carrying an active SIM, so this use case is currently untestable here without adding cellular service
  • iOS's automatic Wi-Fi reconnection and captive-portal detection can silently revert a static-IP-no-gateway configuration after a reboot or a brief Wi-Fi drop, and the only signal is a failed IP-readback
  • Because /device/airplay/connect has no force flag on XP, a phone recovered from a dropped Wi-Fi mid-outage may need /device/airplay/disconnect first, adding another manual-recovery branch beyond the documented blind-HID tap
  • The mechanism by which the vendor Shortcut actually flips cellular data is undocumented beyond the endpoint's parameters and is almost certainly a Settings deep-link or blind UI navigation — the same fragile-across-iOS-versions risk already flagged for language switching elsewhere, but sitting squarely on this entry's critical path; a future iOS release could silently break cdpd while still returning code 0

Scale

The cdpd/flight/wlan toggles accept a comma-separated id list, so one HTTP request switches the whole cohort in a single Shortcut round trip (outtime default 15000 ms; observed Shortcut round trips run seconds, not milliseconds). Frame observation is unaffected by the outage and stays at ~2 ms per raw BMP poll per phone, phones independent. The real ceiling is each phone's AirPlay source rate: ~29 new frames/s on the fast XR, ~4.5/s on the slow one, so timing a reconnection on the slow phone has a ~220 ms resolution floor. IP-verification and screenshot steps are single-id and scale linearly with cohort size; a single online/outage/recovery cycle for a two-phone cohort runs on the order of 30-90 seconds of API/Shortcut time plus however long the app itself takes to notice and recover.

Keyboard-accessibility focus-order audit via Full Keyboard Access

Native APIWith caveats

Full Keyboard Access is already on for every rack phone because the rig needs it to function at all; stepping focus with TAB from the control board and locating the focus ring by frame diff builds a focus-order map of every screen, exposing unreachable controls, focus traps and controls that take focus but do not activate. TAB fans out to every phone in one request, so this audit can run on every screen of every build rather than once a release, at essentially no extra prerequisite cost.

How

  1. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<a,b> — park the pointer and clear any stuck-click state; the dot itself would otherwise show up in the diffs used to find the focus ring, so also move it to a fixed corner with a separate /mouse/move and mask that region.
  2. click (or shortcut#13) /api/mouse/click?id=<a,b>&x=&y=, or GET /api/shortcut/exec/url?id=<a,b>&url=<deep link> — land on the screen under test.
  3. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true — capture the baseline frame; one poller per phone.
  4. send_key GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<a,b>&fn_key=TAB — advance focus one step; whether TAB belongs in fn_key or the key parameter is ambiguous in the doc, so probe once and pin it down. Comma ids step every phone together.
  5. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true — locate the focus ring by mean absolute pixel diff against the previous frame (idle floor 0.02-0.03, real change 20-160), with the status bar and any animated region masked out.
  6. send_key + get_device_screenshot (loop) loop of /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=TAB and /api/pic/screenshot — repeat until focus returns to the first control, recording order and rects; a cycle shorter than the visible-control count is a focus trap, a control the cycle never reaches is unreachable.
  7. send_key GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<a>&key=<single space>, or &fn_key=ENTER — activate the focused control; space is sent as a literal-space key parameter, not a named hotkey, and which of the two actually activates is app-dependent.
  8. send_key GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<a,b>&fn_key=TAB+b — back-navigation check; the hotkey table itself notes it is "not supported by all apps."
  9. key_release_all GET /api/key/upall?id=<a,b> — recover a stuck key or chord between screens.
  10. none (manual) none — Dynamic Type / large-text variant is a manual per-phone setting with no API; run the same golden-diff suite against it and review flagged screens by hand.

Needs

  • Full Keyboard Access ON on each phone, already required by the rig; the vendor's recommended 1 s Auto-Hide raised for this audit or accepted as lossy
  • Board bound with /config/usb/get state 2, since TAB travels over USB, not Wi-Fi
  • Live mirroring with a live air_pid; a per-screen mask for animated regions
  • An inventory of visible controls per screen, since there is no OCR to name what the ring sits on
  • One phone at the largest Dynamic Type size; apps and accounts you own or are permitted to test

Watch out

  • Auto-Hide at 1 s hides the ring a second after each TAB; on the slow phone (~220 ms between frames) that window holds only a handful of frames, so raise Auto-Hide on the audit phone or accept missed captures
  • The audit's throughput is source-rate bound, not API-bound: the poll returns in 2 ms, but a new frame only arrives at the phone's own AirPlay rate
  • Without OCR the audit produces rectangles and an order, not control names; naming needs the vendor plug-in or client-side template matching
  • A missing focus ring is ambiguous between a genuine accessibility defect and a control that simply doesn't draw a system focus indicator — many custom-drawn UIKit/SwiftUI/WebView controls have none even though focus moved; pixel diffing cannot see accessibility-tree focus, only whatever the OS chooses to render. State this as a hard method limitation
  • VoiceOver itself cannot be audited this way: the API has no audio capture, and enabling VoiceOver changes gesture semantics in ways that would break the control path the rig depends on
  • TAB fans out to all phones, but screenshots are single-id, so observation scales linearly and each phone needs its own poller
  • Blindly pressing Space or Return on every focused control will activate destructive actions (delete, send, purchase) as readily as harmless ones; gate activation to reviewed screens
  • Both rack phones are the same model and iOS build, so this validates one iOS version only; a Full Keyboard Access regression specific to a different release would not be caught here
  • Inter-screen navigation has no API-driven discovery without OCR; expect tens of screens audited per hour per phone, not hundreds, once navigation and ambiguous-diff review are included

Scale

One TAB request steps every phone at once and costs a HID report rather than pointer travel, avoiding the ~0.6 ms/px board walk entirely. Observation is single-id and source-rate bound: on the fast phone a new frame lands roughly every 34 ms, so a 30-control screen audits in a couple of seconds; on the slow phone at ~4.5 fps the same screen takes 10-15 seconds, with some risk of missing the ring under a 1 s Auto-Hide. Frame polling and input traffic do not interfere, and ten concurrent pollers sustained 512 req/s total, so the observation side scales to a rack. Including inter-screen navigation and manual review of ambiguous diffs, realistic sustained throughput is roughly 20-60 screens/hour on the fast phone and 5-15 screens/hour on the slow phone.

Long-running reliability and monitoring

Long-duration soak with a self-healing recovery ladder

PartialWith caveats

Run an app scenario for 24-72 hours on every mirrored phone with periodic health probes, recovering with a cost-ordered ladder: pointer reset, key release, board reset, re-cast, phone restart, then app relaunch. Subscribing to the WebSocket callbacks (dev_disconnect, usb_change, error_push, airplay_connect_log) stamps rig events into the same log, so a gap in app data reads as rig degradation rather than an app defect. Memory leaks, slow-downs and rare crashes only surface over hours on real devices, and a soak that cannot tell "the app died" from "the board stopped honouring taps" produces worse than nothing.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get (optionally ?id=a,b) — enumerate the soak target set; read imgw/imgh, state, air_pid, bound vid/pid/uid and location_crc. Both XRs return 500 x 1080 and location_crc B0DBD800; all coordinates below are in this mirror-pixel space, never the 414x896 logical points.
  2. get_usb_list GET /api/config/usb/get — read board health per slot before and during the soak. state 2 = board plus phone attached (control-ready), state 1 = board only. Do not parse ver/uver as a firmware version, it is mojibake on this build.
  3. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<comma list> — hourly rung 0: clear any silent stuck-click state on the whole target set. There is no id=all keyword anywhere in XP, so build the explicit list from /device/get. This is the only call that clears the stuck-click state, and it stays cleared.
  4. send_key (fn_key) GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<list>&fn_key=WIN+h — keyboard-channel liveness probe: Home press, then whole-frame mean-pixel-diff over ~20. Measured 142.15 mean diff while the pointer was stuck, so this proves the board and cable only, never that taps work.
  5. mouse_move GET /api/mouse/move?id=<list>&x=&y= — pointer-channel liveness probe: move to a known point, then diff a ~40 px box around it. A landed pointer dot reads 1.4-9.8 in the box against a 0.02 idle floor; a whole-frame diff cannot see it.
  6. click / mouse_wheel / swipe /api/mouse/click (button 1-8, x, y, time ms), /api/mouse/wheel (direction, len 1-127, number), /api/mouse/swipe (direction, len, stepping, step_sleep, brake, sx/sy/ex/ey) — scenario loop with per-iteration tap-to-paint latency logging. XP button is numeric ("1" left, "2" right), not Phonefarm's "left"/"right" strings; the swipe JSON examples spell the step count "steping" but the parameter table says "stepping" — send the table's spelling.
  7. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true — frame capture for golden-diff assertions and the 5-minute time-lapse archive. id is single-only; binary returns raw bytes with no JSON. Measured 2 ms / 1,620,054 bytes raw BMP versus 40 ms and a ~21 req/s cap for jpg; one poller per phone, phones independent.
  8. mouse_reset_pos / key_release_all /api/mouse/reset?id=<list> then /api/key/upall?id=<list> — recovery rung 1 (pointer) and rung 2 (keyboard). /mouse/up does not clear a stuck click; only reset does.
  9. restart_usb GET /api/device/usb/restart?id=720A|C241 — recovery rung 3 (control board). id is vid|pid, not the phone deviceid and not the 8-hex uid. Confirm success via usb_change codes 20 then 19 then 12, and /config/usb/get returning to state 2.
  10. discon_airplay + auto_connect_screen /api/device/airplay/disconnect?id=<list> then /api/device/airplay/connect?id=<list> (or /connect/all) — recovery rung 4 (mirroring session). XP has no "force" flag, so disconnect is a separate mandatory call; progress arrives only on the airplay_connect_log callback. If the receiver has vanished from the phone's mirroring list, /api/imserver/regmdns re-advertises it without a kernel restart.
  11. restart_device Preferred: GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<list>&fn_key=CTRL+ALT+SHIFT+WIN+r. Shortcut route: /api/shortcut/switch/device?id=<list>&state=1. Last: /api/device/restart?id=<list> — recovery rung 5 (phone restart). The hotkey needs no plug-in and no Shortcut, so it is the only rung-5 route certain to work here; with no OCR plug-in on this rig, /device/restart is expected to answer code 15 or 28.
  12. shortcut#13 GET /api/shortcut/exec/url?id=<list>&url=<scheme or universal link> — recovery rung 6: relaunch the app under test. Requires the Shortcut installed, IP-edited and AssistiveTouch-bound, and the app must expose a URL scheme or universal link. Without it, fall back to two WIN+h presses plus a tap on the app icon.
  13. shortcut#15 GET /api/shortcut/switch/bril?id=<list>&state=0.1 — keep phones cool and dim through the soak. state is a float strictly between 0 and 1, Shortcut-dependent. Keep it consistent, since colour-based assertions sample the mirror frame.
  14. callbacks dev_disconnect / usb_change / error_push ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api — stamp rig events into the soak log so a data gap has a cause. usb_change codes: 19 board-to-PC, 20 board off PC, 12 board-to-phone; error_push carries data.call_fun plus message and is the only asynchronous signal an input call failed at the board. The XP WebSocket path is /api — Phonefarm's /clinet path and port 9912 do not exist here.
  15. restart GET /api/imserver/restart — absolute last resort, off-hours only. Drops every mirroring session and the WebSocket; expect im_connect on reconnect and every phone needing a re-cast. IMConsole.exe had to be running for the rig to come up at all, so a kernel restart can leave the rig needing a human.

Needs

  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in — with only IMService.exe up, /device/get showed both phones state 0 and /config/usb/get returned an empty board list
  • Every soak phone mirroring (non-0 state, live air_pid) and bound to its board (state 2, non-empty location_crc)
  • iOS settings the API cannot see: AssistiveTouch on with max tracking sensitivity, Full Keyboard Access on, mouse tracking speed max, Auto-Lock Never, StandBy off, portrait lock
  • For rungs 5-6 via Shortcut: iMouse Shortcut installed, IP edited, run once with all permissions, bound to an AssistiveTouch key; iOS 15+ for /shortcut/switch/device
  • Passcode-free soak phones, or a human to unlock — neither API can type a passcode after a reboot
  • A per-phone frame baseline and mean-pixel-diff threshold, since that is the only reliable "did it react" signal on this rig

Watch out

  • No id=all shorthand exists on any XP endpoint — build the comma list from /device/get; only /device/get with no id, and /device/airplay/connect/all, act on everything implicitly
  • /device/usb/restart is addressed by vid|pid, never by phone deviceid — a controller that passes the device id silently targets nothing, and board firmware generation is only readable on the phone, never from ver/uver
  • No OCR or image-search plug-in, so every assertion is a client-side mean-pixel-diff on raw BMP; never MD5-compare frames, an untouched phone still differs every frame from clock and encoder noise
  • AirPlay frame rate is per-phone and motion-dependent — one XR delivers ~29 new frames/s, its identical twin ~4.5 — so screen-verification timeouts must be scaled per phone, not assumed at 30 fps
  • The two XRs have different home screens; a shared coordinate is only fair after two WIN+h presses (leave the app, then return to page one)
  • Control-ready (board state 2, bound) and video-ready (mirroring, live air_pid) fail independently — report them separately or the ladder climbs the wrong rung
  • The API is unauthenticated on 9911; firewall 9911 and 17000 to trusted hosts before leaving an overnight soak running
  • Auto-brightness drifts colour-signature thresholds mid-soak unless the Shortcut brightness pin is present and working; Auto-Lock Never does not disable auto-brightness
  • The WebSocket bus has no documented delivery guarantee — if the WS client itself drops during a 24-72 h run, the soak loses its only rig-fault/app-fault signal until it reconnects, so give the harness its own WS-liveness heartbeat independent of HTTP polling
  • Rung 5 does not guarantee the video channel recovers: an iOS reboot does not necessarily reselect AirPlay mirroring, and nothing in the API can browse or pick from the receiver list — test this unattended before relying on it
  • Gate rungs 3+ on a control-channel-negative result specifically (the pointer probe fails), not merely "the scenario did not advance," or the ladder restarts hardware that was never the problem

Scale

Health probes cost a handful of calls per phone per minute and do not interfere with input traffic (moves ran p50 0.5-3.4 ms while both phones were polled flat out; ten pollers sustained 512 req/s at p50 3 ms, so 19 slots of thumbnail polling is comfortable). Recovery costs: reset/upall in milliseconds, board restart in seconds, disconnect-plus-recast seconds to tens of seconds, phone restart 60-90 s plus recast. Time-lapse archiving at one raw BMP per phone per 5 minutes runs about 460 MB per phone per 24 h; crop with rect or re-encode client-side to cut that. The real ceiling on scenario throughput is app render time plus the pixel-diff verification wait: on the slow phone (4.5 fps) each verified step needs at least 220 ms, capping verified actions at roughly 500-2,000/hour on the fast phone and well under half that on the slow one; ladder overhead is near zero unless false-positive escalations are frequent.

Synthetic checkout monitor on real iPhones

Plus external toolingWith caveats

On a schedule, a rack phone walks the operator's own mobile checkout end to end: product page, add to cart, checkout, shipping form, stop at the payment sheet, recording a raw-BMP frame at every step and comparing settled frames against a golden crop from the last known-good run. A broken banner, a moved button, a layout shift or a slower step raises an alert carrying the exact frame. Web synthetic monitors run headless Chrome, not Safari on a real handset on a real network; a mobile-only checkout break is otherwise discovered by customers, and here the evidence is a 2 ms device-level frame with a timestamp.

How

  1. mouse_reset_pos + send_key fn_key /mouse/reset?id=<id> then /key/sendkey?id=<id>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — normalise the phone to a known state. WIN+h is correct for these XRs on iOS 18.7.10; the newer "Home" fn_key needs kernel 2026.2.27+ and iOS 26.1+. Reset first, since a phone can silently ignore taps while hotkeys still work.
  2. shortcut#13 /shortcut/exec/url?id=<comma list>&url=https://shop.example/products/sku123&outtime=15000 — open the product URL. Shortcut-free alternative needing only the board: tap Safari, tap the address bar, /key/sendkey?key=<ascii url>, /key/sendkey?fn_key=ENTER — the URL must be pure ASCII, which the key parameter requires anyway.
  3. click /mouse/click?id=<id>&x=&y=&button=1 — advance one step of the funnel. Mirror-pixel coordinates (500x1080 here), read per device from /device/get; every CTA position comes from a captured raw BMP for that site/app version.
  4. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<one>&binary=true — wait for the step to settle and time it. Poll on a fixed 50 ms period and declare "settled" when the mean absolute diff between consecutive frames stays under ~1 for ~300 ms (idle floor 0.02-0.03; a real transition measures 20-160). Never MD5-compare.
