  5. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot?id=<one>&save_path=D:\monitor\<phone>\<step>\ — write the evidence frame server-side. save_path is a directory; the kernel names the file itself, so record the mapping yourself. The directory must exist or the call returns code 27; save_path and binary are alternative return modes, this is a separate call from the settle poll.
  6. click + send_key /mouse/click on each field, then /key/sendkey?id=<id>&key=<ascii value> — fill the shipping form. ASCII only, so a test name, street, postcode and phone number are fine and an accented address is not (that needs /shortcut/clipboard/set plus fn_key=WIN+v). Full Keyboard Access must be on; verify long values landed by screenshot, since typing speed and max length are undocumented.
  7. ocr / find_image none on this rig — /pic/ocr, /pic/find-text, /pic/find-image, /pic/find-image-cv all require plug-ins (code 28) — compare against the golden frame. This is the load-bearing gap: assertions must be computed by the caller, mean absolute pixel difference of stable regions against the last good crop, alerting above ~20 or on a step time over threshold.
  8. get_device_screenshot /pic/screenshot (capture) then end the run — stop at the payment sheet. Capture it as the final evidence frame and stop; do not automate entry of card numbers or credentials — the API is unauthenticated cleartext on the LAN, and Apple Pay's sheet requires biometric confirmation the board cannot produce.
  9. click /mouse/click on the cart's Remove control, then /key/sendkey fn_key=WIN+h — reset state for the next run. Verify the cart is empty with a settled-frame diff rather than assuming the tap worked.
  10. get_device_list /device/get (per-phone air_* fields, state, air_pid) — interpret a slow run correctly. Run the same flow on two phones: one XR delivers ~29 new frames/s under motion and its twin ~4.5, so step timings on the weak handset carry a ~220 ms quantisation floor versus ~35 ms on the good one.

Needs

  • A dedicated monitor phone per store or app, signed into a flagged test customer account, boards bound (state 2), location_crc present, Auto-Lock Never plus the rest of the accessibility checklist
  • Golden frames and a coordinate map per site/app version, captured from raw BMP on that specific phone, with a documented refresh step for intentional UI changes
  • A test SKU (ideally a test payment mode) so synthetic carts do not consume real inventory or pollute analytics
  • Writable evidence directories on the kernel host, pre-created — otherwise save_path returns code 27
  • Optional: iMouse Shortcut installed and bound for /shortcut/exec/url; without it, the Safari-typing path needs only the board
  • A scheduler in the controller — the XP API has no cron, scripting or scheduled-task concept

Watch out

  • Every assertion is client-side: OCR, find-text and find-image are all unavailable (code 28) — reading a price or an error string needs the vendor plug-in installed or your own OCR over raw frames
  • Pixel-diff golden frames are brittle against legitimately dynamic content — clocks, countdowns, rotating banners, stock counters — mask those regions or the monitor cries wolf nightly
  • Step timings are quantised by AirPlay frame production, not by the store: ~35 ms resolution on the healthy XR, ~220 ms on the weak one, so sub-200 ms regressions are not measurable on the slow handset
  • save_path cannot name the file and is a separate return mode from binary=true — evidence capture is a second call or a client-side write of the polled bytes
  • A phone can silently stop accepting taps, producing false "checkout broken" alerts in an unattended monitor — /mouse/reset at the top of every run plus a pointer-box sanity diff are mandatory
  • No multi-id screenshot, so each monitored phone is its own poller and its own run
  • The monitor stops at the payment sheet by design; completing a real purchase or entering card and credential data through this API is out of scope
  • Long-unattended runs will eventually hit an iOS or carrier interstitial (SIM notice, update prompt, low-storage warning) a fixed coordinate map cannot navigate — budget a periodic full-reset-and-recapture step and a "run did not reach the expected step" alert, not just per-step diffs
  • Concurrency is bounded well below the 19-board count: each monitored phone is an actively mirrored AirPlay stream plus the store's own traffic, realistically single digits of simultaneous monitored properties per PC/Wi-Fi segment
  • Nothing detects or dismisses an unexpected iOS system prompt mid-run (update banner, tracking dialog, captive portal): the pixel-diff can only say "the frame changed a lot," not "this is a system dialog" — this produces false "checkout broken" alerts on a monitor left running for weeks
  • A drifted pointer calibration is indistinguishable from a genuine UI break in this design's own instrumentation — a tap 20 px off target produces a large frame diff and reports as "checkout broken" with no way to tell it apart from a coordinate-map problem
  • The "couple of minutes per phone" estimate undercounts real storefront load time — page render, cart update and shipping-form validation round trips commonly run several seconds to tens of seconds per step — treat it as a lower bound, not typical

Scale

A full flow is roughly 10-15 taps and 10 evidence captures. Capture cost is trivial (raw BMP p50 2 ms, 84 req/s flat out per phone, phones independent, input traffic does not slow polling), so a settle detector can poll at 50 ms without competing with taps. Tap latency is dominated by the pointer walk (~0.6 ms/px: 100 px = 78 ms, 1000 px = 592 ms) and must be subtracted before blaming the store for a slow step. A realistic full-funnel run is more likely 2-5 minutes end to end once real page load time is counted, comfortably inside a 5-15 minute per-phone cadence. Practical concurrency across phones on one PC is limited to roughly 3-6 simultaneously monitored properties by Wi-Fi bandwidth and licence dev_online_num, not by the 19 physical boards; each raw frame is 1.6 MB, so crop with rect or re-encode client-side to bound evidence retention.

Test infrastructure: mocking and replay

Contract and chaos tests against a mock XP kernel, with record and replay of real 9911 traffic

Native APIVerified

Extend the project's existing mock HTTP transport (TestHandler in SelfTests.cs, already serving five fixture devices with deliberate variety) into a full XP kernel simulator, plus an in-process WebSocket bus and a recording proxy for real 9911 traffic. It reproduces the real envelope and error signatures, models failure modes that cannot be reproduced on demand with hardware (the silent stuck-click phone, code 28 OCR, board loss mid-job), and lets a recorded incident replay deterministically with no phones attached. Four of the six test modes need the live rack; the hardest paths, a pointer that silently drops clicks, a board unplugged mid-fan-out, are exactly the states hardware will not produce on request, and both project mistakes to date (the MD5 frame comparison, the wall-starves-the-master bug) were reasoning errors a fixture with honest noise would have caught.

How

  1. POST {"fun":"click","msgid":n,...} on 9912 GET /api/<path>?k=v, POST multipart with fun=/path, or POST JSON {"fun":"/mouse/click","msgid":n,"data":{...}} — all on 9911/api — mock the request envelope and the two wrong-edition failure signatures. Status 200 means accepted while the real result is data.code; the mock must reply 200 + data.code, never a Phonefarm-style top-level status 0. The 404 "接口不存在" and 500 "List index out of bounds (1)" behaviours come from the 10 Sep live probe, not the docs — encode them as probe-derived.
  2. get_device_list GET /api/device/get — mock device inventory including the exclusion cases. The existing TEST:01-05 fixture already covers online-with-board (01, 04), offline-and-unbound (02, 03) and different-geometry (05, imgw 375 x imgh 812) — exactly what a mirroring-exclusion assertion needs.
  3. get_usb_list / usb_change GET /api/config/usb/get and the usb_change WS callback — mock board state and the board-loss event. state 1 = board on PC, 2 = phone attached; callback data.code 19 board-to-computer connected, 20 disconnected, 12 hardware-to-phone connected. Do not parse ver/uver, mojibake on this build.
  4. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true (binary works over plain HTTP on XP) — mock the frame source honestly. Return the exact 1,620,054-byte bottom-up BMP shape with ~0.02 mean-diff noise between frames and a scripted reaction over 20 only when a click is actually honoured. Generate the buffer once and mutate in place, the same Large Object Heap lesson as production.
  5. click / mouse_up / mouse_reset_pos /mouse/click, /mouse/up, /mouse/reset — mock the stuck-pointer fixture. Measured 2026-09-10: the stuck phone returned success with a 0.09 mean diff, /mouse/up did not clear it, WIN+h still worked (142.15), and /mouse/reset restored it permanently (141.96). Reproduce all four, including the key path still working — the trap that makes the phone look healthy.
  6. ocr / find_image /pic/ocr, /pic/ocr-ex, /pic/find-image, /pic/find-image-cv, /pic/find-text, /pic/find-multi-color — mock the plug-in-gated recognition endpoints. code 28 is what /pic/ocr actually returned here; the mock's default for every /pic recognition path except /pic/screenshot should be code 28, so no scheduler path can quietly depend on OCR this rig does not have.
  7. ws://host:9911/clinet callbacks ws://host:9911/api — im_connect, dev_connect, dev_disconnect, dev_change, dev_delete, dev_rotate, group_change, group_delete, usb_change, collection_mouse, airplay_connect_log, restart_log, user_info, im_log, error_push, im_config_change, logout, dev_sort_change — mock the broadcast bus. All eighteen use the {fun,status,message,msgid,data} envelope; user_info pushes every 30 s (accelerate in tests). error_push carrying call_fun is the only asynchronous signal an input call failed at the board.
  8. restart_usb / auto_connect_screen / restart_device /device/usb/restart?id=720A|C241 (vid|pid, not deviceid), /device/airplay/connect, /connect/all, /disconnect, /device/restart — mock the recovery ladder's own endpoints. XP's usb restart takes vid|pid comma lists, a real regression risk; the docs do not specify which usb_change codes /device/usb/restart emits, so the 20-then-19-then-12 sequence is an assumption to validate against a recording.
  9. msgid echo documented: each interface returns msgid as-is — record and replay real traffic. A proxy in front of 9911 logs path, params, id list, reply body, msgid and delta-t; replay serves the logged reply for the same path plus ids at recorded or compressed timing, so an observed incident reruns the same scheduler code with no rack.

Needs

  • The existing --self-test / --ui-test harness and TestHandler in src/iMouse.Console/SelfTests.cs (75 self-tests, 76 UI checks passing as of 10 Sep 2026)
  • Gesture stages BeginGesture / TrackGesture / EndGestureAsync taking plain Points, so a test can drive the exact path a real press follows
  • One recording session against the live rack to capture realistic device records, the 19-board list and at least one genuine failure, for replay fixtures
  • Somewhere to keep recorded fixtures that is not shared — this project is not a git repository and build/ already holds a live credential

Watch out

  • A mock that always answers code 0 is worse than no mock — the fixtures that carry value are the ones that lie the way the kernel lies: 200-with-no-effect, code 28 on every recognition path, code 25/26 on a phone that looks online, a board vanishing mid-fan-out
  • Several mocked behaviours are probe-derived, not documented — the 404 body, the 500 "List index out of bounds (1)", the usb_change sequence from /device/usb/restart — mark them as dated observations so a future kernel build that changes them is diagnosable, not mysterious
  • Replay fidelity is per path plus id list: it reproduces what the kernel said, not what the phones did, proving the client behaved identically given identical replies, nothing about whether a gesture actually landed
  • Recorded fixtures embed real screenshots and device records (MAC, IP, user_name) — scrub or quarantine them, and budget for size at 1.6 MB per captured frame
  • XP documents no WebSocket binary push, so there is deliberately nothing to mock there — a mock of Phonefarm's 261-byte binary frame header would model an edition this rig does not run
  • A recording proxy in front of an unauthenticated LAN API is itself a new listening service capturing live screenshots and device identity — do not run it with elevated privileges or leave it running outside test sessions
  • Contract tests that assert on Chinese-language error strings are fragile to a locale or firmware update — key assertions off the numeric or status codes (404/500, code 28) and treat the string as secondary
  • Serving the full 1,620,054-byte BMP payload per screenshot call, thousands of times per second, is measurable memory and copy overhead — budget for it rather than assuming the mock is free just because it has no network hop
  • Building a WebSocket bus for all 18 documented callback events is a bigger scope item than the rest of the chain; only error_push and usb_change are actually exercised by the recovery ladder today, so the other ~16 could be stubbed "defined but never fired" initially

Scale

The mock side needs no rack and no network: mocked runs execute thousands of steps per second, bounded mainly by the BMP fixture, which should be allocated once and mutated in place (the production lesson: 488 MB/s allocation and 496 gen-2 GCs per 8 s before buffer reuse, versus 2.9 MB/s and 0-1 after). Recording against the live rack costs whatever the recorded session costs, a raw-BMP step is ~1.62 MB, so an hour of frame-inclusive recording is not storable — record request/reply metadata continuously and capture full frame bytes only at marked steps. Replay can run at recorded delta-t for timing-sensitive assertions, or compressed to zero for throughput; there is no phones-per-PC or actions-per-hour ceiling here, since nothing depends on a live phone or AirPlay.

Concurrency and race-condition testing

Synchronised N-phone race and contention testing

Native APIWith caveats

One /mouse/click carrying a comma-separated id list makes every listed board tap at the same moment, measured latency was identical for one phone and for two, so N real devices with real client retry logic can hit "claim", "buy" or "join" within a very short window to exercise backend races, rate limiters and idempotency. Pre-position the pointer with a multi-id /mouse/move first so no per-phone pointer walk adds skew, then verify each phone's outcome from its own raw BMP frame. Load generators simulate concurrency at the HTTP layer but not the client; real apps with real local state and retry logic hitting one endpoint simultaneously is the scenario that produces double-bookings and duplicate redemptions in production.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get — build the eligible set: online, bound, identical mirror geometry. Exclude any phone whose imgw/imgh differs from the rest — the same coordinate on a differently sized mirror is a different place. Both XRs here are 500x1080.
  2. shortcut#13 GET /api/shortcut/exec/url?id=<comma list>&url=<deep link> — drive every phone to the identical screen. The only reliable normalisation, since the two XRs have different home screens. Without the Shortcut, fall back to two /key/sendkey fn_key=WIN+h presses plus a per-phone tap map.
  3. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<comma list> — clear stuck-click state across the whole firing set. Mandatory before a race: a stuck phone follows /mouse/move and hotkeys while producing a 0.09 mean diff on a click (idle floor 0.02), so it would silently drop out and look like a backend loss. Measured 141.96 after reset.
  4. mouse_move GET /api/mouse/move?id=<comma list>&x=250&y=900 — pre-position every pointer on the target control so the firing call has zero travel. The board walks the pointer at ~0.6 ms/px; N phones walked in parallel cost the same as one.
  5. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=a,b,c&x=250&y=900 — fire: one request, all phones, log the send timestamp. Coordinates are mirror pixels; optional "time" sets the press-to-release hold; add &button=2 for a secondary click — XP uses numeric codes 1-8, not "left"/"right" strings.
  6. send_key GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<comma list>&fn_key=ENTER — keyboard-triggered variant for focused buttons. Requires Full Keyboard Access on and the control focused; a second, independent trigger path to see whether the skew profile differs from the HID mouse path.
  7. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true — capture each phone's outcome frame. Single-id, so N concurrent requests, one per phone. Raw BMP 2 ms / 1,620,054 bytes; jpg 40 ms, caps ~21 req/s. Start pollers before firing so the first post-tap frame is captured.
  8. ocr / find_image /api/pic/ocr, /api/pic/find-text, /api/pic/find-image-cv — NOT AVAILABLE on this rig — classify each outcome. /api/pic/ocr answers data.code 28; substitute client-side classification: a golden-diff against stored "success"/"sold out" crops, or a colour-signature check.
  9. (no equivalent) ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api callback error_push (data.call_fun, data.message) — watch for per-board dispatch failures during the volley. A failed /mouse/click reports only here, never in the HTTP reply — without this subscription a hardware drop-out is indistinguishable from a lost race.
  10. (outside the API) none — external — correlate with the server side. The rack gives only the client-side send timestamp; actual request arrival spread must come from the service's own logs.

Needs

  • One pre-existing test account per phone that you own, on a staging or test tenant — never production, and never accounts created in bulk for the test
  • All firing phones online, bound, with identical imgw/imgh and identical app screen state at fire time
  • Full Keyboard Access on for the ENTER variant; iMouse Shortcut installed and bound for deep-link normalisation
  • A stored golden crop per outcome state (success, sold out, error) per phone, since no OCR or image-search plug-in is available
  • WebSocket client attached to ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api before firing, to catch error_push

Watch out

  • N is 2 on this rig today: 19 boards exist, but only two iPhone XRs are present and mirroring — 19 is the board ceiling, not a demonstrated concurrency
  • Sub-millisecond simultaneity across boards is unverified beyond two phones: three chained 7-port hubs are a plausible serialisation point at higher N — treat it as a hypothesis to measure at mid-N (4-8), not a specification
  • thread_mode in /config/imserver/get/set plausibly governs parallel-versus-serial dispatch and was never probed here (ships false in the doc example) — read it and record the value before quoting any skew number, including the "identical latency for one or two phones" baseline itself
  • Near-simultaneous taps are not the same as near-simultaneous backend requests: each phone still independently renders, runs app logic and issues its own network request over its own Wi-Fi link, and that jitter (plausibly tens to hundreds of ms, given the 4.5x fps disparity measured between identical phones) will dominate over any HID-layer skew — the rig controls tap simultaneity, not request simultaneity
  • Verification is the weak link, not firing: with no OCR or image-search (code 28), outcome classification is client-side pixel work that must be validated against known-good frames
  • The slow phone's outcome frame can lag ~220 ms or more behind — infer a lost race only from frame content, never from frame timing
  • /pic/screenshot is single-id, so observation is N concurrent requests even though firing is one (phones are independent: measured 83+85 req/s at two phones, 512 req/s aggregate at ten pollers)
  • A stuck-click phone silently drops out of the volley and reads as a backend loss — /mouse/reset to the full set before firing is part of the experiment's validity, not hygiene
  • Golden-diff classification only holds once all firing phones are on pixel-identical UI state; an app that personalises the result screen (name, avatar, locale) breaks a shared golden crop even on a correct deep link — crop from a region free of per-account content, not just free of chrome or wallpaper differences
  • Running N accounts against a service you do not operate can breach its terms and trip its rate limiter — use staging, and back off on any block or throttle response rather than retrying through it

Scale

Firing and pre-positioning are each one HTTP request regardless of N. Observation is N concurrent /pic/screenshot calls at 2 ms each on loopback (measured 84 req/s per phone flat out, 512 req/s across ten pollers), so observation scales to the full 19-slot rack even though only two phones exist today. 2 phones are race-testable now; 19 is the board ceiling, not a working number, until thread_mode is read and a mid-N (4-8) skew measurement is taken — firing stays one request at any N, so the API itself is not the constraint.

Diagnostics extraction via the iOS Shortcut

Harvest iOS crash logs (.ips) through Files without Xcode

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

After a crash, drive the phone's own UI to Settings > Privacy and Security > Analytics and Improvements > Analytics Data, open the app's .ips entry, use Share > Save to Files into an /iMouse/ folder, then pull the file to the PC with /shortcut/file/get and /shortcut/file/down for symbolication, no Xcode, no Mac, and no free Lightning port, since the only port is occupied by the control board. A crash frame from the mirror tells you the app died; the .ips log tells you why, and getting it off a rack phone normally needs a human with a cable and a Mac.

How

  1. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true (optionally &rect=[l,t,r,b]) — trigger: watch for a crash-to-home transition. rect is a flat [left, top, right, bottom] array in XP, not Phonefarm's four-corner-point form. Detect with a mean-absolute-pixel-diff against a stored home-screen crop, never MD5.
  2. send_key + click GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<id>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice), then /api/mouse/click on the Settings icon — normalise to a known state, then walk into Settings. Two Home presses: first leaves the app, second returns to page one — the XRs have different home screens, so the icon coordinate is per-phone.
  3. click + mouse_wheel /api/mouse/click and /api/mouse/wheel?id=<id>&direction=down&len=30&number=3 — walk Settings > Privacy and Security > Analytics and Improvements > Analytics Data. Wheel scrolling avoids the ~0.6 ms/px pointer-walk cost of a swipe. Verify each step with a golden diff before the next tap; this is roughly 10-15 taps and the fragile part of the chain.
  4. ocr / find_text /api/pic/find-text?id=<id>&text=["MyApp-2026-09"]&contain=true&similarity=0.8 — NOT AVAILABLE, do client-side instead — find the app's .ips row in the alphabetical list. /pic/ocr returns code 28 here, so find-text will too. Pull the raw BMP, run OCR on the PC, click the row's centre converted into mirror-pixel space.
  5. click /api/mouse/click?id=<id>&x=&y= per step — share sheet: open the entry, tap Share, tap "Save to Files", navigate to On My iPhone > iMouse, tap Save. The suggestion row reorders between runs and iOS versions, so locate "Save to Files" by content each time and golden-diff after each tap.
  6. shortcut#4 GET /api/shortcut/file/get?id=<one id>&path=/iMouse/&outtime=20000 — confirm the file landed. id single-only, outtime ms (default 15000, note Phonefarm's was seconds). Returns data.list[{name, ext, size, create_time}]. iOS 15+ only.
  7. shortcut#5 POST /api fun=/shortcut/file/down, id=<one id>, path=/iMouse/, list=[{"name":"MyApp-2026-09-10-101010","ext":"ips"}], zip=1, outtime=60000 — pull it to the PC. Single id only; list entries are {name, ext} split, not a Phonefarm full-path string; files land in the iMouse install directory's Shortcut\File folder. Raise outtime well above the 15 s default for anything but a tiny log.
  8. shortcut#6 POST /api fun=/shortcut/file/del, id=<comma list allowed>, path=/iMouse/, list=[{"name":...,"ext":"ips"}] — clean up on the phone. Comma list allowed here, unlike get/down; returns the 10 newest directory entries. Destructive, no undo, only run after the download is confirmed on disk.
  9. (outside the API) none — external (the build's dSYM on the PC or a Mac) — symbolicate. Neither API symbolicates; the rack's job ends at a raw .ips on the PC.

Needs

  • iOS 15 or later — the whole /shortcut/file/* family is gated on it
  • iMouse Shortcut installed, IP edited, run once with every prompt allowed, bound to an AssistiveTouch key via Send Binding Key; Advanced permissions: allow running scripts, allow sharing/deleting large amounts of data, allow deleting without confirmation
  • An /iMouse/ folder created in Files > On My iPhone beforehand — a missing path answers code 27
  • Settings > Privacy and Security > Analytics and Improvements > Share iPhone Analytics enabled, or there is no Analytics Data list to harvest
  • Board bound and working (the Shortcut launches via a HID hotkey) and the phone reachable on TCP 9911 over the LAN
  • A per-model, per-iOS coordinate map for the Settings walk in mirror pixels, plus a golden crop per step, or client-side OCR to locate rows

Watch out

  • No server-side row-finding on this rig: /pic/ocr answers code 28, so /pic/find-text will too — run OCR on the PC against the raw BMP and convert hits back into mirror-pixel coordinates
  • The Settings and share-sheet walk is the fragile part: Apple reorganises it between iOS versions and the share sheet's suggestion row reorders between runs, so every tap needs a content check and the whole map must be re-captured per model and iOS build
  • File list and download take a single id ("Multiple is not allowed"); only /shortcut/file/del accepts a comma list — this is one phone at a time, serially
  • outtime is milliseconds and defaults to 15000 in XP, not seconds as in the Phonefarm sibling — a ported controller will time out on every transfer, and 15 s is also too short for a large .ips, so raise it and set zip=1
  • XP's list entries are {name, ext} pairs plus a separate path, not a Phonefarm full-path array — sending "/iMouse/1.ips" as a name will simply not match
  • Analytics entries are not reliably named after your app alone, .ips files may arrive suffixed (for example .ips.synced), and the list on a busy phone is long — budget scrolling and be prepared for the extension the file actually carries
  • Crash logs are personal data: an .ips can carry the device name, installed process names and paths; the download lands unencrypted under the iMouse install directory's Shortcut\File folder on an API with no authentication — harvest only from phones you own
  • This is a per-phone serial walk of roughly 15 taps plus two Shortcut round trips, and a stuck-click state mid-walk would silently abandon it partway — send /mouse/reset before starting and verify each tap actually moved the screen
  • Analytics Data entries are timestamped when Apple processes the crash, not when it happens, and can lag the crash-to-home transition by seconds to a few minutes — a fixed-delay walk needs a retry or poll loop, not a single attempt
  • The Shortcuts Advanced permissions have no API-visible status; only a live file transfer confirms them, and an iOS update can silently reset them
  • The automation can assert what it sent and what changed on screen, but never "did the Share Sheet actually save this to /iMouse/" — a Share Sheet failure surfaces several steps later as a missing file, indistinguishable from a mis-tap, a slow analytics index, or a full disk
  • No /shortcut/* path has actually been probed on this rig — run the cheap /shortcut/device/ip round-trip check before designing anything downstream; steps fail with code 30 "Call timeout" if the Shortcut is not installed or bound
  • Share iPhone Analytics is normally an opt-in accepted during first-run setup; a rack phone provisioned unattended may have it off, in which case the walk fails at step 3 with no clean error the API can see
  • A major iOS update can pop a full-screen consent prompt mid-walk; a coordinate-driven tap lands on whatever the prompt shows, not on Settings

Scale

About a minute per crash per phone: roughly 15 taps (pointer walk up to ~600 ms per full-height traverse), a scroll pass through an alphabetical list, plus two Shortcut calls each bounded by outtime. File get and download are single-id, so harvesting is strictly serial across the rack. Comfortable for dozens of crashes a day, not a high-frequency CI loop. Budget 20-60 s of API and board time per crash normally, worst case another 1-2 minutes for the analytics-lag retry, plus a few extra seconds per walk on the slow XR (~4.5 fps) for content checks. For a 19-board rig, expect 15-30 minutes to sweep every phone once.

Native screen-recording harvest for bug reports and animation review

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Start iOS's own Screen Recording from Control Centre by hotkey plus one tap, run the flow under test, stop it the same way, then list the newest album item with /shortcut/album/get, pull the RPReplay .mp4 with /shortcut/album/down, and clear it with /shortcut/album/del. The result is a native-resolution, encoder-noise-free recording at the phone's own frame rate, something the 500x1080 AirPlay mirror cannot produce, and the only usable motion capture on the slower XR (~4.5 new frames/s). The vendor's own /shortcut/album/get response example already returns an RPReplay .mp4, so this is a documented path, not a hack.

How

  1. n/a (phone-side setup) none — one-time per phone: add the Screen Recording tile to Control Centre. No API starts or stops iOS screen recording, nothing in the 62 documented XP paths covers it. Keep the vendor's required "two rows of icons at the bottom" Control Centre shape; re-check /device/airplay/connect after the change.
  2. send_key (fn_key) + click GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=ControlBar then GET /api/mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=<tile x>&y=<tile y> — open Control Centre and tap the record tile. Both calls take comma-separated id lists, so N phones start recording from two requests. The tile coordinate must be read off a screenshot frame in mirror pixels; no find-image or OCR is available to locate it automatically.
  3. send_key (fn_key WIN+h), click, swipe, wheel GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+h then the regression script's mouse calls — leave Control Centre and run the flow under test. These XRs are on iOS 18.7.10 (the newer "Home" fn_key needs kernel 2026.2.27+ for iOS 26.1+). Remember /mouse/swipe walks the pointer at ~0.6 ms/px, so a full-height 1080 px swipe is ~580 ms of travel and iOS may read it as a slow drag rather than a flick.
  4. send_key (fn_key) + click GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=ControlBar then click the tile again — stop the recording. Tapping the same tile is the deterministic stop; tapping the red status pill instead raises a Stop/Cancel confirmation sheet whose coordinates differ per iOS version.
  5. shortcut id 1 GET /api/shortcut/album/get?id=<id>&num=1&outtime=<ms> — find the new file. id single-only, album_name blank for the most recent project's album, outtime ms default 15 s. The doc's own example returns {"album_name":"","name":"RPReplay_Final1718703292","ext":"mp4","size":"5.4 MB","create_time":"2024-12-18 23:54:08"}. XP has no date filter, unlike Phonefarm.
  6. shortcut id 2 POST /api fun=/shortcut/album/down, id=<id>, list=[{"album_name":"","name":"RPReplay_Final<ts>","ext":"mp4"}], outtime=120000 — pull the mp4 to the PC. Single id, zip 0/1, outtime ms default 15 s; list entries split name and extension unlike Phonefarm's whole filename. Files land under the iMouse install directory's Shortcut\Media folder; raise outtime well past the default for a clip of any length.
  7. shortcut id 3 POST /api fun=/shortcut/album/del, id=<a,b>, list=[{"album_name":"","name":"RPReplay_Final<ts>","ext":"mp4"}] — clear the clip off the phone. id IS comma-separated here; returns the 10 newest album records to confirm the file is gone. /shortcut/album/clear wipes a whole album, never wire it to an unattended step. Deletion needs the Shortcuts "allow deleting without confirmation" and "allow deleting large amounts of data" permissions.

Needs

  • Screen Recording added to Control Centre on each phone, without breaking the vendor's "two rows of icons at the bottom" layout that automatic screencasting depends on
  • iMouse Shortcut installed, IP edited, run once with all prompts allowed, bound to an AssistiveTouch key; Advanced permissions per the crash-log entry above
  • USB board bound and connected (both the Control Centre taps and the Shortcut hotkey travel over it) plus LAN reachability from phone to kernel on 9911
  • Free storage on the phone for the clip, and disk space under the iMouse install directory's Shortcut\Media folder on the PC
  • The record-tile coordinate captured per phone/iOS version from a screenshot frame in mirror-pixel space, since no OCR or image-search is available here to find it
  • Phone unlocked, portrait locked, Auto-Lock Never

Watch out

  • Shortcut status is unverified on this rig, no /shortcut/* path was probed on 10 Sep 2026 — prove it with the /shortcut/device/ip round trip before depending on the harvest
  • Start and stop are blind UI taps at a fixed coordinate; with no recognition plug-in, verification is only a mean-pixel-diff on a small box around the tile (idle floor 0.02-0.03, real reaction 20-160) or the red recording pill appearing — never MD5-compare
  • Adding the record tile changes the Control Centre layout, which the vendor docs explicitly tie to automatic screencasting — re-test /device/airplay/connect after the change, and re-locate every other required tile, since insertion shifts everything after it
  • /shortcut/album/get and /album/down are both single-id, listing and downloading are strictly one phone at a time even though start, stop and delete fan out over a comma list
  • XP dropped Phonefarm's date filter on the album list (album_name plus num only) — identify the new clip by create_time or by clearing the album first
  • outtime defaults to 15 s; a multi-megabyte mp4 will exceed that with no documented ceiling for a raised value — a timeout surfaces as code 30
  • Screen recording adds CPU and thermal load to the device under test and can itself change the performance being measured
  • Apps that block screen capture (DRM video, some banking and streaming apps) record as black — iOS or app behaviour, not something the API reports
  • Whether the AssistiveTouch pointer appears in an on-device recording is unverified — confirmed visible in the AirPlay frame, not established for the on-device recorder
  • Every phone must keep the AssistiveTouch floating button on as a control prerequisite, and iOS screen recording captures it as a real on-screen overlay — every harvested clip shows a persistent floating button unless it is hidden, and hiding it either removes the pointer needed for the rest of the automation or needs its own blind, unverifiable re-show step afterward
  • The 3-second start countdown means the flow under test should include a deliberate pause after "start recording," or the opening seconds of every clip show the countdown UI, not the app
  • Recordings capture notifications, account names and any personal data on screen — record only on test devices and accounts you own, and review before attaching a clip to a bug report

Scale

Start, stop and delete are multi-id, so a whole rack can begin recording the same flow from a handful of requests. Harvest is the bottleneck: get and down are single-id, and a one-minute clip is tens of megabytes per phone over the LAN, so a 19-phone rack's harvest phase alone runs on the order of 5-15 minutes serially with a generous (~120 s) outtime, meaning a handful of full-rack record-and-harvest cycles per hour rather than a per-test-case capture for a large regression suite. Screenshot polling for tile verification costs nothing measurable alongside this, since phones are independent.

Clipboard as a structured test channel: pull diagnostics out, push Unicode fixtures in

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Give a test build a hidden "copy diagnostics" action that writes JSON (build hash, feature flags, last error, counters, memory) to the iOS pasteboard; a long-press via /mouse/click triggers it and /shortcut/clipboard/get returns the text for exact assertions with no OCR. In the other direction, /shortcut/clipboard/set seeds Unicode and hostile fixture strings onto many phones in one request, and fn_key=WIN+v pastes them into the focused field for rendering, truncation and crash checks. This rig has no server-side OCR at all, so the clipboard is a lossless Unicode side channel already exposed in both directions, turning screen-scraping assertions into structured ones.

How

  1. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=<id>&x=<x>&y=<y>&time=1000 — trigger the test build's copy-diagnostics action with a long press. time is the press-to-popup delay in ms, so a long-press needs no separate API. x/y must be mirror-image pixels (500x1080 here), never iOS points (414x896).
  2. shortcut id 11 (professional version only) GET /api/shortcut/clipboard/get?id=<id>&outtime=<ms> — wait, then pull the JSON off the pasteboard. id single-only, outtime ms default 15 s. Response is data.text plus data.code/data.id; parse the JSON on the PC and assert build hash, flags, last error, counters. XP states no edition gate on this path.
  3. shortcut id 10 (professional version only) POST /api {"fun":"/shortcut/clipboard/set","data":{"id":"a,b,c","text":"<fixture>","sleep":1}} — seed a fixture string onto every phone under test in one request. id comma-separated; sleep is a SECONDS delay ("on some phones paste may take a while to become effective"), outtime is ms. Use POST application/json UTF-8 rather than a GET query string for non-ASCII text.
  4. send_key (fn_key) GET /api/mouse/click?id=<ids>&x=&y= then GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+v — focus the field and paste. The hotkey table lists WIN+v Paste, plus OPENKeyboard, WIN+a Select All, WIN+x Cut, SwitchIme, BACKSPACE — useful for clearing a field between fixtures. Requires Full Keyboard Access on.
  5. send_key (key) GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&key=<ascii text> — ASCII typing-speed cases (search-as-you-type, per-keystroke handlers) with no Shortcut at all. key supports only English, numbers and English characters; Chinese and Unicode are explicitly unsupported, which is why the clipboard route exists.
  6. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true — verify what landed on screen. Raw BMP measured 2 ms / 1,620,054 bytes; jpg 40 ms, capped ~21 req/s. Compare frames with mean absolute pixel difference, never MD5.
  7. shortcut id 10 then id 11 /api/shortcut/clipboard/set?id=<id>&text=imouse-<ts> then /api/shortcut/clipboard/get?id=<id> — round-trip self-test before trusting any assertion. The identical string must come back in data.text; this pair proves the Shortcut is installed, the AssistiveTouch hotkey fires, and the phone can reach the kernel on 9911. data.code 30 "Call timeout" means the hotkey never launched the Shortcut.

Needs

  • iMouse Shortcut installed on every phone, IP edited to the kernel (192.168.4.29 here), run once with all prompts allowed, bound to an AssistiveTouch key via Send Binding Key; Advanced permissions as above
  • USB board bound and connected (the Shortcut launches via a HID hotkey) and the phone reachable on the LAN, since the Shortcut posts its result back to the kernel on 9911
  • Full Keyboard Access on with Auto-Hide 1 s, for WIN+v and OPENKeyboard
  • A test build with a copy-diagnostics affordance — this is an app-side change, not an API capability
  • Per-phone imgw/imgh read from /device/get so the long-press coordinate is in mirror-pixel space
  • Phone unlocked, Auto-Lock Never, portrait locked

Watch out

  • Shortcut status is unverified on this rig, the 10 Sep 2026 probe never called any /shortcut/* path — run the cheap round-trip check before building anything on this
  • Asymmetric fan-out: /shortcut/clipboard/set takes a comma-separated id list, but /clipboard/get is single-id only — harvesting diagnostics is strictly one request per phone
  • Unit trap: sleep is in SECONDS, outtime is in MILLISECONDS (default 15000) on XP; the Phonefarm sibling's outtime was in seconds — getting this backwards produces either a 15 ms timeout or a 15,000 s stall
  • The diagnostics JSON sits on the system pasteboard, readable by any app, over an API with no authentication — keep credentials, tokens and customer data out of it
  • iOS shows a "pasted from <app>" banner and may prompt for cross-app paste permission the first time; this changes pixels (allow for it in diff thresholds) and needs answering once per phone
  • No OCR fallback if the clipboard path fails: /pic/ocr and its variants sit behind the plug-in, which reported code 28 here — any screen-side assertion must be client-side on raw BMP
  • A long-press is state-dependent: assert what you sent and verify by pixel diff, never assume the debug menu opened; normalise with two Home presses first, since the XRs have different home screens
  • Round-trip latency for the Shortcut path is not measured on this rig, the "1-3 s" estimate is a guess; the only documented bound is outtime (default 15 s)
  • Phonefarm's Chinese-entry hotkey (CTRL+ALT+SHIFT+WIN+v with a send_text_ok callback) does not exist on the XP kernel, it is absent from the endpoint list and bare Phonefarm names return HTTP 500 — clipboard plus WIN+v is the only documented Unicode path here
  • A full-rack pre-flight adds one serial 15-s-capped call per phone before any real test cycle — budget this into CI wall-clock
  • No documented ceiling exists for clipboard text length; before relying on large fixtures, empirically determine the truncation point, since POST body size, Shortcut action limits and iOS pasteboard limits are three separate places it can be capped
  • WIN+v only pastes if a field currently has keyboard focus; a bare tap does not always raise the keyboard on iOS (a field behind a picker, or one needing a second tap) — verify a text cursor or keyboard is visible before trusting a paste, since a failed focus produces no visible page change worth a pixel diff
  • A "pasted from clipboard" banner or first-use permission prompt is itself UI state the automation must detect and dismiss — a phone stuck on an undismissed system alert fails every subsequent tap the same way a mis-click does

Scale

Fixture seeding, the paste hotkey and the focusing tap are each one request for the whole rack, comma-id fan-out at board-walk cost. Diagnostics harvesting is the bottleneck: /clipboard/get is single-id, bounded by outtime (default 15 s, though a small read is likely well under 1 s once the Shortcut fires). Screenshot verification is also single-id but phones are independent (83-85 req/s per phone measured, 512 req/s across ten pollers) and does not compete with input traffic. A full rack can likely run one fixture cycle every 1-3 seconds on the push side; harvesting realistically adds well under a minute per fixture across 19 phones once the per-phone Shortcut pre-flight is amortised, giving on the order of 30-60 fixture cycles per hour, gated entirely by the unmeasured Shortcut round-trip.

Also worth knowing

Game QA and landscape apps

Game QA: onboarding runs, IAP sandbox checks, crash and hitch detection, landscape

PartialWith caveats

Games are one of the largest mobile-only categories and the one case where a rack of real handsets, not a simulator, is obviously the right tool: real touch latency, real StoreKit purchase sheets, real GPU-bound frame delivery. The tutorial and onboarding run, the frame-arrival crash and hitch signal, and the multi-device soak loop all reuse the visual-regression and watchdog machinery built above; the new pieces are held-key and drag-based game controls, and landscape, which is the default orientation for this whole category and is otherwise covered in this document only as a portrait-lock assumption.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get?id=<ids> — read rotate, imgw/imgh and state per phone before a run; rotate flags which phones are already in landscape.
  2. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<ids> — clear the silent stuck-click state before any tap-critical sequence; a missed tutorial tap derails the whole run and looks identical to a game bug.
  3. send_key WIN+h GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+h — two presses, force every phone to home page one before launch.
  4. click GET /api/mouse/click?x=<px>&y=<py> — launch the game icon; per-phone coordinates, home layouts differ.
  5. WS callback dev_rotate ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api — subscribe before the game forces landscape; the callback carries the full device record with rotate flipped to 1 and imgw/imgh swapped, the cue to load that phone's landscape coordinate map and goldens.
  6. mouse_down + mouse_move + mouse_up GET /api/mouse/down, GET /api/mouse/move, GET /api/mouse/up — the general touch-control path: press at a virtual joystick or button origin, stream move for a drag or analog gesture, release; works for any touch-driven title.
  7. key_down / key_up GET /api/key/down?id=<ids>&key=<key>, GET /api/key/up?id=<ids>&key=<key> — hold and release a single key as a game control, for the minority of titles built to accept a hardware keyboard.
  8. key_release_all GET /api/key/upall?id=<ids> — release every held key on that phone in one call; run before ending or restarting a session so a stuck hold does not bleed into the next run.
  9. click with time GET /api/mouse/click?x=<cx>&y=<cy>&time=<ms> — a tap-and-hold action: charge a shot, skip a cutscene, or confirm on a store sheet that requires a long-press.
  10. get_device_screenshot, polled GET /api/pic/screenshot?binary=true — the frame-arrival poll that stands in for a crash and hitch signal, reusing the watchdog design above; also captures the purchase-sheet, tutorial-step and landing frames for pixel-diff verification.
  11. send_key WIN+h + config/imserver/set flip_right GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+h, GET /api/config/imserver/set?flip_right=<bool> — return to home between runs; flip_right is the kernel's landscape mirroring option, worth testing once against a game whose taps land offset.

Needs

  • A per-phone, per-orientation coordinate map for the tutorial taps, joystick origin and purchase-sheet buttons; rotation swaps imgw/imgh, so a portrait map does not carry over to landscape.
  • Orientation lock off, or set to allow landscape, on any phone running a landscape-only game. Every other use case in this section assumes orientation lock on for normalisation; a rack running both portrait apps and landscape games needs a per-phone accessibility policy, not one rack-wide setting.
  • A sandbox or test Apple ID (an App Store Connect sandbox tester) signed in on each phone used for IAP testing, against the developer's own app.
  • A game confirmed to accept hardware-keyboard input before building any control scheme around key_down/key_up; most touch-only titles will not react to a held key at all.
  • The same board, mirror and IMConsole.exe prerequisites as every other use case in this section, plus per-phone golden frames captured separately for portrait and landscape.

Watch out

  • /key/down's own parameter table lists fn_key (combination hotkeys) alongside key, but its documented example URL calls fun=/key/sendkey, not /key/down. Confirm on this rig which fun value the kernel actually accepts for a held key before depending on it.
  • key_down/key_up only reaches games that read a hardware keyboard (GameController-framework titles, some emulators, a few keyboard-compatible arcade or strategy games). The general-purpose control path for touch games is mouse_down, mouse_move, mouse_up, still subject to the measured ~0.6 ms per pixel board-walk latency, which reads as input lag against twitch, precision-timing gameplay.
  • Frame-arrival timing detects the AirPlay mirror stalling, not the game engine's true internal frame rate. On the slow XR (~4.5 new frames/s under motion versus ~29 on its twin) a normal frame gap can look identical to a hitch, so baseline per phone first, exactly as in the crash and hang watchdog above.
  • flip_right is one kernel-wide toggle, not per device: a rack cannot mirror some phones flipped and others not at the same time. Beyond "Horizontal screen flip right mode" its effect on the tap-coordinate mapping is undocumented; verify it empirically on one landscape phone before trusting any landscape tap coordinate.
  • dev_rotate firing reliably is unconfirmed on this rig. Treat rotate in /device/get as the source of truth and dev_rotate as a push convenience until it has been observed live.
  • The purchase sheet is real system UI: tapping its confirm control completes a real transaction unless the signed-in account is a sandbox tester. Never script past that tap without a human check that the account is a test account, and scope this only to the developer's own app.
  • No OCR (code 28) means no reading of tutorial copy, currency counters or dialog text; tutorial-completion and IAP-success checks fall back to whole-frame or masked pixel diff against per-orientation goldens, the same ceiling as the rest of this section.

Scale

Touch and key input fan out over id lists at effectively no marginal cost, so the pacing limit is the same one measured for visual regression: each phone's own frame-capture and settle budget, roughly 300 to 600 verified checks per phone per hour on this hardware. Running one tutorial-to-IAP loop continuously across the two live phones is a straightforward multi-hour soak today. Scaling to the other 17 boards means bringing them onto mirroring first, since board count here is control capacity, not video capacity, and does not by itself multiply a soak's throughput.

Open What flip_right actually flips is undocumented

The kernel config doc defines flip_right only as "Horizontal screen flip right mode," true by default, settable through /config/imserver/set without a kernel restart. It does not say whether the flip changes the mirrored image, the tap-coordinate mapping, both, or neither, and it is one value for the whole kernel, not one per device. Before trusting a single landscape tap coordinate, flip the setting on one phone, capture a screenshot, and confirm by test click where the coordinate space actually lands, the same verification discipline already used for portrait in this rig's measurements.

Dynamic Type, Bold Text, Reduce Motion, Increase Contrast and colour-filter sweeps against golden frames

PartialWith caveats

Accessibility QA is not just focus order. Put one phone into a single Accessibility setting at a time, re-run the exact same navigation script and golden-frame suite used for visual regression, and diff every screen against its default-state golden. Larger text and Bold Text catch truncation and overlap; Reduce Motion and Increase Contrast catch missing states that only differ under those flags; a colour filter is the one variant a script can grade on its own, because grayscale and inversion are checkable arithmetic on the raw BMP rather than a judgement call. This reuses the golden-frame pipeline already in this section rather than inventing a new one.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get — confirm the phone is mirroring, read imgw/imgh, and require rotate == 0 before trusting any golden.
  2. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<id> — clear the silent stuck-click state before the walk.
  3. send_key WIN+h GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+h — two presses, normalize to home before touching Settings.
  4. shortcut#13 Open URL (attempt) GET /api/shortcut/exec/url?id=<id>&url=App-Prefs:root=ACCESSIBILITY — try to land directly on the Accessibility pane; this URL scheme is Apple's own, not documented anywhere in the iMouse doc set, and is not confirmed to still work on iOS 18.7.10. Treat it as a probe, not a dependency.
  5. click (fallback) GET /api/mouse/click — the no-dependency path when the deep link fails: tap through Settings by per-phone coordinate, same as any other native navigation in this section.
  6. none (manual) Settings > Accessibility, one toggle at a time — turn on exactly one of: Larger Text at the maximum slider position, Bold Text, Reduce Motion, Increase Contrast, or one Color Filter (Grayscale or a colour-blindness filter). No XP or Phonefarm function reads or writes any of these; this step is off the API entirely.
  7. send_key WIN+h + shortcut#13 / click GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=WIN+h, then the same navigation calls as the golden-frame suite — walk the identical screen list used to build the default-state goldens; a different script or a different order invalidates the comparison.
  8. get_device_screenshot, polled GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true — settle loop on new frames at a fixed 33-50 ms period, exactly as the golden-frame card does, before capturing each screen.
  9. get_device_screenshot with rect GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true&rect=[l,t,r,b] — crop to a specific control (a button, a label) when the whole-frame diff is too noisy to localize a clipped element under larger text.
  10. none (client-side) mean absolute pixel diff, masked, against the default-state golden — for Larger Text, Bold Text, Reduce Motion and Increase Contrast this only flags "something changed here," since the setting is supposed to change the render; a human or vision-model pass classifies each flagged region as expected reflow or actual clipping.
  11. none (client-side) channel-level check on the raw BMP: near-zero colour saturation for Grayscale, inverted luminance ordering for Smart Invert — the one variant with an objective automatic pass, since a true colour filter is a deterministic transform of the pixels, not a subjective layout change.
  12. find_image_cv (optional) POST /api/pic/find-image-cv?id=<id>&img_list=[...]&similarity=0.8 — assert a specific control template still matches under the filter instead of eyeballing the crop; plug-in gated, code 28 on this rig.
  13. send_key OPENKeyboard GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<id>&fn_key=OPENKeyboard — raise the on-screen keyboard on a text field and capture it separately; keyboard chrome is a common place for Bold Text and Larger Text to clip a key label or push the return key off-frame.
  14. send_key TAB+b / WIN+h GET /api/key/sendkey?fn_key=TAB+b|WIN+h — leave the screen and advance; watch dev_rotate, which invalidates every golden in the sweep for that phone.

Needs

  • A complete set of default-state goldens per screen per phone, built by the golden-frame visual-regression card above; this sweep is a second pass over the same screens, not a standalone suite.
  • One phone held in a single Accessibility state for the whole pass; none of Larger Text, Bold Text, Reduce Motion, Increase Contrast or a colour filter can be read or set through either XP or the Phonefarm API, confirmed absent across the configuration, shortcuts and equipment-related docs.
  • A masking strategy that is per-region, not whole-frame: Larger Text and Bold Text change glyph size everywhere on every screen, so an unmasked whole-frame diff will flag every single screen as changed, hiding the genuinely broken ones among the expected ones.
  • A reviewer, human or vision-model, for every flagged screen under the size- and contrast-based variants; only the colour-filter variant supports a fully automatic pass.

Watch out

  • No API reports which Accessibility setting is currently active on a phone. The script has to trust whoever set it; there is no readback to catch a state that silently reverted (an iOS update, an accidental tap) before or during a run.
  • App-Prefs deep links are an Apple convention Apple has restricted release over release specifically because third parties abused them; treat step 4 as opportunistic, confirm it lands on the Accessibility pane on this exact iOS build before relying on it, and keep the tap-through fallback as the real path.
  • Increase Contrast and colour filters can shift colours the app never renders under default settings (system-drawn borders, button fills), which is correct behaviour, not a defect; a naive full-image similarity score will read every screen as "failed" unless the comparator is filter-aware.
  • Never hash-compare frames here either: the same AirPlay encoder noise applies under every Accessibility state, and the idle floor (0.02-0.03) and reaction range (20-160) from the base golden-frame suite still apply as the significance threshold.
  • Running each state serially on one phone means the sweep cannot be parallelized across states the way the base suite parallelizes across screens; budget one full pass per state, not five states at once.

Scale

Capture cost is identical to the base golden-frame suite: about 2 ms per raw BMP poll, a 1-2 second settle on the fast XR and 2-4 seconds on the slow one, so a 20-screen suite still runs in roughly 30-60 seconds per phone per state. The state change itself is the added cost, not the API: each of the five variants here (Larger Text, Bold Text, Reduce Motion, Increase Contrast, one colour filter) is a manual toggle plus a full re-run, so a five-state sweep over a 20-screen suite is five sequential 30-60 second passes on one phone, on the order of 5-10 minutes of capture, plus however long the human or vision-model review of flagged screens takes for the four variants that are not the colour-filter check.

Wrong The rack is not silent

An earlier draft refuted automated VoiceOver auditing on the premise that "the API exposes no audio capture at all." That overstates it. air_play_audio (global, configuration-related doc) and the per-device air_audio field returned by /device/get and set by /device/airplay/set control whether the AirPlay mirror itself carries system audio, VoiceOver's spoken output included; with it on, a human sitting at IMConsole's own mirror window hears the phone. What is actually true, and what the refutation should have said, is narrower: no documented HTTP endpoint captures, records or returns that audio stream. /pic/screenshot returns a video frame only, and no function in any of the nine reference docs offers an audio-equivalent capture call. So live human listening against a mirrored phone is possible today with air_audio enabled; turning that into an automated, scripted VoiceOver pass or fail is not, because there is nothing to poll. The separate point about VoiceOver changing gesture semantics (single-tap-to-select instead of single-tap-to-activate) still stands on its own and remains a real reason this rig's pointer-based control path cannot drive a phone with VoiceOver on.

MARK-FLEET-MARK

Section 9 · Fleet ops

Fleet operations and self-healing

A rack is not one phone repeated nineteen times, it is nineteen independent pairs of channels, control over USB and video over AirPlay, each of which fails on its own schedule. This part covers the registry that makes every slot findable, the health board that reports the two channels separately instead of collapsing them into one flag, the two background watchdogs that catch failures the vendor console does not surface (licence headroom, silent post-update miscalibration), and a scheduler pattern that keeps a job queue running against whichever channel is actually up rather than idling a slot the moment either one drops.

Rack registry and live health

Rack roster: slot names, groups and board bindings as the registry

Native APIWith caveats

Treat the kernel's own device list as the rack's system of record instead of a side spreadsheet. Every phone record already carries a free-text slot name, a group id, the bound board's vid/pid/uid, video state plus air_pid, and location_crc, and every edit broadcasts to all connected consoles as dev_change, group_change or dev_sort_change. On this rig both XRs still show empty names, group 0 (未分组) and boards C241BFBD/C214BEBD, exactly the kind of identifier nobody can find by hand across nineteen boards.

How

  1. get_usb_list + get_device_list GET /api/config/usb/get ; GET /api/device/get — read boards and phones, the two lists this whole roster joins on
  2. set_group GET /api/device/group/set?id=0&name=ClientA-iOS18 — create a fleet group (id=0 means add new)
  3. set_dev GET /api/device/set?id=<deviceid>&name=H10-P02&gid=<gid> — label the slot and assign the fleet in one call, comma-list id for bulk renames
  4. set_dev (vid+pid) GET /api/device/set?id=<deviceid>&vid=720A&pid=<pid> — bind the phone to its control board, one device per call by vendor rule
  5. mouse_collection_open/cfg/close + save_dev_location GET /api/device/collection/mouse?id=<id>&cmd=1|0|2 ; GET /api/device/collection/mouse/save?id=<id>&describe=... — require a calibration before declaring the slot usable
  6. none GET /api/device/group/get-dev?id=<gid> — query a fleet server-side instead of filtering the full list client-side (id=0 is the ungrouped bucket)
  7. none GET /api/device/sort/set?sort_index=<n>&sort_value=-1|0|1 — sort the roster into rack order, mirrors the vendor console's own column order
  8. callbacks ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api — subscribe once, take dev_change, dev_delete, group_change, group_delete, dev_sort_change, usb_change instead of polling
  9. discon_airplay + del_dev + del_group GET /api/device/airplay/disconnect?id=... ; GET /api/device/del?id=... ; GET /api/device/group/del?id=... — retire a slot (disconnect before delete; empty a group before deleting it, code 34 refuses otherwise)
  10. none none — Windows PnP — enrich with the physical hub/port label; neither API edition exposes topology

Needs

  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in; with only IMService.exe up, /device/get read state 0 for both phones and /config/usb/get returned no boards at all.
  • A device record only exists after the phone has cast to the AirPlay receiver at least once; there is no create-device call.
  • Board cabled to the PC before the phone is cabled to the board (state 1 then state 2), vendor cable only.
  • Windows PnP read access if hub/port slot labels are wanted.
  • No plug-in, Shortcut, OCR or Pro-edition gate applies to any call in this chain, the one capability class on this rig that needs none of them.

Watch out

  • The read side is proven live on this rig; the write side (/device/group/set, /device/set, the deletes, /device/sort/set) was never exercised in the read-only probe. The first write is integration testing against production hardware with two live, cabled phones.
  • Board state 1 vs 2 carries the whole control-channel signal, but the XP field table only documents vid/pid/uid/ver, not state. The 1/2 reading is a measured rig fact, not a vendor guarantee, re-verify after any kernel update.
  • "Controllable" and "visible" are independent and must display separately: board state 2 plus a bound vid/pid is control-ready, /device/get state non-0 with a live air_pid is video-ready. One rig snapshot showed 13 boards with a phone attached and only 1 phone mirroring.
  • location_crc non-empty proves a calibration is assigned, not that it fits this handset. Both XRs share library CRC B0DBD800; a wrong CRC silently misplaces every tap, only a pixel-diff probe can catch it.
  • Neither edition exposes hub or port; the slot label has to come from Windows PnP and be maintained by hand whenever a board is reseated.
  • sort_index maps to the vendor console's own header columns with no published column list, probe which index is which before shipping it.
  • Calibration is strictly serial, one device at a time (code 5), and it is a QR-scan flow driven from the console, not an instant API call. Budget a full-rack sweep as multi-hour, largely manual work, not a batch job.
  • Names have no documented length limit, character set or uniqueness constraint; the kernel will let two slots share a name, enforce uniqueness in the controller.
  • Nothing enforces matching imgw/imgh within a group; a controller that treats group membership as a safe-to-mirror-together signal needs its own filter on top.
  • Auto-binding a board by pixel-diffing the pointer only works once a phone is already mirroring; a phone that is only control-ready has no board-to-screen confirmation available for its very first bind and must be identified by the cable and port it was physically plugged into.

Scale

Every read returns the whole rack in one call, /device/get with no id, /config/usb/get, /device/group/get-dev per fleet. Renaming and regrouping batch over a comma id list; hardware binding is strictly one phone per call by vendor rule, so a fresh nineteen-slot rack costs nineteen bind calls, once. Calibration is the real cost center, serialized one device at a time and gated on an operator confirming a QR scan, so treat a fleet-wide sweep as operator-hours, a handful of phones per hour, not an API rate. Steady state after the initial build is free: the kernel broadcasts every edit to every connected client, so a roster refresh never needs to poll, and this traffic does not compete with the measured frame pipeline (84 req/s per phone) or with input traffic.

Two-channel health board: control state versus video state per slot

Native APIWith caveats

A live dashboard that renders every slot as two independent lights, CONTROL (board enumerated on the PC with a phone cabled and bound) and VIDEO (an AirPlay session actually up), instead of one "online" flag. Two HTTP reads at startup join phone records to board records on uid; after that one WebSocket carries the kernel's broadcast callbacks, and a slow fixed-period reconcile poll covers the events the callback vocabulary does not emit.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get — read the phone inventory at startup (optional id filter)
  2. get_usb_list GET /api/config/usb/get — read the board inventory at startup (19 boards, VID 720A on this rig)
  3. none client-side join on uid — CONTROL green = board.state 2 AND a device record carries that uid; CONTROL amber = board.state 1
  4. device record state /device/get list[].state — decide VIDEO on state alone, never on air_pid, which the vendor's own disconnect example leaves populated after disconnect
  5. callbacks ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api — open one socket and take the broadcast stream, there is no subscribe call, holding it open is the subscription
  6. get_airplaysrvnum im_connect callback, data.ver — read the kernel version once, the only source of it on XP
  7. callbacks dev_connect, dev_disconnect, dev_rotate — drive the VIDEO light
  8. callback usb_change (data.code 19/20/12) — drive the CONTROL light
  9. none dev_change, dev_delete — catch a rebind, rename or delete made by any other client on the LAN
  10. get_device_list + get_usb_list GET /api/device/get + GET /api/config/usb/get on a fixed 5-15s timer — reconcile poll as the safety net for events the callbacks do not emit
  11. none error_push callback, data.call_fun — surface per-call hardware failures as a rack-level ticker
  12. none none — Windows PnP — label each row with a findable physical slot

Needs

  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in; otherwise the board renders all-dark, all-state-0, which looks like a hardware failure but is a missing software prerequisite.
  • XP-edition kernel on TCP 9911 only, path style, Phonefarm-style function names return HTTP 500 on this kernel.
  • One long-lived WebSocket client with reconnect-and-refetch on drop, there is no replay or sequence number, a missed broadcast is invisible until the reconcile poll catches it.
  • Phones bound to boards via /device/set with vid and pid sent together (single-device call) so uid exists for the join.
  • Everything in this chain is a GET or a callback, no /mouse, /key or write call is needed to render the two lights.

Watch out

  • The CONTROL light's whole premise, state 1 versus 2, is not in the documented field table, only vid/pid/uid/ver are. It is a measured rig fact, re-verify after any kernel update by pulling one cable and watching the value.
  • usb_change has no documented event for "phone unplugged but board stays on the PC" (only connected/disconnected-from-computer and connected-to-phone). A callback-only CONTROL light latches green after a cable pull, the reconcile poll is mandatory, not optional.
  • air_pid is not a disconnect signal, the vendor's own dev_disconnect example carries state 0 with air_pid still populated. Use state as sole authority; air_pid is a hint only when it matches the running AirplayMirroring.exe PID.
  • air_pid and air_handle are example-only fields, absent from the documented field table entirely.
  • error_push's worked example carries an empty data.id, so per-slot attribution is not guaranteed, render it rack-level keyed by call_fun unless id is actually populated at runtime.
  • Two green lights mean necessary, not sufficient. iOS-side prerequisites (AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, tracking speeds, Auto-Lock Never) are invisible to the API, and neither light can see the measured stuck-click state where /mouse/move keeps working while /mouse/click silently does nothing until /mouse/reset.
  • The WebSocket has no replay or sequence numbers, a dropped connection during a state change is a permanently missed event until the reconcile poll catches it. Document the reconcile interval as the real staleness bound, not the socket.
  • Use a fixed reconcile period, never one derived from observed event gaps, adaptive pacing on the frame pump measured decaying 23 fps to 16.5 fps through positive feedback on this rig, and the same trap applies to any self-timed polling loop.
  • The hub/port slot label needs a Windows PnP or WMI reader entirely outside the HTTP API, real added engineering scope, not a REST call.
  • "The same code handles roughly a hundred phones" is an assumption, not a measurement, only 19 boards and 2 phones were observed here.

Scale

Two GETs at startup regardless of rack size, then one shared WebSocket that costs the kernel the same whether one console or several are watching, plus a reconcile poll of the same two GETs on a fixed low-rate timer, five to fifteen seconds, never adaptive. Measured control-plane and input traffic do not contend with frame polling (83-85 req/s per phone unaffected by concurrent input), so a health board running beside a live video wall is free, well under 1 req/s aggregate for this 19-board rack. The practical ceiling is the kernel's own device-count licensing and AirPlay bandwidth, not this board.

Trap A latched green light is worse than no light

There is no usb_change code for "phone detached from a board that stays on the PC", so a health board driven only by callbacks will show CONTROL green forever after a cable pull. The fixed reconcile poll (five to fifteen seconds, never adaptive) is not an optimization here, it is the only thing standing between the dashboard and a false green.

Account and calibration watchdogs

Licence headroom and expiry watchdog on the kernel account

Native APIWith caveats

The kernel refuses to bring phones online when it is not logged in or over its authorised device count, and the only signal is a Chinese log line pushed on the WebSocket. This watchdog holds one connection, reads the licence and account fields the kernel already pushes every 30 seconds, computes headroom against the correct ceiling for the account type, counts days to expiry from the kernel's own clock, and raises a dated warning before a phone silently sits at state 0. Re-login stays a manual operator action in IMConsole.exe, the controller only reads state, never a password.

How

  1. callbacks ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api — open one WebSocket for the push channel, the Phonefarm /clinet path does not exist here
  2. get_airplaysrvnum im_connect callback, data.ver — record the kernel version on connect, the only version readout on XP
  3. none GET /api/config/user/info — read licence and account state on demand, no parameters
  4. none callback user_info — consume the unsolicited 30-second push, same payload as the GET above
  5. none client-side arithmetic — ceiling = total_license when user_state == 1, else local_total_license (cross-check test_num); headroom = ceiling minus dev_online_num
  6. none client-side, overdue_time vs network_time — compute days to expiry from the kernel's clock, not the PC's, alert at 14/7/1 days
  7. none callback im_log, data.message — surface the refusal string 未登录，不允许上线 as a hard alert, data.code is 0 even here
  8. none callback logout (and pass == false in user_info) — alert on the account dropping out
  9. none GET /api/config/user/switch?id=1-10 — optionally move the rack to another sub-account pool
  10. get_device_list GET /api/device/get — correlate the licence ceiling to actual slots, count state != 0 against dev_online_num
  11. none /config/user/login and /config/user/logout — operator actions in IMConsole.exe, never automated

Needs

  • XP kernel on TCP 9911, path style only, Phonefarm-style function names return HTTP 500 here and 9912 is closed.
  • A WebSocket client to catch im_connect, user_info, im_log and logout; an HTTP-only fallback still works via polling /config/user/info but loses all three plus the kernel version.
  • The kernel logged in via IMConsole.exe; with only IMService.exe running, both phones read state 0 and the board list comes back empty.
  • Account credentials held only by the operator, entered in the vendor console, never by the controller.
  • Nothing else: no plug-in, Shortcut, board or phone accessibility setting, this watches kernel-side account state only.

Watch out

  • /config/user/info was never exercised in the 10 September probe, which hit a wrong guessed path, /user/get, and 404'd. Probe the real path once before trusting the numbers.
  • There is no Phonefarm equivalent for any of this, the sibling doc has no user, login or licence concept at all, this idea is XP-only by construction.
  • The headroom formula must branch on user_state; min(total_license, local_total_license) is wrong and would report negative headroom on a healthy trial rig, per the vendor's own worked example.
  • overdue_time is not a reliable gate by itself, in the vendor's own example it sits roughly 19 months in the past while pass is still true. Report it next to pass and user_state, not as a standalone verdict.
  • dev_num is documented with two contradictory descriptions, "number of users" and "verification passed". Count phones from /device/get instead of trusting it.
  • im_log carries data.code 0 even for the refusal message, detection is string-matching Chinese text. Surface any unmatched im_log verbatim rather than swallowing it, other over-licence wordings are undocumented.
  • Sub-account switching is documented in one paragraph with no statement of how licence pools or online devices behave across the switch. Test on an idle rig before using it as remediation.
  • Kernel version is only ever available from the im_connect callback, there is no HTTP version endpoint on XP.
  • This watchdog explains only why a phone will not come ONLINE. It says nothing about the USB control channel, a licence-refused phone can still be board-state 2 and controllable.
  • The 30-second push is not a guaranteed heartbeat by the doc's own wording, "when logging in and at other times". Give the watchdog its own staleness timer, alert if neither user_info nor im_connect arrives for 90-plus seconds, rather than assuming silence means nothing to report.

Scale

Effectively free and independent of rack size. The kernel already pushes a small JSON message every 30 seconds on an existing socket whether the rig has 2 phones or 100, and /config/user/info is a single parameterless call used only at startup and after a reconnect. No screenshot traffic, no board traffic, nothing that can contend with the measured frame pipeline or input traffic. Evaluate on each push and de-duplicate so a persistent condition alerts once per threshold crossing, 14, 7 and 1 days, headroom at or below 3, not every 30 seconds.

Trap Do not take the minimum of the two ceilings

The obvious headroom formula, min(total_license, local_total_license), is wrong. The vendor's own worked example (user_state 2, total_license 0, local_total_license 100, test_num 100) would report negative headroom on a rack that is actually fine. Branch on user_state first: total_license only applies to a formal account (user_state 1), everything else is a test authorisation and reads against local_total_license.

iOS-update tripwire that queues recalibration and re-verification

PartialWith caveats

The pointer-calibration library is keyed by phone model plus iOS version, so an overnight OTA can silently invalidate a phone's calibration while every other signal stays green, it mirrors, it moves the pointer, and it taps 30 px off. Every device record and the dev_connect/dev_change callbacks carry a version field, so a controller that stores the last-seen version per phone gets a free tripwire, quarantine on change, corner-probe and tap-test to confirm, recollect once per model and iOS version if needed, then fan the new calibration out to every same-model phone in one call.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get (version field) — store a per-device iOS version baseline in the controller, the kernel persists nothing beyond name and gid
  2. callback ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api — dev_connect, dev_change — tripwire, compare data.list[0].version against the stored value on every callback
  3. set_group / set_dev GET /api/device/group/set?id=0&name=Quarantine then GET /api/device/set?id=<deviceid>&gid=<gid> — quarantine the changed phone so the scheduler skips it, gid is inert metadata, the kernel does not enforce it
  4. get_devicemodel_list GET /api/config/devicemodel/get — ask whether a calibration already exists for this model plus the new iOS version, response shape undocumented
  5. mouse_reset_pos + mouse_move + get_device_screenshot GET /api/mouse/reset?id=... ; GET /api/mouse/move?id=&x=&y= ; GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=&binary=true — corner probe: reset, move to three points, screenshot each, mean absolute pixel diff in a box around the commanded point
  6. send_key + click GET /api/key/sendkey?id=&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) ; GET /api/mouse/click?id=&x=&y= — functional tap test on a known home-screen icon, whole-frame mean diff
  7. mouse_collection_open/cfg/close GET /api/device/collection/mouse?id=&cmd=1 (0 query, 2 stop) — if the probe fails, collect once on one phone of that model, operator opens the collection page from a console QR
  8. save_dev_location GET /api/device/collection/mouse/save?id=&describe=XR-18.7.10-rack1 — publish the collected parameters to the shared library, XP has no delete endpoint for this
  9. set_dev location_crc GET /api/device/get?id=<collected id> then GET /api/device/set?id=<id1,id2,...>&location_crc=<crc> — read the resulting CRC back and fan it out to every remaining same-model phone in one multi-id call
