  10. set_dev GET /api/device/set?id=<ids>&gid=<fleet gid> — re-run the probe and tap test on every phone that received the new CRC, release on pass, leave quarantined on fail
  11. shortcut#24 (external IP) GET /api/shortcut/device/ip?id=&state=0 — optional: re-check the Shortcut round trip, since an OTA can re-prompt its permissions

Needs

  • XP kernel, path style only; IMConsole.exe running and logged in, the console is also the only documented way to present the phone-side collection QR.
  • A controller that persists per-device iOS version history and a quarantine flag, plus a Quarantine group and a scheduler that actually honours gid.
  • Client-side BMP decode and a mean-absolute-pixel-difference routine, no OCR or image-search plug-in required, which is the point since /pic/ocr returns code 28 on this rig.
  • Per-phone imgw/imgh and a known home-screen icon coordinate for the tap test, the two XRs have different home screens.
  • An operator at the rack for the collection leg only: phone bound to its board, portrait, no other device collecting.

Watch out

  • The collection leg cannot be fully automated, the phone-side page is opened by hand from a console QR code. Budget an operator per model-and-iOS wave.
  • /config/devicemodel/get's response shape is undocumented, "too many, omitted" in the vendor doc, and was never exercised live. Probe it once, or skip that step and let the corner probe be the sole authority.
  • Quarantine is advisory only, nothing in the kernel blocks input to a quarantined phone, and the API has no authentication, so another host can still drive it.
  • An offset probe result has two indistinguishable causes, a stale calibration or an OTA resetting AssistiveTouch or Trackpad tracking settings, and neither is queryable. Check phone-side settings before recollecting, or a bad collection is baked into the shared library permanently, there is no delete endpoint on XP.
  • The tripwire only fires when a phone appears on a callback or poll; keep a periodic reconciliation poll as backstop for a phone that updates while offline or across a dropped socket.
  • iOS auto-update is entirely outside the API, this detects an update after the fact and cannot prevent or defer one, and a passcode lock after an OTA reboot is a hard stop with no typed remediation.
  • Screenshot verification must race the real AirPlay source rate, not a 30 fps assumption, the slow XR delivers roughly 4.5 new frames a second, so a timeout tuned to the fast phone at roughly 29 fps will false-fail the slow one.
  • The three-point corner probe catches uniform scale or translation error but is weak against rotation or shear, a small rotational term can partially cancel across two far corners and still pass while the UI centre is off. Add a fourth, off-diagonal point if rotation error matters for a given model.
  • Version-change tripwires fire more than once per real OTA, iOS commonly reboots twice and drops Wi-Fi while optimising. Debounce on a version value held stable across several polls before quarantining, or the scheduler thrashes a phone in and out mid-update.
  • A raw inequality compare on version strings quarantines on every point release, not just the bumps that risk calibration drift, treat a version change as far more frequent than a version change that actually needs recollection.
  • The home-screen tap test assumes the phone is already past any post-OTA prompts, Apple ID re-auth, Wi-Fi rejoin, updated terms. WIN+h will not dismiss those, and a whole-frame diff cannot distinguish an opened app from a phone stuck on a dialog.

Scale

Costs nothing until an update actually lands, the tripwire is one WebSocket or one no-id /device/get poll per interval. Per-phone verification is dominated by pointer travel, roughly 0.6 ms per pixel, so the three corner moves cost about 1.1 seconds, plus three 2 ms raw-BMP screenshots and a wait for a fresh frame on the slow phone, call it two to four seconds per phone end to end, and phones verify in parallel (measured 512 req/s across ten concurrent pollers, input traffic does not slow frame polling). Reset and the two Home presses take comma-separated id lists, so they cost one request for the whole wave regardless of fleet size. The expensive step is the collection itself, and it is once per model and iOS version, not per phone, one collection on this rig covers both XRs; at 19 boards, a fleet-wide OTA wave is one manual collection, minutes, needing an operator, plus roughly 20 to 80 seconds of parallel automated re-verification.

Trap Every published calibration is permanent

XP has no endpoint to delete a record from the mouse-parameter library. A collection run against a phone whose accessibility settings had already drifted bakes bad parameters into a record that auto-matches every future same-model phone on that iOS version, forever. Verify AssistiveTouch tracking sensitivity and Trackpad and Mouse tracking speed on the phone before collecting, and make the describe string identify the rig and date so a bad record is at least findable.

Scheduling through partial failure

Degraded-mode operation: keep running blind jobs when video is down

PartialWith caveats

Control and video are separate channels, and either can die alone. Classify every phone continuously into FULL, BLIND (control only, no picture), MIRROR-ONLY (picture, no usable board) or DEAD, then let the job queue keep running whatever work each class can still do instead of idling the slot. A BLIND phone still accepts taps, swipes and keys over USB, so fixed-coordinate, idempotent, keyboard-driven work can run blind and be verified once mirroring returns; a MIRROR-ONLY phone can still be screenshotted for observation-only jobs. On this rack the weak XR delivers roughly 4.5 new frames a second against its twin's 29 on the same LAN, video is the flaky channel, USB is the reliable one.

How

  1. get_usb_list GET /api/config/usb/get — read the control channel for every slot
  2. get_device_list GET /api/device/get (optional id=comma list) — read the video channel for every slot
  3. none (derived) client-side logic over the two reads — classify FULL / BLIND / MIRROR-ONLY / DEAD; control-ready and video-ready are independent, the API offers no combined health field
  4. callbacks ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api — dev_connect, dev_disconnect, dev_change, usb_change, error_push — re-classify on events, not only on a timer
  5. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<comma list> — clear the invisible stuck-click state before any blind work, mandatory since there are no frames to diff it against
  6. send_key fn_key WIN+h GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<comma list>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — normalise to a known screen, blind; the keyboard path is the liveness probe that survives a dead pointer
  7. click / swipe / send_key / mouse_wheel /api/mouse/click, /api/mouse/swipe, /api/mouse/wheel, /api/key/sendkey, /api/key/down, /api/key/up, /api/key/upall — run only blind-safe work: fixed-coordinate taps, ASCII typing, documented hotkeys, all take a comma id list
  8. send_key fn_key /api/key/sendkey fn_key=TAB+l, MuteSoundSwitch, VolumeDown, Play/Pause — give BLIND phones a verification-free housekeeping queue, one request drives the whole BLIND set
  9. shortcut / ocr / find_image /api/shortcut/* and /api/pic/* — exclude on BLIND phones — exclude every job that needs the phone's own LAN path or a frame
  10. auto_connect_screen(_all) GET /api/device/airplay/connect?id=<comma list> or /api/device/airplay/connect/all — recover the video channel; no force flag on XP, disconnect a degraded session first
  11. none GET /api/imserver/regmdns — re-broadcast AirPlay mDNS if the receiver has vanished from the phone's mirroring list
  12. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<single id>&binary=true — verify the blind work once the picture is back, single id only, compare by mean absolute pixel diff
  13. restart_usb GET /api/device/usb/restart?id=720A|C241 (vid|pid, comma list) — recover the control channel for MIRROR-ONLY slots, video is untouched
  14. set_usb_autoairplay none per-device; nearest is the global auto_connect in /api/config/imserver/set — no per-device auto-cast switch exists on XP

Needs

  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in; with only IMService.exe up, both channels read as empty or state 0.
  • A job queue where every job declares which channel it needs, control, video, or the phone's own LAN path, there is nothing to schedule against without that tag.
  • Per-phone board binding present and location_crc non-empty, otherwise mouse calls return code 2, 3 or 11.
  • The five iOS accessibility settings on every phone, none queryable over the API: AssistiveTouch on with tracking sensitivity max, Full Keyboard Access on, Trackpad and Mouse tracking speed max, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock with StandBy off.
  • A WebSocket client, HTTP polling alone cannot see airplay_connect_log and is blind to why a re-cast failed.
  • Each phone's imgw/imgh cached from its last good /device/get record, so a BLIND phone's coordinate space is known without a fresh frame.

Watch out

  • The blind leg is genuinely blind, no observation channel exists at all on a BLIND phone. Screenshot, OCR and find-image all need the mirror; Shortcut fallbacks need the phone's own Wi-Fi, which is the thing that is down. The only feedback is data.code plus async error_push, and neither proves the UI reacted, only that the board accepted the command.
  • The stuck-click state is undetectable blind, /mouse/reset is the only known cure and is confirmed only to clear that specific state, not to correct a drifted pointer, which is still unverified. A drifted pointer taps the wrong place on every call while still returning code 0.
  • Re-casting is not proven on this rig, the OCR plug-in it may lean on reports code 28, not connected, here. Plan for manual re-cast from the phone's own Control Center until that path is probed.
  • Auto-cast and a blind job fight over the same board and the same screen, serialise "auto-cast retry pending" and "blind job pending" as mutually exclusive locks per phone, not just as a stated risk, or the retry taps through whatever the blind job has on screen.
  • There is no per-device auto-cast flag on XP, only a global switch, you cannot leave auto-cast on for just the flaky phone.
  • There is no server-push frame stream on XP; observation-only work on MIRROR-ONLY phones is one polling thread per phone, since screenshot takes a single id.
  • Board state semantics are measured, not documented, a kernel update that changes the encoding fails the classifier silently.
  • A phone that reboots or locks comes back on the lock screen with no documented way to type a passcode, a BLIND phone that locks is effectively out of the rack until touched.
  • A phone BLIND from a real hardware fault looks identical over the API, in the seconds right after the state changes, to one an operator just unplugged for a swap, both read board-state not-2, and a stale cached control-ready flag can send taps into nothing.
  • The five iOS accessibility prerequisites are unqueryable, so a phone can pass every classifier check and still never confirm a blind tap landed even after mirroring returns, because the tap never registered on the iOS side at all, indistinguishable from a slow-mirroring phone until a human watches a replay.
  • Cap the verification backlog, a phone stuck BLIND indefinitely needs an explicit limit, N unverified actions or T minutes, after which it is pulled from the blind queue and flagged for a manual check rather than trusting a reconciliation that may never come.
  • Filter the reset target list by current board state first, sending /mouse/reset to a board with no phone attached is harmless but wastes a call across the whole id list every cycle.

Scale

Classification is nearly free, one /device/get and one /config/usb/get per sweep, with WebSocket callbacks triggering off-cycle re-polls. Blind execution actually scales better than sighted execution: every input endpoint takes a comma-separated id list and the boards walk in parallel, so a hotkey sweep across the whole BLIND set is one request, not many, at the same latency as driving a single phone. Verification is the bottleneck and does not batch, screenshot is single-id, so budget one poller per phone, measured 83-85 req/s per phone independently, about 1.6 MB per raw BMP poll. The real ceiling is the per-phone AirPlay source rate, 29 fps on the strong XR versus 4.5 fps on the weak one, so a verification step on the weak phone has to tolerate roughly 220 ms per new frame rather than a 30 fps assumption. Command issuance batches across the whole BLIND set in one call and does not compete with frame polling, measured independent, so recovered-phone verification can run concurrently with ongoing blind work on others. For a job with no branching, expect on the order of 2,000 to 4,000 fixed-coordinate blind actions per hour per phone; the moment a job needs to branch on screen state, blind execution stalls until video returns and the real ceiling becomes recast latency, not the API.

Trap Blind means idempotent and reversible, or it does not run

Blind input into a phone whose screen has changed underneath you, a system dialog, an app-update prompt, a session that logged itself out, types into whatever field happens to hold focus. That is how text meant for one field ends up in a search box or a composed message. Restrict the blind queue to steps with no irreversible tail: never a send, submit, publish, post, confirm, purchase or delete while blind, and never any credential or personal data at all, that belongs in a password manager the operator drives, not a scripted keystroke. Treat any blind job as provisional until a frame confirms it.

Keeping the rack connected

Cast-on-connect plus periodic re-cast sweeper

PartialWith caveats

Keeps a rack mirroring without a human, by combining a global kernel flag with a timed sweep. The auto_connect flag (with connect_failed_retry) tells the kernel to re-cast a phone on its own; a background sweeper calls the connect-all endpoint for anything still offline. AirPlay sessions drop on Wi-Fi hiccups, after any phone restart, and whenever a per-device cast profile changes, since that change disconnects by design. This recovers the video channel only: the USB control channel is independent of it, so it fixes "controllable but blind," never the separate stuck-click fault that makes a phone "visible but deaf."

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get — enumerate what is actually offline (state 0) before acting; state says nothing about the USB control channel, so cross-check that separately.
  2. get_usb_autoairplay (no per-device XP equivalent) GET /api/config/imserver/get — read the current global auto_connect / connect_failed_retry policy.
  3. set_usb_autoairplay GET /api/config/imserver/set?auto_connect=true&connect_failed_retry=0 — turn on cast-on-connect with unlimited retry; applies live, no kernel restart, no lost sessions.
  4. WebSocket ws://host:9911/clinet ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api — open before casting; it is the only channel carrying airplay_connect_log, dev_connect and dev_disconnect.
  5. auto_connect_screen_all GET /api/device/airplay/connect/all — sweeper: re-cast every offline device on a timer (roughly every 5 minutes); takes no id filter and cannot be scoped.
  6. auto_connect_screen GET /api/device/airplay/connect?id=<id1>,<id2> — targeted re-cast of named phones, e.g. one rack row, without touching phones mid-task.
  7. auto_connect_screen force:true GET /api/device/airplay/disconnect?id=<ids> then /device/airplay/connect?id=<ids> — XP has no force flag, so a degraded-but-connected session must be dropped before it can be recast.
  8. (no Phonefarm equivalent) WS callback airplay_connect_log — trace every attempt's numeric code against the XP error table; never branch on the Chinese message text.
  9. callback dev_connect then GET /api/device/get?id=<id> — confirm the cast really came up by comparing the new air_pid/air_handle to the pre-cast snapshot, not just checking state != 0.
  10. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true — state-free proof the picture is live: body starts "BM" and is exactly 1,620,054 bytes at this rig's geometry.
  11. (none) GET /api/imserver/regmdns — re-advertise the receiver if every phone loses it at once, without the full-rack outage of /imserver/restart.
  12. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<ids> — reset the pointer on the whole re-cast set before any tap-critical sequence; a re-cast does nothing for the separate stuck-click fault.

Needs

  • XP kernel on 9911 with path-style calls; Phonefarm fun names return HTTP 500 here.
  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in — without it both channels read as empty or offline even with the kernel service up.
  • Each phone bound to its board (vid+pid together) with a non-empty location_crc, and board state 2 in /config/usb/get for every phone expected to auto-cast.
  • Phone-side settings invisible to the API: AssistiveTouch on with tracking sensitivity maxed, Trackpad & Mouse speed maxed, Full Keyboard Access on, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock, and the phone already unlocked on its home screen with no passcode or Face ID prompt pending.
  • Control Centre arranged with two rows of icons at the bottom — the vendor states this affects automatic screencasting.
  • Phone on the same LAN segment, the receiver name visible in the phone's Screen Mirroring list, AirplayMirroring.exe listening on port 17000.

Watch out

  • Every call in this chain is documented native XP with no plug-in gate in the docs — but the Phonefarm sibling's equivalent needs a point-capture step that explicitly requires the OCR and image-search plug-ins, and the OCR plug-in reports code 28 on this rig. If XP shares that dependency, auto-cast fails here until the plug-ins are installed; that is unverified, which is why this entry is graded partial rather than native. Test on one phone before enabling it rack-wide.
  • auto_connect is a global flag with no per-device exemption — you cannot arm auto-cast for one row and leave a flaky phone out of it. The only per-phone lever is leaving the flag off and driving targeted connects yourself.
  • The connect-all endpoint cannot be scoped; use the comma-list connect endpoint for anything less than the whole rack.
  • No force flag exists: an already-connected but degraded session must be disconnected first, or the connect call returns code 22, "Equipment online."
  • A re-cast changes air_pid/air_handle and can change imgw/imgh — re-derive any cached tap coordinates per device afterwards, and reset the pointer before the next tap-critical sequence.
  • This fixes the video channel only. A phone that fails to re-cast is still fully controllable and simply blind; a phone that re-casts cleanly may still be in the stuck-click state. Report the two channels separately, never as one health light.
  • Validated only on two calibration-identical iPhone XRs; a fleet with mixed models or iOS versions is exactly the case most likely to break the internal cast-swipe coordinates, and a phone lacking a matching calibration profile can return code 0 while having tapped the wrong control — a live screenshot proves a picture, not that the right control was pressed.
  • An AirPlay receiver can optionally require an on-screen pairing PIN depending on the console's security setting; nothing in this API surface exposes or controls it, and no endpoint can enter one. If it is on, unattended re-cast attempts stall silently and unlimited retry loops forever — confirm it is off before relying on this unattended.

Scale

The connect-all and comma-list connect calls are O(1) regardless of fleet size; the cost is on the phone, not the wire. The board drives each phone's own Control Centre through USB at a measured ~0.6 ms/px, so a swipe-and-tap sequence costs low hundreds of milliseconds of pointer travel per phone before UI settling, and every listed phone is driven concurrently by one request. Run the sweeper as a background timer, not an inline retry inside a task, and cap connect_failed_retry rather than leaving it infinite, or a phone stuck at a lock screen gets tapped forever. Verification does not contend with any of this: /device/get is one call for the whole rack, and per-phone screenshot polling measured no interference with input traffic in either direction. This rig has only 2 of 19 boards actually mirroring, so batch-size and recast-reliability numbers beyond that are a design assumption, not a measurement.

Self-healing input and hardware

Stuck-click self-healing runbook with escalation ladder

PartialWith caveats

Automated recovery for the measured fault in which a phone silently ignores /mouse/click while /mouse/move and hardware keys keep working. A prevent-detect-escalate loop climbs only as far as needed: pointer reset (the measured cure) first, then a two-channel triage read, then board reset, then phone reboot, then kernel restart as a last resort. Detection is state-independent: normalise with two WIN+h presses, fire one click at a per-phone known target, and threshold the mean absolute pixel difference of a raw BMP frame — measured 0.09 stuck versus 141.96 healthy against a 0.02-0.03 idle floor, never MD5. This is the one measured fault on this rig that returns data.code 0 for a click that did nothing, so no status field catches it, and every rung except the screenshot takes a comma id list, so the preventive reset and each escalation is one request for the whole rack.

How

  1. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<idA>,<idB>,... — Rung 0, preventive: reset the whole target set before any tap-critical sequence; cheap insurance that stays cleared across repeated clicks.
  2. send_key (fn_key) GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — Detect A, normalise: leave then return to a known home screen; the Home hotkey still works even while the pointer is stuck, which is exactly why a keyboard-only probe would miss the fault.
  3. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true — Detect B: baseline raw BMP frame, one request per phone (2.0 ms p50, 1,620,054 bytes).
  4. click GET /api/mouse/click?id=<id>&x=442&y=245 then screenshot — Detect C: one tap at a per-phone home-screen target (coordinates are per-phone, not portable across different home screens), then a second frame.
  5. (client-side) none — computed locally — Detect D: mean absolute pixel diff between the two frames — idle 0.02-0.03, stuck click 0.09, healthy click 142-163; threshold above 20 is alive, below 1 is stuck. Never MD5.
  6. mouse_up + key_release_all GET /api/mouse/up?id=<ids> and /api/key/upall?id=<ids> — Rung 1, cheap and expected not to fix it: release any held button or key, in case an aborted drag left one down, a different fault this call does cure.
  7. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<ids> — Rung 2, the measured cure: reset, then re-run the detect probe; most incidents terminate here.
  8. get_usb_list + get_device_list GET /api/config/usb/get and /api/device/get?id=<id> — Rung 2.5, triage before escalating: read control-channel state (board 2) and video-channel state (device non-zero plus air_pid) separately, at no cost, before rebooting a phone whose board simply fell off.
  9. restart_usb GET /api/device/usb/restart?id=720A|C241 — Rung 3: reset the control board, addressed by VID|PID rather than the phone id, the single biggest addressing difference from the Phonefarm doc.
  10. callback usb_change ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api — Rung 3 confirmation: watch for code 20 then 19 then 12 for that board, falling back to polling /config/usb/get since the ordering is inferred, not documented.
  11. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<id> — Rung 3 aftercare: reset again now that the board has re-enumerated with a fresh, unsynchronised pointer state.
  12. restart_device / shortcut switch device / send_key GET /api/device/restart?id=<ids> OR /api/shortcut/switch/device?id=<ids>&state=1 OR /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=CTRL+ALT+SHIFT+WIN+r — Rung 4: reboot the phone; the driven restart route is expected to fail here since its Phonefarm sibling needs the OCR plug-in, which reads code 28 on this rig.
  13. callback dev_disconnect / auto_connect_screen restart_log then dev_disconnect, then GET /api/device/airplay/connect?id=<id> — Rung 4 aftercare: confirm via the callback plus a new air_pid, never via a screenshot diff since the mirror is gone during reboot; a passcode-locked phone stops here and needs a human.
  14. restart GET /api/imserver/restart — Rung 5, maintenance window only: restarts the kernel, dropping every session and socket on the rack; try the far cheaper /imserver/regmdns first if the symptom is just a vanished receiver.
  15. (no Phonefarm equivalent) ws callback error_push — continuous signal: the only asynchronous proof an input call failed at the board; it will not fire for this fault's code 0, but it catches neighbouring hardware faults.
  16. (local) none — local store keyed on deviceid + uid — bookkeeping: log which rung cleared each incident; a phone repeatedly needing rung 3 or higher is a cable or board candidate, and the physical hub/port slot (from Windows PnP, not the API) is the only label a technician can act on.

Needs

  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in — with only IMService.exe up, this rig showed both phones state 0 and an empty board list, leaving the runbook nothing to act on.
  • Per phone: board bound and /config/usb/get state 2 for that board, plus a non-empty location_crc, or every mouse call returns "No mouse parameters."
  • iOS-side settings that are invisible to the API and are the usual cause of "looks fine, ignores input": AssistiveTouch on with sensitivity maxed, Full Keyboard Access on (needed for both hotkey probes), Trackpad & Mouse speed maxed, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock. The probe in this runbook is the only proof any of it is actually set.
  • A per-phone detect target chosen from that device's own imgw/imgh, since the two XRs on this rig do not share a home screen.
  • A WebSocket client for usb_change, restart_log, airplay_connect_log and error_push; rungs 0-3 work over plain HTTP, only the confirmations need the socket.
  • Rung 3 only: board firmware and kernel floors per the Phonefarm doc, unverifiable here since ver/uver read as mojibake on this build. Rung 4's shortcut route needs the iMouse Shortcut installed and bound, not confirmed present on this rig.
  • The API has no authentication at all — firewall 9911 before wiring this runbook to anything automatic.

Watch out

  • Rungs 0 through 3 and the whole detect loop are natively achievable and were confirmed answering on 9911 in the 10 September probe; rung 4's driven route is expected to fail here because its OCR-plug-in dependency reads code 28. Treat the hotkey route as the primary rung-4 attempt and the Shortcut route as unavailable until installed.
  • The detect click opens whatever is under that coordinate. It must be followed by Home, must target something idempotent, and must never sit inside an open app where it could send, post, or delete. A long-press into icon-jiggle mode is a plausible lower-risk variant but is unverified here — measure before trusting it.
  • /mouse/reset is confirmed only to clear the stuck-click state; whether it corrects a drifted (offset) pointer is unverified, so do not advertise it as a calibration fix. Its own round-trip and settle latency is also never measured — verify with a timed probe before wiring it into a high-frequency sequence.
  • The usb_change sequence 20-19-12 after a board reset is inferred, not documented as an order; fall back to polling /config/usb/get for that pid returning to state 2. The board's state field itself is undocumented, a measurement from this rig, not the vendor's field table.
  • The fault returns code 0, so no rung can be triggered by a status check alone — the probe is mandatory, and error_push does not catch this specific fault.
  • Rung 5 drops every mirroring session and socket on the rack; gate it behind an explicit human maintenance window, never an automatic loop, and try /imserver/regmdns first when the symptom is a vanished receiver.
  • Frame timing is per-phone — one XR delivers ~29 new frames/s under motion, its twin ~4.5 — so a detect loop assuming 30 fps will read the slow phone as stuck. Wait for a genuinely new frame (and on the slow phone, several of them, since one iOS UI transition needs 2-4 visually distinct frames to be judged stable) rather than a fixed sleep.
  • The detect click is a real tap that opens whatever is under the coordinate, and repeated probing multiplies the chance it lands somewhere destructive if a phone has drifted off its expected state — the two-Home normalisation must run immediately before every probe, never be assumed still valid from a prior cycle.
  • Everything here is XP path-style on 9911; Phonefarm function names return HTTP 500 and the WebSocket path is /api, not /clinet.
  • The throughput reasoning has two different ceilings: screenshot latency describes HTTP capacity, not how soon a genuinely new frame exists — the real ceiling is the AirPlay source fps, 4.5-29 per phone, so a rack sweep's real wall time is bounded by the slowest phone's frame arrival, not by request count.

Scale

Rungs 0, 1, 2, 4 and the WIN+h normalisation all accept a comma id list, so recovering 50 phones is one request each, not 50, and the board walks every listed phone in parallel. /device/usb/restart takes a comma list of VID|PID pairs too, so a bank of boards resets in one call. The only per-phone cost is the detect probe — screenshot is single-id, so two 1.62 MB frames per phone at ~2.0 ms each, plus the frame-arrival wait, which is the dominant and per-phone term (~35 ms on the fast XR, ~220 ms or more on the slow one). Phones are independent, measured at 83-85 req/s on two concurrent pollers and 512 req/s aggregate on ten, so probing fans out with one poller per phone and no scheduling. A whole-rack preventive sweep is two requests regardless of fleet size; a whole-rack verification sweep on 19 slots is on the order of one second of wall time. Given the detect click's own risk, run it once per job as a pre-flight gate rather than continuously; as a background watchdog, once per 30-60 s per phone stays well inside every measured ceiling.

USB flap watchdog: board reset driven by usb_change and a state-2 poll

Native APIWith caveats

Holds one WebSocket and treats the usb_change callback as the control-channel event bus: code 19 board attached to PC, 20 detached, 12 phone attached to board, with a live board table joined to phone deviceids from /device/get. A board reset fires only where it can actually reach the board — a flap that returned but settled at state 1 with no code 12, or a board at state 2 whose control is dead per an error_push fault or a hardware-not-connected error code. A control-board flap takes a phone out of every job while the mirror still looks perfect, because video and control are independent channels; catching the transition from a callback is instant, discovering it from a click that did nothing is minutes to hours later and is easily misdiagnosed as a mirroring fault.

How

  1. WebSocket ws://host:9911/clinet ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api — open and hold one socket; every attach/detach event arrives here, no polling loop needed for the events themselves.
  2. get_usb_list + get_device_list /config/usb/get and /device/get — build the board table once at startup and join uid to deviceid; neither call takes an id filter for boards, so re-read the whole list.
  3. callback usb_change usb_change (WS callback) — on every event, journal data.code (19/20/12) and data.list per uid with a timestamp; that log is the flap counter.
  4. restart_usb GET /api/device/usb/restart?id=720A|<pid> — Trigger A: code 20 then 19 for the same uid, settling at state 1 with no code 12 — the board came back to the PC but not to the phone.
  5. (none — no Phonefarm error callback) error_push (WS) then /device/usb/restart — Trigger B: an error_push naming /mouse/down or /mouse/click as failed, or a mouse call returning hardware-not-connected/not-working, while the board still shows state 2.
  6. callback usb_change + get_usb_list usb_change (WS) + /config/usb/get — confirm recovery: expect 20 then 19 then 12, and re-poll until the pid is back at state 2; treat silence as failure on a bounded timeout, not success.
  7. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<deviceid> — preventive after any control-path disturbance: the measured cure for the silent stuck-click state, sent to the whole affected set in one call.
  8. get_device_screenshot + mouse_move + send_key /pic/screenshot?binary=true, /mouse/move, /key/sendkey — prove control is really back: move, then a mean-pixel-diff of a ~40 px box around the commanded point (landed pointer 1.4-9.8 vs an idle 0.02 floor); never MD5.
  9. (none — Windows PnP) none — if the board settles at state 1 after a reset, stop retrying and flag the slot for a hands-on reseat labelled by hub and port, since the API exposes no topology.
  10. restart_usb /api/device/usb/restart?id=720A|C241,720A|C214 — count flaps per uid per rolling day; three or more marks a swap candidate, and a whole hub can be reset in one comma-separated call if an operator confirms it.

Needs

  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in — with only IMService.exe up this rig showed both phones at state 0 and an empty board list, which would otherwise read as 19 simultaneous flaps.
  • Each phone bound to its board so a usb_change uid resolves to a deviceid; unbound boards can still be reset by vid|pid but yield nothing to verify against.
  • Firmware and kernel floors that cannot be checked from the API on this rig, since ver/uver read as mojibake.
  • A persistent event journal keyed by board uid, so flap counts survive a watchdog restart, and a hub/port map from Windows PnP to turn an opaque pid into a rack slot.
  • Per-phone iOS accessibility settings for the verification probe to mean anything — none is queryable, so a phone can be perfectly cabled and still ignore input.

Watch out

  • Resetting on a bare code 20 with no code 19 targets a board that has left the USB bus entirely — there is no addressee for a vid|pid reset. That is a physical-layer failure (board, cable, hub, or a human unplug) and belongs in a hands-on queue, not an automated reset.
  • There is no callback for the phone detaching from an otherwise-present board; a state 2 to state 1 transition, the most common rack fault, may raise no event at all. Cover it with a slow poll of /config/usb/get diffed against the board table, and do not claim the design is purely callback-driven.
  • The state field the whole design keys on is undocumented — the vendor's field table lists only vid/pid/uid/ver. The 1-versus-2 mapping is a measurement from this rig, corroborated by usb_change code 12, and should be re-checked after any kernel update.
  • /device/usb/restart has never been exercised on this rig, so the 20-19-12 sequence, the return to state 2, and the time it takes are all inference, not measurement. Validate on one expendable slot off-hours before letting the watchdog act unattended. A reset is also electrically equivalent to unplugging and replugging the cable, which can trigger iOS's "Trust This Computer?" prompt on that reconnection; nothing distinguishes that state from a plain failure, and the automation cannot reliably dismiss it.
  • Whether a code 20 callback carries the departed board's identity at all is unverified — the doc's only example is code 19. If it arrives empty, diff /config/usb/get instead of relying on the callback payload.
  • The firmware precondition is unverifiable here; a board too old for the reset will simply return an uncertain error code or produce no event, so treat silence as failure and stop retrying that board.
  • A reset is blind to whether a job is in flight — it can drop a held button mid-drag with no /mouse/up ever reaching the phone. Give the watchdog the same per-phone lock the job runner takes, or defer until the phone is idle.
  • Video is untouched by a board reset — air_pid stays the same and frames keep arriving — which is exactly why the fault is invisible without this watchdog, and why "the mirror looks fine" must never be read as evidence the reset worked.
  • Rate-limit resets (something like one per board per 10 minutes, a handful per day) or an automatic loop can mask a dying board, quietly bouncing a failing slot for weeks instead of escalating it. Hub-wide comma-list resets are tempting but blunt — every phone on that hub loses control at once, so keep them operator-confirmed only.
  • A partial-fleet firmware mismatch, undetectable given the mojibake version fields, could silently no-op the restart call on older boards with no distinguishable error code, inflating the flap counter for boards that are simply outdated rather than failing.

Scale

Event-driven and effectively free: one WebSocket carries callbacks for all 19 boards, with no per-board subscription, and the supplementary poll is a single small JSON list for the whole rack that can run every 2-5 seconds without noticeable cost. Recovery itself is a comma-list call, so N boards is one request. Measurements show input and control traffic do not interfere with frame polling in either direction, so the watchdog's own probes will not disturb a running wall. The only per-phone cost is the verification probe — one 1.62 MB raw BMP plus a short move — kept to the affected phone rather than swept across the rack. The expensive part is wall clock, not CPU: budget seconds of control outage per reset plus whatever settle time the attach sequence needs, and at the recommended one-reset-per-board-per-10-minutes rate limit this stays well under ten driven resets per hour per board even during a bad patch.

Scheduled fleet maintenance

Rolling reboot maintenance window with re-cast and input self-test

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

A scheduled overnight job that cycles a phone farm a batch at a time: disconnect the mirror so the drop is expected, reboot the batch in one call, wait for the boards to re-enumerate, re-cast, then prove each phone is genuinely usable again with a two-channel self-test before handing it back to the scheduler. The reboot is easy; proving the phone came back genuinely controllable is the real payload, and it is the difference between a rack that reports healthy and a rack that is healthy, since no health check that only watches "is it mirroring" will ever catch a phone that mirrors fine but silently ignores taps.

How

  1. get_device_list (+ get_group_list) /device/get, /device/group/get-dev — select the batch and record a "before" snapshot of state, ip, vid/pid/uid, imgw/imgh and air_pid for each device.
  2. get_usb_list /config/usb/get — snapshot the control channel before touching anything, so "never came back" can be told apart from "came back but did not re-cast" later.
  3. WebSocket ws://host:9911/clinet ws://<host>:9911/api — open before the batch starts and hold it for the window; it is the only way to receive dev_disconnect, usb_change, dev_connect, restart_log, airplay_connect_log and error_push.
  4. discon_airplay GET /api/device/airplay/disconnect?id=<ids> — announce the drop so it reads as maintenance, not a fault; wait for dev_disconnect before rebooting.
  5. (no Phonefarm equivalent) GET /api/shortcut/switch/device?id=<ids>&state=1 — reboot the batch via the iMouse Shortcut, needing no OCR plug-in and able to reboot a phone whose video channel is already dead.
  6. send_key GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=CTRL+ALT+SHIFT+WIN+r — fallback A if the Shortcut is not installed; needs Full Keyboard Access on but no Shortcut.
  7. restart_device GET /api/device/restart?id=<ids> — fallback B, do not lead with this; it drives the phone's own Settings UI and its Phonefarm sibling needed the OCR plug-in first.
  8. callback usb_change usb_change (WS) / /config/usb/get — wait for the phone using the control channel as the readiness signal (code 12, or polling for state 2), not a network ping that can answer before iOS accepts HID input.
  9. auto_connect_screen / auto_connect_screen_all /device/airplay/connect, /device/airplay/connect/all — re-cast the batch, watching airplay_connect_log for code 0 then dev_connect; this is the weak leg on this rig, since auto-cast drives Control Centre by sight and the plug-in it may need reads code 28 here.
  10. set_usb_autoairplay / get_usb_autoairplay /config/imserver/set, /config/imserver/get — alternative to a driven re-cast: set the global auto_connect flag once and let the kernel re-cast on its own; applies live with no restart.
  11. mouse_reset_pos /api/mouse/reset?id=<ids> — on each dev_connect, clear the input channel first; mandatory after a fresh board enumeration, not optional.
  12. mouse_move + get_device_screenshot /mouse/move, /pic/screenshot — self-test, pointer leg: move, then a mean-pixel-diff box around the target (landed 1.4-9.8 versus a 0.02 idle floor).
  13. send_key /key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) — self-test, keyboard leg and normalisation: a whole-frame diff above ~20 confirms hardware keys, but this alone proves nothing about taps.
  14. get_device_list + get_usb_list /device/get, /config/usb/get — mark the phone healthy only if board state 2, a fresh air_pid, the pointer-box diff, and the WIN+h diff all pass; report "controllable but blind" and "visible but deaf" as distinct outcomes.

Needs

  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in — without it the rack reports state 0 with an empty board list even though the kernel service is up, and the job cannot start it through the API.
  • iMouse Shortcut installed, kernel-IP-edited, permission-granted, and hotkey-bound on every phone in scope — not confirmed present on this rig; the hotkey fallback is likelier to actually work since it needs no Shortcut.
  • Each phone bound to its board with a non-empty location_crc, and a vendor-supplied cable only, since substituting a cable is a real failure mode.
  • Phone-side accessibility settings invisible to the API, and phones without a passcode or a human available to unlock afterward — nothing in either API can type a passcode.
  • A WebSocket client for the six callbacks this job depends on, and an external scheduler, since the kernel has no scheduling of its own.
  • For the driven reboot and (probably) the re-cast: the OCR and image-search plug-ins, not installed on this rig.

Watch out

  • The re-cast leg is the unverified half of this job here: the API error table's "no coordinates" and "plug-in not connected" codes point at the same OCR/image-search dependency the Phonefarm sibling states outright, and this rig's OCR plug-in reads code 28. Until someone fires the connect call and sees code 0, assume a rebooted phone may need to be re-cast by hand — turning an unattended nightly job into one that files a work order.
  • The reboot path itself is equally unverified: nothing in this rig's data confirms the iMouse Shortcut is actually installed on the two live XRs. Treat both the reboot and the recast as unproven in practice, not just the recast.
  • A passcode-locked phone reboots to a locked screen and stays out of service until a human types the code; only run this on phones configured without one, or accept a morning unlock round.
  • A data.code 30 "call timeout" on the reboot call is expected, not diagnostic — the phone is powering off and cannot answer in time. Do not retry on a 30, or you may reboot it again mid-boot; confirm by absence then return on the control channel instead.
  • auto_connect is a global kernel flag, not a per-device switch — you cannot arm auto-cast for just the maintenance batch.
  • Per-device air_* overrides disconnect the current cast and apply only on the next connect, so any override applied mid-window will not show up until the phone re-casts; order a config sweep before a cast sweep, not after.
  • Screenshot, image-find and OCR calls are single-id only, so the self-test cannot be batched the way mouse and key calls can; run one poller per phone concurrently, which measurement shows has no shared bottleneck.
  • Several of the vendor doc's own curl examples in the sections this job uses point at the wrong endpoint — trust the parameter tables, not the examples.
  • The API has no authentication and listens on all interfaces, so any host on the LAN can reboot the whole rack with one request; firewall 9911 before wiring anything to a scheduler.
  • This rig has only 2 phones mirroring out of 19 boards, so nothing about batch size or recast reliability at scale extrapolates from measurement here — it is a design assumption.
  • A reboot power-cycles USB enumeration too — expect the board to dip to state 1 before returning to state 2, and do not treat that intermediate dip as a fault.
  • The pointer-box threshold was measured at one specific coordinate and wallpaper; compute an idle floor per phone rather than hardcoding these numbers, since the two XRs already have different home screens.

Scale

Batch operations are genuinely one round trip — the shortcut, disconnect, connect, reset and sendkey calls all take a comma id list, and the board walks every listed phone in parallel. The per-batch cost is dominated by physics, not the API: roughly 60-90 seconds for an iPhone to reboot, plus the re-cast, plus a few seconds of self-test. The self-test is the only non-batchable part, since screenshot is single-id, but phones are independent and their polling measured no interference with input traffic, so the whole batch's self-tests run concurrently in well under a second each. A batch of 7 at roughly 3 minutes extrapolates to ~45 minutes for 100 phones, but that arithmetic is untested here; size batches by how many phones the rack can afford to have offline at once, not by API speed. If recast succeeds automatically every time, that is on the order of 20-30 verified cycles/hour/phone; if it needs manual Control Centre intervention, as the OCR code 28 result suggests it might, unattended throughput is effectively zero and this becomes a human-paced task rather than a script.

Proving the fleet is actually alive

Pointer-nudge liveness heartbeat that proves input is honoured

Native APIWith caveats

A per-phone background probe that proves the control path is actually alive, using an observation channel no API field provides: move the pointer between two fixed points in a visually dead zone and look for the small grey pointer dot arriving, by taking the mean absolute pixel difference in a small box around the destination. Every status field this rack exposes is a lie of omission — a bound board and a live mirror session say nothing about whether iOS is honouring input, and the accessibility settings that decide it are not queryable at all. This rig demonstrated the gap directly: a phone silently stopped accepting every click while moves and hardware keys kept working, and it looked perfect in every API field throughout. A landed pointer measures 1.4-9.8 against an idle noise floor of 0.02, needs no OCR plug-in, no image-search plug-in, no Shortcut and no professional edition, and turns "this phone has been silently dead since Tuesday" into a one-minute alert.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get (optionally ?id=a,b) — build the candidate set: only phones with a non-zero state and live air_pid, reading imgw/imgh per phone so a follower with different geometry is excluded from a shared move.
  2. get_usb_list GET /api/config/usb/get — confirm the control channel is physically present before blaming the pointer; state 2 means the board is enumerated and the phone is attached.
  3. get_device_screenshot (binary=true) GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true[&rect=...] — baseline capture of the probe box; works over plain HTTP on XP, measured 2.0 ms p50 for a full raw frame.
  4. mouse_move GET /api/mouse/move?id=<id1,id2,...>&x=<X>&y=<Y> — nudge the pointer at least ~40 px between two fixed points in a dead zone; one request drives every listed phone in parallel, and a 2 px hop is too small to move the low-contrast dot off its own prior position.
  5. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<one id>&binary=true[&rect=...] — wait for a genuinely new frame, then diff client-side; a landed pointer measures 1.4-9.8, idle noise is 0.02-0.03. Never MD5.
  6. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<id1,id2,...> — Rung 1 remediation: the only call confirmed to clear the silent stuck-click state; it also re-parks the pointer, so re-baseline after it.
  7. send_key (fn_key WIN+h) GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<id>&fn_key=WIN+h — on-demand escalation only, never on the routine timer: disambiguates a frozen mirror from a dead pointer path by producing a large whole-frame change.
  8. restart_usb GET /api/device/usb/restart?id=720A|<pid> — Rung 2 remediation: reset the control board, addressed by VID|PID from /device/get or /config/usb/get, not by phone id.
  9. (no Phonefarm equivalent) ws://127.0.0.1:9911/api — callback error_push — complementary passive signal at no polling cost: the only asynchronous proof an input call failed at the board, naming the failing function.
  10. discon_airplay / auto_connect_screen GET /api/device/airplay/disconnect?id=<ids> then /device/airplay/connect?id=<ids> — mirror recovery, only once the video channel is the confirmed fault; XP has no force flag, so disconnect first.

Needs

  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in — without it, both channel reads go empty regardless of hardware state.
  • Per phone: mirroring up, board bound and cabled, and mouse parameters present, or every mouse call fails outright.
  • Phone-side accessibility settings, none queryable over the API: AssistiveTouch on with tracking maxed, Trackpad & Mouse speed maxed, Full Keyboard Access on, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock.
  • A per-phone probe pair at least ~40 px apart in a visually stable dead zone, expressed in that phone's own imgw x imgh, and a per-phone landed-pointer threshold calibrated from that phone's own signal rather than assumed.
  • A client-side BMP decoder and mean-absolute-difference routine with a reused frame buffer, since unreused 1.6 MB frames measured 488 MB/s of allocation and 496 gen-2 collections per 8 s, falling to 2.9 MB/s and 0-1 with reuse.
  • A lease/mutex shared with the job queue so the nudge never fires mid-drag, and, optionally, one WebSocket for error_push, dev_disconnect and usb_change.

Watch out

  • The probe is necessary but not sufficient for taps. The measured stuck-click phone passed a move probe cleanly while every click produced only 0.09 mean diff against a 0.02 floor — a green heartbeat proves only that the board moves this phone's pointer, never that the phone honours taps. Label the metric control_pointer_alive, not "healthy," and pair it with a periodic real click-and-verify against a safe dead-zone target.
  • A failed probe is ambiguous between a frozen mirror and a dead pointer path — both read as roughly a 0.02 box diff. Only the state-changing WIN+h follow-up separates them, so the routine timer cannot classify the fault on its own, and that hotkey must stay an on-demand escalation, never a periodic call, since it leaves whatever app is open.
  • The pointer dot is low-contrast and only a few pixels across; on a bright or busy wallpaper the diff can fall under 1. Calibrate the threshold per phone from its own landed-pointer signal, not a fleet-wide constant, since wallpaper brightness changes the dot's contrast.
  • A "visually stable dead zone" and its coordinates are per-phone, not per-fleet — the two XRs already have different home screens, and any phone with different mirror geometry must be excluded from a shared comma-list move.
  • Frame arrival, not API latency, dominates the probe: one XR delivers ~29 new frames/s under motion, its twin only ~4.5, so a fixed timeout tuned for the fast phone will falsely fail the slow one. Wait on an actually-changed frame with a per-phone deadline.
  • No server-side comparison is available on this rig — the OCR plug-in reads code 28 and the image-search plug-in is presumed absent too, so the mean-pixel-diff must be implemented entirely in the caller.
  • The nudge is visible on the mirror and perturbs the hover target in whatever app is open; it must be gated by the job-queue lease so it can never land inside a drag, and server-side rect cropping's latency benefit is unmeasured on this rig, so do not assume it beats the full-frame baseline without checking.
  • The whole scheme presumes the vendor console is running — with only the kernel service up, both channels read as empty, and a fleet-wide "all dead" reading usually means the console crashed, not that every board failed. Board-reset remediation needs a kernel and firmware floor that is only readable on the phone, since the version fields are mojibake on this build.
  • The API has no authentication; a monitor that can nudge every pointer in the rack is reachable by any host on the LAN, so firewall 9911 to trusted hosts.

Scale

Cost per phone per probe: two screenshot calls at ~2.0 ms p50 each, plus a share of two move requests that carry the whole comma-separated id list — because the board walks all listed phones in parallel, the two ~40 px hops cost roughly 25 ms of board time for the entire fleet, not per phone. For 19 phones once a minute, that is 38 screenshot requests and 2 move requests per minute against a measured ceiling of 84 req/s per phone and 512 req/s aggregate across ten concurrent pollers. Bandwidth is the real constraint, not CPU: 38 full frames a minute is roughly 62 MB/min on loopback, which is why rect cropping and a reused per-poller buffer matter more than the request count. The wall-clock probe duration is dominated by frame arrival — ~100 ms on the fast phone versus ~700 ms on the slow one — and screenshots are inherently one request per phone by documented rule, so run pollers concurrently and stagger start times. At a conservative once-a-minute cadence this is roughly 120 screenshot requests/hour/phone with orders of magnitude of headroom below the measured ceiling; the fastest sustainable cadence bounded by the slowest phone is on the order of one cycle per second, though a production heartbeat should run far below that to leave headroom for real job traffic.

Mirroring bandwidth policy

Energy-mode policy by time of day, and the capacity it buys

PartialWith caveats

Run the rack on two mirroring profiles: high fidelity while an operator is watching a wall of live tiles, low bandwidth overnight while only scripts drive the phones. On this XP kernel there is no single mode switch, only per-device knobs on /device/airplay/set (air_ratio, air_refresh, air_fps, air_img_fps, air_audio) plus a global floor in /config/imserver/set. Mirroring bandwidth, not CPU or USB, is what decides how many phones one PC and one access point can carry, and the vendor's own figures give a rough capacity model, though the switch is cheap while the re-cast and re-verification that follow it are not.

How

  1. get_airplay_mode GET /api/device/get — snapshot air_ratio/refresh/fps/img_fps/audio and imgw/imgh per phone before changing anything; XP has no /device/airplay/get, so /device/get is the only read-back.
  2. none GET /api/config/imserver/get — read the global air_play_* baseline that per-device zero fields fall back to.
  3. none GET /api/config/user/info — read total_license and dev_online_num, the other half of the capacity ceiling.
  4. set_airplay_mode airplay_mode=0 GET /api/device/airplay/set?id=<ids>&air_ratio=720&air_fps=10&air_img_fps=5&air_audio=1 — drop the whole fleet to a low-bandwidth night profile in one request.
  5. set_airplay_mode airplay_mode=2 GET /api/device/airplay/set?id=<ids>&air_ratio=0&air_fps=30&air_img_fps=30&air_refresh=60&air_audio=0 — restore day fidelity; 0 means "use the global setting," not a literal maximum.
  6. restart GET /api/config/imserver/set?air_play_ratio=720&air_play_fps=10 then GET /api/imserver/restart — move the kernel-wide floor instead of per-device overrides; needs a full restart that drops every session.
  7. auto_connect_screen(_all) GET /api/device/airplay/connect?id=<ids> or /connect/all — re-cast, because the profile change itself dropped the picture.
  8. dev_connect callback WS callbacks airplay_connect_log then dev_connect / dev_change — watch the re-cast rather than sleeping on a fixed delay.
  9. get_device_list GET /api/device/get?id=<ids> — re-read imgw/imgh; the tap coordinate space is not guaranteed stable across a profile change.
  10. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<ids> — clear the stuck-click state a re-cast can leave behind.
  11. loop_device_screenshot poll GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true — confirm the new profile is actually delivering the frame rate you expect.
  12. shortcut#15 GET /api/shortcut/switch/bril?id=<ids>&state=0.1 — optional phone-side brightness lever; not set up or confirmed on this rig.

Needs

  • XP kernel reachable at 9911 with path-style calls; Phonefarm function names such as set_airplay_mode return HTTP 500 here.
  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in — with only IMService.exe up, /device/get and /config/usb/get both come back empty.
  • A way to re-cast after every switch: /device/airplay/connect (unverified, needs the OCR plug-in path), the global auto_connect flag, or a manual Control Centre re-cast.
  • Every phone already mirroring and bound before the transition starts; an offline phone is not "restored" by the policy.
  • Vision assets re-tuned per profile, since colour tables and coordinates are resolution-specific.
  • An external scheduler — there is no cron, timer or schedule primitive in either API.

Watch out

  • The three named Phonefarm modes (0/1/2) do not exist on XP; the night/day air_* combinations here are a home-grown mapping, not a vendor-defined mode.
  • The 5/10/20 Mbps and ~100/50/25-phone figures come from a single Phonefarm-doc sentence about "one landscape game"; nothing on this two-phone rig can confirm or refute them — treat any capacity number as a hypothesis.
  • Every /device/airplay/set call, even one that only touches air_audio, is documented to drop the cast — schedule the switch inside a maintenance window, never mid-job.
  • The global route needs /imserver/restart, which drops every mirroring session and every WebSocket client fleet-wide at once.
  • Automated re-cast is unverified on this rig: /device/airplay/connect drives Control Centre through the board, and the OCR plug-in this depends on reports code 28 here.
  • Type mismatch trap: global air_play_audio is Boolean, per-device air_audio is an Integer (0/1/2); crossing them is a silent-looking parameter error (code 36).
  • imgw/imgh is not guaranteed stable across a profile change; a stale cached coordinate taps the wrong place with no error — taps return code 0 either way.
  • Lowering the profile does not fix a slow phone: two identical XRs on this rig measured ~29 and ~4.5 new frames per second on the same LAN, which is the phone's own Wi-Fi link, not the profile.
  • There is no per-device auto-cast flag on XP; auto_connect is one global Boolean, so "these phones re-cast themselves, those don't" is not expressible.
  • No scheduler exists in the API — the time-of-day half of this idea is entirely external tooling holding unauthenticated control of every phone on the subnet.

Scale

The switch calls themselves are free at any fleet size: /device/airplay/set, /connect, /disconnect and /mouse/reset all take a comma-separated id list, so flipping 100 phones is one request per operation, and as a scheduled transition it is two calls a day, not a continuous action. Verification does not scale the same way: /pic/screenshot is single-id only, so proving the new profile is delivering frames costs one poller per phone — measured at 83-85 req/s per two concurrent pollers and 512 req/s aggregate across ten, with input and video traffic non-interfering, but that is a two-phone loopback measurement and says nothing about 100 phones over real Wi-Fi. The vendor-sourced 5/10/20 Mbps figures translate to roughly 100/50/25 phones per typical access point in theory; treat that as an unverified extrapolation pending a real multi-phone contention test. Budget ~1.6 MB per raw BMP poll with a reused buffer per poller, and expect the re-cast, not the profile call, to dominate the real transition cost.

Physical fleet management

Torch beacon and slot roll-call: finding a phone physically in the rack

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Turn an opaque device id into something a technician can pick up: light the target phone's camera LED with /shortcut/switch/torch so it is the only glowing unit in a wall of identical XRs, and run a periodic roll-call that lights each slot in turn to audit whether the kernel's name labels still match physical positions. The LED is a camera flash, not part of the AirPlay picture, so this beacon has no observation channel on this rig; it is paired with a second, plug-in-free fallback beacon over /key/sendkey whose whole-screen repaint IS visible in the mirror and confirmable by pixel diff. Nineteen boards on three hubs with identical cables and identical phones means a MAC address or PID tells a technician nothing about which unit to unplug, and the API exposes no physical location at all.

How

  1. get_device_list + get_usb_list GET /api/device/get?id=<id> and GET /api/config/usb/get — confirm video-ready (state, air_pid) and control-ready (board state 2) before beaconing.
  2. none none — Windows PnP, not the API — build the physical hub/port slot map once; no XP endpoint returns hub or port.
  3. set_dev GET /api/device/set?id=<id>&name=H10-P02 — persist the slot label into the device record's name field so an alert can name it.
  4. shortcut#16 GET /api/shortcut/switch/torch?id=<id>&state=1&outtime=3000 — light the target phone's camera LED (Phonefarm marks the equivalent professional-version only; the XP docs carry no such gate).
  5. none none — human in the loop — technician walks to the one glowing slot; there is no API way to confirm the LED actually lit.
  6. shortcut#17 GET /api/shortcut/switch/torch?id=<id>&state=0 — beacon off, always sent from a finally block; a comma list makes an "all torches off" sweep one call.
  7. send_key (fn_key) GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<id>&fn_key=ControlBar — USB-only fallback beacon (also NoticeBar, WIN+h) that repaints the phone's own screen, visible in the mirror.
  8. get_device_screenshot GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true — confirm the fallback beacon fired via a before/after mean-pixel-diff.
  9. get_group_list / get_device_list GET /api/device/group/get-dev?id=<gid> — enumerate a rack section, then loop the beacon per device in your own PnP-derived slot order, not the API's own order.
  10. set_dev (vid+pid) GET /api/device/set?id=<id>&vid=720A&pid=<pid> — rebind when the light comes up in the wrong slot; one call per phone.
  11. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<ids> — clear the stuck-click state before any tap-critical follow-up on the located phone.

Needs

  • iMouse iOS Shortcut installed and AssistiveTouch-bound on every phone to beacon via torch — unverified and unprobed on this rig.
  • Both channels alive at once for the torch: the USB board bound and connected (fires the hotkey) and the phone reachable on the LAN (the Shortcut answers over Wi-Fi).
  • Phone unlocked, Auto-Lock Never, and no pending iOS "Allow" prompt blocking the Shortcut.
  • Fallback path needs only a bound, connected board plus Full Keyboard Access on — works with Wi-Fi down and no Shortcut installed.
  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in.
  • A hand-built slot map joining Windows PnP hub and port to the device record's name field, since nothing in the API supplies it.

Watch out

  • No observation channel for the torch: the LED is a camera flash, not carried in the AirPlay stream, so data.code 0 only proves the Shortcut answered, never that the light came on — any console UI should say "beacon requested," never "beacon on."
  • A multi-id torch call returns one aggregate result code, so an audit needing per-phone truth means one call per id — 19x the calls for a full rack.
  • The beacon fails on exactly the phones you most want to find, since it needs both the board and Wi-Fi paths a broken phone has likely lost; the fn_key fallback is the primary tool for a genuinely dead slot, not an afterthought.
  • Default outtime is 15000 ms; 19 unresponsive slots at default is nearly five minutes of dead air — lower it to roughly 3000 ms.
  • The realistic state of this rig today: the torch path has never been demonstrated to work at all; only the fn_key fallback is verified-workable.
  • /device/group/get-dev order is the kernel's, not physical order — the roll-call must be sequenced from your own PnP-derived slot map.
  • Rebinding via /device/set is one phone per call, and vid/pid must be sent together — a rack-wide rebind is N calls.
  • Prefer a steady-on LED over a blink pattern; a strobing wall of phones is a real photosensitivity hazard for little added visibility.
  • The torch does not need the OCR or image-search plug-ins, so this rig's code-28 blocker does not apply here — the dependency is the separately unverified on-phone Shortcut.

Scale

Beacon-on and beacon-off are each one call for the whole rack, since /shortcut/switch/torch takes a comma id list, at the cost of a single aggregate result code with no per-phone breakdown. A sequential per-phone roll-call is two calls per slot plus dwell: at a 2 s dwell with outtime lowered to ~3000 ms, 19 slots is roughly 40 seconds plus call latency. The fn_key fallback beacon also fans out on a comma list and costs the same wall time for one phone or all of them, since it never touches /mouse/move or the ~0.6 ms/px pointer-walk cost. Verifying the fallback is single-id only, measured at 84 req/s and p50 2 ms per raw BMP poll with phones fully independent (two pollers 83+85 req/s, ten pollers 512 req/s aggregate); the weak XR's ~4.5 fps means a before/after diff there needs 220 ms or more for a genuinely new frame. The torch path itself has no measurable throughput, because code 0 has never been confirmed to correspond to a lit LED on this rig.

Storage housekeeping

Storage hygiene: scheduled album and file cleanup with size-growth tracking

Needs ShortcutWith caveats

Sweep every phone on a schedule through the iMouse iOS Shortcut: enumerate the camera roll and the Files directory the rig writes into, optionally harvest anything worth keeping to the PC, then delete by name or wipe a whole album. Each listing returns name, ext, size and create_time, so the controller can sum a per-phone byte total each run and trend it. The XP API has no storage, free-space or battery endpoint of any kind, so this enumerated total is the only available proxy for "how full is this phone getting," converting an otherwise unobservable failure into a trended number with a threshold.

How

  1. shortcut#24 GET /api/shortcut/device/ip?id=<id>&state=0 — cheapest proof the Shortcut path is alive before trusting any listing.
  2. shortcut#1 GET /api/shortcut/album/get?id=<id>&album_name=&num=200&outtime=60000 — enumerate the camera roll; size comes back as a formatted string, not a number.
  3. shortcut#4 GET /api/shortcut/file/get?id=<id>&path=/iMouse/&outtime=60000 — enumerate the Files directory the rig writes into; per-directory only, not recursive.
  4. shortcut#2 / shortcut#5 POST /api/shortcut/album/down and /api/shortcut/file/down — optionally harvest anything worth keeping to the PC before deleting.
  5. shortcut#3 / shortcut#6 POST /api/shortcut/album/del and /api/shortcut/file/del — delete named items; a comma id list applies one shared filename list to every listed device.
  6. none (XP-only) POST /api/shortcut/album/clear {id, album_name, outtime} — wipe a whole album; irreversible from the API's side, so harvest first.
  7. none none — controller-side — parse each size string to bytes, sum per phone per run, persist and trend, alert on absolute total or daily delta.
  8. none none — external scheduler — there is no cron or job endpoint in either edition; raise outtime well above the 15000 ms default for long listings and transfers.

Needs

  • iMouse Shortcut installed on every phone with Allow Running Scripts, Allow Sharing Large Amounts of Data, and both delete-without-confirmation permissions on.
  • Shortcut fetched from the console's QR code, its IP field edited to the kernel PC, run once with every "Allow" prompt answered.
  • Shortcut bound to an AssistiveTouch key, triggered by a HID hotkey from a board that is bound and at /config/usb/get state 2.
  • Phone reachable from the kernel on the LAN — the Shortcut posts its results back to port 9911 — and unlocked with Auto-Lock Never.
  • iOS 15+ for every file call (these XRs qualify on 18.7.10).
  • IMConsole.exe running and logged in.
  • Deliberately does not need the OCR or image-search plug-ins; this chain never touches /pic/*.

Watch out

  • None of the /shortcut/* endpoints have actually been probed on this rig; the 10 Sep probe never touched them — treat the whole chain as unverified until the device-ip check passes.
  • size comes back as a human-readable string ("5.4 MB"), so a summed total is a relative trend indicator, not an accounting figure.
  • No date filter exists on XP; age-based retention has to be computed client-side from create_time, which means listing everything you might delete first.
  • num defaults to 10 with no documented maximum, and ordering is only implied — a phone with thousands of photos may under-report growth from a truncated listing.
  • The listing only sees the Photos library and the queried Files directory; app caches, mail attachments and system storage are invisible, so this is a leading indicator, not a storage gauge.
  • Deletion likely moves items to Recently Deleted for 30 days on iOS, which would leave the enumerated total reduced without freeing space immediately — unverified by either vendor doc, so test before trusting cleanup to recover space.
  • Multi-device addressing is asymmetric: listings and transfers are single-id only, while deletes take a comma id list applied to one shared filename list — only correct for identically named rig-generated files.
  • outtime is milliseconds on XP and seconds in the Phonefarm doc; porting Phonefarm sample values gives 15 ms timeouts instead of 15 seconds.
  • The Shortcut round trip (board hotkey, AssistiveTouch, app launch, Wi-Fi POST-back) is unmeasured and almost certainly does not share the concurrency headroom of the measured /pic/screenshot and /mouse/* numbers — budget serial execution or very low concurrency (2-4 phones) until measured.
  • A phone with a weak Wi-Fi link should be expected to have a slower, less reliable Shortcut round trip too, since the POST-back rides the same link that delivers only ~4.5 fps on this rig's weak XR.

Scale

Each phone's cost is dominated by the Shortcut round trip, not the HTTP call itself — board hotkey, AssistiveTouch, app launch, Wi-Fi POST-back — with a default 15 s ceiling per call, so a full sweep of one phone is seconds, not milliseconds. Listings are single-id, so a 19-slot rack is at least 38 sequential listing calls; deletes collapse onto a comma list only where filenames are shared across phones. Whether shortcut calls from different phones run in parallel is unverified — the measured per-phone independence on this rig (two pollers 83+85 req/s, ten pollers 512 req/s) applies to /pic/screenshot and /mouse/*, not to the hotkey-plus-LAN Shortcut path, which funnels through each phone's own board and Wi-Fi link. Plan a bounded concurrency of 4-8 phones inside a maintenance window and measure before widening; a realistic full-rack sweep runs on the order of 3-10 minutes, longer with any zip harvest, so this is designed as one sweep per maintenance window rather than a repeating loop.

Calibration and link-health diagnostics

Calibration library curation and pointer-accuracy drift audit

PartialWith caveats

Treat the mouse-parameter calibration record as a curated fleet asset rather than something the kernel silently auto-matches. For every phone: confirm a library record exists for its model and iOS version, confirm the device record actually carries a non-empty location_crc, then measure real pointer accuracy by commanding three known mirror-pixel coordinates and locating the pointer dot in a raw BMP frame by pixel diff. Both XRs on this rig share one library CRC, byte-identical to the vendor's own doc example rather than a per-device measurement; nothing in the API tells you whether that profile is correct, and a wrong record does not error, it just puts every tap a few percent off.

How

  1. get_device_list GET /api/device/get — read location/location_crc, model, version and imgw/imgh per phone; an empty location_crc fails every /mouse call with code 11.
  2. get_devicemodel_list GET /api/config/devicemodel/get — confirm a library record exists for this model plus iOS version; the XP doc elides the response shape, so probe it once before parsing.
  3. mouse_reset_pos GET /api/mouse/reset?id=<ids> — reset the pointer to a known origin before the probe.
  4. mouse_move + get_device_screenshot GET /api/mouse/move?id=<ids>&x=&y= then GET /api/pic/screenshot?id=<id>&binary=true — command three known mirror-pixel points (near-origin, far corner, centre) and grab a frame after each.
  5. (analysis) (analysis, no call) — a small constant offset is normal; an error that grows toward the far corner is a scale error needing a per-device collection.
  6. send_key (fn_key) + click GET /api/key/sendkey?id=<ids>&fn_key=WIN+h (twice) then GET /api/mouse/click?id=<id>&x=&y= — functional cross-check to rule out the stuck-click state before condemning a calibration record.
  7. mouse_collection_open + cfg GET /api/device/collection/mouse?id=<id>&cmd=1 — start a per-device collection; XP collapses Phonefarm's open/cfg/close trio into one cmd-coded path.
  8. mouse_collection_cfg_ret + collection WS callback collection_mouse — watch progress codes (8 scan QR, 9 enter collection page, 14 start working, 21 working) rather than polling.
  9. mouse_collection_close GET /api/device/collection/mouse?id=<id>&cmd=2 — always stop collection; a stuck session blocks every other phone's collection with code 5.
  10. save_dev_location GET /api/device/collection/mouse/save?id=<id>&describe=<text> — publish the record to the shared library so same-model phones auto-match on connect; irreversible on XP, no delete endpoint exists.
  11. set_dev (location_crc) GET /api/device/set?id=<ids>&location_crc=<crc> — pin other same-model phones to the known-good CRC; a comma list covers a whole model group in one call.
  12. dev_connect callback WS callbacks dev_connect / dev_change — re-arm the audit whenever a phone's iOS version changes, since the library key is model plus iOS version.

Needs

  • XP kernel reachable at 9911 with path-style calls; IMConsole.exe running and logged in.
  • Board bound and at /config/usb/get state 2 per phone — control readiness is a separate channel from video readiness.
  • Phone-side accessibility settings the calibration was collected against (AssistiveTouch on at maximum sensitivity, tracking speed at maximum, Full Keyboard Access on, Auto-Lock Never, portrait lock) — none of these are queryable over the API.
  • For collection only: the vendor console's QR code to open the phone-side collection page; the XP docs do not document that URL directly.
  • Only one phone collecting at a time per kernel.
  • No plug-in required for any step — the probe uses pointer-dot pixel diff rather than OCR or image-search.

Watch out

  • The audit half is fully native and already live-probed on this rig; the collection half needs a manual QR-driven step, which is what keeps this out of "native."
  • /config/devicemodel/get's response body is elided in the XP doc ("too many, omitted") — the field shape must be probed before parsing, not assumed from the Phonefarm sibling's shape.
  • The doc contradicts itself on collection concurrency (comma-list id versus a "device is collecting" error) — assume serial, one phone at a time.
  • There is no delete endpoint for a bad library record on XP; a bad publish is permanent and can only be superseded by collecting again and re-pinning phones to the new CRC.
  • A wrong location_crc is worse than an empty one — empty fails loudly with code 11, wrong succeeds and lands taps somewhere plausible. Never write a CRC that was not read from the library or freshly collected.
  • The probe measures where the pointer went, not whether a tap registered — always reset first, since a move-lands-but-click-does-nothing result is the stuck-click state, not bad calibration.
  • Frame timing bounds the probe: the board walks at ~0.6 ms/px, and the two XRs deliver wildly different frame rates (~29 versus ~4.5 new frames/s) — wait for a genuinely new frame rather than assuming a fixed rate.
  • Grouping probe moves into one comma-separated request only works for phones sharing identical imgw/imgh.
  • Only two of nineteen boards currently have a bound, mirroring phone — the full-rack throughput numbers are extrapolated, not measured beyond n=2; a realistic estimate is 5-15 seconds of wall time for a 19-board rack, not an optimistic 3-5 seconds, once per-phone frame-wait stacks on top of board-walk time.
  • Publishing to the shared library carries the uploading phone's own device name in an "upname" field — rename the phone and use a neutral describe string before publishing, since this is a fleet-wide, irreversible record.

Scale

Per phone the probe is one reset, three moves and three raw-BMP grabs: board time dominates at ~0.6 ms/px, roughly 1.05 s of pointer walk across the three probe points, while raw BMP grabs are cheap at p50 2 ms. The real per-phone cost is waiting for a new frame after each move, about 35 ms on the fast XR and 220 ms or more on the slow one, so budget roughly 2 s per phone end to end. Because /mouse/move fans out on a comma list and the board walks every listed phone in parallel for the same wall time, a whole geometry-matched group costs the same as one phone to move; only the screenshots are single-id and fan out independently (measured 83+85 req/s with two pollers, 512 req/s with ten). A more defensible estimate for a 19-board rack of identical geometry is 5-15 seconds of wall time, not an optimistic 3-5, once frame-wait is stacked on top of board-walk rather than assumed simultaneous. Collection is the opposite: strictly serial, one phone at a time with a manual QR step, so budget 1-3 minutes per phone and treat it as a per-model-per-iOS one-off rather than a fleet loop.

Wi-Fi link-quality scorer: rank phones by delivered frames per second

Native APIWith caveats

Drive every phone with one mirrored swipe request, poll each phone's raw AirPlay frames in parallel, and count how many are genuinely new by mean absolute pixel difference. The resulting new-frames-per-second figure is each phone's delivered mirror rate, trended per phone per day and fed into the scheduler as that phone's screen-verification timeout.
